lessons.title: How Did Rome Hold an Empire Together?
lessons.title_zh: 羅馬怎麼管住那麼大的地方？
lessons.blurb_en: Build a stone arch in 3D, take away its wooden frame, and find out when it stands and when it falls. Then watch Rome grow on a map, and sort out which Roman wonders were older than Rome.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 裡蓋一座石拱，拆掉木頭拱架，看看它什麼時候站得住、什麼時候會塌。再從地圖上看羅馬怎麼長大，分一分哪些羅馬的奇蹟其實比羅馬還早。
lessons.big_idea_en: Rome grew from one city into an empire that stretched from Britain to the Middle East. It was held together not only by armies, but also by roads, shared laws, the spread of citizenship, aqueducts, and cities. It was also built by conquest, and the people who were conquered paid a heavy price.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 羅馬從一座城市長成一個從不列顛延伸到中東的帝國。把它連在一起的，不只是軍隊，還有道路、共同的法律、公民權的擴大、水道和城市。它也是征服來的，被征服的人付出了沉重的代價。

lab.title_en: How Does a Stone Arch Hold Itself Up?
lab.title_zh: 一座石拱怎麼撐住自己？
lab.how_en: Press Build it to place the wedge-shaped stones on a wooden frame, from both sides, with the keystone last. Then remove the centering and see whether the arch stands. Try leaving out the keystone, or dragging the thickness down: when the arch is too thin, or a stone is missing, it falls in the typical way, with the top dropping and the sides pushed outward.
lab.how_zh: 按「蓋起來」，楔形石會從兩邊放到木頭拱架上，拱心石最後放。接著拆掉拱架，看拱站不站得住。試試少放拱心石，或把厚度往下拉：拱太薄、或少了一塊石頭時，它會用典型的方式塌下來：頂端往下掉，兩側被推向外面。

centering.en: The wooden centering is holding the stones up. Take it away to see whether the arch can stand on its own.
centering.zh: 現在是木頭拱架托著石頭。把拱架拆掉，看看拱能不能自己站住。

missing.en: A stone is missing. Without the keystone the two halves lean in and fall.
missing.zh: 少了一塊石頭。沒有拱心石，兩邊的半拱往中間倒，就塌下來了。

thin.en: Every stone is in place, but the arch is too thin. The push inside the arch runs outside the stones, and it folds.
thin.zh: 石頭都到位了，但拱太薄。拱裡面推來推去的力跑到石頭外面，拱就折下來了。

ok.en: The arch stands by itself. Each stone presses on its neighbors, and the abutments hold the push at the ends.
ok.zh: 拱自己站住了。每一塊石頭都壓著旁邊的石頭，兩端的拱座擋住往外推的力。

lab.numbers_note_en: A half-circle arch carrying only its own weight needs a thickness of at least about 0.1075 times its radius, measured to the middle of the stones (Milankovitch's solution; Heyman's simpler method gives about 0.106). This assumes the stones do not slide or crush and the abutments do not move. Real arches also carry roads, water, or walls.
lab.numbers_note_zh: 一座只承受自己重量的半圓拱，厚度至少要有半徑（量到石頭的中線）的大約 0.1075 倍（米蘭科維奇的解；海曼比較簡單的方法算出約 0.106）。這假設石頭不會滑動、不會被壓碎，拱座也不會移動。真實的拱上面還壓著道路、水道或牆。

legend.en: Wooden centering that holds the stones until the arch is closed
legend.zh: 木頭拱架：拱合起來之前先托住石頭

lab.scale_en: This is a teaching sketch. The size, the number of stones, and the way it falls are illustrations; the rule for how thin an arch can be comes from a simplified model described below.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意。大小、石頭的數量和塌下來的樣子都是示意；拱最薄能多薄，依下面說明的簡化模型。
lab.credit_html: Model: an illustration made for this lesson. The minimum thickness follows the sources listed at the bottom of the page. 模型：為這一課製作的示意。最小厚度依本頁最下面列出的資料。

paras: In Lesson 5, Athens was a small city-state. Rome began small too, as a city in central Italy. Later Romans said it was founded in 753 BCE and became a republic in 509 BCE, but these are traditions; the early centuries are poorly recorded. By about 275 BCE Rome ruled Italy. Over the next two and a half centuries it fought its way around the Mediterranean Sea, and in 27 BCE the republic became an empire ruled by emperors.

How do you hold together lands from Britain to Egypt? One answer was roads. A recent digital atlas maps about 300,000 kilometers of roads in the Roman Empire around 150 CE, though the exact route of most of them is not known for certain. Soldiers, messengers, traders, and travelers used them. Roads let the government send orders and armies quickly, and let goods and ideas move too.

Another answer was building. The Romans did not invent the arch, but they used it on a huge scale, in bridges, aqueducts, and great buildings. Over about 500 years, eleven aqueducts were built to bring water to the city of Rome. One aqueduct for the city of Nîmes, in Gaul, ran about 50 kilometers and dropped only about 11 meters along the way, crossing a valley on the three-level bridge now called the Pont du Gard. Rome's water commissioner Frontinus compared the aqueducts with the “idle Pyramids.”

Rome also spread its laws and its citizenship. At first, Roman citizens were mainly the people of the city of Rome and the lands near it. Over time, citizenship was given to more and more people, and in 212 CE the emperor Caracalla gave it to almost all free people in the empire. Much later, in the 500s CE, Roman law was collected into one great work. Taiwan's civil law belongs to the continental European civil-law tradition, whose roots go back to Roman law.

But the empire was built by conquest. The Romans destroyed Carthage in 146 BCE and enslaved its people. Ancient writers such as Plutarch claimed that Julius Caesar's wars in Gaul killed a million people; historians doubt the exact figures, but the losses were enormous. In Britain, Queen Boudica led a revolt after Roman officials seized her family's kingdom. In 70 CE, Roman soldiers captured Jerusalem and burned its Temple.

At the same time, at the other end of Asia, the Han dynasty ruled China. In 97 CE a Han envoy named Gan Ying traveled west toward Rome and reached a great sea, but turned back. In 166 CE, a Chinese history records, men who said they came from the king of Da Qin, the Chinese name for Rome, arrived through what is now Vietnam. The western half of the Roman Empire ended in 476 CE, while the eastern half lasted much longer. Lesson 7 looks at how the Han held their own empire together.
paras_zh: 第五課的雅典是一個小城邦。羅馬一開始也很小，是義大利中部的一座城市。後來的羅馬人說，羅馬建於西元前 753 年，在西元前 509 年成為共和國；不過這些都是傳統的說法，最早的幾百年記錄很少。大約西元前 275 年，羅馬統治了義大利。接下來的兩百五十年左右，它一路打到地中海四周；西元前 27 年，共和國變成由皇帝統治的帝國。
從不列顛到埃及，這麼大的地方要怎麼連在一起？一個答案是道路。一份新的數位地圖集，畫出西元 150 年前後羅馬帝國大約三十萬公里的道路；不過其中大部分的確切路線，並不能確定。士兵、信差、商人和旅人都走這些路。有了路，政府可以很快送出命令、調動軍隊，貨物和想法也跟著流動。
另一個答案是建設。拱不是羅馬人發明的，但他們把拱用到很大的規模：橋、水道和大型建築。五百年間，羅馬一共蓋了十一條把水送進城裡的水道。高盧的尼姆城有一條水道，長約 50 公里，一路上只下降大約 11 公尺，還靠一座三層的橋跨過一個山谷，就是今天所說的加爾橋。羅馬的水務官弗朗提努斯，把這些水道拿來和「閒置的金字塔」相比。
羅馬也把它的法律和公民權傳了出去。一開始，羅馬公民主要是羅馬城和附近地方的人。後來公民權給了越來越多的人；西元 212 年，卡拉卡拉皇帝把它給了帝國裡幾乎所有的自由人。很久以後，在西元 500 年代，羅馬法被整理成一部大全。台灣的民法屬於歐陸法（大陸法）傳統，這個傳統的根源可以追溯到羅馬法。
但是這個帝國是征服來的。西元前 146 年，羅馬人摧毀了迦太基，把那裡的人變成奴隸。普魯塔克等古代的作者說，凱撒在高盧的戰爭殺了一百萬人；歷史學家懷疑確切的數字，但損失非常巨大。在不列顛，羅馬官員奪走布狄卡女王家族的王國以後，她領導了一場起事。西元 70 年，羅馬軍隊攻下耶路撒冷，燒毀了聖殿。
在同一個時代，亞洲的另一端是漢朝統治的中國。西元 97 年，一位叫甘英的漢朝使者往西朝羅馬走，到了一片大海邊，卻折返了。一部中國的史書記載，西元 166 年，自稱是大秦（中國對羅馬的稱呼）國王派來的人，經由今天的越南來到中國。羅馬帝國的西半部在西元 476 年結束，東半部則延續了更久。第七課要看漢朝怎麼把自己的帝國連在一起。
questions: Name three things, other than armies, that helped hold the Roman Empire together.
Why does a stone arch need a wooden frame while it is being built, and what lets it stand afterward?
The lesson says the Romans did not invent the arch. What did they do with it instead?
answers: Roads, shared laws, the spread of citizenship, aqueducts, and cities. Any three are correct.

Until the last stone, the keystone, is in place, the two halves of the arch cannot lean on each other, so they must be held up. Once the arch is closed, each stone presses on its neighbors, the abutments hold the outward push, and if the arch is thick enough it stands on its own.
They used it on a huge scale, in bridges, aqueducts, and great buildings, and combined arches in new ways, such as the groin vault.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Press Build it. The stones go up from both sides at once, resting on the wooden centering, and the keystone closes the arch at the top.
parts.text_zh: 按「蓋起來」。石頭從兩邊同時往上放，靠木頭拱架托著，最後由拱心石在頂端把拱合起來。

parts.text_en: With every stone in place and the arch thick enough, the frame can be taken away. Each stone presses on its neighbors, and the abutments hold the outward push.
parts.text_zh: 每一塊石頭都到位、拱又夠厚，拱架就可以拆掉。每一塊石頭都壓著旁邊的石頭，兩端的拱座擋住往外推的力。

parts.text_en: Without the last stone, the two halves cannot lean on each other. The top drops and the sides swing outward.
parts.text_zh: 少了最後一塊，兩個半拱就沒辦法互相靠著。頂端往下掉，兩側往外甩。

parts.text_en: Drag the thickness down. In a simple model, a half-circle arch under its own weight needs a thickness of about 0.11 of its radius, or it folds.
parts.text_zh: 把厚度往下拉。在簡化的模型裡，一座只受自己重量的半圓拱，厚度要有半徑的大約 0.11 倍，不然就會折下來。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try your own arch. What is the thinnest arch you can make that still stands without the centering?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著自己試試看。拆掉拱架還站得住的拱，最薄可以多薄？

empire.lead_en: Pull the slider from 300 BCE toward 120 CE. Each region lights up when it came under Roman rule. Click a number to read how it happened. The map shows Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East, land only, with no modern borders.
empire.lead_zh: 把滑桿從西元前 300 年往西元 120 年拉。每個地區在被羅馬統治的時候亮起來。點一個號碼，看看是怎麼發生的。地圖畫的是歐洲、北非和中東，只畫陸地，不畫今天的國界。
empire.idle_en: Click a numbered circle on the map, or a name below it.
empire.idle_zh: 點地圖上有號碼的圓，或是地圖下面的名字。
empire.foot_en: Only seven regions are shown, each with a date from a standard reference. Rome also ruled many other lands, such as Spain, Asia Minor, and Syria, and the borders moved over time.
empire.foot_zh: 地圖上只畫七個地區，每一個都附上參考書裡的年代。羅馬也統治過很多其他的地方，例如西班牙、小亞細亞和敘利亞；邊界也一直在變。

centers.crops_en: After wars against the Samnites and against King Pyrrhus, Rome became the master of Italy.
centers.crops_zh: 打敗薩莫奈人和皮洛士王以後，羅馬成了義大利的主人。
centers.when_en: By about 275 BCE, after the Pyrrhic War (280–275 BCE).
centers.when_zh: 大約西元前 275 年，皮洛士戰爭（西元前 280–275 年）之後。
centers.note_en: Rome itself began as a small city; its founding date of 753 BCE is a later tradition.
centers.note_zh: 羅馬本身一開始只是一座小城；西元前 753 年建城是後來的傳統說法。
centers.src: Britannica, “Roman Republic”

centers.crops_en: After three Punic Wars, the Romans destroyed the city of Carthage and enslaved its people.
centers.crops_zh: 經過三次布匿戰爭，羅馬人摧毀了迦太基城，並把城裡的人變成奴隸。
centers.when_en: 146 BCE, at the end of the Punic Wars (264–146 BCE).
centers.when_zh: 西元前 146 年，布匿戰爭（西元前 264–146 年）結束時。
centers.note_en: The story that the Romans then salted the earth there appears in no ancient source.
centers.note_zh: 「羅馬人在那裡的土地上撒鹽」的故事，古代的史料裡都找不到。
centers.src: Britannica, “Punic Wars”; Ridley, Classical Philology 81 (1986)

centers.crops_en: After a series of wars, Macedonia was made a Roman province, Rome's first in the Greek-speaking east.
centers.crops_zh: 經過一連串的戰爭，馬其頓成了羅馬的行省，是羅馬在說希臘語的東方的第一個行省。
centers.when_en: 146 BCE, the same year Carthage was destroyed.
centers.when_zh: 西元前 146 年，和迦太基被摧毀同一年。
centers.note_en: Greek learning and art, from Lesson 5, now flowed into Roman life.
centers.note_zh: 第五課談到的希臘學問和藝術，從此流進了羅馬人的生活。
centers.src: Britannica, “Macedonian Wars”

centers.crops_en: Julius Caesar conquered Gaul in the Gallic Wars and defeated the Gallic leader Vercingetorix in 52 BCE.
centers.crops_zh: 凱撒在高盧戰爭中征服了高盧，在西元前 52 年打敗了高盧的領袖維欽托利。
centers.when_en: 58 to 50 BCE.
centers.when_zh: 西元前 58 到 50 年。
centers.note_en: Ancient writers such as Plutarch claimed that a million Gauls were killed and another million taken prisoner; historians treat these figures with doubt.
centers.note_zh: 普魯塔克等古代作者說，有一百萬高盧人被殺、另有一百萬人被俘；歷史學家對這些數字存疑。
centers.src: Britannica, “Gallic Wars”; Plutarch, Life of Caesar 15

centers.crops_en: Rome conquered Egypt, the land of the pyramids from Lesson 4.
centers.crops_zh: 羅馬征服了埃及，也就是第四課金字塔的故鄉。
centers.when_en: 30 BCE.
centers.when_zh: 西元前 30 年。
centers.note_en: By then the Great Pyramid of Lesson 4 was already about 2,500 years old.
centers.note_zh: 那時候，第四課的大金字塔已經大約兩千五百歲了。
centers.src: Britannica, “ancient Egypt”

centers.crops_en: The emperor Claudius began the conquest of Britain. Roman rule there lasted until about 410 CE.
centers.crops_zh: 克勞狄烏斯皇帝開始征服不列顛。羅馬在那裡的統治一直到大約西元 410 年。
centers.when_en: From 43 CE.
centers.when_zh: 西元 43 年起。
centers.note_en: In 60 or 61 CE, Queen Boudica led a great revolt against Roman rule.
centers.note_zh: 西元 60 或 61 年，布狄卡女王領導了一場反抗羅馬統治的大起事。
centers.src: Britannica, “Roman Britain” and “Boudicca”

centers.crops_en: The emperor Trajan conquered Dacia after two wars. Many of its people were killed or driven north.
centers.crops_zh: 圖拉真皇帝打了兩次仗，征服了達契亞。那裡很多人被殺，或被趕到北方。
centers.when_zh: 西元 106 年。
centers.note_en: Under Trajan (98–117 CE), the empire reached about its greatest size.
centers.note_zh: 在圖拉真（西元 98–117 年在位）的時候，帝國差不多到了最大的範圍。
centers.src: Britannica, “Dacia”, “Trajan”, and “Roman Empire”

borrowed.en: Older Than Rome, or a Roman Idea?
borrowed.zh: 比羅馬還早，還是羅馬人的點子？
borrowed.lead_en: The Romans were great builders and organizers, but they also borrowed a lot. For each one, decide whether it existed before Rome, or whether it was something the Romans developed. There is no timer.
borrowed.lead_zh: 羅馬人很會蓋、很會組織，但他們也借了很多。每一題判斷：這是羅馬以前就有的，還是羅馬人發展出來的？不計時。
borrowed.ask_en: Older than Rome, or a Roman development?
borrowed.ask_zh: 比羅馬還早，還是羅馬人發展的？

buckets.en: Older than Rome; the Romans used it widely
buckets.zh: 比羅馬還早；羅馬人大量使用

items.why_en: Arches were known in ancient Egypt and Greece, but seldom used for great buildings. The Romans used them everywhere: in bridges, aqueducts, and large buildings.
items.why_zh: 古埃及和希臘就知道拱，但很少用在大型建築上。羅馬人把它用在各種地方：橋、水道和大型建築。
items.hint_en: Look at the lesson's first map: who built before Rome?
items.hint_zh: 想想比羅馬更早的建築者。

items.en: The barrel vault, a long tunnel-shaped roof
items.zh: 筒形拱頂，像隧道一樣長長的屋頂
items.why_en: The barrel vault appeared first in ancient Egypt and the Middle East.
items.why_zh: 筒形拱頂最早出現在古埃及和中東。
items.hint_en: It is a long arch.
items.hint_zh: 它就是拉長的拱。

items.en: The groin vault, made where two barrel vaults cross
items.zh: 交叉拱頂：兩個筒形拱頂十字交叉
items.why_en: Roman architects discovered that two barrel vaults crossing at right angles make a groin vault, which can cover a wide square space.
items.why_zh: 羅馬的建築師發現，兩個筒形拱頂直角交叉，就成了交叉拱頂，可以蓋住一大片方形的空間。
items.hint_en: Two old ideas, combined in a new way.
items.hint_zh: 兩個舊點子，用新的方式合在一起。

items.en: Channels that carry water over long distances
items.zh: 把水送到很遠地方的水道
items.why_en: The Assyrians built a stone aqueduct around 691 BCE, and underground channels called qanats were used in Persia and elsewhere hundreds of years before Rome's.
items.why_zh: 亞述人大約在西元前 691 年就蓋了石造的水道；波斯等地也比羅馬早好幾百年使用叫做「坎兒井」的地下水道。
items.hint_en: Rome's first aqueduct dates from 312 BCE. Were there older ones?
items.hint_zh: 羅馬第一條水道是西元前 312 年。有沒有更早的？

items.en: Concrete made by hot-mixing quicklime with volcanic ash
items.zh: 用生石灰和火山灰「熱拌」做成的混凝土
items.why_en: A 2023 study found that Roman builders hot-mixed quicklime with volcanic ash (the best-known source was near Pozzuoli). The researchers propose that small lumps of lime left inside helped the concrete heal its own cracks.
items.why_zh: 2023 年的一項研究發現，羅馬的工匠把生石灰和火山灰（最有名的產地在波佐利附近）一起「熱拌」；研究者認為，留在裡面的小石灰塊可能幫混凝土自己修補裂縫。
items.hint_en: Lime mortar is old, but this recipe is special.
items.hint_zh: 石灰砂漿很早就有，但這個配方很特別。

items.en: The alphabet the Romans wrote with
items.why_en: As Lesson 3 showed, the alphabet passed from the Phoenicians to the Greeks, and then, through the Etruscans, to the Romans.
items.why_zh: 第三課說過，字母從腓尼基人傳到希臘人，再經過伊特拉斯坎人傳到羅馬人。
items.hint_en: Think back to Lesson 3.
items.hint_zh: 回想第三課。

items.en: Citizenship for all the free people of an empire, in 212 CE
items.zh: 西元 212 年，讓整個帝國的自由人都成為公民
items.why_en: The emperor Caracalla gave Roman citizenship to all free inhabitants of the empire. The historian Cassius Dio says his real purpose was to raise more taxes; modern historians debate his motives.
items.why_zh: 卡拉卡拉皇帝把羅馬公民權給了帝國所有的自由居民。史家卡西烏斯・狄奧說，他真正的目的是收更多的稅；現代歷史學家對他的動機有不同看法。
items.hint_en: Compare Athens in Lesson 5.
items.hint_zh: 和第五課的雅典比一比。

items.en: Gathering Rome's laws into one great collection
items.zh: 把羅馬的法律整理成一套大全
items.why_en: Under the emperor Justinian, in the 500s CE, existing Roman law was collected and organized. Taiwan's civil law belongs to the continental European tradition whose roots go back to Roman law.
items.why_zh: 在西元 500 年代查士丁尼皇帝的時候，既有的羅馬法被蒐集、整理起來。台灣的民法屬於歐陸法傳統，這個傳統的根源可以追溯到羅馬法。
items.hint_en: These were Rome's own laws.
items.hint_zh: 這些是羅馬自己的法律。

borrowed.end_en: The Romans were not the first to build arches, aqueducts, or alphabets. Their gift was to use old ideas on a huge scale, combine them in new ways, and keep them working across an empire.
borrowed.end_zh: 拱、水道、字母，都不是羅馬人最先發明的。他們厲害的地方，是把舊點子用到很大的規模、用新的方式組合起來，並讓它們在整個帝國裡持續運作。

timeline.zh: 同一個時代的兩個大帝國
timeline.lead_en: Rome is in the Europe lane and the Han dynasty in the East Asia lane. Notice how long they overlap, and the two moments when they almost met.
timeline.lead_zh: 羅馬在歐洲那一條線，漢朝在東亞那一條線。注意它們重疊了多久，以及兩次差一點碰面的時刻。
timeline.idle_en: Click a bar or a diamond to read its dates.
timeline.idle_zh: 點一條長條或一個菱形，讀出它的年代。

tips.en: The Roman Empire and the Han dynasty overlapped for more than two centuries, but the surviving records show only a few, indirect contacts.
tips.zh: 羅馬帝國和漢朝重疊了兩百多年，但留下來的記錄只顯示少數幾次間接的接觸。

tips.en: A striped bar marks traditional dates that are not well recorded, such as Rome's early republic.
tips.zh: 有條紋的長條，是記錄不多的傳統年代，例如羅馬早期的共和國。

tips.en: The gray diamonds mark single events: the empire begins, citizenship for almost all, and the end of the western empire.
tips.zh: 灰色的菱形標的是單一事件：帝國開始、幾乎所有人成為公民，以及西羅馬的結束。

events.note_en: Traditionally 509 to 27 BCE; the early centuries are poorly documented.
events.note_zh: 傳統上是西元前 509 到 27 年；最早的幾百年記錄很少。

events.note_en: In 27 BCE, under Augustus.
events.note_zh: 西元前 27 年，奧古斯都的時候。

events.note_en: The end of the Punic Wars; its people were enslaved.
events.note_zh: 布匿戰爭結束；城裡的人被變成奴隸。

events.note_en: 206 BCE to 220 CE; Lesson 7 looks at it closely.
events.note_zh: 西元前 206 年到西元 220 年；第七課會仔細談。

events.en: Gan Ying reaches a western sea
events.note_en: A Han envoy sent toward Da Qin (Rome) reached Tiaozhi, next to a great sea, and turned back.
events.note_zh: 漢朝派往大秦（羅馬）的使者抵達條支，靠著一片大海，然後折返。

events.note_en: The Book of the Later Han records envoys from “Andun,” king of Da Qin, arriving through Rinan, in today's Vietnam. Modern scholars doubt they were official Roman envoys.
events.note_zh: 《後漢書》記載大秦王「安敦」的使者經由日南（今越南中部）來到中國。現代學者懷疑他們不是羅馬官方派的使者。

events.en: Citizenship for almost all free people
events.zh: 幾乎所有的自由人都成為公民
events.note_en: The edict of the emperor Caracalla.
events.note_zh: 卡拉卡拉皇帝的敕令。

events.note_en: Odoacer deposed the last western emperor; the eastern half went on.
events.note_zh: 奧多亞克廢掉西部最後一位皇帝；東半部繼續存在。

how_we_know.eyebrow: How Do We Know? · 我們怎麼知道？
how_we_know.en: Standing stones, a water commissioner, and a digital map
how_we_know.zh: 還站著的石頭、一位水務官，和一張數位地圖
how_we_know.lead_en: Rome left more physical remains than most ancient empires, but even these have gaps.
how_we_know.lead_zh: 羅馬留下的實物比大多數古代帝國都多，但這些證據也有缺口。

items.limit_en: Even standing buildings leave questions: UNESCO's own description dates the bridge both to shortly before the Common Era and to the middle of the first century CE.
items.limit_zh: 就算是還站著的建築也有疑問：聯合國教科文組織自己的說明裡，對這座橋的年代就有「西元前不久」和「西元一世紀中葉」兩種寫法。
items.src: UNESCO World Heritage List, Pont du Gard (Roman Aqueduct)
items.text_en: The Pont du Gard, part of an aqueduct of about 50 kilometers, still stands almost 50 meters high on three levels. Its lower arches were built of stones carved with positioning marks.
items.text_zh: 加爾橋是一條大約 50 公里長的水道的一部分，到今天還站著，有三層、將近 50 公尺高。它下層的拱，是用刻了定位記號的石頭砌成的。

items.limit_en: Frontinus wrote as a proud official. His praise of Roman works over the “idle Pyramids” tells us what he valued, not what everyone thought.
items.limit_zh: 弗朗提努斯是以一位驕傲的官員的身分寫的。他稱讚羅馬的工程勝過「閒置的金字塔」，說明的是他看重什麼，不是每個人的想法。
items.src: Frontinus, De aquis 1, tr. Bennett (Loeb, 1925)
items.text_en: Around 97 CE, Frontinus was put in charge of Rome's water supply and wrote a book about the aqueducts, listing them, their builders, and how much water they carried.
items.text_zh: 大約西元 97 年，弗朗提努斯負責管理羅馬的供水，寫了一本關於水道的書，列出各條水道、建造的人，以及它們送多少水。

items.limit_en: The researchers say the location of only about 2.7 percent of that length is known with certainty; most of the rest is conjectured, and some is a hypothesis.
items.limit_zh: 研究者說，這些長度裡只有大約百分之 2.7 的位置是確定的；其餘大多是推測，也有一些只是假設。
items.src: de Soto et al., Scientific Data 12 (2025)
items.text_en: In 2025 researchers published Itiner-e, a digital map of about 299,000 kilometers of Roman roads around 150 CE, combining excavations, milestones, ancient road lists and maps, and modern maps and satellite images.
items.text_zh: 2025 年，研究者發表了 Itiner-e，一張大約 29.9 萬公里的羅馬道路數位地圖（約西元 150 年），結合了考古發掘、里程碑、古代的路線表與地圖，以及現代的地圖和衛星影像。

views.en: Four questions with more than one answer
views.zh: 不只一個答案的四個問題
views.lead_en: Even numbers about Rome are argued over. Here are four questions, with the views set side by side.
views.lead_zh: 就連關於羅馬的數字也有爭論。下面是四個問題，各種說法並列。
views.rule_en: Notice that new tools, such as digital maps and better physics, can change the numbers, not only new discoveries in the ground.
views.rule_zh: 留意能改變數字的，不只是地底下的新發現，也包括新的工具，例如數位地圖和更精確的力學。

items.topic_en: How long were the Roman roads?
items.topic_zh: 羅馬的道路有多長？

sides.en: An earlier digital atlas of Roman and medieval roads mapped about 188,555 kilometers.
sides.zh: 較早的一份羅馬與中世紀道路數位地圖集，畫出大約 188,555 公里。
sides.src: As reported in de Soto et al. (2025)

sides.en: The Itiner-e project (2025) mapped about 299,171 kilometers, nearly double, by including every road with evidence, conjecture, or a hypothesis for its route.
sides.zh: Itiner-e 計畫（2025）畫出大約 299,171 公里，幾乎是兩倍；因為它把每一條有證據、有推測或有假設路線的道路都算進去。
sides.src: de Soto et al., Scientific Data 12 (2025)

items.note_en: The two numbers count different things. Asking “what was counted?” matters as much as the number.
items.note_zh: 兩個數字算的東西不一樣。問「算了什麼？」和數字本身一樣重要。

items.topic_en: How thin can a stone arch be?
items.topic_zh: 石拱最薄能多薄？

sides.en: The engineer Jacques Heyman, in the 1960s, gave a simple method that puts the minimum at about 0.106 of the radius for a half-circle arch.
sides.zh: 工程師海曼在 1960 年代提出一個簡單的方法，算出半圓拱最薄大約是半徑的 0.106 倍。
sides.src: Heyman, International Journal of Mechanical Sciences 11 (1969)

sides.en: A more exact solution, published by Milutin Milankovitch in 1907, gives about 0.1075. A 2021 study says Heyman's method finds the main features more simply, but puts one of the hinges in the wrong place.
sides.zh: 米蘭科維奇在 1907 年發表了更精確的解，大約是 0.1075。2021 年的一項研究說，海曼的方法比較簡單、也抓得到主要的特徵，但有一個鉸點的位置算錯了。
sides.src: Nikolić, Acta Mechanica (2017); Cocchetti and Rizzi, Archive of Applied Mechanics (2021)

items.note_en: Both are simplified models, and both measure the radius to the middle of the stones. Real arches also depend on the load above them and on their abutments. The 3D model uses 0.1075.
items.note_zh: 兩個都是簡化的模型，半徑都量到石頭的中線。真實的拱還要看上面壓了什麼、拱座穩不穩。這一課的 3D 模型用 0.1075。

items.topic_en: How many people lived in the Roman Empire?
items.topic_zh: 羅馬帝國住了多少人？

sides.en: The historian Bruce Frier estimated about 46 million people under Augustus.
sides.zh: 歷史學家弗里爾估計，奧古斯都的時候大約有四千六百萬人。
sides.src: As summarized by the University of St Andrews, “Uncertain Past” (2018)

sides.label_zh: 五千九百萬到七千二百萬
sides.en: Walter Scheidel estimated 59 to 72 million in 164 CE, just before a great epidemic.
sides.zh: 沙伊德爾估計，西元 164 年、一場大瘟疫之前，大約有五千九百萬到七千二百萬人。
sides.src: As summarized by the University of St Andrews, “Uncertain Past” (2018)

items.note_en: The estimates are for different dates and use different methods. No full census of the empire survives.
items.note_zh: 這些估計的年代不同、方法也不同。整個帝國的完整人口普查，沒有留下來。

items.topic_en: Is “Romanization” a good way to describe what happened?
items.topic_zh: 「羅馬化」這個說法恰當嗎？

sides.en: An older picture said conquered peoples gradually took up Roman language, dress, cities, and ways of life, a process called Romanization.
sides.zh: 比較早的說法認為，被征服的民族慢慢採用了羅馬的語言、服裝、城市和生活方式，這個過程叫做「羅馬化」。
sides.src: Described in Mattingly, Imperialism, Power, and Identity (Princeton, 2011)

sides.label_en: A word that hides too much
sides.en: The archaeologist David Mattingly rejects “outdated notions about Romanization” and looks at Roman rule from the point of view of the ruled, whose lives it could improve, challenge, or destroy.
sides.zh: 考古學家馬丁利拒絕「關於羅馬化的過時觀念」，改從被統治者的角度看羅馬的統治：它可能讓人的生活變好、受到挑戰，或被毀掉。

items.note_en: The debate is about whose experience counts: the people who prospered under Rome, or also those who lost land, freedom, or lives.
items.note_zh: 這場爭論問的是：誰的經驗算數？是在羅馬統治下過得好的人，還是也包括失去土地、自由或生命的人？

phrases.en: Eight sentences about building and connecting
phrases.zh: 談建造與連接的八句英文
phrases.lead_en: These sentences help you describe what something was built to do and how places were linked. Listen, repeat, then make your own sentence with the words in bold.
phrases.lead_zh: 這八句幫你說明一樣東西是為了什麼而蓋的，以及地方和地方怎麼連起來。先聽、再跟著唸，然後用粗體的字自己造一句。

rows.en: The aqueduct was built to carry water to the city.
rows.html: The aqueduct was built to carry water to the city.
rows.zh: 這條水道是為了把水送進城裡而蓋的。
rows.note_en: was built to: had the purpose of

rows.en: The empire stretched from Britain to Egypt.
rows.html: The empire stretched from Britain to Egypt.
rows.zh: 這個帝國從不列顛延伸到埃及。
rows.note_en: stretched from … to …: covered the distance between

rows.en: Roads connected the provinces with Rome.
rows.html: Roads connected the provinces with Rome.
rows.zh: 道路把各行省和羅馬連在一起。
rows.note_en: connected … with …: joined

rows.en: The wooden frame held the stones until the keystone was in place.
rows.html: The wooden frame held the stones until the keystone was in place.
rows.zh: 木頭拱架托著石頭，直到拱心石放好為止。
rows.note_en: until: up to the time when

rows.en: The aqueduct sloped gently so that water could flow by itself.
rows.html: The aqueduct sloped gently so that water could flow by itself.
rows.zh: 水道緩緩地往下斜，好讓水自己流。
rows.note_en: so that: in order that

rows.en: The Romans did not invent the arch, but they used it everywhere.
rows.html: The Romans did not invent the arch, but they used it everywhere.
rows.zh: 拱不是羅馬人發明的，但他們到處都用。
rows.note_en: did not … but …: contrast

rows.en: In exchange for citizenship, people also paid new taxes.
rows.html: In exchange for citizenship, people also paid new taxes.
rows.zh: 得到公民身分的同時，人們也要繳新的稅。
rows.note_en: in exchange for: receiving one thing for another

rows.en: The empire was held together by roads, laws, and armies.
rows.html: The empire was held together by roads, laws, and armies.
rows.zh: 這個帝國是靠道路、法律和軍隊連在一起的。
rows.note_en: was held together by: kept united through

taiwan_then.eyebrow: Taiwan at That Time · 那時候的台灣
taiwan_then.en: Glass, gold, and trade across the sea
taiwan_then.zh: 玻璃、黃金與海上的交易
taiwan_then.lead_en: Around the time of the Roman Empire, about 2,000 years ago, people in Taiwan were also part of trade networks across the sea, though on a very different scale.
taiwan_then.lead_zh: 大約在羅馬帝國的時代，距今大約兩千年，台灣的人也身在海上的交易網絡裡，只是規模和形式非常不一樣。
taiwan_then.intro_en: Archaeologists in Taiwan give dates as “years ago” (before 1950). About 2,000 years ago is roughly the first century BCE or CE.
taiwan_then.intro_zh: 台灣的考古學家用「距今幾年」（以 1950 年為準）說年代。距今大約兩千年，差不多是西元前一世紀到西元一世紀。

facts.en: The National Museum of Prehistory says the Shisanhang culture rose near the Taipei Basin about 2,000 years ago. Its gold ornaments and glass bracelets, from different periods, point to trade with lands overseas.
facts.zh: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館說，「大約二千年前，十三行文化在臺北盆地附近興起」；那裡不同時期的金飾和玻璃手環，顯示他們和海外有交易。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

facts.en: At Jiuxianglan in Taitung, an Iron Age site dated from about the third century BCE to the eighth century CE, archaeologists found glass beads and waste from bead-making. A 2018 study found that the beads did not match the waste, so the beads may have been made elsewhere and brought in.
facts.zh: 台東的舊香蘭是一處鐵器時代的遺址，年代大約從西元前三世紀到西元八世紀。考古學家在那裡找到玻璃珠和做珠子留下的廢料。2018 年的一項研究發現，珠子和廢料的成分對不上，所以這些珠子可能是在別的地方做好、再帶進來的。
facts.src: Wang et al., Archaeological and Anthropological Sciences (2018)

facts.k_zh: 製鐵技術什麼時候來的？
facts.en: The same museum says the technique of making iron tools reached Taiwan about 1,500 years ago, while it also describes iron in the Shisanhang culture. Dates for Taiwan's metal age differ between sources.
facts.zh: 同一座博物館說，「約一千五百年前，製作鐵器的技術傳入臺灣」；它也說十三行文化有鐵器。台灣金屬器時代的年代，各資料說法不一。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

facts.en: There was no empire in Taiwan, but the Shisanhang people traded across the sea: the museum points to gold ornaments and glass bracelets from overseas. Rome was held together by roads; Taiwan's ancient connections ran over water.
facts.zh: 台灣沒有帝國，但十三行的人透過海洋和外地交易；博物館指出，那裡出土了金飾和玻璃手環。羅馬靠道路連在一起；台灣古代的連結，走的是水路。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

links.en: Taiwan's Story, Lesson 2: Who Lived in Taiwan Thousands of Years Ago?
links.zh: 台灣歷史第二課：幾千年前，誰住在台灣？

links.en: Taiwan's Story, Lesson 3: Who Are Taiwan's Indigenous Peoples?
links.zh: 台灣歷史第三課：台灣的原住民族是誰？

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Evidence · 證據背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: Idle pyramids, a queen's revolt, a Chinese name for Rome, and a saying
culture_cards.title_zh: 閒置的金字塔、一位女王的起事、中國對羅馬的稱呼，和一句俗語
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how the Romans saw themselves, and how others saw them.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事：羅馬人怎麼看自己，別人又怎麼看羅馬。

cards.body_en: Frontinus, in charge of Rome's water, wrote that the city's many aqueducts were far more useful than “the idle Pyramids” or the famous works of the Greeks. It is a proud official's opinion, and a reminder that Lesson 4's pyramids were already ancient to him.
cards.body_zh: 負責羅馬供水的弗朗提努斯寫道，羅馬那麼多的水道，比「閒置的金字塔」或希臘人有名的作品有用得多。這是一位驕傲的官員的看法；也提醒我們，第四課的金字塔對他來說已經很古老了。

cards.body_en: When her husband, a local king, died, he left part of his wealth to the emperor, hoping to protect his family. Instead Roman officials seized the kingdom. Queen Boudica led a revolt that burned the Roman towns of Camulodunum (Colchester), Verulamium (St Albans), and Londinium (London) before it was defeated. The Roman historian Tacitus gives huge casualty figures; the editor of a standard translation calls them “equally incredible.”
cards.body_zh: 她的丈夫是當地的國王，死前把一部分財產留給皇帝，希望能保護家人。結果羅馬官員卻奪走了他的王國。布狄卡女王領導起事，燒了卡姆洛杜努姆（今科爾切斯特）、維魯拉米恩（今聖奧爾本斯）和倫蒂尼恩（今倫敦）這幾座羅馬城鎮，最後被打敗。羅馬史家塔西佗寫下的死傷數字非常大，一部標準譯本的編者認為雙方的數字「同樣不可信」。

cards.k: 97 and 166 CE · Han China · 漢朝
cards.en: Da Qin, the land west of the sea
cards.body_en: The Book of the Later Han calls Rome Da Qin, also Lijian, a country “west of the sea.” It records that Gan Ying reached Tiaozhi but did not cross the sea, and that in 166 CE envoys from Da Qin's king Andun arrived through Rinan, on the southern frontier, with ivory, rhinoceros horn, and tortoiseshell. The same text adds that the gifts were nothing rare, and doubts the reports.
cards.body_zh: 《後漢書・西域傳》說：「大秦國，一名犂鞬，以在海西，亦云海西國。」書裡記載甘英「抵條支」，沒有渡海；又說延熹九年（西元 166 年），「大秦王安敦遣使自日南徼外獻象牙、犀角、瑇瑁，始乃一通焉。」書裡也說，他們的貢品「並無珍異，疑傳者過焉」。

cards.body_en: The saying is not Roman. It probably goes back to a Latin line in a medieval book of proverbs by Alain de Lille: “a thousand roads lead people to Rome.” The next line speaks of seeking the Lord. English and French versions followed centuries later.
cards.body_zh: 這句俗語不是羅馬人說的。它大概來自中世紀里爾的阿蘭（Alain de Lille）一本諺語集裡的一句拉丁文：「千條道路把人帶到羅馬」，下一句說的是尋求上主。英文和法文的說法，是好幾百年以後才出現的。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum for social studies (October 2018).
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要社會領域（民國 107 年 10 月）。

items.area: 國中・古代文化的遺產
items.area_en: Junior high · the heritage of ancient cultures
items.text: 希臘、羅馬的政治及文化。
items.note_en: The curriculum asks for the political changes and cultural features of Greece and Rome, without going into detail. Lesson 5 covered Athens; this lesson covers Rome.
items.note_zh: 課綱要學生認識希臘、羅馬的政治演變與文化特色，不必詳敘細節。第五課談雅典，這一課談羅馬。

items.area: 國中・歷史考察（五）
items.area_en: Junior high · historical inquiry (5)
items.text: 從主題 N 或 O 挑選適當課題深入探究，或規劃與執行歷史踏查或展演。
items.note_en: One suggested topic is the relationship between Athenian democracy, the Roman Republic, and modern democracy. Lessons 5 and 6 together give a starting point.
items.note_zh: 課綱建議的探究課題之一是「雅典民主、羅馬共和與現代民主的關係」。第五、六課合起來可以當作起點。

myths.myth_en: The Romans invented the arch.
myths.myth_zh: 拱是羅馬人發明的。
myths.fact_en: Arches were known in ancient Egypt and Greece. The Romans used them on a far larger scale and combined them in new ways, such as the groin vault.
myths.fact_zh: 古埃及和希臘就知道拱。羅馬人把它用到大得多的規模，並用新的方式組合，例如交叉拱頂。

myths.myth_en: “All roads lead to Rome” is an ancient Roman saying.
myths.myth_zh: 「條條大路通羅馬」是古羅馬的俗語。
myths.fact_en: It probably comes from a medieval Latin proverb of about 1175 CE, long after the western empire ended.
myths.fact_zh: 它大概來自大約西元 1175 年中世紀的一句拉丁諺語，那時西羅馬帝國早就結束了。

myths.myth_en: Everyone in the empire was a Roman citizen from the start.
myths.myth_zh: 帝國裡的每個人一開始就是羅馬公民。
myths.fact_en: Citizenship spread slowly. Only in 212 CE did it reach almost all free people, and enslaved people were still left out.
myths.fact_zh: 公民權是慢慢擴大的。要到西元 212 年才給了幾乎所有的自由人，被奴役的人仍然不在其中。

myths.myth_en: Roman concrete was just ordinary mortar.
myths.myth_zh: 羅馬混凝土只是普通的砂漿。
myths.fact_en: A 2023 study found Roman builders hot-mixed quicklime with volcanic ash, and the lime lumps left inside may help it heal small cracks, one reason some Roman structures have lasted so long.
myths.fact_zh: 2023 年的一項研究發現，羅馬的工匠把生石灰和火山灰熱拌；留在裡面的石灰塊可能幫它修補細小的裂縫，這是有些羅馬建築能撐這麼久的原因之一。

tricks.body_en: Four things besides armies that held the empire together.
tricks.body_zh: 除了軍隊之外，把帝國連在一起的四樣東西。

tricks.body_en: An arch needs a frame until it is closed; then it holds itself.
tricks.body_zh: 拱合起來之前要靠拱架；合起來以後就自己撐住。

tricks.body_en: Arches, aqueducts, alphabet: older than Rome, used by Rome on a huge scale.
tricks.body_zh: 拱、水道、字母：比羅馬還早，被羅馬用到很大的規模。

tricks.body_en: Every map of Rome's growth is also a map of wars.
tricks.body_zh: 每一張羅馬擴張的地圖，也是一張戰爭的地圖。

materials.en: Sugar cubes or small wooden blocks, a butter knife to shape them, and two stacks of books as abutments
materials.zh: 方糖或小木塊、一把奶油刀用來修形狀，以及兩疊書當拱座

materials.en: A curved piece of cardboard as centering
materials.zh: 一片彎曲的硬紙板當拱架

steps.en: Shape the cubes into wedges, a little narrower at the bottom than at the top.
steps.zh: 把方糖修成楔形，下面比上面窄一點。

steps.en: Stand the cardboard between the two book stacks and lay the wedges over it from both sides. Put the keystone in last.
steps.zh: 把硬紙板立在兩疊書中間，從兩邊把楔形塊放上去，最後放拱心石。

steps.en: Slide the cardboard out. Does the arch stand? Now slide one book stack a little outward. What happens?
steps.zh: 把硬紙板抽出來。拱站得住嗎？接著把一疊書稍微往外推。會發生什麼事？

steps.en: Explain in English: “The arch stands because …” and “It fell when …”
steps.zh: 用英文說明：「The arch stands because …」和「It fell when …」

activities.tip_en: Step 3 shows why abutments matter: an arch pushes outward, and if its ends can move, it falls.
activities.tip_zh: 第三步讓學生看到拱座為什麼重要：拱會往外推，兩端一動，拱就塌了。

materials.en: A large sheet of paper divided into two columns: Rome and Han China
materials.zh: 一張大紙，分成兩欄：羅馬和漢朝

materials.en: This lesson, and Lesson 7 when it is ready
materials.zh: 這一課，以及之後的第七課

steps.en: List what held each empire together: roads, laws, writing, money, armies, officials.
steps.zh: 列出把兩個帝國各自連在一起的東西：道路、法律、文字、錢、軍隊、官員。

steps.en: Mark what was similar with a ✓ and what was different with a ✗.
steps.zh: 相似的打 ✓，不同的打 ✗。

steps.en: Add one row for the people who paid the price of each empire.
steps.zh: 加一列：寫下每個帝國裡付出代價的人。

steps.en: Share one sentence using “whereas”: “Rome used …, whereas the Han used …”
steps.zh: 用 whereas 分享一句：「Rome used …, whereas the Han used …」

activities.tip_en: Comparing without ranking is the goal: two different ways to hold a huge land together, each with its own costs.
activities.tip_zh: 目標是比較而不排名：兩種把一大片土地連在一起的方法，各有各的代價。

links.en: How Did Qin and Han Unite China?
links.zh: 秦和漢怎麼統一中國？
links.note_en: At the other end of Asia, another huge empire was held together by writing, measures, roads, and officials.
links.note_zh: 在亞洲的另一端，另一個大帝國靠文字、度量衡、道路和官員連在一起。

links.en: What Did the Greeks Start?
links.zh: 希臘人開了什麼頭？
links.note_en: Athens' citizens and assembly, before Rome's republic.
links.note_zh: 在羅馬共和之前，雅典的公民和公民大會。

links.en: Why Did the First Cities Grow Beside Rivers?
links.zh: 最早的城市為什麼都在河邊？
links.note_en: The pyramids that Frontinus called idle, and four ideas about how their blocks were raised.
links.note_zh: 弗朗提努斯說「閒置」的金字塔，以及石塊怎麼運上去的四種想法。

links.en: How Can One Document Run a Country?
links.zh: 一份文件怎麼管一個國家？
links.note_en: A modern republic whose founders read about Rome's.
links.note_zh: 一個現代的共和國，它的創建者讀過羅馬共和的歷史。

lessons.sources_note_en: Checked November 2026. Many numbers about Rome are estimates or ancient claims; where they differ, the lesson gives the range or says so
lessons.sources_note_zh: 2026 年 11 月查證。很多關於羅馬的數字是估計或古代的說法；遇到不一致時，課文寫出範圍或註明

sources.en: Voussoirs, the keystone, and wooden centering until the keystone is set; thrust and buttressing; arches known in Egypt and Greece; the Romans used the semicircular arch widely
sources.zh: 楔形石、拱心石，以及拱心石放好前的木頭拱架；推力與扶壁；埃及與希臘就知道拱；羅馬人大量使用半圓拱

sources.en: The barrel vault appeared first in Egypt and the Middle East; the Roman groin vault
sources.zh: 筒形拱頂最早出現在埃及與中東；羅馬的交叉拱頂

sources.en: The safety of masonry arches (minimum thickness, about 0.106 of the radius)
sources.zh: 石造拱的安全性（最小厚度約為半徑的 0.106 倍）
sources.src: Heyman, International Journal of Mechanical Sciences 11 (1969)

sources.en: The Stone Skeleton
sources.zh: 〈石頭的骨架〉
sources.src: Heyman, International Journal of Solids and Structures 2 (1966)

sources.en: Couplet's problem rigorously solved by Milankovitch (about 0.1075)
sources.zh: 米蘭科維奇嚴格解出庫普萊問題（約 0.1075）
sources.src: Nikolić, Acta Mechanica (2017); Makris, University of Cambridge talk

sources.en: Heyman's solution is simpler but misplaces the intrados hinge; the Milankovitch and CCR solutions are very close
sources.zh: 海曼的解比較簡單，但內弧鉸點的位置不對；米蘭科維奇的解與 CCR 解非常接近
sources.src: Cocchetti and Rizzi, Archive of Applied Mechanics (2021)

sources.en: The Pont du Gard: the Nîmes aqueduct almost 50 km long, the bridge almost 50 m high on three levels; voussoirs with positioning marks
sources.zh: 加爾橋：尼姆水道長約 50 公里，橋有三層、將近 50 公尺高；刻了定位記號的楔形石
sources.src: UNESCO World Heritage List, Pont du Gard

sources.en: The Nîmes aqueduct: a drop of only 11.2 m over 50 km
sources.zh: 尼姆水道：50 公里只下降 11.2 公尺

sources.en: Eleven aqueducts built for Rome from 312 BCE to 226 CE; an Assyrian aqueduct of about 691 BCE; qanats earlier
sources.zh: 西元前 312 年到西元 226 年為羅馬建了十一條水道；約西元前 691 年的亞述水道；更早的坎兒井

sources.en: Frontinus as water commissioner; “the idle Pyramids”
sources.zh: 弗朗提努斯擔任水務官；「閒置的金字塔」
sources.src: Frontinus, De aquis 1.1 and 1.16, tr. Bennett (Loeb, 1925)

sources.en: About 299,171 km of Roman roads around 150 CE; only about 2.7% located with certainty; an earlier dataset of 188,555 km
sources.zh: 約西元 150 年的羅馬道路約 299,171 公里；只有約 2.7% 的位置確定；較早的資料是 188,555 公里
sources.src: de Soto et al., “Itiner-e,” Scientific Data 12 (2025)

sources.en: Founding in 753 BCE and the republic in 509 BCE as traditions; master of Italy after the Pyrrhic War
sources.zh: 西元前 753 年建城與西元前 509 年成為共和國是傳統說法；皮洛士戰爭後成為義大利的主人

sources.en: The empire from 27 BCE; the end in the west in 476
sources.zh: 西元前 27 年起的帝國；476 年西部結束

sources.en: The Punic Wars (264–146 BCE): Carthage destroyed and its people enslaved
sources.zh: 布匿戰爭（西元前 264–146 年）：迦太基被摧毀，人民被奴役

sources.en: Macedonia made a Roman province in 146 BCE
sources.zh: 西元前 146 年馬其頓成為羅馬行省

sources.en: The Gallic Wars (58–50 BCE)
sources.zh: 高盧戰爭（西元前 58–50 年）

sources.en: Plutarch's claim of a million Gauls killed and as many taken prisoner
sources.zh: 普魯塔克說一百萬高盧人被殺、同樣多的人被俘
sources.src: Plutarch, Life of Caesar 15, tr. Perrin (Loeb)

sources.en: No ancient source mentions the salting of Carthage
sources.zh: 沒有古代史料提到在迦太基撒鹽
sources.src: Ridley, “To Be Taken with a Pinch of Salt,” Classical Philology 81 (1986)

sources.en: The Roman conquest of Egypt, 30 BCE
sources.zh: 羅馬征服埃及，西元前 30 年

sources.en: Roman Britain from 43 CE to about 410 CE
sources.zh: 羅馬統治不列顛，從西元 43 年到約 410 年

sources.en: Dacia subdued in 106 CE
sources.zh: 西元 106 年達契亞被征服

sources.en: Trajan (r. 98–117) extended the empire
sources.zh: 圖拉真（西元 98–117 年在位）擴張帝國

sources.en: Caracalla's edict of 212 giving citizenship to all free inhabitants; ancient sources called it a device for taxes
sources.zh: 卡拉卡拉 212 年的敕令，給所有自由居民公民權；古代史料說它是收稅的手段

sources.en: Cassius Dio on Caracalla's purpose: to increase revenues
sources.zh: 卡西烏斯・狄奧說卡拉卡拉的目的是增加稅收
sources.src: Cassius Dio, Roman History 78.9, tr. Cary (Loeb)

sources.en: Boudica's revolt, 60 or 61 CE; Camulodunum, Verulamium, and Londinium burned
sources.zh: 布狄卡的起事，西元 60 或 61 年；卡姆洛杜努姆、維魯拉米恩、倫蒂尼恩被燒

sources.en: Jerusalem fell and the Temple was burned in 70 CE
sources.zh: 西元 70 年耶路撒冷陷落、聖殿被燒

sources.en: The civil law tradition from the Twelve Tables to Justinian's Corpus Iuris Civilis
sources.zh: 從十二銅表法到查士丁尼《民法大全》的大陸法傳統
sources.src: Library of Congress, “The Civil Law System” (2015)

sources.en: Taiwan's civil law dominated by continental European, especially German, law (the civil-law tradition with roots in Roman law)
sources.zh: 台灣民法以歐陸法、特別是德國法為主

sources.en: Hot-mixed Roman concrete with lime clasts
sources.zh: 含石灰塊的熱拌羅馬混凝土
sources.src: Seymour et al., Science Advances 9 (2023); MIT News (2023)

sources.en: Population estimates: Frier about 46 million; Scheidel 59–72 million in 164 CE
sources.zh: 人口估計：弗里爾約四千六百萬；沙伊德爾西元 164 年五千九百萬到七千二百萬

sources.en: Rejecting outdated notions about Romanization; Roman rule from the perspective of the ruled

lessons.title: How Did Qin and Han Unite China?
lessons.blurb_en: Watch the coins of the Warring States turn into one round coin with a square hole in 3D. Then follow Qin's ten-year conquest on a map, and sort out what the Qin did and what the Han did to hold China together.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 裡看戰國各國的錢，變成同一種圓形方孔的錢。再從地圖上看秦花十年攻下六國，分一分：把中國連在一起的辦法，哪些是秦朝的、哪些是漢朝的。
lessons.big_idea_en: In 221 BCE the kingdom of Qin conquered the other Warring States and tied them together with one script, one set of weights and measures, one coin, and new roads. The Qin fell within fifteen years, but the Han dynasty kept many of its standards and lasted about four centuries. Unification brought connection, and also heavy forced labor and harsh punishments.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 西元前 221 年，秦國攻下了其他戰國的國家，用同一套文字、度量衡、錢和新的道路把它們連在一起。秦朝十五年就亡了，但漢朝保留了很多標準，延續了大約四百年。統一帶來了連結，也帶來了沉重的勞役和嚴厲的刑罰。

lab.how_en: Before 221 BCE, the Warring States paid with coins of very different shapes: spades, knives, round coins, and the small “ant-nose” coins of Chu. Pick a state to read about its money. Then press Unify the coins: every coin turns into the round Qin coin with a square hole. Finally, switch to the Han dynasty's wuzhu coin, used for centuries afterward.
lab.how_zh: 西元前 221 年以前，戰國各國用的錢形狀差很多：鏟子形、刀形、圓形，還有楚國小小的「蟻鼻錢」。選一個國家，看看它的錢。接著按「統一錢幣」：每一枚錢都變成秦朝圓形方孔的錢。最後換成漢朝的五銖錢，之後用了好幾百年。

states.coin_en: Round coin with a square hole (banliang)
states.note_en: Qin already used this coin before 221 BCE. A Qin banliang in the British Museum is 31 millimeters across and weighs about 7 grams. After unification it became everyone's coin.
states.note_zh: 秦國在西元前 221 年以前就用這種錢。大英博物館的一枚秦半兩，直徑 31 公釐、重大約 7 公克。統一以後，它變成了大家的錢。

states.note_en: Spade-shaped bronze coins were used in Zhao, Wei, and other central states. A Zhao spade coin in the British Museum is 56 millimeters long. Zhao also issued knife money.
states.note_zh: 鏟子形的青銅錢在趙、魏等中原的國家使用。大英博物館的一枚趙國布幣長 56 公釐。趙國也發行刀幣。

states.note_en: Wei issued spade money, and also round coins whose inscriptions give a weight. The model shows a spade coin at a size similar to Zhao's.
states.note_zh: 魏國發行布幣，也發行錢上寫著重量的圓錢。模型畫的是布幣，大小照趙國的相近。

states.note_en: Chu used small bronze coins modeled on cowrie shells, about 2 centimeters long, as well as spade money and gold.
states.note_zh: 楚國用仿照貝殼做的小小青銅錢，長大約 2 公分；也用布幣和黃金。

states.note_en: The states in the north and northeast issued knife-shaped coins. The model draws Yan's knife at the size of a Warring States knife coin in the British Museum, 157 millimeters long.
states.note_zh: 北方和東北方的國家發行刀子形的錢。模型裡燕國的刀幣，照大英博物館一枚戰國刀幣的大小畫，長 157 公釐。

states.note_en: Qi's knife coins were large and heavy. One in the British Museum is 183 millimeters long and weighs 45 grams, more than six Qin coins.
states.note_zh: 齊國的刀幣又大又重。大英博物館的一枚長 183 公釐、重 45 公克，比六枚秦半兩還重。

banliang.note_en: In 221 BCE the Qin made their banliang the standard coin of the empire and declared all other coins obsolete. The round coin with a square hole stayed the standard shape of East Asian coins for about 2,000 years.
banliang.note_zh: 西元前 221 年，秦把半兩錢定為全國通用的錢，其他的錢都不能再用。圓形方孔的錢，此後大約兩千年都是東亞錢幣的標準形狀。

wuzhu.note_en: In 118 BCE the Han emperor Wu stopped the banliang and issued the wuzhu coin. The History of the Former Han says that by about 1 CE some 28 billion had been cast.
wuzhu.note_zh: 西元前 118 年，漢武帝「罷半兩錢，行五銖錢」。《漢書》說，到平帝元始年間（約西元 1 年）一共鑄了「二百八十億萬餘」枚。

modes.text_en: Each state had its own money. A trader moving from Qi to Zhao had to deal in coins of a different shape and weight.
modes.text_zh: 每個國家都有自己的錢。從齊國到趙國做生意的人，得改用形狀和重量都不一樣的錢。

modes.text_en: One coin for the whole empire: round, with a square hole, marked banliang, “half an ounce.”
modes.text_zh: 全國用同一種錢：圓形、方孔，上面寫著「半兩」。

modes.text_en: The Han kept the round coin with a square hole, and from 118 BCE cast the wuzhu, which stayed in use for centuries.
modes.text_zh: 漢朝保留了圓形方孔的錢；從西元前 118 年起鑄造五銖錢，之後用了好幾百年。

lab.numbers_note_en: Sizes follow coins in the British Museum: a Zhao spade (56 mm), a Warring States knife (157 mm), a Qi knife (183 mm), Chu ant-nose coins (about 20 mm), and a Qin banliang (31 mm). Wei and Yan are drawn at similar sizes, and the Han wuzhu at a typical size. Real coins varied a great deal.
lab.numbers_note_zh: 尺寸依大英博物館的館藏：趙國布幣（56 公釐）、一枚戰國刀幣（157 公釐）、齊國刀幣（183 公釐）、楚國蟻鼻錢（約 20 公釐）、秦半兩（31 公釐）。魏和燕照相近的大小畫，漢五銖照常見的大小畫。實物的大小差很多。

legend.en: Bronze coins of the Warring States
Qin round coin with a square hole

lab.scale_en: This is a teaching sketch. The coins are drawn at the sizes noted, but real coins varied a lot, and their inscriptions are not drawn. The table layout does not show where each state was; the map below does.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意。錢幣照標示的大小畫，但實物差很多，錢上的字也沒有畫。桌上的排列不代表各國的位置；各國在哪裡，請看下面的地圖。
lab.credit_html: Model: an illustration made for this lesson. Coin shapes and sizes follow British Museum records listed at the bottom of the page. 模型：為這一課製作的示意。錢幣的形狀和大小，依本頁最下面列出的大英博物館館藏資料。

paras: For more than two centuries before 221 BCE, China was divided among rival kingdoms, a time known as the Warring States. Each kingdom had its own coins, its own weights and measures, and its own laws. A trader from Qi in the east paid with heavy bronze knives; in Chu in the south, people used small coins shaped like shells. Between 230 and 221 BCE, the western kingdom of Qin conquered the other six, one after another.

The king of Qin took a new title, Huangdi, “emperor,” and is remembered as the First Emperor. His government ordered one standard for laws, weights and measures, the width of cart axles, and writing. An old Qin measuring cup in the Shanghai Museum, made in 344 BCE, also carries the edict of 221 BCE. The round Qin coin with a square hole became the only legal bronze coin, and that shape was used in East Asia for about 2,000 years.

The Qin also built roads, including the Straight Road toward the northern frontier, and joined sections of earlier walls into one line of defense. All this took the forced labor of huge numbers of people. Qin law was strict, and in 213 BCE the government ordered private copies of many books to be burned, sparing books on medicine, divination, and farming. The next year, the historian Sima Qian writes, more than 460 scholars were put to death.

The Qin dynasty did not last. Soon after the First Emperor died in 210 BCE, rebellions broke out, and by 207–206 BCE the Qin had fallen. The Han dynasty that followed lasted, with one interruption, until 220 CE. The Han kept many Qin standards and its centralized government, while turning toward Confucian ideas of moderate rule. Emperor Wu appointed scholars for the Confucian classics and asked each region to recommend honest men for office. In 118 BCE he introduced the wuzhu coin, used for centuries afterward.

The Han empire also reached out to the world. Around 138 BCE, the envoy Zhang Qian set out west and returned about thirteen years later with news of distant lands; Lesson 9 follows the roads he opened. A census recorded in the History of the Former Han counts almost 60 million people. In 105 CE, an official named Cai Lun presented a new way of making paper from bark, hemp, rags, and old fishing nets; archaeologists have also found older pieces of paper.

At the same time, at the other end of Eurasia, the Roman Empire also ruled tens of millions of people. Both empires built roads, made laws, and issued coins. Among their differences, Rome spread its citizenship, while the Han relied on a shared script and on officials chosen for their learning and good name. Each empire knew very little about the other. Comparing them shows two different ways of holding a huge land together, each with its own costs.
paras_zh: 西元前 221 年以前的兩百多年，中國分成好幾個互相競爭的國家，這個時代叫做「戰國」。每個國家都有自己的錢、自己的度量衡和自己的法律。東邊齊國的商人用沉重的青銅刀幣付錢；南方的楚國，人們用像貝殼一樣的小錢。從西元前 230 年到 221 年，西邊的秦國一個接一個地攻下了其他六國。
秦王採用了一個新的稱號「皇帝」，後來被稱為秦始皇。他的政府下令，法令、度量衡、車軸的寬度和文字都用同一個標準。上海博物館有一個秦國的舊量器，做於西元前 344 年，上面還刻有西元前 221 年的詔書。秦朝圓形方孔的錢成了唯一合法的銅錢，這個形狀在東亞用了大約兩千年。
秦朝也修築道路，包括通往北方邊境的直道，並把早先各國的城牆連成一條防線。這些都要靠非常多人的強迫勞役。秦朝的法律很嚴；西元前 213 年，政府下令燒掉民間收藏的許多書，醫藥、卜筮、種樹的書不燒。史家司馬遷寫道，第二年有四百六十多個讀書人被處死。
秦朝沒有撐多久。西元前 210 年秦始皇死後不久，各地起兵反抗；到了西元前 207 至 206 年，秦朝就亡了。接下來的漢朝，中間被打斷過一次，一直延續到西元 220 年。漢朝保留了很多秦朝的標準和中央集權的制度，同時轉向儒家溫和治理的理想。漢武帝設立五經博士，又讓各地推薦孝順廉潔的人做官。西元前 118 年，他推行五銖錢，之後用了好幾百年。
漢朝也向外面的世界伸出手。大約西元前 138 年，使者張騫往西出發，大約十三年後帶著遠方的消息回來；第九課會沿著他打通的路走。《漢書》記載的一次人口普查，算出將近六千萬人。西元 105 年，一位叫蔡倫的官員，提出用樹皮、麻、破布和舊魚網造紙的新方法；考古學家也找到過更早的紙片。
在同一個時代，歐亞大陸的另一端，羅馬帝國也統治著好幾千萬人。兩個帝國都修道路、訂法律、發行錢幣。不同的地方之一是：羅馬擴大公民權，而漢朝靠共同的文字，以及因學問和好名聲被選出來的官員。兩個帝國對彼此都所知很少。把它們放在一起比較，可以看到兩種把一大片土地連在一起的方法，各有各的代價。
questions: Name three things the Qin made the same across its empire.
Why might a single coin and single set of measures help hold an empire together?
The lesson says unification brought connection and also costs. Give one example of each.
answers: Laws, weights and measures, the width of cart axles, writing, and coins. Any three are correct.
People in different regions could trade, pay taxes, and check amounts in the same way, and the government could count and collect everywhere using one standard.
Connection: one script, coins, measures, and roads linked distant regions. Costs: forced labor on roads and walls, harsh punishments, and the burning of books.

vocab.ex: Qin united the Warring States in 221 BCE.
vocab.exzh: 秦在西元前 221 年統一了戰國各國。

vocab.ex: The Han dynasty lasted about four hundred years.
vocab.exzh: 漢朝延續了大約四百年。

vocab.ex: The king of Qin called himself emperor.
vocab.exzh: 秦王稱自己為皇帝。

vocab.ex: Everyone used the same standard for weights.
vocab.exzh: 大家用同一個重量的標準。

vocab.ex: Qin made weights and measures the same everywhere.
vocab.exzh: 秦讓各地的度量衡都一樣。

vocab.ex: The coin was round with a square hole.
vocab.exzh: 這種錢是圓形、中間方孔。

vocab.ex: The walls were built with forced labor.
vocab.exzh: 這些城牆是用強迫勞役蓋的。

vocab.ex: The Han chose officials for their learning.
vocab.exzh: 漢朝因為學問而選出官員。

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Each state on the table has its own coin. Count how many different shapes you can find.
parts.text_zh: 桌上每個國家都有自己的錢。數數看有幾種不同的形狀。

parts.en: A coin as long as a ruler
parts.text_en: The knife coins of the northeast were long and heavy. A Qi knife in the British Museum is 18 centimeters long.
parts.text_zh: 東北方的刀幣又長又重。大英博物館的一枚齊國刀幣長 18 公分。

parts.text_en: Press Qin unites them. Every coin turns into the round banliang, and the table becomes a neat grid.
parts.text_zh: 按「秦統一」。每一枚錢都變成圓形的半兩錢，桌上變成整齊的方陣。

parts.text_en: The Han changed the coin, but not its shape: the wuzhu was still round with a square hole.
parts.text_zh: 漢朝換了錢，但沒有換形狀：五銖錢還是圓形方孔。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then imagine you are a trader in 225 BCE. How many kinds of coin would you need to carry to buy salt in Qi, cloth in Chu, and horses in Zhao?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著想像你是西元前 225 年的商人。要在齊國買鹽、在楚國買布、在趙國買馬，你得帶幾種錢？

conquest.lead_en: Pull the slider from 232 BCE to 220 BCE. Each kingdom lights up when Qin conquered it, as recorded in the Records of the Grand Historian. The circles mark capitals; the map shows land only, with no modern borders.
conquest.lead_zh: 把滑桿從西元前 232 年拉到西元前 220 年。每個國家在被秦攻下的那一年亮起來，年代依《史記》的記載。圓圈標的是都城；地圖只畫陸地，不畫今天的國界。
conquest.idle_en: Click a numbered circle on the map, or a name below it.
conquest.idle_zh: 點地圖上有號碼的圓，或是地圖下面的名字。
conquest.foot_en: The dates follow the Records of the Grand Historian (the Basic Annals of Qin and the Table of the Six States). The locations of the capitals are approximate.
conquest.foot_zh: 年代依《史記》〈秦始皇本紀〉及〈六國年表〉。都城的位置是大約的。

centers.crops_en: The kingdom of Qin, in the west, whose king Zheng conquered the others and took the new title of emperor.
centers.crops_zh: 西邊的秦國；秦王政攻下其他國家，並採用了「皇帝」這個新稱號。
centers.when_en: Ruled by King Zheng from 246 BCE.
centers.when_zh: 秦王政從西元前 246 年起在位。
centers.note_en: Xianyang became the capital of the whole empire.
centers.note_zh: 咸陽成了整個帝國的都城。
centers.src: 《史記・秦始皇本紀》

centers.crops_en: The first kingdom to fall. Its king, An, was captured.
centers.crops_zh: 第一個被滅的國家，韓王安被俘。
centers.when_en: 230 BCE.
centers.when_zh: 西元前 230 年。
centers.note_en: This Han state is a different name from the later Han dynasty; in Chinese the two are written with different characters (韓 and 漢).
centers.note_zh: 這裡的韓國和後來的漢朝不一樣，中文是兩個不同的字（韓、漢）。
centers.src: 《史記・秦始皇本紀》

centers.crops_en: Qin armies took Handan and captured the king of Zhao.
centers.crops_zh: 秦軍攻下邯鄲，俘虜了趙王。
centers.when_en: 228 BCE.
centers.when_zh: 西元前 228 年。
centers.note_en: Zhao used both spade money and knife money.
centers.note_zh: 趙國同時用布幣和刀幣。
centers.src: 《史記・秦始皇本紀》

centers.crops_en: Qin flooded the capital Daliang by diverting a river, and the king of Wei surrendered.
centers.crops_zh: 秦軍引河水灌大梁城，魏王投降。
centers.when_en: 225 BCE.
centers.when_zh: 西元前 225 年。
centers.note_en: A river became a weapon, a reminder of Lesson 4's rivers.
centers.note_zh: 河流成了武器，讓人想起第四課的河。
centers.src: 《史記・秦始皇本紀》

centers.crops_en: The largest southern kingdom, which resisted for years. Its king was captured and its last general died.
centers.crops_zh: 南方最大的國家，抵抗了好幾年。楚王被俘，最後的將領也死了。
centers.when_en: 223 BCE, the year usually given for the fall of Chu. The Records place the king's capture in 224 BCE and the end of resistance in 223 BCE.
centers.when_zh: 西元前 223 年，一般以這一年為楚亡。《史記》把楚王被俘記在西元前 224 年，抵抗結束記在西元前 223 年。
centers.note_en: Chu used small ant-nose coins, spade money, and gold.
centers.note_zh: 楚國用小小的蟻鼻錢、布幣和黃金。
centers.src: 《史記・秦始皇本紀》與〈六國年表〉

centers.crops_en: Qin took the capital, Ji, in 226 BCE; the king fled northeast to Liaodong and was captured there four years later.
centers.crops_zh: 秦軍在西元前 226 年攻下燕都薊；燕王逃到東北的遼東，四年後在那裡被俘。
centers.when_en: 222 BCE.
centers.when_zh: 西元前 222 年。
centers.note_en: Yan was a knife-money state.
centers.note_zh: 燕國用刀幣。
centers.src: 《史記・秦始皇本紀》

centers.crops_en: The last kingdom. Qin took its king, Jian.
centers.crops_zh: 最後一個國家，秦「得齊王建」。
centers.when_en: 221 BCE: the unification is complete.
centers.when_zh: 西元前 221 年：統一完成。
centers.note_en: The same year, Qin standardized laws, weights and measures, and writing.
centers.note_zh: 同一年，秦統一了法令、度量衡和文字。
centers.src: 《史記・秦始皇本紀》

qinhan.lead_en: Both dynasties helped hold China together, in different ways. For each one, decide whether it was done by the Qin or by the Han. There is no timer.
qinhan.lead_zh: 兩個朝代都幫忙把中國連在一起，只是方法不一樣。每一題判斷：這是秦朝做的，還是漢朝做的？不計時。

buckets.zh: 漢朝（西元前 206 年–西元 220 年）

items.en: One standard for writing across the empire
items.zh: 全國的文字用同一個標準（書同文字）
items.why_en: The Records of the Grand Historian lists it among the changes of 221 BCE: one standard for laws, measures, axle widths, and writing.
items.why_zh: 《史記》把它列在西元前 221 年的改變裡：「一法度衡石丈尺。車同軌。書同文字。」
items.hint_en: It happened in the year of unification.
items.hint_zh: 統一那一年的事。

items.en: An edict added to an old measuring cup, ordering one standard for all measures
items.zh: 在一個舊量器上加刻詔書，下令度量衡統一
items.why_en: The Shang Yang measure in the Shanghai Museum, made in 344 BCE, carries a second inscription added in 221 BCE.
items.why_zh: 上海博物館的商鞅方升做於西元前 344 年，上面還有西元前 221 年加刻的詔書。
items.hint_en: Look at the date of the second inscription.
items.hint_zh: 看看第二段銘文的年代。

items.en: The Straight Road, cut through hills and valleys toward the northern frontier
items.zh: 直道：削平山、填平谷，一路通往北方邊境
items.why_en: The Records of the Grand Historian dates it to 212 BCE: “cutting through mountains and filling valleys, straight through.”
items.why_zh: 《史記》記在西元前 212 年：「道九原抵雲陽，塹山堙谷，直通之。」
items.hint_en: It was built in the First Emperor's reign.
items.hint_zh: 秦始皇在位時蓋的。

items.en: The wuzhu coin, used for centuries
items.zh: 用了好幾百年的五銖錢
items.why_en: Emperor Wu of Han stopped the banliang and issued the wuzhu in 118 BCE.
items.why_zh: 漢武帝在西元前 118 年「罷半兩錢，行五銖錢」。
items.hint_en: The Qin coin was the banliang.
items.hint_zh: 秦朝的錢是半兩。

items.en: Asking each region to recommend men known for being filial and honest
items.zh: 讓各郡國推薦孝順、廉潔的人（舉孝廉）
items.why_en: In 134 BCE the Han court ordered each commandery and kingdom to recommend one person known as filial and honest for office.
items.why_zh: 西元前 134 年，漢朝下令「郡國舉孝廉各一人」。
items.hint_en: This was a way to choose officials, decades after the Qin fell.
items.hint_zh: 這是選官員的方法，在秦亡幾十年以後。

items.en: Official scholars for the Five Classics
items.why_en: The History of the Former Han dates the appointment of scholars for the five Confucian classics to 136 BCE; historians debate how quickly the system took shape.
items.why_zh: 《漢書》把「置五經博士」記在西元前 136 年；這個制度多快成形，歷史學家有不同看法。
items.hint_en: The Qin court had scholars too, but this step came later.
items.hint_zh: 秦朝也有博士，但這一步比較晚。

items.en: Ordering private copies of many books to be burned
items.zh: 下令燒掉民間收藏的許多書
items.why_en: In 213 BCE, on Li Si's advice, the Qin ordered private copies of the Odes, the Documents, and the works of the hundred schools to be burned; books on medicine, divination, and farming were spared.
items.why_zh: 西元前 213 年，秦採納李斯的建議，下令燒掉民間收藏的《詩》《書》和百家的書；醫藥、卜筮、種樹的書不燒。
items.hint_en: It happened under the First Emperor.
items.hint_zh: 秦始皇的時候。

items.en: A new way of making paper, reported to the emperor
items.zh: 向皇帝報告一種新的造紙方法
items.why_en: The History of the Later Han says Cai Lun made paper from tree bark, hemp, rags, and fishing nets, and presented it in 105 CE.
items.why_zh: 《後漢書》說，蔡倫「用樹膚、麻頭及敝布、魚網以為紙」，西元 105 年奏上。
items.hint_en: This was very late, near the end of this lesson's time.
items.hint_zh: 很晚，接近這一課的年代的尾聲。

qinhan.end_en: The Qin set up the standards in a hurry and fell within fifteen years. The Han kept many of them, added new ways to choose officials and teach scholars, and lasted about four centuries.
qinhan.end_zh: 秦朝很急地訂下各種標準，十五年就亡了。漢朝保留了其中很多，又加上選官員、教育讀書人的新方法，延續了大約四百年。

timeline.lead_en: The Qin and Han are in the East Asia lane, and Rome in the Europe lane. Notice how short the Qin dynasty was, and how long the Han overlapped with Rome.
timeline.lead_zh: 秦和漢在東亞那一條線，羅馬在歐洲那一條線。注意秦朝有多短，漢朝又和羅馬重疊了多久。
timeline.idle_en: Click a bar or a diamond to read its dates.
timeline.idle_zh: 點一條長條或一個菱形，讀出它的年代。

tips.en: The Qin dynasty is a short bar; the Han is one of the longest in this lesson.
tips.zh: 秦朝是一條很短的長條；漢朝是這一課裡最長的之一。

tips.en: A striped bar marks dates that sources give differently, such as when the interruption of the Han ended.
tips.zh: 有條紋的長條，是各資料說法不同的年代，例如漢朝中斷的結束時間。

tips.en: The gray diamonds mark single events: unification, the wuzhu coin, and Cai Lun's paper.
tips.zh: 灰色的菱形標的是單一事件：統一、五銖錢，以及蔡倫的紙。

events.note_en: One standard for laws, measures, axles, and writing.
events.note_zh: 法令、度量衡、車軌和文字都用同一個標準。

events.note_en: 221 to 207 BCE; the dynasty lasted about fifteen years.
events.note_zh: 西元前 221 到 207 年；大約十五年。

events.note_en: 206 BCE to 220 CE, interrupted by Wang Mang's Xin dynasty.
events.note_zh: 西元前 206 年到西元 220 年，中間被王莽的新朝打斷。

events.note_en: From 9 CE; sources end it in 23 CE, when Wang Mang died, or in 25 CE, when the Han was restored.
events.note_zh: 從西元 9 年開始；有的資料算到王莽死的西元 23 年，有的算到漢朝恢復的西元 25 年。

events.note_en: Emperor Wu stopped the banliang and issued the wuzhu.
events.note_zh: 漢武帝罷半兩錢，行五銖錢。

events.note_en: Usually dated from 139 or 138 BCE; he returned about thirteen years later.
events.note_zh: 一般認為從西元前 139 或 138 年出發；大約十三年後回來。

events.note_en: Paper from bark, hemp, rags, and fishing nets.
events.note_zh: 用樹皮、麻、破布和魚網造的紙。

events.note_en: Lesson 6: from 27 BCE until the western half ended in 476 CE.
events.note_zh: 第六課：從西元前 27 年到西部在西元 476 年結束。

how_we_know.eyebrow: How Do We Know? · 我們怎麼知道？
how_we_know.en: A historian, a measuring cup, and slips of bamboo
how_we_know.zh: 一位史家、一個量器，和一片片竹簡
how_we_know.lead_en: Much of the story of the Qin comes from one historian who wrote under the Han, so archaeology matters a great deal.
how_we_know.lead_zh: 秦朝的故事，很多來自一位在漢朝寫書的史家，所以考古的發現特別重要。

items.en: The Records of the Grand Historian
items.limit_en: Sima Qian wrote for the dynasty that replaced the Qin, and readers have long asked how fair he was to it. Newly excavated Qin texts let historians check parts of his story.
items.limit_zh: 司馬遷是為取代秦朝的漢朝寫書，讀者一直在問他對秦朝是否公平。新出土的秦朝文書，讓歷史學家能查核他的一部分說法。
items.src: 《史記・秦始皇本紀》
items.text_en: Sima Qian, a Han court historian, wrote the Shiji about a century after the Qin fell. It tells of the unification, the standards, the roads, the burning of books, and the rebellions.
items.text_zh: 漢朝的史官司馬遷，在秦亡大約一百年後寫成《史記》。書裡記載了統一、各種標準、道路、焚書，以及各地的起兵。

items.limit_en: Objects show what the law ordered, not how strictly it was followed in every village.
items.limit_zh: 器物告訴我們法令下了什麼命令，卻看不出每個村子執行得多嚴格。
items.src: 上海博物館「商鞅方升」；「每月一珍：商鞅方升」
items.text_en: The Shang Yang measuring cup in the Shanghai Museum is 18.7 centimeters long and holds 202 milliliters. One inscription dates it to 344 BCE; a second, added in 221 BCE, orders that all measures be made the same.
items.text_zh: 上海博物館的商鞅方升長 18.7 公分，容量 202 毫升。一段銘文說它做於西元前 344 年；另一段是西元前 221 年加刻的，下令度量衡要統一。

items.limit_en: The slips come from one official's tomb and cover only some kinds of law, so they cannot tell us everything about how Qin law worked.
items.limit_zh: 這些竹簡來自一位官吏的墓，只包含部分種類的法律，不能告訴我們秦朝法律的全部。
items.src: 睡虎地秦簡〈徭律〉（維基文庫錄文）
items.text_en: Qin legal texts written on bamboo slips, found at Shuihudi in Hubei, show the actual rules. One statute on labor service fines people who arrive late and excuses them if it rains.
items.text_zh: 在湖北睡虎地出土、寫在竹簡上的秦朝法律文書，讓我們看到真正的條文。其中一條關於徭役的法律說：遲到要罰，但如果下雨就免除。

views.en: Four questions about the Qin and Han
views.lead_en: Ancient histories and new discoveries do not always agree. Here are four questions, with the views set side by side.
views.lead_zh: 古代的史書和新的發現，說法不一定一樣。下面是四個問題，各種說法並列。
views.rule_en: Notice how a single excavated text can challenge a story told for two thousand years, and how it can also be over-read.
views.rule_zh: 留意一份出土的文書，怎麼挑戰一個流傳了兩千年的故事；也留意它可能被讀得太過頭。

items.topic_en: Was being late really punished by death?
items.topic_zh: 遲到真的要殺頭嗎？

sides.en: Sima Qian writes that Chen Sheng's band, held up by rain, knew that under the law “those who miss the deadline are all beheaded,” so they rebelled.
sides.zh: 司馬遷寫道，陳勝的隊伍被大雨耽誤，知道依法「失期，法皆斬」，所以起兵反抗。

sides.en: A Qin statute on labor service found at Shuihudi punishes lateness with a reprimand or fines, and excuses it in rain. But Chen Sheng's men were garrison soldiers, who fell under different rules.
sides.zh: 睡虎地出土的秦朝〈徭律〉，對遲到的處罰是斥責或罰錢，下雨還可以免除。不過陳勝那群人是去戍守邊境的，適用的可能是另一套規定。
sides.src: 睡虎地秦簡〈徭律〉；郭建，澎湃新聞（2014）

items.note_en: The new evidence shows that one story may be too simple, but it does not settle the question.
items.note_zh: 新的證據說明這個故事可能太簡單了，但還不能下定論。

items.topic_en: What was the burning of books really about?
items.topic_zh: 焚書到底是怎麼回事？

sides.en: The burning of books and the deaths of scholars became a lasting symbol of a harsh ruler attacking learning, especially Confucian learning.
sides.zh: 焚書和處死讀書人，成了暴君打壓學問、特別是儒家學問的長久象徵。

sides.en: The Shiji itself says that books on medicine, divination, and farming were spared, and the court's own scholars kept their copies. One scholar argues that Confucianism as such was not the target.
sides.zh: 《史記》自己就說，醫藥、卜筮、種樹的書不燒，朝廷博士官的藏書也保留。有學者主張，針對的並不是儒家本身。
sides.src: Pines, “Legalism in Chinese Philosophy,” Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy

items.note_en: Both views agree that many books were lost; they differ on what the Qin intended.
items.note_zh: 兩種說法都同意很多書因此失傳；分歧在於秦朝的用意是什麼。

items.topic_en: Is every terracotta warrior's face different?
items.topic_zh: 每一個兵馬俑的臉都不一樣嗎？

sides.en: UNESCO's description of the First Emperor's tomb says that the figures “are all different.”
sides.zh: 聯合國教科文組織對秦始皇陵的說明寫道，這些陶俑「都不一樣」。
sides.src: UNESCO World Heritage List, Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor

sides.en: A Metropolitan Museum essay explains that parts were made with molds and then finished by hand, and that most scholars do not think the statues were modeled on real soldiers.
sides.zh: 大都會藝術博物館的一篇文章說明，陶俑的部分是用模子做的，再用手修整；大多數學者也不認為它們是照著真的士兵做的。
sides.src: Metropolitan Museum of Art, “Making the Warrior” (2017)

items.note_en: The faces are individualized, but made with a mix of molds and handwork. Scholars still debate exactly how.
items.note_zh: 臉是有個別差異的，但是用模子加上手工做出來的；確切的做法學者還在討論。

items.topic_en: Which empire was bigger, Rome or the Han?
items.topic_zh: 羅馬和漢朝，哪一個比較大？

sides.en: A census in the History of the Former Han counts 59,594,978 people. A 2025 study accepts about 57.7 million for the Han around 2 CE and about 75 million for Rome around 165 CE, and says each ruled 60 to 70 million people at its peak.
sides.zh: 《漢書》記載的人口普查是 59,594,978 人。2025 年的一項研究採用的估計是：西元 2 年前後的漢朝約 5,770 萬，西元 165 年前後的羅馬約 7,500 萬；並說兩者全盛時都統治了六、七千萬人。
sides.src: 《漢書・地理志》；Alfani, Bolla, and Scheidel, Nature Communications (2025)

sides.en: Historians who compare the two, such as Michael Loewe, look at how each was governed, and note that each empire was largely ignorant of the other.
sides.zh: 比較這兩個帝國的歷史學家，例如魯惟一（Michael Loewe），看的是它們怎麼治理，並指出兩個帝國對彼此大多一無所知。
sides.src: Loewe, Imperial Institutions in Ancient Rome and Early China (2025)

items.note_en: Size alone does not tell us how well people lived. Lesson 6 gave other estimates for Rome; every number here is an estimate for a different year.
items.note_zh: 光看大小，說明不了人們過得好不好。第六課對羅馬的人口有其他的估計；這裡每一個數字，都是不同年份的估計。

phrases.en: Eight sentences for comparing two empires
phrases.zh: 比較兩個帝國的八句英文
phrases.lead_en: These sentences help you compare Qin and Han China with Rome without ranking them. Listen, repeat, then make your own sentence with the words in bold.
phrases.lead_zh: 這八句幫你比較秦漢和羅馬，而不替它們排名。先聽、再跟著唸，然後用粗體的字自己造一句。

rows.en: Both Rome and the Han ruled tens of millions of people.
rows.html: Both Rome and the Han ruled tens of millions of people.
rows.zh: 羅馬和漢朝都統治了好幾千萬人。
rows.note_en: both … and …: two things that are alike

rows.en: The Qin coin was the same shape as the Han coin.
rows.html: The Qin coin was the same shape as the Han coin.
rows.zh: 秦朝的錢和漢朝的錢形狀一樣。
rows.note_en: the same … as: exactly alike

rows.en: Unlike Rome, the Qin made everyone use one script.
rows.html: Unlike Rome, the Qin made everyone use one script.
rows.zh: 和羅馬不同，秦朝讓大家都用同一套文字。
rows.note_en: unlike: different from

rows.en: Rome spread its citizenship, while the Han chose officials for their learning.
rows.html: Rome spread its citizenship, while the Han chose officials for their learning.
rows.zh: 羅馬擴大公民權，而漢朝依學問選官員。
rows.note_en: while: shows a contrast between two things

rows.en: The Han dynasty lasted much longer than the Qin.
rows.html: The Han dynasty lasted much longer than the Qin.
rows.zh: 漢朝比秦朝延續得久多了。
rows.note_en: lasted longer than: compares time

rows.en: The two empires had a lot in common.
rows.html: The two empires had a lot in common.
rows.zh: 這兩個帝國有很多共同點。
rows.note_en: had … in common: shared features

rows.en: Instead of many coins, there was now only one.
rows.html: Instead of many coins, there was now only one.
rows.zh: 不再有很多種錢，現在只有一種。
rows.note_en: instead of: in place of

rows.en: Each empire knew very little about the other.
rows.html: Each empire knew very little about the other.
rows.zh: 兩個帝國對彼此都所知很少。
rows.note_en: each … the other: two sides, one at a time

taiwan_then.eyebrow: Taiwan at That Time · 那時候的台灣
taiwan_then.lead_en: When the Qin united China, about 2,200 years ago, Taiwan was home to several prehistoric cultures, each in its own region.
taiwan_then.lead_zh: 秦統一中國的時候，大約距今兩千兩百年，台灣有好幾個史前文化，各自分布在不同的地區。
taiwan_then.intro_en: Archaeologists in Taiwan give dates as “years ago” (before 1950). About 2,200 years ago is roughly the third century BCE.
taiwan_then.intro_zh: 台灣的考古學家用「距今幾年」（以 1950 年為準）說年代。距今大約兩千兩百年，差不多是西元前三世紀。

facts.en: In the Taipei Basin, the Yuanshan culture lasted from about 4,500 to a little over 2,000 years ago.
facts.zh: 在臺北盆地，圓山文化從距今約四千五百年延續到二千多年前。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

facts.en: In the south, the Dahu culture, and in central Taiwan, the Yingpu culture, both lasted from about 3,500 to a little over 2,000 years ago.
facts.zh: 南部的大湖文化，以及中部的營埔文化，都是從距今約三千五百年延續到二千多年前。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

facts.en: On the east coast, the Beinan culture was at its height about 3,500 to 2,000 years ago, and lived side by side with the Qilin culture of standing stones. The museum notes that the Beinan culture is completely different from the culture of today's Puyuma people.
facts.zh: 在東海岸，卑南文化極盛的年代大約在三千五百到二千年前，和豎立巨石的麒麟文化並存。博物館也說明，卑南文化和今天的卑南族文化完全不同。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

facts.en: These cultures had different pottery and tools, and there was no kingdom to make them the same. A little later, about 2,000 years ago, the Shisanhang culture rose near the Taipei Basin.
facts.zh: 這些文化各有不同的陶器和工具，也沒有一個王國把它們變成一樣。稍晚，大約二千年前，十三行文化在臺北盆地附近興起。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

links.en: Taiwan's Story, Lesson 2: Who Lived in Taiwan Thousands of Years Ago?
links.zh: 台灣歷史第二課：幾千年前，誰住在台灣？

links.en: Taiwan's Story, Lesson 3: Who Are Taiwan's Indigenous Peoples?
links.zh: 台灣歷史第三課：台灣的原住民族是誰？

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Evidence · 證據背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A measuring cup, a farmers' well, a wall that is not one wall, and a view from space
culture_cards.title_zh: 一個量器、一口農夫挖的井、一道不只一道的牆，和從太空看下來
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how we know what the Qin and Han built.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事：我們怎麼知道秦漢蓋了什麼。

cards.k: 344 and 221 BCE · Shanghai Museum · 上海博物館
cards.zh: 一個有兩個年代的量器
cards.body_en: The Shang Yang measure was made in 344 BCE, when Shang Yang reformed the kingdom of Qin. More than a century later, a new edict was carved on its base: the emperor had united the land, and all measures that were not the same were to be made the same.
cards.body_zh: 商鞅方升做於西元前 344 年，那時商鞅正在秦國變法。一百多年後，器物的底部又刻了新的詔書：皇帝已經統一天下，「法度量則不壹嫌疑者，皆明壹之」。

cards.body_en: In 1974, farmers sinking a well near the First Emperor's tomb found pieces of clay soldiers. The first pit alone is about 210 meters long and holds more than 3,000 figures.
cards.body_zh: 1974 年，在秦始皇陵附近挖井的農夫，挖到了陶俑的碎片。光是第一號坑就長大約 210 公尺，裡面有三千多個陶俑。

cards.k: 220 BCE to 1600s CE · Northern China · 中國北方
cards.body_en: Around 220 BCE, the Qin joined sections of earlier walls into one line of defense. Walls were then built and rebuilt until the 1600s. A national survey published in 2012 measured the walls of all periods at 21,196.18 kilometers; the Ming walls are the longest single part, about 8,850 kilometers.
cards.body_zh: 大約西元前 220 年，秦把各國早先的城牆連成一條防線。之後一直有人修、有人重建，直到十七世紀。2012 年公布的全國調查，量出歷代長城總長 21,196.18 公里；其中明朝的長城最長，大約 8,850 公里。

cards.body_en: When Yang Liwei became China's first astronaut in 2003, he was asked whether he had seen the Great Wall. He said he had not. NASA explains that the wall is about the same color as the land around it, and certainly cannot be seen from the Moon.
cards.body_zh: 2003 年，楊利偉成為中國第一位太空人。被問到有沒有看到長城，他說沒有。美國太空總署解釋，長城和周圍土地的顏色差不多，從月球上當然更看不到。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum for social studies (October 2018).
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要社會領域（民國 107 年 10 月）。

items.area: 國中・從古典到傳統時代
items.area_en: Junior high · from the classical to the traditional age
items.text: 商周至隋唐時期國家與社會的重要變遷。
items.note_en: The curriculum's explanation describes the change “from classical feudalism to the empire of commanderies and counties,” and asks how rulers held power and chose officials. This lesson focuses on how the Qin and Han held a huge land together.
items.note_zh: 課綱的說明談「從古典封建到郡縣帝國時期」，並建議討論「統治階級如何維繫政權、選拔官僚」。這一課聚焦在秦漢怎麼把一大片土地連在一起。

items.area: 高中・國家與社會
items.area_en: Senior high · state and society
items.text: 傳統政治權威的類型。
items.note_en: The explanation suggests comparing types of political authority, using as an example how the Han empire built its authority through ancestral rules, Confucian learning, or law.
items.note_zh: 課綱的說明建議比較傳統政治權威的類型，「可以漢帝國如何藉由祖宗家法、儒術，或律令建構其政治權威為例」。

myths.myth_en: The Great Wall can be seen from space with the naked eye.
myths.myth_zh: 從太空用肉眼看得到長城。
myths.fact_en: China's first astronaut said he did not see it, and NASA explains that from low orbit it generally cannot be seen without help, and certainly not from the Moon.
myths.fact_zh: 中國第一位太空人說他沒有看到；美國太空總署也說明，從低軌道上一般看不到，從月球更不可能。

myths.myth_en: The Great Wall is one continuous wall built by the Qin.
myths.myth_zh: 長城是一道連續的牆，是秦朝蓋的。
myths.fact_en: The Qin joined earlier walls, and walls were built and rebuilt for nearly 2,000 years. The Ming walls are the longest single part.
myths.fact_zh: 秦是把早先的城牆連起來；之後將近兩千年一直有人修建。其中明朝的長城最長。

myths.myth_en: The First Emperor burned all the books.
myths.myth_zh: 秦始皇把所有的書都燒了。
myths.fact_en: The order targeted private copies of certain books. Books on medicine, divination, and farming were spared, and the court kept its own copies.
myths.fact_zh: 命令針對的是民間收藏的某些書。醫藥、卜筮、種樹的書不燒，朝廷也保留了自己的藏書。

myths.myth_en: Unification meant everyone spoke the same language.
myths.myth_zh: 統一以後，大家都說同一種話。
myths.fact_en: The Qin standardized writing, not speech. People in different regions could read the same characters while still speaking very differently.
myths.fact_zh: 秦統一的是文字，不是說話。不同地方的人可以讀同樣的字，說起話來卻還是很不一樣。

tricks.title_en: One script, one coin, one measure
tricks.title_zh: 一種文字、一種錢、一種量器
tricks.body_en: The Qin's tools for holding the land together.
tricks.body_zh: 秦把土地連在一起的工具。

tricks.body_en: The Qin fell fast; the Han kept its standards and lasted.
tricks.body_zh: 秦很快就亡了；漢保留了它的標準，延續很久。

tricks.body_en: The coin shape that lasted about 2,000 years.
tricks.body_zh: 用了大約兩千年的錢幣形狀。

tricks.body_en: Roads and walls were built with forced labor.
tricks.body_zh: 道路和城牆是用強迫勞役蓋的。

materials.en: Paper “coins” cut into four shapes: spades, knives, round coins, and small shells
materials.zh: 剪成四種形狀的紙錢：鏟形、刀形、圓形和小貝殼形

materials.en: Cards for goods: salt, cloth, rice, horses
materials.zh: 商品卡：鹽、布、米、馬

steps.en: Divide the class into four “kingdoms.” Each kingdom gets only one shape of coin and sets its own prices.
steps.zh: 把全班分成四個「國家」。每個國家只拿到一種形狀的錢，自己定價格。

steps.en: Trade between kingdoms for five minutes. How do you agree how many knives equal one spade?
steps.zh: 國家之間交易五分鐘。幾把刀等於一把鏟，要怎麼談？

steps.en: Now “unify”: everyone exchanges their coins for one round coin and uses one price list. Trade again.
steps.zh: 接著「統一」：大家把錢換成同一種圓錢，用同一張價目表，再交易一次。

steps.en: Discuss in English: “Trading was easier because …” and “Some kingdoms lost because …”
steps.zh: 用英文討論：「Trading was easier because …」和「Some kingdoms lost because …」

activities.tip_en: Step 4 matters most. A single coin helps trade, but changing over is not fair to everyone, which is part of why unification was hard.
activities.tip_zh: 第四步最重要。同一種錢讓交易方便，但換錢的過程對每個人不一定公平，這也是統一不容易的原因之一。

materials.en: The comparison table from Lesson 6's activity, or a new sheet with two columns: Rome and Han
materials.zh: 第六課活動的比較表，或一張新的紙，分成羅馬和漢朝兩欄

materials.en: This lesson and Lesson 6
materials.zh: 這一課和第六課

steps.en: Fill in: How did each empire hold itself together? Roads, law, citizenship, script, coins, measures, officials.
steps.zh: 填寫：兩個帝國各用什麼方法把自己連在一起？道路、法律、公民權、文字、錢、度量衡、官員。

steps.en: Add one row: Who paid the price?
steps.zh: 加一列：誰付出了代價？

steps.en: Circle the things they had in common.
steps.zh: 把兩邊的共同點圈起來。

steps.en: Write two sentences: one with “both … and,” one with “while.”
steps.zh: 寫兩句英文：一句用 both … and，一句用 while。

activities.tip_en: Remind students that the goal is to compare, not to decide which empire was “better.”
activities.tip_zh: 提醒學生：目的是比較，不是決定哪一個帝國「比較好」。

links.en: How Did Buddhism Begin and Travel?
links.zh: 佛教怎麼開始、怎麼傳出去？
links.note_en: During the Han dynasty, Buddhism began to reach China along the roads to the west.
links.note_zh: 漢朝的時候，佛教開始沿著往西的路傳進中國。

links.en: How Did Rome Hold an Empire Together?
links.zh: 羅馬怎麼管住那麼大的地方？
links.note_en: The other great empire of the same age, held together by roads, law, and citizenship.
links.note_zh: 同一個時代的另一個大帝國，靠道路、法律和公民權連在一起。

links.en: Where Did Chinese Characters Come From?
links.zh: 漢字從哪裡來？甲骨文到篆書
links.note_en: How characters changed from oracle bones to the seal script the Qin made standard.
links.note_zh: 漢字怎麼從甲骨文，變到秦朝定為標準的篆書。

links.en: Why Does Clerical Script Have Silkworm Heads and Swallow Tails?
links.zh: 隸書：為什麼是蠶頭燕尾？
links.note_en: The everyday script of Qin and Han officials.
links.note_zh: 秦漢官吏日常使用的字體。

lessons.sources_note_en: Checked November 2026. Dates for the end of the Qin and of Wang Mang's Xin differ between sources; where they do, the lesson gives both
lessons.sources_note_zh: 2026 年 11 月查證。秦朝和王莽新朝結束的年代，各資料說法不一；遇到不一致時，課文兩個都寫

sources.en: The conquest of the six kingdoms (230–221 BCE); the title of emperor; one standard for laws, measures, axles, and writing; the Straight Road (212 BCE); the burning of books (213 BCE) and the deaths of more than 460 scholars (212 BCE)
sources.zh: 滅六國（西元前 230–221 年）；皇帝的稱號；「一法度衡石丈尺。車同軌。書同文字。」；直道（西元前 212 年）；焚書（西元前 213 年）與「犯禁者四百六十餘人，皆阬之咸陽」（西元前 212 年）

sources.zh: 秦「中一國之幣為二等」：黃金與「半兩」銅錢

sources.zh: 一枚戰國刀幣長 157 公釐；齊國刀幣長 183 公釐、重 45 公克；楚國蟻鼻錢約 20 公釐

sources.zh: 商鞅方升：西元前 344 年，長 18.7 公分，容 202 毫升

sources.en: The two inscriptions on the Shang Yang measure, including the edict of the 26th year (221 BCE) on its base
sources.zh: 商鞅方升的兩段銘文，包括刻在底部的二十六年（西元前 221 年）詔書
sources.src: 上海博物館「每月一珍：商鞅方升」

sources.zh: 漢武帝「罷半兩錢，行五銖錢」（西元前 118 年）；「置五經博士」（西元前 136 年）；「初令郡國舉孝廉各一人」（西元前 134 年）

sources.zh: 五銖錢「成錢二百八十億萬餘」

sources.zh: 人口普查：「民戶千二百二十三萬三千六十二，口五千九百五十九萬四千九百七十八」

sources.zh: 蔡倫造紙，元興元年（西元 105 年）奏上

sources.en: Qin 221–207 BCE; Han 206 BCE–220 CE; Xin 9–25 CE
sources.zh: 秦西元前 221–207 年；漢西元前 206 年–西元 220 年；新朝西元 9–25 年

sources.en: Zhang Qian sent west in 138 BCE and away for thirteen years
sources.zh: 張騫西元前 138 年出使，在外十三年

sources.zh: 直道的路線與相關史料
sources.src: Sanft, Frontiers of History in China 6 (2011)

sources.zh: 秦律既嚴厲也公開；嚴格的規定主要針對官吏
sources.src: Turner, review of Sanft, Early China 39 (2016)

sources.zh: 秦打壓民間學問，針對的並不是儒家本身

sources.zh: 秦始皇燒了哪些書？

sources.zh: 秦始皇陵：1974 年發現；陶俑都不一樣

sources.en: Farmers sinking a well in 1974; Pit 1 about 210 m long with more than 3,000 figures; stereotyped faces; molds and hand finishing
sources.zh: 1974 年農民挖井；一號坑長約 210 公尺、三千多個陶俑；臉有固定的類型；模製再手工修整
