lessons.title: How Did Buddhism Begin and Travel?
lessons.title_zh: 佛教怎麼開始、怎麼傳出去？
lessons.blurb_en: Follow Buddhism on a 3D globe as it travels from northern India by land and by sea, over about 1,500 years. Find out which dates come from tradition and which from evidence, and match Buddhist words across Chinese, Pāli or Sanskrit, and English.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 地球儀上，跟著佛教從印度北部走陸路、走海路，旅行大約一千五百年。看看哪些年代是傳統的說法、哪些有證據，再把佛教的詞語，在中文、巴利文或梵文、英文之間配對起來。
lessons.big_idea_en: Buddhism began in northern India about 2,400 to 2,500 years ago, with a teacher called the Buddha; scholars disagree about his exact dates. Emperor Ashoka's edicts, carved on rocks and pillars, are the earliest datable written evidence. Monks, traders, pilgrims, and rulers then carried the teaching south by sea and north and east over land, and each place made it its own.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 佛教大約在兩千四、五百年前，從印度北部一位被稱為佛陀的老師開始；他確切的年代，學者看法不一。阿育王刻在岩石和石柱上的詔令，是最早可確定年代的文字證據。後來，僧人、商人、朝聖者和國王，把教法往南走海路、往北往東走陸路帶出去，每一個地方都把它變成自己的。

lab.how_en: Drag the slider from 500 BCE to 1000 CE, or press Play, and watch the routes grow out of northern India. Gold lines went over land, blue lines went by sea, and the dashed line climbs toward Tibet. Every place is marked either “Tradition says” (a gold dot) or “Evidence shows” (a white dot). Click a place to read what happened there, when, and how we know.
lab.how_zh: 把滑桿從西元前 500 年拉到西元 1000 年，或按「播放」，看路線從印度北部長出去。金色的線走陸路，藍色的線走海路，虛線往上爬到西藏。每一個地方都標明是「傳統上說」（金色的點）還是「史料／考古顯示」（白色的點）。點一個地方，讀它發生了什麼、在什麼時候，以及我們怎麼知道。

sites.what_en: Buddhists hold that here, under a tree, Siddhartha Gautama awakened and became the Buddha, “the awakened one.”
sites.what_zh: 佛教徒相信，悉達多・喬達摩在這裡的一棵樹下覺悟，成為佛陀，也就是「覺悟的人」。
sites.when_en: Scholars disagree about when the Buddha lived. An older view puts his life at about 560–480 BCE; many scholars now think he died around 400 BCE. The model uses about 450 BCE, between the two.
sites.when_zh: 佛陀生活在什麼年代，學者看法不一。比較早的看法是大約西元前 560 到 480 年；現在很多學者認為他大約在西元前 400 年前後去世。模型用的是兩者之間的大約西元前 450 年。
sites.how_en: The story comes from Buddhist texts that were passed on by memory and written down centuries later. UNESCO says the first temple here was built by Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE; the temple standing today dates from the 5th–6th centuries CE.
sites.how_zh: 這個故事來自佛教的經典，先靠記憶口耳相傳，好幾百年後才寫下來。聯合國教科文組織說，這裡的第一座寺廟是阿育王在西元前三世紀蓋的；今天看到的寺廟是西元五到六世紀的。
sites.src: UNESCO, Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodh Gaya

sites.what_en: According to tradition, the Buddha gave his first teaching here, in a deer park near Varanasi.
sites.what_zh: 依照傳統的說法，佛陀在這裡，瓦拉納西附近的一座鹿園，第一次說法。
sites.when_en: Soon after the awakening, so the same uncertain date as Bodh Gaya.
sites.when_zh: 在覺悟之後不久，所以年代和菩提伽耶一樣不確定。
sites.how_en: The place is named in early sutras. Much later, Ashoka set up a pillar here topped by four lions; that Lion Capital is now in the museum at Sarnath and is the basis of India's state emblem.
sites.how_zh: 早期的經典提到了這個地方。很久以後，阿育王在這裡立了一根石柱，柱頂是四隻獅子；這個獅子柱頭現在放在鹿野苑的博物館，也是今天印度國徽的根據。

sites.what_en: Buddhists hold that the Buddha was born here. A stone pillar set up by Emperor Ashoka says so in writing: “here the Buddha, the sage of the Sakyans, was born.”
sites.what_zh: 佛教徒相信佛陀在這裡出生。阿育王立的一根石柱，用文字寫明了這件事：「佛陀，釋迦族的聖者，在這裡出生。」
sites.when_en: The birth itself was much earlier. The pillar is dated to about 249 BCE, so it was carved roughly 150 to 250 years after the Buddha's death, depending on which dates you follow.
sites.when_zh: 出生本身早得多。石柱的年代大約是西元前 249 年，所以是在佛陀去世之後大約一百五十到兩百五十年才刻的，要看你採用哪一種年代。
sites.how_en: The inscription is in Brahmi script. The pillar also says Ashoka lowered the village's tax. Excavations found brick buildings from the 3rd century BCE and, beneath them, an older timber structure that the excavators think was a shrine.
sites.how_zh: 銘文用婆羅米文字寫成。石柱上還說，阿育王減輕了這個村子的稅。考古挖掘發現了西元前三世紀的磚造建築，底下還有更早的木造結構，挖掘的學者認為那是一座聖所。
sites.src: UNESCO, Lumbini; Coningham et al., Antiquity (2013)

sites.what_en: A great stupa, a dome-shaped monument holding relics, stands on a hill here. UNESCO says the site began as a sacred center under Ashoka.
sites.what_zh: 這裡的山丘上有一座大佛塔，是收藏舍利的圓頂建築。聯合國教科文組織說，這個地方在阿育王的時候開始成為聖地。
sites.when_en: The first brick stupa is from the 3rd century BCE; it was enlarged in the 2nd–1st centuries BCE, and the carved stone gateways were added around the 1st century CE.
sites.when_zh: 第一座磚造的佛塔是西元前三世紀的；西元前二到一世紀被加大，雕刻的石門大約在西元一世紀加上去。
sites.how_en: The monuments themselves, studied by archaeologists. The early carvings show the Buddha only by symbols, such as a tree, a wheel, or footprints, never in human form.
sites.how_zh: 就是這些建築本身，由考古學家研究。早期的雕刻只用象徵來表現佛陀，例如一棵樹、一個輪子或腳印，從不刻成人的樣子。

sites.zh: 斯里蘭卡阿努拉德普勒
sites.what_en: Sri Lankan chronicles say Ashoka's son Mahinda brought Buddhism to the island, and his daughter Sanghamitta brought a cutting of the tree of awakening. A tree that tradition holds grew from it still stands here.
sites.what_zh: 斯里蘭卡的編年史說，阿育王的兒子摩哂陀把佛教帶到島上，女兒僧伽蜜多帶來了覺悟之樹的一段枝條。傳統上認為由它長成的那棵樹，到今天還在這裡。
sites.when_en: The chronicles place it in the 3rd century BCE. They were written several centuries later.
sites.when_zh: 編年史把它放在西元前三世紀。這些編年史是好幾百年後才寫的。
sites.how_en: Through the chronicles. Archaeologists have found writing in the Brahmi script at Anuradhapura from even earlier, but writing alone does not show when Buddhism arrived. The city was abandoned after an invasion in 993.
sites.how_zh: 靠編年史。考古學家在阿努拉德普勒找到更早的婆羅米文字，但光有文字，不能證明佛教是什麼時候傳到的。這座城在 993 年被入侵後廢棄。
sites.src: UNESCO, Sacred City of Anuradhapura; Britannica, “Ashoka”

sites.zh: 犍陀羅（今巴基斯坦西北部）
sites.what_en: Gandhara, at the crossroads to Central Asia, became a great Buddhist center. It is one of the first places where the Buddha was carved in human form.
sites.what_zh: 犍陀羅位在通往中亞的十字路口，成了佛教的重鎮。它是最早把佛陀刻成人形的地方之一。
sites.when_en: Human images of the Buddha appear in the 1st century CE, here and, at about the same time, at Mathura in India. The oldest Buddhist manuscripts known, on birch bark, also come from this region, from about the 1st century BCE to the 3rd century CE.
sites.when_zh: 佛陀的人形像出現在西元一世紀，在這裡，也差不多同時在印度的秣菟羅。目前所知最古老的佛教寫本，寫在樺樹皮上，也來自這一帶，年代大約在西元前一世紀到西元三世紀之間。
sites.how_en: Sculptures in museums, and birch-bark scrolls in the Gāndhārī language, bought by the British Library in 1994. Scholars give different views on which came first, Gandhara's images or Mathura's.
sites.how_zh: 博物館裡的雕像，以及大英圖書館在 1994 年購得、用犍陀羅語寫的樺樹皮卷子。犍陀羅和秣菟羅，哪一邊的佛像比較早，學者有不同的看法。
sites.src: Metropolitan Museum of Art, “Buddhism and Buddhist Art” (Dehejia, 2007); NEH, “Early Buddhist Manuscripts”

sites.what_en: Liu Ying, the King of Chu, a son of the Han emperor, held fasts and offerings for the Buddha. This is the earliest reliable mention of Buddhism in China.
sites.what_zh: 漢朝皇帝的兒子、楚王劉英，「學為浮屠齋戒祭祀」。這是中國最早可靠的佛教記載。
sites.when_en: The History of the Later Han dates the emperor's reply to the eighth year of his reign, 65 CE. The famous story of Emperor Ming dreaming of a golden man is a later legend.
sites.when_zh: 《後漢書》把皇帝的回覆記在「八年」，也就是永平八年（西元 65 年）。漢明帝夢見金人那個有名的故事，是後來的傳說。
sites.how_en: The emperor's edict, quoted in the History of the Later Han, praises the king for honoring the Buddha's “humane shrines” and mentions lay followers and monks.
sites.how_zh: 《後漢書》引了皇帝的詔書，稱讚楚王「尚浮屠之仁祠」，還提到「伊蒲塞桑門」，也就是在家信徒和出家人。
sites.src: 《後漢書・光武十王列傳・楚王英》

sites.what_en: A monk from Parthia, An Shigao, arrived in the Han capital and began translating Buddhist texts into Chinese.
sites.what_zh: 一位從安息（帕提亞）來的僧人安世高，來到漢朝的都城，開始把佛經翻譯成中文。
sites.when_en: 148 CE, the earliest written date, from a later catalog. About thirty years later, Lokakṣema from the Kushan lands translated some of the first Mahāyāna sutras here.
sites.when_zh: 西元 148 年，這是最早的文字紀錄，出自後來的目錄。大約三十年後，從貴霜來的支婁迦讖，在這裡翻譯了最早的一批大乘經典。
sites.how_en: Later biographies of monks quote an early catalog of translations by the monk Dao'an.
sites.how_zh: 後來的《高僧傳》引用了道安早期整理的譯經目錄。

sites.what_en: At this oasis on the road to the west, monks and donors carved hundreds of cave temples into a cliff, the Mogao Caves.
sites.what_zh: 在這個往西的路上的綠洲，僧人和捐獻的人在山崖上開鑿了好幾百個石窟寺，就是莫高窟。
sites.when_en: UNESCO gives 366 CE for the first caves, a date from a text written about 330 years later. The oldest caves that survive are from the early 400s. Work went on for about a thousand years.
sites.when_zh: 聯合國教科文組織說最早的石窟開鑿於西元 366 年；這個年代出自大約三百三十年後寫的文字。現存最古老的石窟是 400 年代初期的。之後開鑿了大約一千年。
sites.how_en: 492 caves survive, with wall paintings and sculptures. A sealed library cave, found in 1900, held tens of thousands of manuscripts.
sites.how_zh: 現存 492 個石窟，有壁畫和雕塑。1900 年發現的一個封起來的藏經洞，裡面有好幾萬件寫本。

sites.what_en: Kumārajīva, a monk from Kucha in Central Asia, reached Chang'an and led a team that translated many sutras into a clear Chinese still read today.
sites.what_zh: 從中亞龜茲來的僧人鳩摩羅什到了長安，帶領譯經團隊翻譯了許多經典，譯文流暢，今天還在讀。
sites.when_en: He arrived in 401 CE. Chang'an was also where the pilgrim Faxian set out for India, about 399–400, and where Xuanzang came home in 645.
sites.when_zh: 他在西元 401 年抵達。長安也是朝聖者法顯出發去印度的地方（大約 399 到 400 年），玄奘也在 645 年回到這裡。
sites.how_en: Britannica and the monks' own records. Faxian's travel record gives its dates in two ways that do not quite agree, so they are given as a range.
sites.how_zh: Britannica 和僧人們自己的紀錄。法顯的遊記用兩種方式記年代，彼此對不太起來，所以寫成一個範圍。

sites.what_en: A ruler in northern China sent the monk Sundo with Buddha images and sutras to the kingdom of Goguryeo.
sites.what_zh: 中國北方的前秦王苻堅，派僧人順道帶著佛像和經文到高句麗。
sites.when_en: 372 CE, the second year of King Sosurim. Two monasteries were founded three years later; the History calls this “the beginning of the Buddha's teaching east of the sea.”
sites.when_zh: 西元 372 年，小獸林王二年。三年後建了兩座寺；史書說這是「海東佛法之始」。
sites.how_en: From the History of the Three Kingdoms, written in 1145, about 770 years later. It is the main source, so the date is the one tradition gives.
sites.how_zh: 依據《三國史記》，寫於 1145 年，大約七百七十年後。它是主要的資料，所以這個年代是傳統的說法。

sites.what_en: A foreign monk, Maranant'a, came from Jin China, and the king of Baekje welcomed him into the palace.
sites.what_zh: 一位外國僧人摩羅難陀從中國的晉朝而來，百濟王把他迎進宮裡禮敬。
sites.when_en: 384 CE, in the first year of King Chimnyu, the History says: “The Buddha's teaching began here.”
sites.when_zh: 西元 384 年，枕流王元年，史書說：「佛法始於此。」
sites.how_en: The same History of the Three Kingdoms, written about 760 years later.
sites.how_zh: 同樣是《三國史記》，大約七百六十年後寫的。

sites.what_en: In Silla, the court at first opposed the new teaching. The History tells of a young official, Ichadon, who offered his life so that the king could accept it.
sites.what_zh: 在新羅，朝廷起初反對這個新的教法。史書說，有一位年輕的官員異次頓，願意犧牲自己的性命，讓國王能夠接受佛教。
sites.when_en: The 15th year of King Beopheung in the History of the Three Kingdoms (528 CE by its count); another Korean book, the Memorabilia of the Three Kingdoms, puts it in 527.
sites.when_zh: 《三國史記》記在法興王十五年（依它的算法是西元 528 年）；另一部《三國遺事》記在 527 年。
sites.how_en: The History of the Three Kingdoms, which says it follows an older book. Parts of the story, such as white blood flowing at his death, are clearly legend.
sites.how_zh: 《三國史記》，它說自己依據一部更早的書。故事裡的一些部分，例如他死時流出白色的血，顯然是傳說。

sites.what_en: The king of Baekje sent the Japanese court a gilt-bronze Buddha image, banners, and sutras.
sites.what_zh: 百濟的聖明王送給日本朝廷一尊金銅的釋迦佛像、幡蓋和經論。
sites.when_en: The Chronicles of Japan give 552 CE. Other old records give 538. Both dates come from tradition.
sites.when_zh: 《日本書紀》記在西元 552 年。另外一些古老的紀錄記在 538 年。兩個年代都是傳統的說法。
sites.how_en: The Chronicles of Japan were finished in 720, more than 150 years later. The temple of Hōryū-ji, rebuilt after a fire in 670, has some of the oldest wooden buildings in the world.
sites.how_zh: 《日本書紀》在 720 年完成，已經過了一百五十多年。法隆寺在 670 年的大火後重建，有一些全世界最古老的木造建築。

sites.what_en: Nalanda grew into a huge monastery where monks studied and taught. Students came from China and elsewhere in Asia.
sites.what_zh: 那爛陀發展成一座很大的寺院，僧人在這裡學習、講學。學生從中國和亞洲其他地方而來。
sites.when_en: The monasteries were founded in the 5th century CE. Xuanzang studied here in the 630s. The site was sacked around 1200 and abandoned.
sites.when_zh: 這些寺院建於西元五世紀。玄奘在 630 年代在這裡求學。大約 1200 年，這裡遭到洗劫，之後就荒廢了。
sites.how_en: Excavated ruins, and the travel records of Chinese pilgrims such as Xuanzang and Yijing.
sites.how_zh: 挖掘出來的遺址，以及玄奘、義淨等中國朝聖者的遊記。
sites.src: UNESCO, Archaeological Site of Nalanda Mahavihara

sites.zh: 室利佛逝（蘇門答臘巨港）
sites.what_en: The Chinese monk Yijing stopped in Srivijaya, a trading kingdom on Sumatra, to study before sailing on to India.
sites.what_zh: 中國僧人義淨在前往印度的途中，停在蘇門答臘的貿易王國室利佛逝學習。
sites.when_en: 671 CE. Britannica says the voyage from Guangzhou took less than 20 days.
sites.when_zh: 西元 671 年。Britannica 說，從廣州出發，不到二十天就到了。
sites.how_en: Yijing's own writings, which describe many monks in Srivijaya.
sites.how_zh: 義淨自己的著作，裡面描述室利佛逝有很多僧人。

sites.what_en: A huge stone monument built as a mountain of terraces, covered with carved stories and topped by stupas.
sites.what_zh: 一座巨大的石造建築，像一座一層層的山，刻滿了故事浮雕，頂上是一座座佛塔。
sites.when_en: Built in the 8th and 9th centuries CE, under the Sailendra dynasty; Britannica gives about 778 to 850.
sites.when_zh: 建於西元八到九世紀，夏連特拉王朝的時候；Britannica 寫的是大約 778 到 850 年。
sites.how_en: The monument itself, which still stands.
sites.how_zh: 就是這座到今天還在的建築本身。

sites.what_en: The first Buddhist monastery in Tibet, founded under King Trisong Detsen. Teachers came from India to help.
sites.what_zh: 西藏第一座佛教寺院，在赤松德贊王的時候建立。有老師從印度來幫忙。
sites.when_en: Often given as 779 CE, when it was inaugurated. Other histories give 763 or 787–799.
sites.when_zh: 常見的年代是開光的西元 779 年。其他的史書寫 763 年，或 787 到 799 年。
sites.how_en: Tibetan histories written later, and Chinese records. Later Tibetan tradition also credits King Songtsen Gampo, in the 600s, with first bringing Buddhism.
sites.how_zh: 後來寫成的西藏史書，以及中國的紀錄。後來的西藏傳統也認為，600 年代的松贊干布王最先引進了佛教。

lab.numbers_note_en: Each place lights up in the year given on its card. That is the date of the earliest evidence, or the date a tradition gives, not the day Buddhism arrived. Most of these dates are approximate, and several are disputed.
lab.numbers_note_zh: 每一個地方在卡片上寫的那一年亮起來。那是最早的證據的年代，或是傳統說法的年代，不是佛教到達的那一天。這些年代大多是大約的，有好幾個還有爭論。
lab.scale_en: This is a teaching sketch. The routes show only the rough direction and order in which Buddhism spread, not the exact roads; teachers, traders, and pilgrims traveled many different ways. The map shows land only, with no modern borders.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意。路線只表示佛教傳播大致的方向和先後，不是確切的道路；老師、商人和朝聖者走過許多不同的路。地圖只畫陸地，不畫今天的國界。
lab.credit_html: Globe: land outlines from Natural Earth (public domain). Places and dates follow the sources listed at the bottom of the page. 地球儀：陸地外形取自 Natural Earth（公有領域）。地方和年代依本頁最下面列出的資料。

paras: About 2,400 to 2,500 years ago, in the plains of the Ganges River in northern India, a teacher named Siddhartha Gautama began to gather followers. They called him the Buddha, “the awakened one.” He taught that suffering has causes and that a path of ethical living, meditation, and wisdom can bring it to an end. Scholars do not agree on when he lived: an older view puts his life at about 560 to 480 BCE, while many now think he died around 400 BCE.

For centuries, the Buddha's teachings were not written down. Monks and nuns learned them by heart and recited them together. Sri Lankan tradition says the Pāli scriptures were first written down on the island in the 1st century BCE. The oldest Buddhist manuscripts we actually have, written on birch bark, come from Gandhara in today's Pakistan and date from about the 1st century BCE to the 3rd century CE.

The earliest datable written evidence for Buddhism comes from Ashoka, who ruled most of South Asia from about 270 to 232 BCE (some sources give 265 to 238). In one of his own edicts, he says he conquered the land of Kalinga, that 100,000 people were killed, and that he felt deep remorse. He had edicts carved on rocks and pillars across his empire, most in the Brahmi script and a few in other scripts and languages, including Greek and Aramaic. One edict speaks of his faith in the Buddha; another asks people to respect the followers of all religions.

From India, Buddhism traveled south and east by sea. Sri Lankan chronicles say Ashoka's son Mahinda brought it to the island in the 3rd century BCE. Later, ships carried monks and traders across the Bay of Bengal. In 671 CE the Chinese monk Yijing studied in Srivijaya, on Sumatra, before sailing on to India, and in the 8th and 9th centuries the great stone monument of Borobudur rose on Java.

Buddhism also traveled north and east over land. In Gandhara, artists carved some of the first images of the Buddha in human form in the 1st century CE. By 65 CE a Han prince in China was making offerings to the Buddha, and from about 148 CE, according to a later catalog of translations, monks such as An Shigao were translating texts into Chinese. Chinese pilgrims walked to India to find more: Xuanzang left in 629 and came home in 645 with 657 texts. The teaching reached Korea in the 4th century, Japan in the 6th, and Tibet in the 7th and 8th, according to each land's histories.

Each place made Buddhism its own, in its own language, art, and buildings. In India itself, Buddhism slowly declined, and the great monastery of Nalanda was sacked around 1200. Today about 324 million people, roughly 4 percent of the world, are counted as Buddhists, and almost all of them live in the Asia-Pacific region. The teaching traveled with monks, traders, pilgrims, and rulers who chose to support it, over about 1,500 years.
paras_zh: 大約兩千四、五百年前，在印度北部恆河的平原上，一位名叫悉達多・喬達摩的老師開始有了追隨者。他們稱他為「佛陀」，意思是「覺悟的人」。他教導：苦有它的原因，而一條包含正當的生活、禪修和智慧的道路，能讓苦止息。他生活在什麼年代，學者看法不一：比較早的看法是大約西元前 560 到 480 年，現在很多學者則認為他大約在西元前 400 年前後去世。
好幾百年裡，佛陀的教導沒有寫下來。比丘和比丘尼把它背起來，大家一起誦念。斯里蘭卡的傳統說，巴利文的經典在西元前一世紀第一次在島上寫成文字。我們手上真正有的最古老的佛教寫本，寫在樺樹皮上，來自今天巴基斯坦的犍陀羅，年代大約在西元前一世紀到西元三世紀之間。
佛教最早可確定年代的文字證據來自阿育王。他大約從西元前 270 年到 232 年統治南亞的大部分地方（也有資料寫西元前 265 到 238 年）。在他自己的一篇詔令裡，他說他征服了羯陵伽，有十萬人被殺，他深深地懊悔。他在帝國各地的岩石和石柱上刻下詔令，大多用婆羅米文字，也有少數用其他文字和語言，包括希臘文和亞蘭文。有一篇詔令說到他對佛陀的信心；另一篇則要人尊重所有宗教的信徒。
佛教從印度出發，走海路往南、往東傳。斯里蘭卡的編年史說，阿育王的兒子摩哂陀在西元前三世紀把佛教帶到島上。後來，船隻載著僧人和商人橫越孟加拉灣。西元 671 年，中國僧人義淨在前往印度以前，先在蘇門答臘的室利佛逝學習；八到九世紀，巨大的石造建築婆羅浮屠在爪哇蓋了起來。
佛教也走陸路往北、往東傳。在犍陀羅，藝術家在西元一世紀刻出了最早的一批人形佛像。到了西元 65 年，中國漢朝的一位王子已經在供養佛陀；依後來的譯經目錄，從大約西元 148 年起，安世高等僧人開始把經典翻成中文。中國的朝聖者走路到印度去找更多的經典：玄奘在 629 年出發，645 年帶著 657 部經論回來。依照各地自己的史書，佛教在四世紀傳到朝鮮半島，六世紀傳到日本，七、八世紀傳到西藏。
每一個地方，都用自己的語言、藝術和建築，把佛教變成自己的。在印度本地，佛教慢慢衰落，偉大的那爛陀寺大約在 1200 年遭到洗劫。今天，大約有 3 億 2,400 萬人被算作佛教徒，大約是全世界的百分之四，幾乎全部住在亞洲及太平洋地區。這個教法跟著僧人、商人、朝聖者，以及選擇支持它的國王，旅行了大約一千五百年。
questions: Why do we have to say “about” when we give the Buddha's dates?
Name one way Buddhism traveled by sea and one way it traveled over land.
What is the difference between a date that tradition gives and a date that evidence shows? Give one example of each.
answers: The teachings were passed on by memory for centuries, and the written sources give different dates, so scholars disagree. An older view is about 560–480 BCE; many now think he died around 400 BCE.

By sea: to Sri Lanka, and across the Bay of Bengal to Southeast Asia, where Yijing studied in Srivijaya. Over land: through Gandhara and Central Asia to China, then on to Korea and Japan, partly by sea; also over the mountains to Tibet.

A traditional date comes from a story written down much later, such as Mahinda reaching Sri Lanka or Buddhism reaching Japan in 552. Evidence comes from close to the time, such as Ashoka's pillar at Lumbini or the Han edict of 65 CE.

vocab.ex: Buddhists believe the Buddha awakened under a tree.
vocab.exzh: 佛教徒相信佛陀在一棵樹下覺悟。

vocab.ex: Monks carried the Buddha's teaching to new lands.
vocab.exzh: 僧人把佛陀的教法帶到新的地方。

vocab.ex: A monk from Parthia translated texts in Luoyang.
vocab.exzh: 一位從安息來的僧人在洛陽翻譯經典。

vocab.ex: Nalanda was a huge monastery where people studied.
vocab.exzh: 那爛陀是一座很大的寺院，大家在那裡求學。

vocab.ex: The pilgrim walked all the way to India.
vocab.exzh: 那位朝聖者一路走到印度。

vocab.ex: Kumārajīva translated many sutras into Chinese.
vocab.exzh: 鳩摩羅什把許多經典翻成中文。

vocab.ex: The inscription on the pillar names the Buddha.
vocab.exzh: 石柱上的銘文提到了佛陀。

vocab.ex: Tradition says Mahinda brought Buddhism to Sri Lanka.
vocab.exzh: 傳統上說，摩哂陀把佛教帶到斯里蘭卡。

quiz.q: Where did Buddhism begin?
What does “Buddha” mean?
Who left the earliest written evidence for Buddhism, on rocks and pillars?
How were the Buddha's teachings passed on for the first few centuries?
options: On paper made by Cai Lun

quiz.q: Which Chinese pilgrim left for India in 629 and came home in 645?

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Two gold dots in northern India: Bodh Gaya and Sarnath. Both are dated by tradition, because the Buddha's dates are uncertain.
parts.text_zh: 印度北部有兩個金色的點：菩提伽耶和鹿野苑。兩個都是傳統說法的年代，因為佛陀的年代不確定。

parts.text_en: Now white dots appear at Lumbini and Sanchi. These are the first places dated by evidence: inscriptions and buildings from Ashoka's time.
parts.text_zh: 這時候藍毘尼和桑奇出現了白色的點。這是最早有證據的地方：阿育王時代的銘文和建築。

parts.text_en: The blue line has reached Sri Lanka and is crossing the Bay of Bengal. Look for Anuradhapura and read why its date is tradition.
parts.text_zh: 藍色的線已經到了斯里蘭卡，正在橫越孟加拉灣。找找阿努拉德普勒，讀讀為什麼它的年代是傳統的說法。

parts.text_en: By 700, the gold lines have crossed Central Asia to China and Korea, short sea crossings have reached Japan, and the dashed line is climbing toward Tibet.
parts.text_zh: 到了 700 年，金色的線已經越過中亞，到了中國和朝鮮半島，短短的海路也到了日本，虛線也正往西藏爬上去。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then drag the slider back and forth. Which dots appear first: the gold ones or the white ones? What does that tell you about how much we know about the earliest years?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著把滑桿拉來拉去。哪一種點先出現：金色的還是白色的？這告訴我們，對最早的那幾百年，我們知道得有多少？

terms.lead_en: Buddhist words traveled with the teaching. Pāli is the language of the Theravāda scriptures, Sanskrit was used by many other schools, and Chinese translators found their own words. For each Chinese term, pick its Pāli or Sanskrit form and an English meaning. There is no timer.
terms.lead_zh: 佛教的詞語跟著教法一起旅行。巴利文是南傳上座部經典的語言，很多其他的部派用梵文，中文的譯經師則找出了自己的譯詞。每一個中文詞，選出它的巴利文或梵文，以及英文的意思。不計時。
terms.ask_en: Which is its Pāli or Sanskrit form and English meaning?
terms.ask_zh: 它的巴利文或梵文、英文是哪一個？

items.note_en: Buddha is a title, not a name. It comes from a word meaning “to wake up.” The Chinese 佛陀 imitates the sound.
items.note_zh: 「佛陀」是稱號，不是名字，來自意思是「醒過來」的字。中文的「佛陀」是音譯。

items.note_en: Dhamma has many meanings; here it means the Buddha's teaching. Ashoka used the same word in his edicts for a broad way of right living.
items.note_zh: dhamma 的意思很多，這裡指佛陀的教法。阿育王在詔令裡也用這個字，指更廣的正當生活之道。

items.en: the community of monks and nuns
items.note_en: Buddha, dhamma, and saṅgha are called the Three Jewels. Ashoka's edict at Bairat names all three.
items.note_zh: 佛、法、僧合稱「三寶」。阿育王在拜拉特（Bairat）的詔令，三個都提到了。

items.en: blowing out; the end of suffering
items.note_en: The word literally means a flame going out. Buddhists use it for the end of greed, hatred, and delusion.
items.note_zh: 這個字原本的意思是火焰熄滅。佛教用它來指貪、瞋、癡的止息。

items.note_en: Karma means action, especially action done on purpose. The English word “karma” comes from the Sanskrit form.
items.note_zh: 業的意思是行為，特別是有意的行為。英文的 karma 就是從梵文借來的。

items.note_en: Translators disagree about the best English word. “Suffering” is common; some prefer “unsatisfactoriness” or “stress.”
items.note_zh: 翻譯的人對最好的英文說法看法不一。suffering 最常見；也有人用 unsatisfactoriness 或 stress。

items.note_en: The teaching that nothing in body or mind is a permanent, unchanging self.
items.note_zh: 這個教法說：身體和心裡，沒有任何東西是永遠不變的「我」。

items.note_en: The great stupa at Sanchi is one. When the form reached East Asia, it often grew into a tall pagoda.
items.note_zh: 桑奇的大佛塔就是一座。這種建築傳到東亞以後，常常變成高高的寶塔。

items.note_en: Before his awakening, the Buddha was called a bodhisatta. Mahāyāna Buddhism, which spread across East Asia, teaches that the bodhisattva path is open to all.
items.note_zh: 佛陀在覺悟以前被稱為菩薩。傳遍東亞的大乘佛教教導：菩薩道是每個人都可以走的路。

items.note_en: Monks, and nuns (bhikkhunī, 比丘尼), carried the teaching from place to place. The Chinese 比丘 imitates the sound.
items.note_zh: 比丘和比丘尼（bhikkhunī）把教法從一個地方帶到另一個地方。中文的「比丘」是音譯。

terms.end_en: Some Chinese terms imitate the sound (佛陀, 比丘, 菩薩), while others translate the meaning (法, 業, 苦, 無我). Translators chose between the two again and again.
terms.end_zh: 有些中文譯詞是模仿聲音的音譯（佛陀、比丘、菩薩），有些是翻出意思的意譯（法、業、苦、無我）。譯經師一次又一次在兩者之間做選擇。

legend.lead_en: Historians ask two questions about every story: what does it say, and how close in time is the source? For each statement, decide whether it comes from a later tradition or from evidence close to the time. There is no timer.
legend.lead_zh: 歷史學家對每一個故事都問兩個問題：它說了什麼？資料離那件事的時間有多近？每一題判斷：這是後來的傳統說法，還是離那個時代很近的證據？不計時。

items.en: Ashoka was sorry for the many people killed when he conquered Kalinga.
items.zh: 阿育王為征服羯陵伽時死了很多人而懊悔。
items.why_en: Ashoka says so himself, in a rock edict carved in his own reign.
items.why_zh: 阿育王自己這樣說，刻在他在位時的岩石詔令裡。
items.hint_en: Who wrote it, and when?
items.hint_zh: 是誰寫的？什麼時候寫的？

items.en: Emperor Ming of Han dreamed of a golden man and sent envoys west to ask about the Buddha.
items.zh: 漢明帝夢見金人，派使者往西去問佛的道理。
items.why_en: The History of the Later Han introduces it with “it is passed down that…,” and the story appears only in later sources.
items.why_zh: 《後漢書》用「世傳」兩個字開頭，這個故事只出現在比較晚的資料裡。
items.hint_en: Look at the words the History uses to begin the story.
items.hint_zh: 看看史書用什麼字開頭。

items.en: Liu Ying, King of Chu, held Buddhist fasts and offerings.
items.zh: 楚王劉英為佛陀齋戒、供養。
items.why_en: The History of the Later Han quotes the emperor's own edict of 65 CE, which praises the king for honoring the Buddha's “humane shrines.”
items.why_zh: 《後漢書》引了西元 65 年皇帝自己下的詔書，稱讚楚王「尚浮屠之仁祠」。
items.hint_en: There is a document from the time.
items.hint_zh: 有當時的文件。

items.en: Ashoka's son Mahinda brought Buddhism to Sri Lanka.
items.zh: 阿育王的兒子摩哂陀把佛教帶到斯里蘭卡。
items.why_en: This comes from the Sri Lankan chronicles, written several centuries later. Ashoka's own edicts do not name Mahinda.
items.why_zh: 這來自斯里蘭卡的編年史，是好幾百年後寫的。阿育王自己的詔令沒有提到摩哂陀。
items.hint_en: When were the chronicles written?
items.hint_zh: 編年史是什麼時候寫的？

items.en: Buddhist texts were written on birch bark in Gandhara about two thousand years ago.
items.zh: 大約兩千年前，犍陀羅有人把佛經寫在樺樹皮上。
items.why_en: The scrolls themselves survive, dated to about the 1st century BCE to the 3rd century CE.
items.why_zh: 這些卷子本身留下來了，年代大約在西元前一世紀到西元三世紀之間。
items.hint_en: Can you hold it in your hands?
items.hint_zh: 拿得到實物嗎？

items.zh: 佛教在西元 552 年傳到日本。
items.why_en: The date comes from the Chronicles of Japan, finished in 720; another old record gives 538. No object fixes either date.
items.why_zh: 這個年代來自 720 年完成的《日本書紀》；另一份古老的紀錄寫 538 年。沒有實物能確定哪一個對。
items.hint_en: Two old books give two different years.
items.hint_zh: 兩本古書寫了兩個不同的年份。

items.en: The pilgrim Xuanzang brought 657 texts back to Chang'an in 645 CE.
items.zh: 朝聖者玄奘在西元 645 年帶了 657 部經論回到長安。
items.why_en: The preface to Xuanzang's own Record of the Western Regions, written by a court official of his time, gives the number.
items.why_zh: 玄奘自己的《大唐西域記》，前面有一篇同時代官員寫的序，記了這個數字。
items.hint_en: It was written down in his own lifetime.
items.hint_zh: 在他活著的時候就寫下來了。

items.en: When the Silla official Ichadon was executed, white blood flowed.
items.zh: 新羅的異次頓被處死的時候，流出了白色的血。
items.why_en: The History of the Three Kingdoms tells this story about 600 years later, saying the white blood made the court stop opposing the teaching.
items.why_zh: 《三國史記》在大約六百年後講這個故事，說這件事讓朝廷不再反對佛教。
items.hint_en: Ask whether it could happen, and how late the source is.
items.hint_zh: 想想這有可能發生嗎？資料又有多晚？

legend.end_en: “Tradition” does not mean false, and “evidence” does not mean the whole story. A tradition tells us what later believers remembered and cared about; evidence close to the time lets us check the dates.
legend.end_zh: 「傳統說法」不等於假的，「證據」也不等於完整的故事。傳統說法告訴我們後來的信徒記得什麼、在乎什麼；離那個時代很近的證據，讓我們能查核年代。

timeline.lead_en: Buddhism's story runs in the South Asia and East Asia lanes. Notice how long it took to travel, and that Buddhism reached China while the Han and Rome were both still standing.
timeline.lead_zh: 佛教的故事在南亞和東亞兩條線上。注意它旅行了多久，也注意佛教傳到中國的時候，漢朝和羅馬都還在。
timeline.idle_en: Click a bar or a diamond to read its dates.
timeline.idle_zh: 點一條長條或一個菱形，讀出它的年代。

tips.en: The Buddha's life is a striped bar, because scholars give very different dates.
tips.zh: 佛陀的一生是一條有條紋的長條，因為學者給的年代差很多。

tips.en: Ashoka's reign is striped too: sources give about 273 or about 265 BCE for its start.
tips.zh: 阿育王在位也有條紋：各資料說的開始年代，大約是西元前 273 年或 265 年。

tips.en: The gray diamonds mark single events, such as the Han edict of 65 CE.
tips.zh: 灰色的菱形標的是單一事件，例如西元 65 年漢朝的詔書。

events.note_en: An older view: about 560–480 BCE. Many scholars now: died around 400 BCE.
events.note_zh: 比較早的看法：大約西元前 560–480 年。現在很多學者：大約西元前 400 年前後去世。

events.note_en: About 273–232 BCE, or about 265–238 BCE.
events.note_zh: 大約西元前 273–232 年，或大約西元前 265–238 年。

events.note_en: Founded in the 5th century CE; sacked around 1200.
events.note_zh: 西元五世紀建立；大約 1200 年遭到洗劫。

events.note_en: Lesson 7. Buddhism arrived during the Han.
events.note_zh: 第七課。佛教在漢朝的時候傳進來。

events.en: A Han prince honors the Buddha
events.note_en: The earliest reliable mention of Buddhism in China.
events.note_zh: 中國最早可靠的佛教記載。

events.note_en: He came home with 657 texts.
events.note_zh: 帶回 657 部經論。

events.note_en: Two traditions: 538 or 552 CE.
events.note_zh: 兩種傳統說法：西元 538 年或 552 年。

events.note_en: Lesson 6.
events.note_zh: 第六課。

how_we_know.eyebrow: How Do We Know? · 我們怎麼知道？
how_we_know.en: Stones, birch bark, and travelers' notes
how_we_know.zh: 石頭、樺樹皮和旅人的筆記
how_we_know.lead_en: The earliest Buddhist teachings were memorized, not written, so historians have to look hard for evidence.
how_we_know.lead_zh: 最早的佛教教導是背下來的，不是寫下來的，所以歷史學家得很用心地找證據。

items.limit_en: The edicts tell us what Ashoka wanted people to read. They do not tell us how ordinary people lived or what they believed.
items.limit_zh: 詔令告訴我們阿育王希望人們讀到什麼，卻沒有告訴我們一般人怎麼生活、相信什麼。
items.src: Dhammika, The Edicts of King Asoka
items.text_en: Ashoka's edicts survive on rocks and pillars across South Asia, most in the Brahmi script. They tell us about his conquest of Kalinga, his regret, and his ideas of right living, in his own words.
items.text_zh: 阿育王的詔令留在南亞各地的岩石和石柱上，大多用婆羅米文字寫成。它們用他自己的話，告訴我們他征服羯陵伽、他的懊悔，以及他對正當生活的想法。

items.limit_en: They are fragile pieces, often broken, and were written centuries after the Buddha. They show which texts existed, not exactly what he said.
items.limit_zh: 它們是很脆弱的碎片，常常是斷的，而且是佛陀之後好幾百年才寫的。它們告訴我們當時有哪些經典，卻不能確定佛陀確切說了什麼。
items.src: NEH, “Early Buddhist Manuscripts”
items.text_en: Birch-bark scrolls in the Gāndhārī language, written in the Kharoṣṭhī script, are the oldest Buddhist manuscripts known. The British Library acquired several in 1994.
items.text_zh: 用犍陀羅語、佉盧文寫的樺樹皮卷子，是目前所知最古老的佛教寫本。大英圖書館在 1994 年購得了好幾卷。

items.limit_en: Pilgrims wrote as believers, looking for holy places, and they sometimes repeated local legends as fact. Even Faxian's own dates do not quite agree with each other.
items.limit_zh: 朝聖者是以信徒的身分寫的，一路在找聖地，有時也把當地的傳說當成事實記下來。連法顯自己記的年代，彼此都對不太起來。
items.src: 《大唐西域記》；法顯《佛國記》
items.text_en: Chinese pilgrims wrote down what they saw on the way to India. Faxian left around 399–400; Xuanzang traveled from 629 to 645 and described more than a hundred places in his Record of the Western Regions.
items.text_zh: 中國的朝聖者把去印度路上看到的寫了下來。法顯大約在 399 到 400 年出發；玄奘從 629 年走到 645 年，在《大唐西域記》裡描述了一百多個地方。

views.en: Four questions about Buddhism's early history
views.zh: 關於佛教早期歷史的四個問題
views.lead_en: Believers, scholars, and old books do not always agree. Here are four questions, with the views set side by side.
views.lead_zh: 信徒、學者和古書，說法不一定一樣。下面是四個問題，各種說法並列。
views.rule_en: Notice that these disagreements are about dates and evidence, not about whether Buddhism is right or wrong. History cannot answer that question.
views.rule_zh: 留意這些分歧是關於年代和證據，不是關於佛教對不對。那個問題，歷史回答不了。

items.topic_en: When did the Buddha live?
items.topic_zh: 佛陀生活在什麼年代？

sides.en: The traditional dates in Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia are 623–543 BCE. UNESCO's page on Lumbini uses 623 BCE for his birth.
sides.zh: 斯里蘭卡和東南亞傳統的年代是西元前 623–543 年。聯合國教科文組織的藍毘尼網頁，用的就是西元前 623 年出生。

sides.en: For a long time, scholars dated his life to about 560–480 BCE. Taiwan's Ministry of Education dictionary still gives 566 BCE for his birth.
sides.zh: 很長一段時間，學者把他的一生定在大約西元前 560–480 年。台灣教育部的《重編國語辭典》到今天還寫西元前 566 年出生。
sides.src: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “The Buddha”; 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》

sides.en: After the papers of a 1988 conference in Göttingen were published (1991–92), many scholars place his death around 400 BCE, though they still disagree by decades.
sides.zh: 1988 年在哥廷根的研討會，論文集在 1991–92 年出版以後，很多學者把他的去世定在大約西元前 400 年，不過彼此還是差了幾十年。

items.note_en: This lesson says “about 2,400 to 2,500 years ago” so that it fits the main scholarly views. The early sources were memorized, so no single date can be proved.
items.note_zh: 這一課寫「大約兩千四、五百年前」，好讓它符合主要的學術看法。早期的資料是背下來的，所以沒有一個年代能被證明。

items.topic_en: Was Ashoka a “Buddhist king”?
items.topic_zh: 阿育王是「佛教的國王」嗎？

sides.en: In an edict found at Bairat, Ashoka tells the monks how great his faith in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha is.
sides.zh: 在拜拉特發現的一篇詔令裡，阿育王告訴僧人，他對佛、法、僧的信心有多大。
sides.src: Dhammika, The Edicts of King Asoka

sides.en: Britannica notes that in his public edicts Ashoka spoke of no particular creed; another edict asks people to respect all religions. A 2024 book presents him as a ruler, a Buddhist, a moral philosopher, and someone who reached across religions.
sides.zh: Britannica 指出，阿育王在公開的詔令裡沒有提倡某一種教義；另一篇詔令要人尊重所有的宗教。2024 年的一本書把他描寫成一位統治者、一位佛教徒、一位道德哲學家，也是一位跨越宗教的人。
sides.src: Britannica, “Ashoka”; Olivelle, Ashoka: Portrait of a Philosopher King (2024)

items.note_en: Both can be true: he could be a Buddhist himself and still speak to all his people in broader terms.
items.note_zh: 兩者可能都對：他自己可以是佛教徒，同時用更廣的話對所有的人民說話。

items.topic_en: Where was the first image of the Buddha made?
items.topic_zh: 第一尊佛像是在哪裡做的？

sides.en: In the 1st century CE, one of the first places to show the Buddha in human form was India's northwestern frontier, in Gandhara.
sides.zh: 西元一世紀，最早把佛陀做成人形的地方之一，是印度西北邊境的犍陀羅。
sides.src: Metropolitan Museum of Art, “Buddhism and Buddhist Art” (2007)

sides.en: At about the same time, artists in Mathura, in north India, made a different-looking Buddha image.
sides.zh: 差不多同時，印度北部秣菟羅的藝術家，做出了樣子不一樣的佛像。
sides.src: Metropolitan Museum of Art, “Buddhism and Buddhist Art” (2007)

items.note_en: Scholars still debate which came first. Before that, for centuries, artists showed the Buddha only through symbols such as footprints or an empty seat.
items.note_zh: 學者還在討論哪一邊比較早。在那之前的好幾百年，藝術家只用腳印、空的座位這類象徵來表現佛陀。

items.topic_en: When did Buddhism reach Japan?
items.topic_zh: 佛教什麼時候傳到日本？

sides.en: The Chronicles of Japan, finished in 720, say that the king of Baekje sent a gilt-bronze Buddha and sutras in the 13th year of Emperor Kinmei, 552 CE.
sides.zh: 720 年完成的《日本書紀》說，欽明天皇十三年（西元 552 年），百濟的聖明王送來金銅的釋迦佛像和經論。

sides.en: Other old records give 538 CE for the same gift. Britannica gives both years: “in 538 or 552.”
sides.zh: 另外一些古老的紀錄，把同一份禮物記在西元 538 年。Britannica 兩個年份都寫：「538 年或 552 年」。

items.note_en: Both dates come from texts written long afterward. Either way, Buddhism reached Japan from Korea, and Japan's oldest temples were built soon after.
items.note_zh: 兩個年代都來自很久以後寫的書。不管哪一個，佛教都是從朝鮮半島傳到日本，日本最古老的寺院也在不久以後蓋了起來。

phrases.en: Eight sentences for telling how ideas travel
phrases.zh: 說「想法怎麼旅行」的八句英文
phrases.lead_en: These sentences help you describe how a teaching spread, and how sure we are. Listen, repeat, then make your own sentence with the words in bold.
phrases.lead_zh: 這八句幫你描述一個教法怎麼傳出去，以及我們有多確定。先聽、再跟著唸，然後用粗體的字自己造一句。

rows.en: Buddhism spread from India to many parts of Asia.
rows.html: Buddhism spread from India to many parts of Asia.
rows.zh: 佛教從印度傳到亞洲的許多地方。
rows.note_en: spread: moved out to more and more places

rows.en: Monks traveled along the trade routes.
rows.html: Monks traveled along the trade routes.
rows.zh: 僧人沿著貿易路線旅行。
rows.note_en: along: following a road, river, or route

rows.en: The teaching reached China by the first century CE.
rows.html: The teaching reached China by the first century CE.
rows.zh: 這個教法在西元一世紀以前就傳到了中國。
rows.note_en: reached: arrived at a place

rows.en: The sutras were carried by pilgrims and traders.
rows.html: The sutras were carried by pilgrims and traders.
rows.zh: 經典是由朝聖者和商人帶過去的。
rows.note_en: were carried by: tells who moved something

rows.en: Kumārajīva translated the sutras into Chinese.
rows.html: Kumārajīva translated the sutras into Chinese.
rows.zh: 鳩摩羅什把經典翻成中文。
rows.note_en: translate … into …: from one language to another

rows.en: According to the chronicles, Mahinda went to Sri Lanka.
rows.html: According to the chronicles, Mahinda went to Sri Lanka.
rows.zh: 依照編年史的說法，摩哂陀去了斯里蘭卡。
rows.note_en: according to: shows where a claim comes from

rows.en: Tradition says the Buddha was born at Lumbini.
rows.html: Tradition says the Buddha was born at Lumbini.
rows.zh: 傳統上說，佛陀在藍毘尼出生。
rows.note_en: tradition says: a belief handed down over time

rows.en: The pillar shows that Ashoka visited Lumbini.
rows.html: The pillar shows that Ashoka visited Lumbini.
rows.zh: 這根石柱說明阿育王到過藍毘尼。
rows.note_en: shows that: evidence supports a claim

taiwan_then.eyebrow: Taiwan at That Time · 那時候的台灣
taiwan_then.en: Far from the routes, for a long time
taiwan_then.zh: 離路線很遠，很長一段時間
taiwan_then.lead_en: When Buddhism reached China, about 2,000 years ago, Taiwan was home to several prehistoric cultures. The first Buddhist temples we know of in the records came about 1,600 years later.
taiwan_then.lead_zh: 佛教傳到中國的時候，大約距今兩千年，台灣有好幾個史前文化。紀錄裡最早的佛寺，要再過大約一千六百年才出現。
taiwan_then.intro_en: Archaeologists in Taiwan give dates as “years ago.” About 2,000 years ago is roughly the time of the Han edict of 65 CE.
taiwan_then.intro_zh: 台灣的考古學家用「距今幾年」說年代。距今大約兩千年，差不多就是西元 65 年漢朝那道詔書的時候。

facts.en: Around 2,000 years ago, the Shisanhang culture rose in the Taipei Basin area.
facts.zh: 大約二千年前，十三行文化在臺北盆地附近興起。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

facts.en: Around the same time, the Fengbitou culture in the south ended after about 1,500 years, and the Beinan culture in the east was passing the end of its peak, about 3,500 to 2,000 years ago.
facts.zh: 差不多同時，南部的鳳鼻頭文化（距今約三千五百到二千年前）結束；東部卑南文化極盛的年代（大約三千五百到二千年前）也在這時告一段落。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

facts.en: Buddhist temples in Taiwan appear in the records only in the 17th century. The district office in Tainan says Zhuxi Temple was founded between 1665 and 1672.
facts.zh: 台灣的佛寺要到十七世紀才出現在紀錄裡。臺南市南區區公所說，竹溪寺「創建於明永曆19年(1665)至26年(1672)間」。
facts.src: 臺南市南區區公所

facts.en: Zheng Jing built a garden residence in Tainan in 1680; in 1690 it was rebuilt as a temple. Today it is a national monument. Other sources give slightly different years.
facts.zh: 鄭經在 1680 年於臺南建了「北園別館」；1690 年改建成寺院。今天它是國定古蹟。其他資料寫的年份稍有不同。
facts.src: 內政部 臺灣宗教文化地圖「開元寺」

links.en: Taiwan's Story, Lesson 2: Who Lived in Taiwan Thousands of Years Ago?
links.zh: 台灣歷史第二課：幾千年前，誰住在台灣？

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Evidence · 證據背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A king's regret, four lions, a hidden library, and 657 texts
culture_cards.title_zh: 一個國王的懊悔、四隻獅子、一個藏起來的圖書館，和 657 部經論
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about the objects and journeys that tell Buddhism's history.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事：告訴我們佛教歷史的那些器物和旅程。

cards.en: A king who said he was sorry
cards.body_en: Ashoka's thirteenth rock edict counts the cost of his war: 150,000 people taken away, 100,000 killed, and many more who died. Then he writes that he feels deep remorse, and that the best conquest is conquest by Dhamma. It is a rare thing to find in a royal inscription.
cards.body_zh: 阿育王的第十三篇岩石詔令，算出了這場戰爭的代價：十五萬人被帶走，十萬人被殺，還有更多人死去。接著他寫道，他深深懊悔，而最好的征服，是用「法」來征服。在國王的銘文裡，這是很少見的。

cards.body_en: Ashoka set up a pillar at Sarnath, where tradition says the Buddha first taught. On top, four lions sit back to back. That Lion Capital, now in the museum at Sarnath, is the basis of India's state emblem today.
cards.body_zh: 阿育王在傳統上說佛陀第一次說法的鹿野苑，立了一根石柱。柱頂是四隻背靠背坐著的獅子。這個獅子柱頭現在放在鹿野苑的博物館，也是今天印度國徽的根據。

cards.body_en: In 1900, a small cave at Mogao was found sealed behind a wall. Inside were tens of thousands of manuscripts and paintings, many of them Buddhist texts, in several languages.
cards.body_zh: 1900 年，莫高窟有一個小石窟被發現封在一道牆後面。裡面有好幾萬件寫本和畫，很多是佛經，用了好幾種語言。

cards.k: 629–645 CE · Chang'an to India · 長安到印度
cards.body_en: Xuanzang left Chang'an in 629 and returned in 645 with 657 Buddhist texts. He spent the rest of his life translating them, and his travel record is still used by archaeologists to find ancient sites in India.
cards.body_zh: 玄奘在 629 年離開長安，645 年帶著 657 部佛教經論回來。他用後半生翻譯它們，他的遊記到今天還被考古學家拿來尋找印度的古代遺址。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum for social studies (October 2018).
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要社會領域（民國 107 年 10 月）。

items.area: 國中・世界史
items.area_en: Junior high · world history
items.text: 佛教的起源與發展。
items.note_en: The explanation suggests discussing the origin and spread of Buddhism without too much detail, focusing on how world religions shaped cultures and the map of the world. That is the focus of this lesson.
items.note_zh: 課綱的說明建議討論「佛教的起源與傳播」，「不必詳敘細節，重點在討論普世宗教所形塑的文化樣貌及世界版圖」。這正是這一課的重點。

items.area: 國中・從古典到傳統時代
items.area_en: Junior high · from the classical to the traditional age
items.text: 商周至隋唐時期民族與文化的互動。
items.note_en: The explanation asks about exchanges among peoples in religion, customs, and thought. Buddhism's arrival in Han and Tang China is one of the biggest examples.
items.note_zh: 課綱的說明談不同民族在「宗教禮俗、飲食服飾、生活方式或學術思想上有哪些重要的特色與交流」。佛教傳入漢唐，是其中最大的例子之一。

myths.myth_en: Buddhists believe the Buddha is a god.
myths.myth_zh: 佛教徒相信佛陀是神。
myths.fact_en: In an early sutra (AN 4.36), a brahmin asks the Buddha whether he is a god, a spirit, or a human. The Buddha says he is none of these and asks to be remembered as a Buddha, “one who is awake.” Buddhist traditions differ in how they honor him.
myths.fact_zh: 在一部早期的經典（AN 4.36）裡，有位婆羅門問佛陀是不是神、是精靈，還是人。佛陀回答都不是，請他記住自己是「佛陀」，也就是覺醒的人。各個佛教傳統禮敬他的方式不一樣。

myths.myth_en: Buddhism began in China.
myths.myth_zh: 佛教是從中國開始的。
myths.fact_en: Buddhism began in northern India. The earliest reliable record of it in China is from 65 CE, centuries after Ashoka's edicts.
myths.fact_zh: 佛教從印度北部開始。中國最早可靠的佛教記載是西元 65 年，比阿育王的詔令晚了好幾百年。

myths.myth_en: There have always been statues of the Buddha.
myths.myth_zh: 一直都有佛像。
myths.fact_en: For centuries, artists showed the Buddha only through symbols such as footprints, an empty seat, or a tree. Images in human form appear in the 1st century CE.
myths.fact_zh: 好幾百年裡，藝術家只用腳印、空的座位或一棵樹這類象徵來表現佛陀。人形的佛像到西元一世紀才出現。

myths.myth_en: All Buddhists are vegetarian.
myths.myth_zh: 所有的佛教徒都吃素。
myths.fact_en: An early Pāli sutra lets monks eat meat they did not see, hear, or suspect was killed for them. In China, Emperor Wu of Liang ordered monks and nuns to give up meat and alcohol, around 519–523 CE. Practice still differs from place to place.
myths.fact_zh: 一部早期的巴利文經典說，僧人可以吃沒有看到、聽到或懷疑是為他們而殺的肉。在中國，梁武帝大約在西元 519 到 523 年之間，要求僧尼斷酒肉。各地的做法到今天還是不一樣。

tricks.body_en: The teachings were recited for centuries before anyone wrote them down.
tricks.body_zh: 教法誦念了好幾百年，才有人把它寫下來。

tricks.title_en: Ashoka's stones are the first datable proof
tricks.title_zh: 阿育王的石頭是最早可確定年代的證據
tricks.body_en: Edicts on rocks and pillars, from the 3rd century BCE.
tricks.body_zh: 西元前三世紀，刻在岩石和石柱上的詔令。

tricks.title_en: South by sea, north by land
tricks.body_en: Ships to Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia; roads to Central Asia and China, then on to Korea and Japan, partly by sea.
tricks.body_zh: 船到斯里蘭卡和東南亞；路到中亞和中國，再到朝鮮半島和日本，有一段要渡海。

tricks.body_en: Always ask where a date comes from.
tricks.body_zh: 每一個年代，都要問它從哪裡來。

materials.en: A short teaching of four lines, written on one card
materials.zh: 一張卡片，上面寫四行短短的教導

materials.en: Paper and pencils for each team
materials.zh: 每一組紙和鉛筆

steps.en: Divide the class into two teams. Show the card only to the first student in each team.
steps.zh: 把全班分成兩組。卡片只給每一組的第一個學生看。

steps.en: Team A whispers the lines from student to student, one at a time. Team B recites them together, out loud, as a group, each time someone new joins.
steps.zh: A 組一個傳一個地悄悄說。B 組則是每加入一個人，大家就一起大聲誦念一次。

steps.en: At the end, both teams write down what they heard. Compare with the card.
steps.zh: 最後，兩組都把聽到的寫下來，和卡片比一比。

steps.en: Discuss in English: “Reciting together helps because …” and “Writing it down helps because …”
steps.zh: 用英文討論：「Reciting together helps because …」和「Writing it down helps because …」

activities.tip_en: Early monks recited the teachings together, which helps explain how they were kept for centuries without writing. The game also shows why historians still ask how much changed.
activities.tip_zh: 早期的僧人一起誦念教法，這有助於說明為什麼沒有文字也能保存好幾百年。這個遊戲也說明了，為什麼歷史學家還是會問：中間改變了多少？

materials.en: The 3D globe in this lesson
materials.zh: 這一課的 3D 地球儀

materials.en: A worksheet with three columns: Place, Date, How do we know?
materials.zh: 一張學習單，分三欄：地方、年代、我們怎麼知道？

steps.en: In pairs, choose six places on the globe and read their cards.
steps.zh: 兩人一組，在地球儀上選六個地方，讀它們的卡片。

steps.en: Fill in the three columns. Mark each date T (tradition) or E (evidence).
steps.zh: 填寫三欄。每個年代標上 T（傳統說法）或 E（證據）。

steps.en: Find the place whose source is furthest in time from the event. How many years apart?
steps.zh: 找出資料和那件事相隔最久的地方。差了幾年？

steps.en: Write one sentence with “According to …” and one with “… shows that …”.
steps.zh: 用 According to … 寫一句，再用 … shows that … 寫一句。

activities.tip_en: Remind students that a traditional date is not “wrong.” It is a different kind of source, and it tells us what later people believed.
activities.tip_zh: 提醒學生：傳統說法的年代不是「錯的」。它是另一種資料，告訴我們後來的人相信什麼。

links.en: What Traveled Along the Silk Road?
links.zh: 絲路上走的是什麼？
links.note_en: Buddhism was one of many things that moved along the roads between China and the west.
links.note_zh: 佛教只是在中國和西方之間的路上流動的許多東西之一。

links.en: How Did Qin and Han Unite China?
links.zh: 秦和漢怎麼統一中國？
links.note_en: The Han empire, where Buddhism first arrived in China.
links.note_zh: 漢朝，佛教最早傳進中國的時候。

links.k_zh: 哲學・佛法與西方哲學
links.en: The Four Noble Truths as an Argument
links.zh: 四聖諦作為一個論證
links.note_en: What the Buddha taught, step by step.
links.note_zh: 佛陀教了什麼，一步一步看。

links.k_zh: 哲學・佛法與西方哲學
links.en: No-Self and the West
links.zh: 無我與西方哲學
links.note_en: The teaching of anattā, compared with Western ideas of the self.
links.note_zh: 無我的教法，和西方對「自我」的想法比較。

links.en: Why Do People Copy Sutras by Hand?
links.zh: 抄經：書法與修行
links.note_en: How translated sutras were copied in China.
links.note_zh: 翻成中文的經典，在中國怎麼被抄寫。

lessons.sources_note_en: Checked November 2026. The dates of the Buddha, of Ashoka, of Faxian's journey, and of Buddhism's arrival in Japan and Tibet differ between sources; where they do, the lesson gives more than one
lessons.sources_note_zh: 2026 年 11 月查證。佛陀、阿育王、法顯的旅程，以及佛教傳到日本和西藏的年代，各資料說法不一；遇到不一致時，課文寫出不只一種

sources.en: The Buddha's dates: about 560–480 BCE (older view); death around 405 BCE (many scholars now); teachings passed on orally and written down centuries later
sources.zh: 佛陀的年代：大約西元前 560–480 年（較早的看法）；大約西元前 405 年去世（現在很多學者）；教法口傳，好幾百年後才寫下

sources.en: The Pāli collection perhaps first written down in Sri Lanka in the 1st century BCE
sources.zh: 巴利文的經典可能在西元前一世紀第一次在斯里蘭卡寫成文字

sources.en: Theravāda dates 623–543 BCE; proposed death dates after the Göttingen symposium (1988; papers 1991–92)
sources.zh: 上座部傳統年代西元前 623–543 年；哥廷根研討會後學者提出的去世年代

sources.en: The Buddha lived between the mid-6th and mid-4th centuries BCE
sources.zh: 佛陀生活在西元前六世紀中到四世紀中之間

sources.en: Birth given as 566 BCE
sources.zh: 「生於西元前五六六年」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「釋迦牟尼」

sources.en: Lumbini: Ashoka's pillar inscription; brick structures from the 3rd century BCE
sources.zh: 藍毘尼：阿育王石柱的銘文；西元前三世紀的磚造建築

sources.en: Early timber structures beneath Ashoka's rebuilding at Lumbini
sources.zh: 藍毘尼阿育王重建之下更早的木造結構

sources.en: The earliest structure at Lumbini dated to the 6th century BCE; its Buddhist link only suggested
sources.zh: 藍毘尼最早的結構定為西元前六世紀；和佛教的關聯只是推測
sources.src: Reay et al., Frontiers in Geochemistry (2025)

sources.en: Mahabodhi: first temple by Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE; present temple 5th–6th centuries CE
sources.zh: 摩訶菩提寺：阿育王在西元前三世紀建第一座寺；現在的寺是西元五到六世紀
sources.src: UNESCO World Heritage List, Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodh Gaya

sources.en: Sarnath: the first teaching by tradition; the Lion Capital, basis of India's state emblem
sources.zh: 鹿野苑：傳統上第一次說法的地方；獅子柱頭是印度國徽的根據

sources.en: The first teaching in the deer park at Isipatana near Varanasi
sources.zh: 初轉法輪：瓦拉納西附近仙人住處的鹿野苑

sources.en: The four places of pilgrimage: birth, awakening, first teaching, final passing
sources.zh: 四個朝聖的地方：出生、覺悟、初轉法輪、般涅槃

sources.en: Ashoka's edicts: Kalinga (Rock Edict XIII), respect for all religions (XII), faith in the Buddha, Dhamma, and Saṅgha (Bairat), Lumbini pillar; Brahmi script and a Greek-Aramaic edict
sources.zh: 阿育王詔令：羯陵伽（第十三岩石詔令）、尊重所有宗教（第十二）、對佛法僧的信心（拜拉特）、藍毘尼石柱；婆羅米文字與希臘文—亞蘭文詔令
sources.src: Dhammika, The Edicts of King Asoka (Wheel 386)

sources.en: Ashoka c. 265–238 or c. 273–232 BCE; the Kalinga war and remorse; Mahinda and Sanghamitta in the Sri Lankan chronicle; edicts naming no particular creed
sources.zh: 阿育王約西元前 265–238 或 273–232 年；羯陵伽之戰與懊悔；斯里蘭卡編年史裡的摩哂陀與僧伽蜜多；詔令不提倡特定的教義

sources.en: Ashoka as ruler, Buddhist, moral philosopher, and ecumenist
sources.zh: 阿育王是統治者、佛教徒、道德哲學家，也跨越宗教
sources.src: Olivelle, Ashoka: Portrait of a Philosopher King (Yale University Press, 2024)

sources.en: Sanchi: a sacred center from Ashoka's time; later enlargements; aniconic art
sources.zh: 桑奇：從阿育王時代開始的聖地；後來的擴建；不刻佛像的藝術
sources.src: UNESCO World Heritage List, Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi

sources.en: Anuradhapura: the tree cutting brought by Sanghamitta in the 3rd century BCE; abandoned after 993
sources.zh: 阿努拉德普勒：僧伽蜜多在西元前三世紀帶來的樹枝；993 年後廢棄
sources.src: UNESCO World Heritage List, Sacred City of Anuradhapura

sources.en: Early Brahmi writing at Anuradhapura
sources.zh: 阿努拉德普勒早期的婆羅米文字
sources.src: Coningham et al., Cambridge Archaeological Journal (1996)

sources.en: Gandhāran birch-bark scrolls, 1st century BCE to 3rd century CE; Kharoṣṭhī script; British Library 1994
sources.zh: 犍陀羅樺樹皮卷子，西元前一世紀到西元三世紀；佉盧文；大英圖書館 1994 年
sources.src: National Endowment for the Humanities, “Early Buddhist Manuscripts”

sources.en: Gandhara as a center for spreading Buddhism to Afghanistan and Central Asia; its art from the 1st century BCE
sources.zh: 犍陀羅是佛教傳往阿富汗和中亞的中心；西元前一世紀起的藝術

sources.en: Early Buddhist art without human images; the first Buddha images in Gandhara and Mathura in the 1st century CE
sources.zh: 早期佛教藝術沒有人形；西元一世紀犍陀羅與秣菟羅最早的佛像
sources.src: Dehejia, “Buddhism and Buddhist Art,” Metropolitan Museum of Art (2007)

sources.en: Liu Ying, King of Chu, and the edict of the eighth year (65 CE)

sources.en: Goguryeo, 372 CE: the monk Sundo with images and sutras; “the beginning of the Buddha's teaching east of the sea”
sources.zh: 高句麗小獸林王二年：「秦王苻堅，遣使及浮屠順道，送佛像、經文」；五年「此海東佛法之始」

sources.zh: 百濟枕流王：「胡僧摩羅難陁自晉至……佛法始於此」

sources.en: Silla: the teaching begins in the 15th year of King Beopheung (528 by its count); the story of Ichadon and the white blood
sources.zh: 新羅法興王十五年「肇行佛法」；異次頓的故事

sources.zh: 後來的史家認為松贊干布引進了佛教

sources.zh: 開元寺：1680 年北園別館，1690 年改建為寺；國定古蹟

units.blurb_en: What moved along the Silk Road, how two world religions began and spread, who kept knowledge alive, and what life was like in a castle.
units.blurb_zh: 絲路上走的是什麼、兩個世界宗教怎麼開始與傳開、誰把知識保存下來，以及住在城堡裡是什麼樣子。

lessons.title: What Traveled Along the Silk Road?
lessons.blurb_en: Watch land routes and sea routes join into a web on a 3D globe, then follow silk, horses, pepper, paper, and porcelain as they change hands from one stretch to the next. Sort what traveled east and what traveled west.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 地球儀上看陸路和海路連成一張網，再跟著絲、馬、胡椒、紙和瓷器，看它們一段一段換手。分一分：哪些往東走，哪些往西走。
lessons.big_idea_en: The “Silk Road” was not one road but a web of land and sea routes linking Asia, Africa, and Europe. Few people traveled the whole way; most goods were passed from trader to trader, one stretch at a time. Along with silk went horses, spices, paper, glass, porcelain, religions, skills, and even diseases.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 「絲路」不是一條路，而是一張連起亞洲、非洲和歐洲的陸路和海路的網。很少有人從頭走到尾；大部分的貨物是一段一段、從一個商人傳到下一個商人手上。跟著絲一起走的，還有馬、香料、紙、玻璃、瓷器、宗教、技術，甚至疾病。

lab.title_en: A Web of Roads and Sea Lanes
lab.how_en: Drag the slider from 200 BCE to 1400 CE, or press Play, and watch overland routes (gold) and sea routes (blue) join into a web. Click a city to read why it mattered. Then choose “Follow one thing”: a pink dot carries silk, horses, pepper, paper, or porcelain along its journey, one stretch at a time, and the card shows who carried it on each stretch.
lab.how_zh: 把滑桿從西元前 200 年拉到西元 1400 年，或按「播放」，看陸路（金色）和海路（藍色）連成一張網。點一座城市，讀它為什麼重要。接著選「跟著一件東西走」：粉紅色的小點帶著絲、馬、胡椒、紙或瓷器，一段一段走完它的旅程，小卡會寫出每一段是誰帶的。

cities.what_en: The capital of China under the Han and Tang dynasties, at the eastern end of the overland routes. Under the Tang it held Daoist, Buddhist, Zoroastrian, and Christian places of worship.
cities.what_zh: 漢朝和唐朝的都城，在陸路的東端。唐朝時，城裡有道教、佛教、祆教和基督教的禮拜場所。
cities.when_en: In 138 BCE the envoy Zhang Qian set out from here toward the west (Lesson 7). The Tang city, from 618, was one of the largest in the world.
cities.when_zh: 西元前 138 年，使者張騫從這裡往西出發（第七課）。從 618 年起的唐朝長安，是當時世界上最大的城市之一。
cities.how_en: Han histories, UNESCO's description of the Chang'an–Tianshan corridor, and the British Museum, which describes the city's places of worship.
cities.how_zh: 漢朝的史書，以及聯合國教科文組織對「長安—天山廊道」的說明。
cities.src: UNESCO, Silk Roads: the Routes Network of Chang'an-Tianshan Corridor; British Museum, Silk Roads (2024)

cities.what_en: An oasis town where the routes into China met. Travelers left China through two gates nearby, the Jade Gate and the Yang Gate.
cities.what_zh: 一座綠洲城市，往中國的幾條路在這裡會合。旅人從附近的玉門關和陽關兩個關口出去。
cities.when_en: The History of the Former Han places the founding of the Dunhuang commandery under Emperor Wu, in the section for 111 BCE; historians discuss the exact year.
cities.when_zh: 《漢書》把設立敦煌郡記在漢武帝的時候，放在西元前 111 年那一段；確切的年份歷史學家還在討論。
cities.how_en: The History of the Former Han says that “two roads” led from the Jade Gate and the Yang Gate into the Western Regions.
cities.how_zh: 《漢書・西域傳》說：「自玉門、陽關出西域有兩道」。
cities.src: 《漢書・武帝紀》；《漢書・西域傳》

cities.what_en: An oasis at the western edge of the Tarim Basin, where routes from China met routes over the mountains to Central Asia and India.
cities.what_zh: 塔里木盆地西邊的綠洲，從中國來的路，在這裡和翻過高山往中亞、印度的路會合。
cities.when_en: Britannica says Chinese forces first took Kashgar in the 2nd century BCE.
cities.when_zh: Britannica 說，中國的軍隊在西元前二世紀第一次取得喀什。
cities.how_en: Chinese histories and later travelers' accounts.
cities.how_zh: 中國的史書，以及後來旅人的紀錄。

cities.what_en: A great Mediterranean port. Goods from India came by ship up the Red Sea, overland to the Nile, and down the river to Alexandria.
cities.what_zh: 地中海的大港。從印度來的貨物，坐船到紅海，走陸路到尼羅河，再順著河到亞歷山卓。
cities.when_en: In Roman times, about 2,000 years ago. The city had been the capital of Egypt since its founding in 332 BCE.
cities.when_zh: 羅馬時代，大約兩千年前。這座城從西元前 332 年建立起，就是埃及的首都。
cities.how_en: Roman writers, papyrus documents, and finds of Indian goods; the Metropolitan Museum explains the route.
cities.how_zh: 羅馬的作家、莎草紙文書，以及出土的印度貨物；大都會博物館說明了這條路線。
cities.src: Metropolitan Museum of Art, “Trade between the Romans and the Empires of Asia”

cities.what_en: A desert city whose caravans linked the Roman world with Persia and the lands beyond.
cities.what_zh: 一座沙漠城市，它的商隊把羅馬世界和波斯，以及更遠的地方連起來。
cities.when_en: UNESCO says Palmyra came under Roman control in the mid-1st century CE.
cities.when_zh: 聯合國教科文組織說，帕邁拉在西元一世紀中期歸羅馬控制。
cities.how_en: Its ruins and inscriptions. UNESCO calls it a city on the trade route linking Persia, India, and China with the Roman Empire.
cities.how_zh: 城市的遺址和銘文。聯合國教科文組織說，它是連起波斯、印度、中國和羅馬帝國的貿易路線上的城市。

cities.what_en: The home city of the Sogdians, merchants who built a trading network that stretched into China.
cities.what_zh: 粟特人的家鄉。粟特商人建立了一張一直延伸到中國的貿易網。
cities.when_en: One of the letters Sogdian merchants wrote in China around 313 CE was addressed to partners back in Samarkand.
cities.when_zh: 大約西元 313 年，在中國的粟特商人寫的信裡，有一封是寄給在撒馬爾罕的夥伴的。
cities.how_en: The “Ancient Letters,” found in 1907 in a watchtower west of the Jade Gate, list goods such as silver, linen, musk, and pepper. Their date is debated.
cities.how_zh: 1907 年在玉門關西邊一座烽燧裡找到的「粟特古信札」，列出銀、麻布、麝香、胡椒等貨物。它們的年代還有爭論。
cities.src: The Sogdian Ancient Letters, trans. Sims-Williams (University of Washington)

cities.what_en: An oasis kingdom on the northern route around the Taklamakan Desert.
cities.what_zh: 繞過塔克拉瑪干沙漠的北路上的一個綠洲王國。
cities.when_en: The kingdom of Gaochang arose around 450 CE; Tang forces ended its power in 640.
cities.when_zh: 高昌國大約在西元 450 年興起；640 年被唐朝的軍隊滅掉。
cities.how_en: Tombs nearby held Sasanian silver coins from Persia and a few Byzantine gold coins, probably brought by Sogdian merchants.
cities.how_zh: 附近的墳墓裡有波斯薩珊王朝的銀幣，還有幾枚拜占庭的金幣，大概是粟特商人帶來的。
cities.src: British Museum, Silk Roads exhibition (2024); Britannica, “Turfan”

cities.what_en: The capital of the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire, a huge market for silk.
cities.what_zh: 東羅馬（拜占庭）帝國的首都，是絲的大市場。
cities.when_en: Around 550 CE, the historian Procopius tells of monks who brought silkworm eggs to Emperor Justinian, so that silk could be made in the empire.
cities.when_zh: 大約西元 550 年，史家普羅科匹厄斯說，有僧人把蠶卵帶給查士丁尼皇帝，讓帝國自己也能生產絲。
cities.how_en: Procopius's story is one report, written down in the 500s. Another Byzantine writer tells it differently, so it is told here as his version.
cities.how_zh: 這是普羅科匹厄斯的記載，寫於六世紀；另一位拜占庭作家的說法不一樣，所以這裡當作他的說法來寫。
cities.src: UNESCO, Historic Areas of Istanbul; UNESCO, About the Silk Roads

cities.what_en: China's great southern port. Under the Tang, ships sailed from here to India, the Persian Gulf, and East Africa.
cities.what_zh: 中國南方的大港。唐朝時，船從這裡開往印度、波斯灣和東非。
cities.when_en: Britannica calls it a doorway for foreign influence since the 3rd century CE.
cities.when_zh: Britannica 說，從西元三世紀起，它就是外國影響進來的門戶。
cities.how_en: Chinese records, and shipwrecks such as the Belitung ship, which probably sailed from here (some scholars think from Yangzhou).
cities.how_zh: 中國的紀錄，以及勿里洞沉船等沉船；勿里洞的船大概是從這裡出發的（也有人認為是揚州）。
cities.src: Britannica, “Guangzhou”; Metropolitan Museum of Art, “Internationalism in the Tang Dynasty”

cities.what_en: A port on India's southwest coast, once famous for weaving cotton cloth; the word “calico” comes from its name. The coast around it was a major source of pepper.
cities.what_zh: 印度西南海岸的港口，過去以織棉布出名；英文的 calico（印花棉布）就是從它的名字來的。附近的海岸是胡椒的重要產地。
cities.when_en: Britannica says Arab traders first settled there in the 7th century CE.
cities.when_zh: Britannica 說，阿拉伯商人在西元七世紀第一次在這裡定居。
cities.how_en: Arab and Chinese records, and later the accounts of Ibn Battuta, who was shipwrecked nearby in the 1340s.
cities.how_zh: 阿拉伯和中國的紀錄，以及後來伊本・巴杜達的遊記；他在 1340 年代在附近遇到船難。

cities.zh: 室利佛逝（蘇門答臘巨港）
cities.what_en: The traditional capital of Srivijaya, a trading kingdom that controlled the straits between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea. Scholars still debate exactly where its center was.
cities.what_zh: 傳統上認為是室利佛逝的首都。這個貿易王國控制著印度洋和南海之間的海峽；它的中心確切在哪裡，學者還在討論。
cities.when_en: The Chinese monk Yijing stopped here in 671 CE (Lesson 8). Britannica says it was Srivijaya's capital from the 7th to the late 12th century.
cities.when_zh: 中國僧人義淨在西元 671 年停在這裡（第八課）。Britannica 說，從七世紀到十二世紀末它都是室利佛逝的首都。
cities.how_en: Yijing's writings, and stone inscriptions in Old Malay from the 680s found near Palembang.
cities.how_zh: 義淨的著作，以及在巨港附近找到、680 年代用古馬來文刻的石碑。

cities.what_en: Founded as the capital of the Abbasid caliphs, Baghdad drew goods by river and by road from the Persian Gulf, Central Asia, and the Mediterranean.
cities.what_zh: 阿拔斯王朝哈里發的首都。貨物從波斯灣、中亞和地中海，順著河、沿著路來到巴格達。
cities.when_en: Founded in 762 CE. Britannica says the first paper was made in Baghdad in 793.
cities.when_zh: 建於西元 762 年。Britannica 說，巴格達在 793 年第一次造出了紙。
cities.how_en: Arabic histories and geographies, written by scholars in the city.
cities.how_zh: 城裡的學者寫的阿拉伯文史書和地理書。

cities.what_en: A ship of a Persian Gulf type, its planks sewn together with rope, sank near the island of Belitung on its way from China.
cities.what_zh: 一艘波斯灣式的船，船板是用繩子縫起來的，從中國出發後，在勿里洞島附近沉沒。
cities.when_en: One bowl in the cargo seems to carry a date equal to 826 CE; the ceramics date to about the 820s and 830s.
cities.when_zh: 貨物裡有一個碗，上面好像刻著相當於西元 826 年的年代；這些瓷器大約是 820 到 830 年代的。
cities.how_en: Fishermen found it in 1998. About 60,000 objects were brought up, including more than 50,000 painted bowls from the Changsha kilns.
cities.how_zh: 1998 年漁民發現了它。打撈上來大約六萬件東西，其中有五萬多個長沙窯的彩繪碗。
cities.src: Singapore National Heritage Board, “Sunken Treasure”; Asian Civilisations Museum, “Tang Shipwreck”

cities.what_en: One of the busiest ports in the world, called Zaytun by foreign traders. Its sites include the 11th-century Qingjing Mosque, one of the earliest in China, Islamic tombs, and Buddhist pagodas.
cities.what_zh: 世界上最繁忙的港口之一，外國商人稱它為「刺桐」（Zaytun）。城裡有十一世紀建的清淨寺（中國最早的清真寺之一）、伊斯蘭教的墓，還有佛塔。
cities.when_en: UNESCO describes it as a maritime hub of the East and Southeast Asian trade network in the 10th to 14th centuries CE.
cities.when_zh: 聯合國教科文組織說，它是西元十到十四世紀東亞和東南亞貿易網的海上樞紐。
cities.how_en: Its mosques, tombs, pagodas, and inscriptions, inscribed as a World Heritage site in 2021.
cities.how_zh: 清真寺、墓、佛塔和碑刻，2021 年列入世界遺產。
cities.src: UNESCO, Quanzhou: Emporium of the World in Song-Yuan China

cities.what_en: An island port on the coast of East Africa. Gold and ivory from inland were traded here for silver, carnelian beads, perfume, Persian pottery, and Chinese porcelain.
cities.what_zh: 東非海岸的一個島上的港口。內陸的黃金和象牙，在這裡換成白銀、紅玉髓珠、香水、波斯陶器和中國瓷器。
cities.when_en: UNESCO says the island was occupied from the 9th to the 19th century, and its trade was at its height in the 13th and 14th centuries, around 1300. Ibn Battuta visited in 1331–32.
cities.when_zh: 聯合國教科文組織說，這個島從九世紀到十九世紀都有人住，貿易在十三、十四世紀（大約 1300 年前後）最興盛。伊本・巴杜達在 1331–32 年來過。
cities.how_en: Ruins of mosques and palaces. Chinese porcelain was set into the domes and vaults of the Great Mosque.
cities.how_zh: 清真寺和宮殿的遺址。中國瓷器被嵌在大清真寺的圓頂和拱頂上。
cities.src: UNESCO, Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Ruins of Songo Mnara

cities.what_en: Two cemeteries here hold gravestones from 1338–39 that give “pestilence” as the cause of death.
cities.what_zh: 這裡的兩座墓地有 1338–39 年的墓碑，寫著死因是「瘟疫」。
cities.when_en: 1338–39 CE, a few years before the Black Death reached the Mediterranean in 1347.
cities.when_zh: 西元 1338–39 年，比黑死病在 1347 年傳到地中海早幾年。
cities.how_en: A 2022 study found DNA of the plague bacterium in seven people buried here and argues the strain arose in this region. Other historians argue the plague spread across Central Eurasia earlier, in the 1200s.
cities.how_zh: 2022 年的一項研究，在這裡七個人的遺骸中找到鼠疫桿菌的 DNA，並主張那一株病菌就是在這一帶出現的。也有歷史學家主張，鼠疫更早在 1200 年代就已經傳遍歐亞大陸中部。

cities.what_en: A port on the narrow strait between Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula, where ships stopped for food and fresh water.
cities.what_zh: 蘇門答臘和馬來半島之間窄窄的海峽上的港口，船在這裡停下來補充糧食和淡水。
cities.when_en: Founded around 1400 CE; it grew into a great trading sultanate in the 15th century.
cities.when_zh: 大約在西元 1400 年建立；十五世紀發展成一個重要的貿易蘇丹國。
cities.how_en: Malay and Chinese records, and later Portuguese ones.
cities.how_zh: 馬來和中國的紀錄，以及後來葡萄牙人的紀錄。
cities.src: Britannica, “Melaka”; UNESCO, Melaka and George Town

legs.en: Silk went out along the Hexi Corridor to the frontier town of Dunhuang.
legs.zh: 絲沿著河西走廊，運到邊境的敦煌。

legs.en: Oasis traders carried it around the Taklamakan Desert to Kashgar.
legs.zh: 綠洲的商人帶著它繞過塔克拉瑪干沙漠，到了喀什。

legs.en: Parthian middlemen passed it west. The History of the Later Han says Parthia wanted to keep the silk trade with Rome for itself.
legs.zh: 安息（帕提亞）的中間商把它往西轉賣。《後漢書》說，安息想把和羅馬的絲綢買賣留給自己。

goods.note_en: From Palmyra, caravans carried it on toward the Mediterranean coast and Roman markets. This is one likely journey, not the record of one cargo. Silk reached the Roman world in the 1st century BCE; the Roman writer Pliny complained that India, the “Seres,” and Arabia took 100 million sesterces a year from the empire.
goods.note_zh: 從帕邁拉，商隊再把它往地中海沿岸、羅馬的市場帶。這是一條可能的旅程，不是某一批貨的紀錄。絲在西元前一世紀傳到羅馬世界；羅馬作家老普林尼抱怨，印度、「賽里斯」（絲國）和阿拉伯每年從帝國拿走一億塞斯特斯。
goods.src: UNESCO, Silk Roads; 《後漢書・西域傳》

legs.en: Han envoys and armies brought horses back from Ferghana, west of Kashgar. Emperor Wu called them “heavenly horses.”
legs.zh: 漢朝的使者和軍隊，從喀什西邊的大宛帶回馬。漢武帝稱牠們為「天馬」。

goods.note_en: The same envoys brought back seeds of alfalfa, which the horses ate, and grapes, and planted them near the capital.
goods.note_zh: 同一批使者也帶回了馬吃的苜蓿和葡萄的種子，種在都城附近。

legs.en: Ships carried it from India's southwest coast, a major pepper source, around Sri Lanka and across the Bay of Bengal to the straits controlled by Srivijaya.
legs.zh: 船把它從印度西南海岸這個胡椒的重要產地運出，繞過斯里蘭卡、橫越孟加拉灣，到室利佛逝控制的海峽。

legs.en: Other ships carried it north to Guangzhou.
legs.zh: 另一批船再把它往北運到廣州。

goods.note_en: This is one likely journey, not the record of one cargo. UNESCO says the sea routes were used in particular for the spice trade, and that merchants often sold their cargo on at points along the way.
goods.note_zh: 這是一條可能的旅程，不是某一批貨的紀錄。聯合國教科文組織說，海路特別用來做香料的買賣，商人也常常在途中把貨轉賣出去。
goods.src: UNESCO, Silk Roads; Metropolitan Museum of Art, “Internationalism in the Tang Dynasty”

legs.en: Paper was made in China by about 100 CE (Britannica names the official Cai Lun, 105 CE; some finds are older), and it traveled west with officials and merchants.
legs.zh: 西元 100 年左右，中國已經在造紙（Britannica 說是蔡倫，西元 105 年；也有更早的出土紙），紙再跟著官員和商人往西走。

legs.en: The skill reached Samarkand by 751. A famous story says Chinese prisoners from a battle that year taught it, but some historians think paper was already used there earlier.
legs.zh: 到 751 年，造紙的技術已經傳到撒馬爾罕。有一個有名的故事說，是那一年一場戰役裡被俘的中國人教的，但有些歷史學家認為，在那以前那裡就已經有人用紙了。

legs.en: By 793 paper was being made in Baghdad. Later, papermaking reached Europe from the Islamic world.
legs.zh: 到 793 年，巴格達已經在造紙。後來，造紙術再從伊斯蘭世界傳到歐洲。

goods.note_en: Here what traveled was a skill, not just an object, and people used the materials they had: plant fibers in China, rags of linen and cotton later in Europe.
goods.note_zh: 這一次旅行的是一種技術，不只是一件東西；各地的人用手邊有的材料來做：中國用植物纖維，後來的歐洲用麻布和棉布的破布。

legs.en: Chinese ships carried porcelain from the great port of Quanzhou to ports in Sumatra and Java.
legs.zh: 中國的船把瓷器從泉州這個大港運到蘇門答臘和爪哇的港口。

legs.en: Traders of many peoples carried it across the Bay of Bengal and around Sri Lanka to India's west coast.
legs.zh: 許多不同民族的商人，把它帶過孟加拉灣、繞過斯里蘭卡，到印度的西海岸。

legs.en: Traders from Arabia, Persia, and the Swahili coast probably carried it down the coast of East Africa.
legs.zh: 來自阿拉伯、波斯和斯瓦希里海岸的商人，大概把它沿著東非海岸往南運。

goods.note_en: This is one likely journey, not the record of a single bowl. At Kilwa, Chinese porcelain was set into the domes and vaults of the Great Mosque.
goods.note_zh: 這是一條可能的旅程，不是某一個碗的紀錄。在基爾瓦，中國瓷器被嵌在大清真寺的圓頂和拱頂上。
goods.src: UNESCO, Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani; UNESCO, Quanzhou

lab.numbers_note_en: Each city lights up in the year given on its card, roughly when our evidence places it on the network; many were founded much earlier. Routes show only the rough direction of travel, and the five journeys show likely paths, not the record of one cargo.
lab.numbers_note_zh: 每一座城市在卡片上寫的那一年亮起來，大約是證據顯示它在這張網上的時候；很多城市其實更早就有了。路線只表示大致的方向，五段旅程是可能的路徑，不是某一件東西的紀錄。
lab.scale_en: This is a teaching sketch. Real travelers used many more routes than the ones drawn, and few of them went the whole way. The map shows land only, with no modern borders.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意。真正的旅人走過的路比畫出來的多很多，而且很少有人從頭走到尾。地圖只畫陸地，不畫今天的國界。
lab.credit_html: Globe: land outlines from Natural Earth (public domain). Places and dates follow the sources listed at the bottom of the page. 地球儀：陸地外形取自 Natural Earth（公有領域）。地方和年代依本頁最下面列出的資料。

paras: Nobody in ancient times called these routes the “Silk Road.” The German geographer Ferdinand von Richthofen used the name in 1877, though earlier German writers had used it too, and it spread widely only in the 1900s. UNESCO describes the Silk Roads as a network of land and sea routes, used for well over 1,500 years, along which silk and many other goods were exchanged.

On land, the routes linked China with Central Asia, Persia, and the Mediterranean. Around 138 BCE the Han envoy Zhang Qian set out west, and the Han set up commanderies along the Hexi Corridor, including Dunhuang. Travelers had to cross deserts, mountains, and the lands of many different kingdoms, so caravans moved from oasis to oasis.

Few people traveled the whole way. Britannica puts it simply: goods were handled stage by stage by middlemen. Sogdian merchants from around Samarkand built a network of partners in many towns; letters they wrote around 313 CE mention silver, linen, musk, and pepper. In 97 CE a Han envoy, Gan Ying, reached the sea in the west and turned back, after sailors there warned him the crossing could take years.

The sea routes were just as important. Ships sailed between China, Southeast Asia, India, the Persian Gulf, the Red Sea, and East Africa, timing their voyages to the monsoon winds. A ship that sank near the island of Belitung around the 820s or 830s carried about 60,000 objects from China, most of them painted bowls. Later, ports such as Quanzhou in China and Kilwa in East Africa grew rich on this trade.

Silk was only one of many things that traveled. Horses, grapes, and alfalfa came east to China; paper and the skill of making it went west, reaching Samarkand by 751 and Baghdad by 793. Glass, spices, porcelain, and coins moved too. So did beliefs: Buddhism, Manichaeism, Christianity, and Islam all spread along these routes. And so did disease: the Black Death of the 1340s probably traveled along these routes, though scholars still debate exactly how.

No single people controlled the routes. Chinese, Sogdian, Persian, Indian, Arab, Malay, Swahili, and many other traders each knew their own stretch. What made the network work was not one long road, but many shorter connections, each linking one place to the next. That is why ideas and goods could travel so far, even though most people did not.
paras_zh: 古代沒有人把這些路叫做「絲路」。德國地理學家李希霍芬在 1877 年用了這個名字，更早的德國作家也用過；它在二十世紀才真正流行起來。聯合國教科文組織說，絲路是一張由陸路和海路組成的網，用了一千五百多年，絲和許多其他的貨物沿著它交換。
在陸地上，這些路把中國和中亞、波斯、地中海連起來。大約西元前 138 年，漢朝的使者張騫往西出發；漢朝也沿著河西走廊設了幾個郡，包括敦煌。旅人要穿過沙漠、高山，還有許多不同國家的土地，所以商隊是從一個綠洲走到下一個綠洲。
很少有人從頭走到尾。Britannica 說得很簡單：貨物是由中間商一段一段轉手的。撒馬爾罕一帶的粟特商人，在許多城鎮都有夥伴；他們大約在西元 313 年寫的信，提到了銀、麻布、麝香和胡椒。西元 97 年，漢朝的使者甘英往西走到了海邊，當地的船夫告訴他渡海可能要好幾年，他就回頭了。
海路一樣重要。船在中國、東南亞、印度、波斯灣、紅海和東非之間航行，看季風決定什麼時候出發。大約在 820 或 830 年代，一艘在勿里洞島附近沉沒的船，載著大約六萬件來自中國的東西，大部分是彩繪的碗。後來，中國的泉州、東非的基爾瓦等港口，都因為這些貿易而富裕起來。
絲只是許多旅行的東西之一。馬、葡萄和苜蓿往東傳到中國；紙和造紙的技術往西走，751 年到了撒馬爾罕，793 年到了巴格達。玻璃、香料、瓷器和錢幣也在流動。信仰也一樣：佛教、摩尼教、基督宗教和伊斯蘭教都沿著這些路傳播。疾病也是：1340 年代的黑死病，很可能是沿著這些路傳開的，只是到底怎麼傳的，學者還在討論。
沒有哪一個民族控制這些路。中國、粟特、波斯、印度、阿拉伯、馬來、斯瓦希里，還有許多其他的商人，各自熟悉自己的那一段。讓這張網運作起來的，不是一條很長的路，而是許多比較短的連結，每一段把一個地方連到下一個地方。這就是為什麼大部分的人沒有走得很遠，想法和貨物卻能傳得那麼遠。
questions: Why do historians say “Silk Roads” or “a network” instead of “the Silk Road”?
Name two things that traveled east toward China and two that traveled west.
If few people traveled the whole way, how did goods and ideas get so far?
answers: There was no single road. Many land and sea routes connected different places at different times, and the name itself was first used in the 1800s.
East: horses, grapes, alfalfa, Mediterranean glass, Christianity (any two). West: silk, papermaking, Changsha bowls and porcelain (any two).
They were passed from trader to trader, stage by stage. Each group knew its own stretch, and the connections between them carried things across the whole network.

parts.text_en: After Zhang Qian's journeys, the gold line reaches from Chang'an through Dunhuang to Kashgar.
parts.text_zh: 張騫出使以後，金色的線從長安經過敦煌，一直到喀什。

parts.text_en: Follow a bolt of silk from Chang'an toward the Mediterranean. Count how many groups carried it.
parts.text_zh: 跟著一匹絲，從長安往地中海走。數數看有幾批人帶過它。

parts.text_en: By now the blue lines link China, Southeast Asia, India, the Persian Gulf, and East Africa. Find the Belitung wreck.
parts.text_zh: 這時藍色的線已經連起中國、東南亞、印度、波斯灣和東非。找找勿里洞沉船。

parts.text_en: Papermaking moves west to Samarkand and Baghdad. This time what travels is knowledge, not just an object.
parts.text_zh: 造紙術往西傳到撒馬爾罕和巴格達。這一次旅行的是知識，不只是一件東西。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then press Play and watch the whole web grow. Which grows faster after about 700 CE: the gold lines or the blue lines?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著按「播放」，看整張網長出來。大約 700 年以後，金色的線和藍色的線，哪一種長得比較快？

eastwest.lead_en: Things moved in all directions along these routes. For each one, decide whether it mostly traveled east, toward China, or west, toward western Asia, Africa, and Europe. There is no timer.
eastwest.lead_zh: 東西沿著這些路往各個方向流動。每一題判斷：它主要是往東走（往中國），還是往西走（往西亞、非洲和歐洲）？不計時。
eastwest.ask_en: Which way did it mostly travel?

buckets.en: West, toward western Asia, Africa, and Europe
buckets.zh: 往西，往西亞、非洲和歐洲

items.why_en: Han envoys brought them back to China, and Emperor Wu named them “heavenly horses,” according to the Records of the Grand Historian.
items.why_zh: 《史記》記載，漢朝的使者把牠們帶回中國，漢武帝稱牠們為「天馬」。
items.hint_en: Ferghana is in Central Asia.
items.hint_zh: 大宛在中亞。

items.why_en: Chinese silk reached the Roman world in the 1st century BCE, and Chinese textiles have been found as far as Egypt.
items.why_zh: 中國的絲在西元前一世紀傳到羅馬世界，在遠到埃及的地方也找到過中國的紡織品。
items.hint_en: The routes are named after it.
items.hint_zh: 這些路就是用它命名的。

items.why_en: Han envoys brought the seeds back from Central Asia, and the emperor had them planted near the capital.
items.why_zh: 漢朝的使者從中亞帶回種子，皇帝下令種在都城附近。
items.hint_en: Horses eat alfalfa.
items.hint_zh: 馬吃苜蓿。

items.why_en: Papermaking reached Samarkand by 751 and Baghdad by 793, according to Britannica.
items.why_zh: Britannica 說，造紙術在 751 年傳到撒馬爾罕，793 年傳到巴格達。
items.hint_en: Paper was first made in China.
items.hint_zh: 紙最早是在中國做出來的。

items.why_en: A 2021 study concluded that Mediterranean-type glass had probably reached East Asia by the 5th century BCE, and a late-Roman-type glass cup was buried in a royal tomb in Korea.
items.why_zh: 2021 年的一項研究認為，至少在西元前五世紀，地中海一類的玻璃就已經傳到東亞；朝鮮半島的一座王陵裡，也埋了一個晚期羅馬式的玻璃杯。
items.hint_en: Glassmaking was an old craft around the Mediterranean.
items.hint_zh: 製造玻璃是地中海一帶的老手藝。

items.why_en: More than 50,000 of them were on the Belitung ship, which probably sailed from Guangzhou toward the west around the 820s–830s (some scholars think it left from Yangzhou).
items.why_zh: 勿里洞沉船上有五萬多個，這艘船大概在 820 到 830 年代從廣州往西開（也有人認為是從揚州出發）。
items.hint_en: Changsha is in China.
items.hint_zh: 長沙在中國。

items.en: The first recorded Christian mission to China
items.zh: 第一次有紀錄的基督教傳教團到中國
items.why_en: In 635 a priest called Aluoben, from Byzantium or the Persian empire, came to Chang'an, according to a stone stele in Chinese and Syriac.
items.why_zh: 一塊用中文和敘利亞文寫的石碑記載，635 年一位叫阿羅本的教士，從拜占庭或波斯來到長安。
items.hint_en: Christianity began in western Asia.
items.hint_zh: 基督宗教從西亞開始。

items.why_en: Gravestones of 1338–39 in Central Asia mention a pestilence, and the Black Death reached the Mediterranean in 1347. Scholars debate exactly how it traveled.
items.why_zh: 中亞 1338–39 年的墓碑提到瘟疫，黑死病在 1347 年傳到地中海。它到底怎麼傳過去的，學者還在討論。
items.hint_en: Look at where the gravestones were and where it arrived next.
items.hint_zh: 看看墓碑在哪裡，下一個到的地方在哪裡。

eastwest.end_en: Goods, skills, beliefs, and even diseases moved in both directions. The routes connected many peoples, not just two ends.
eastwest.end_zh: 貨物、技術、信仰，甚至疾病，都往兩個方向走。這些路連起的是許多民族，不只是兩端。
