lessons.title: Who Kept Knowledge Alive?
lessons.blurb_en: Follow seven books on a 3D globe as they are copied and translated from Greek, Sanskrit, and Arabic into Syriac, Arabic, Latin, and Chinese, from Alexandria and Baghdad to Toledo, Pisa, and Chang'an. Find out where words like algebra and zero came from.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 地球儀上跟著七本書走，看它們從希臘文、梵文和阿拉伯文，被抄寫、翻譯成敘利亞文、阿拉伯文、拉丁文和中文，從亞歷山卓、巴格達一路到托雷多、比薩和長安。找一找 algebra（代數）、zero（零）這些字從哪裡來。
lessons.big_idea_en: Knowledge did not stay in one place. Greek, Persian, and Indian books were translated into Syriac and Arabic in Baghdad, studied and improved there, and later translated into Latin in Spain and Italy; Buddhist books went from Sanskrit into Chinese. The people who kept knowledge alive spoke many languages and followed different religions.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 知識沒有一直待在同一個地方。希臘、波斯和印度的書在巴格達被譯成敘利亞文和阿拉伯文，在那裡被研究、被改進，後來又在西班牙和義大利被譯成拉丁文；佛經則從梵文譯成中文。保存知識的人說很多種語言，也信不同的宗教。

lab.how_en: Drag the slider from 400 BCE to 1500 CE, or press Play, and watch places of learning light up. Then choose a book under “Follow a book.” A glowing dot carries it from one place to the next, and the card shows which language it was translated into at each stop. Click a place to read what happened there and how we know.
lab.how_zh: 把滑桿從西元前 400 年拉到西元 1500 年，或按「播放」，看學術的地方一個一個亮起來。接著在「跟著一本書走」選一本書：發光的小點把它從一個地方帶到下一個地方，卡片會寫出每一站它被譯成什麼語言。點一個地方，讀那裡發生了什麼、我們怎麼知道。

cities.what_en: Plato set up his school, the Academy, outside the city, at a place with an olive grove, a park, and a gymnasium sacred to the hero Academus.
cities.what_zh: 柏拉圖在城外辦了他的學校「學園」（Academy）；那裡有一片橄欖林、一座公園，和一座獻給英雄阿卡德摩斯的體育場。
cities.when_en: Plato acquired the property about 387 BCE. The Academy lasted until 529 CE, when the emperor Justinian closed it together with the other pagan schools.
cities.when_zh: 柏拉圖大約在西元前 387 年取得這塊地。學園一直延續到西元 529 年，被皇帝查士丁尼和其他異教學校一起關閉。
cities.how_en: Plato's own dialogues, and later writers who described the school.
cities.how_zh: 柏拉圖自己寫的對話錄，以及後來描述這所學校的作家。

cities.what_en: The Museum, a research institute, and its Library tried to collect “all the books in the world,” mostly in Greek. Euclid taught geometry here, and later Ptolemy wrote his astronomy.
cities.what_zh: 博物院（Mouseion）是一座研究機構，它的圖書館想收集「世界上所有的書」，大多是希臘文。歐幾里得在這裡教幾何，後來托勒密在這裡寫他的天文學。
cities.when_en: The Library and Museum were founded about 295 BCE. Euclid lived about 300 BCE; Ptolemy wrote about 150 CE.
cities.when_zh: 圖書館和博物院大約在西元前 295 年建立。歐幾里得大約生活在西元前 300 年；托勒密大約在西元 150 年寫作。
cities.how_en: Ancient writers. No catalog of the Library survives, and even Britannica gives different dates for when it was destroyed (see “Different Accounts”).
cities.how_zh: 古代的作家。圖書館的目錄沒有留下來，連 Britannica 對它什麼時候被毀，都寫了不同的年代（見「不同的說法」）。

cities.what_en: The physician Galen was born here. He wrote in Greek, and his ideas about the body guided medicine in Europe and the Muslim world for centuries.
cities.what_zh: 醫生蓋倫在這裡出生。他用希臘文寫作，他對人體的看法，好幾百年間引導著歐洲和穆斯林世界的醫學。
cities.when_en: Galen was born in 129 CE and died about 216; he worked mostly in Rome.
cities.when_zh: 蓋倫生於西元 129 年，大約死於 216 年；他主要在羅馬行醫。
cities.how_en: His books. Many survive in Greek; some of those lost in Greek survive only in Arabic translation.
cities.how_zh: 他的著作。很多有希臘文本留下來；有些希臘文已經失傳的，只靠阿拉伯文譯本留下來。

cities.what_en: A great Buddhist monastery and center of learning (Lesson 8). The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang spent much of his time in India here, learning Sanskrit and Buddhist philosophy.
cities.what_zh: 一座很大的佛教寺院和學術中心（第八課）。中國的朝聖者玄奘在印度的時候，大部分時間待在這裡，學梵文和佛教哲學。
cities.when_en: Excavations date the monasteries to the 5th century CE. Xuanzang was in India from 629 and left in 643.
cities.when_zh: 挖掘顯示寺院建於西元五世紀。玄奘從 629 年到 643 年在印度。
cities.how_en: Excavated ruins, and the travel records of Chinese pilgrims such as Xuanzang.
cities.how_zh: 挖掘出來的遺址，以及玄奘等中國朝聖者的遊記。

cities.what_en: Xuanzang came home from India with Buddhist scriptures and spent the rest of his life translating them from Sanskrit into Chinese.
cities.what_zh: 玄奘從印度帶回佛經，餘生都在把它們從梵文譯成中文。
cities.when_en: He returned in 645 and died in 664.
cities.when_zh: 他在 645 年回來，664 年去世。
cities.how_en: His translations and his detailed travel records, which historians and archaeologists still use.
cities.how_zh: 他的譯本，以及他詳細的旅行紀錄；歷史學家和考古學家到今天還在用。

cities.what_en: The astronomer Brahmagupta wrote a great work on astronomy and mathematics. He treated zero as a number, defining it as what you get when you subtract a number from itself.
cities.what_zh: 天文學家婆羅摩笈多寫了一部天文與數學的大書。他把零當成一個數，定義為一個數減去自己所得到的結果。
cities.when_en: He wrote it in 628, probably while living here.
cities.when_zh: 他在 628 年寫成，那時大概住在這裡。
cities.how_en: The book itself, in Sanskrit, and its later Arabic translation.
cities.how_zh: 這本書本身（梵文），以及後來的阿拉伯文譯本。

cities.what_en: The Abbasid caliphs kept a royal library, the House of Wisdom, and their court supported many scholars. Translators of Persian, Greek, Syriac, and Indian works into Arabic worked in Baghdad, some close to the court. Al-Khwārizmī wrote here on numbers and algebra.
cities.what_zh: 阿拔斯王朝的哈里發有一座王室圖書館，叫「智慧宮」，宮廷也支持許多學者。把波斯、希臘、敘利亞和印度的著作譯成阿拉伯文的譯者在巴格達工作，有些和宮廷關係密切。花拉子密（al-Khwārizmī）在這裡寫了數字與代數的書。
cities.when_en: Baghdad was founded in 762. The House of Wisdom flourished under Hārūn al-Rashīd and al-Maʾmūn (786–833).
cities.when_zh: 巴格達在 762 年建城。智慧宮在哈倫・拉希德和馬蒙的時候（786–833）最興盛。
cities.how_en: The translations themselves, and later book lists and biographies of scholars. Historians debate what kind of place the House of Wisdom was (see “Different Accounts”).
cities.how_zh: 譯本本身，以及後來的書目和學者傳記。智慧宮到底是什麼樣的地方，歷史學家有不同的看法（見「不同的說法」）。

cities.what_en: A copy of the Diamond Sutra, printed from carved wooden blocks, was sealed in a hidden cave here with tens of thousands of other scrolls.
cities.what_zh: 一部用雕版印成的《金剛經》，和好幾萬件其他的卷子一起，被封在這裡的藏經洞裡。
cities.when_en: Its note at the end gives a date equal to May 11, 868. The British Library says it is the oldest printed book that carries a date.
cities.when_zh: 卷末的題記寫的日期相當於 868 年 5 月 11 日。大英圖書館說，它是現存有日期的印刷書裡最古老的。
cities.how_en: The scroll itself, found in the early 20th century and now in the British Library.
cities.how_zh: 這卷經本身，二十世紀初被發現，現在收藏在大英圖書館。
cities.src: British Library, International Dunhuang Programme, “Buddhist texts: the Diamond Sutra”

cities.what_en: Byzantine scribes went on copying Greek books. Works of Archimedes, the great Greek mathematician, were probably copied into bound books here; one copy from the 900s was later scraped and reused for a prayer book, and modern scientists read the hidden text again.
cities.what_zh: 拜占庭的抄寫員繼續抄寫希臘文的書。阿基米德（希臘的大數學家）的著作，大概就是在這裡被抄成書冊；其中一部 900 年代的抄本，後來被刮掉、拿來寫祈禱書，現代的科學家又把底下藏著的字讀了出來。
cities.when_en: The Archimedes copy was made in the 900s. In 1229 a priest at a monastery near Bethlehem reused it for a prayer book.
cities.when_zh: 這部阿基米德的抄本做於 900 年代。1229 年，伯利恆附近一座修道院的教士把它拿來寫祈禱書。
cities.how_en: The manuscript itself, which scientists studied with ultraviolet light and X-rays after a collector bought it in 1998.
cities.how_zh: 就是這部抄本本身；1998 年被一位收藏家買下以後，科學家用紫外光和 X 光研究它。

cities.what_en: Avicenna (Ibn Sina), born nearby in 980, became the most famous of the philosopher-scientists of the medieval Islamic world. His Canon of Medicine joined Greek medicine with new observations.
cities.what_zh: 阿維森納（伊本・西那）980 年生在附近，成為中世紀伊斯蘭世界最有名的哲學家兼科學家。他的《醫典》把希臘的醫學和新的觀察結合起來。
cities.when_en: Born 980, died 1037. The model uses about 1000.
cities.when_zh: 生於 980 年，死於 1037 年。模型用大約 1000 年。
cities.how_en: His own books, and the account of his life written down by his pupil.
cities.how_zh: 他自己的著作，以及他的學生記下來的生平。

cities.what_en: Constantine the African, who knew Arabic, Greek, and Latin, entered this Benedictine monastery and translated 37 books from Arabic into Latin, mostly on medicine, including two by Isaac Israeli, a Jewish physician.
cities.what_zh: 懂阿拉伯文、希臘文和拉丁文的「非洲人」君士坦丁，進了這座本篤會修道院，把 37 本書從阿拉伯文譯成拉丁文，大多是醫學書，其中兩本是猶太醫生以撒・以色列利寫的。
cities.when_en: Late 11th century; he died at the monastery in 1087.
cities.when_zh: 十一世紀後期；他在 1087 年死在修道院裡。
cities.how_en: The translations, which spread quickly through Europe and were still studied in the 16th century.
cities.how_zh: 這些譯本，很快傳遍歐洲，到十六世紀還有人在讀。

cities.what_en: Averroes (Ibn Rushd), born here in 1126, wrote commentaries on most of Aristotle's works. He worked in Seville and Córdoba. His commentaries later shaped how Jewish and Christian thinkers, including Thomas Aquinas, read Aristotle.
cities.what_zh: 阿威羅伊（伊本・魯世德）1126 年生在這裡，替亞里斯多德大部分的著作寫了注釋。他在塞維亞和科爾多瓦工作。這些注釋後來影響了猶太和基督徒思想家（包括阿奎那）怎麼讀亞里斯多德。
cities.when_en: He wrote the commentaries between 1169 and 1195, at the caliph's request.
cities.when_zh: 他在 1169 到 1195 年間，應哈里發的要求寫這些注釋。
cities.how_en: The commentaries survive in Arabic, Hebrew, and Latin.
cities.how_zh: 這些注釋有阿拉伯文、希伯來文和拉丁文的版本留下來。

cities.what_en: Under Muslim rule Toledo had an Arabic-speaking Christian community, the Mozarabs. After it was taken by King Alfonso VI in 1085, scholars came here to translate Arabic books into Latin. Gerard of Cremona came to read Ptolemy's astronomy and stayed for the rest of his life.
cities.what_zh: 在穆斯林統治的時候，托雷多有一個說阿拉伯語的基督徒社群（穆札拉布人）。1085 年被國王阿方索六世攻下以後，學者到這裡把阿拉伯文的書譯成拉丁文。克雷莫納的傑拉德為了讀托勒密的天文學而來，從此一輩子留在這裡。
cities.when_en: Gerard finished his Latin translation of the Almagest in 1175. About 80 translations are attributed to him, perhaps with a team.
cities.when_zh: 傑拉德在 1175 年譯完拉丁文的《天文學大成》。大約有 80 部譯作歸在他名下，可能是一個團隊做的。
cities.how_en: The Latin manuscripts and early printed editions, many of which do not name the translator.
cities.how_zh: 拉丁文的抄本和早期的印刷本，其中很多沒有寫譯者是誰。

cities.zh: 北非貝賈亞（古稱布吉亞）
cities.what_en: A boy from Pisa, later known as Fibonacci, studied calculation here with an Arab teacher while his father worked as a merchant.
cities.what_zh: 一個來自比薩的男孩，就是後來的費波那契，父親在這裡做生意，他跟著一位阿拉伯老師學計算。
cities.when_en: In his boyhood; he was born about 1170. The model uses 1180.
cities.when_zh: 在他小時候；他大約生於 1170 年。模型用 1180 年。
cities.how_en: Britannica's account of his life.
cities.how_zh: Britannica 對他生平的記載。

cities.what_en: Fibonacci wrote the Liber abaci, the “Book of the Abacus” (that is, of calculation), which helped spread the Hindu-Arabic numerals, 0 to 9, in Europe.
cities.what_zh: 費波那契寫了《算盤書》（也就是計算的書），幫助印度—阿拉伯數字（0 到 9）在歐洲傳開。
cities.how_en: The book itself.
cities.how_zh: 這本書本身。

cities.what_en: A trading city on the trans-Saharan caravan routes that became a center of Islamic culture and learning.
cities.what_zh: 撒哈拉商隊路線上的貿易城市，成為伊斯蘭文化與學術的中心。
cities.when_en: A center of Islamic culture from about 1400 to 1600; Britannica says it reached the height of its commercial and intellectual development in the Askia period (1493–1591).
cities.when_zh: 大約 1400 到 1600 年是伊斯蘭文化的中心；Britannica 說，它的商業和學術在阿斯基亞王朝（1493–1591）最興盛。
cities.how_en: Its three old mosques, built in the 14th and early 15th centuries, which still stand.
cities.how_zh: 城裡三座十四到十五世紀初蓋的老清真寺，到今天還在。

legs.en: The Elements, written in Greek in Alexandria about 300 BCE, was translated into Arabic in the Islamic world; Baghdad is one likely place.
legs.zh: 大約西元前 300 年在亞歷山卓用希臘文寫成的《幾何原本》，在伊斯蘭世界被譯成阿拉伯文；巴格達是可能的地方之一。

legs.en: In the 12th century Adelard of Bath, who traveled in Italy, Syria, and perhaps Spain, translated an Arabic version into Latin, and tradition credits Gerard of Cremona in Toledo with another translation.
legs.zh: 十二世紀，曾在義大利、敘利亞，也許還有西班牙遊歷的巴斯的阿德拉德，把一個阿拉伯文版本譯成拉丁文；傳統上也說，托雷多的傑拉德譯過另一個版本。

goods.note_en: Adelard's Latin version served for centuries as the chief geometry textbook in the West. This is a likely journey: the stops show where the language changed, not the path of one copy.
goods.note_zh: 阿德拉德的拉丁文版本，好幾百年間是西方主要的幾何課本。這是一條可能的旅程：每一站表示語言換了的地方，不是某一本書走過的路。
goods.src: Britannica, “Adelard of Bath,” “Gerard of Cremona,” and “Euclid”

legs.en: Written in Greek about 150 CE, it was translated into Arabic in the late 8th and early 9th centuries, probably in Baghdad. Its Arabic name, al-majisṭī, “the greatest,” became Almagest.
legs.zh: 大約西元 150 年用希臘文寫成，在八世紀末到九世紀初被譯成阿拉伯文，大概是在巴格達。它的阿拉伯文名字 al-majisṭī（「最偉大的」）後來變成 Almagest。

legs.en: Gerard of Cremona went to Toledo to learn Arabic so he could read it, and finished his Latin translation in 1175.
legs.zh: 克雷莫納的傑拉德為了讀它，到托雷多學阿拉伯文，在 1175 年完成拉丁文譯本。

goods.note_en: It served as the basic guide for Islamic and European astronomers until about 1600. Scholars in the Islamic world also checked it: Ibn al-Haytham wrote a book called Doubts about Ptolemy. This is a likely journey: the stops show where the language changed.
goods.note_zh: 直到大約 1600 年，它都是伊斯蘭世界和歐洲天文學家的基本指南。伊斯蘭世界的學者也檢查它：伊本・海什木寫了一本《對托勒密的懷疑》。這是一條可能的旅程：每一站表示語言換了的地方。

legs.en: Hunayn ibn Ishaq, a Christian physician in Baghdad, gathered Greek manuscripts in Syria, Palestine, and Egypt and, with his students, translated Galen into Syriac and Arabic.
legs.zh: 巴格達的基督徒醫生侯奈因・伊本・易斯哈格，到敘利亞、巴勒斯坦和埃及收集希臘文抄本，和學生一起把蓋倫譯成敘利亞文和阿拉伯文。

legs.en: Tradition says Gerard of Cremona translated Galen from Arabic into Latin in Toledo.
legs.zh: 傳統上說，克雷莫納的傑拉德在托雷多把蓋倫從阿拉伯文譯成拉丁文。

goods.note_en: Many of Galen's Greek works are lost, and some survive only in Arabic translation, so these translations are especially important. This is a likely journey: the stops show where the language changed.
goods.note_zh: 蓋倫有很多希臘文著作已經失傳，有些只靠阿拉伯文譯本留下來，所以這些譯本特別重要。這是一條可能的旅程：每一站表示語言換了的地方。
goods.src: Britannica, “Hunayn ibn Ishaq” and “Gerard of Cremona”

goods.en: Indian ideas about numbers and zero
goods.zh: 印度的數字與零的觀念

legs.en: Brahmagupta's book of 628 was translated into Arabic in Baghdad about 771. Later, mathematicians writing in Arabic, especially al-Khwārizmī and al-Kindī, wrote about the Indian numerals.
legs.zh: 婆羅摩笈多 628 年的書，大約 771 年在巴格達被譯成阿拉伯文。後來，用阿拉伯文寫作的數學家，特別是花拉子密和金迪，寫了印度的數字。

legs.en: The numerals spread west across the Islamic world. In Bugia, a boy from Pisa learned them from an Arab teacher.
legs.zh: 這些數字在伊斯蘭世界往西傳。在布吉亞，一個比薩來的男孩跟阿拉伯老師學會了它們。

legs.en: In 1202 that boy, Fibonacci, explained them in Latin in his Liber abaci.
legs.zh: 1202 年，這個男孩費波那契在拉丁文的《算盤書》裡介紹它們。

goods.note_en: The numerals began in India in the 6th or 7th century. In English they are called Hindu-Arabic numerals: Indian in origin, and named for the writers in Arabic who passed them on. This is a likely journey: the stops show where the language changed.
goods.note_zh: 這些數字在六或七世紀起源於印度。英文叫它們「印度—阿拉伯數字」：起源在印度，又以把它們傳下去、用阿拉伯文寫作的作者命名。這是一條可能的旅程：每一站表示語言換了的地方。

legs.en: In Baghdad, translators including Hunayn ibn Ishaq put Aristotle into Syriac and Arabic.
legs.zh: 在巴格達，包括侯奈因在內的譯者把亞里斯多德譯成敘利亞文和阿拉伯文。

legs.en: In Seville and Córdoba, Averroes wrote commentaries on most of Aristotle's works between 1169 and 1195.
legs.zh: 在塞維亞和科爾多瓦，阿威羅伊在 1169 到 1195 年間替亞里斯多德大部分的著作寫了注釋。

legs.en: Michael Scot was in Toledo by 1217. Around then he translated works of Aristotle from Arabic and Hebrew into Latin, probably including On the Soul with Averroes' commentary.
legs.zh: 麥可・史考特 1217 年已經在托雷多。大約在那個時候，他把亞里斯多德的著作從阿拉伯文和希伯來文譯成拉丁文，大概也包括《論靈魂》和阿威羅伊的注釋。

goods.note_en: Averroes' commentaries became part of the Latin version of Aristotle's complete works, and they shaped how thinkers such as Thomas Aquinas read him. They also survive in Hebrew translations. This is a likely journey: the stops show where the language changed.
goods.note_zh: 阿威羅伊的注釋成了拉丁文亞里斯多德全集的一部分，影響了阿奎那等思想家怎麼讀亞里斯多德；它們也有希伯來文譯本留下來。這是一條可能的旅程：每一站表示語言換了的地方。

legs.en: Avicenna wrote the Canon in Arabic. Gerard of Cremona, in Toledo, is credited with translating it into Latin before he died in 1187.
legs.zh: 阿維森納用阿拉伯文寫《醫典》。在托雷多的克雷莫納的傑拉德，被認為在 1187 年去世以前把它譯成拉丁文。

goods.note_en: This book did not start in Greek: it was a new work, written in Arabic. It served as a textbook in Europe until the mid-17th century. This is a likely journey: the stops show where the language changed.
goods.note_zh: 這本書不是從希臘文開始的：它是一部用阿拉伯文寫的新著作。它在歐洲當教科書，一直用到十七世紀中期。這是一條可能的旅程：每一站表示語言換了的地方。

legs.en: Xuanzang studied Sanskrit at Nalanda, brought scriptures home, and from 645 translated them into Chinese in Chang'an.
legs.zh: 玄奘在那爛陀學梵文，把佛經帶回家，從 645 年起在長安把它們譯成中文。

goods.note_en: Not every journey ended in Europe. Buddhist learning traveled from India to China, and from China on to Korea and Japan (Lesson 8). Xuanzang's travel records are still used by historians and archaeologists.
goods.note_zh: 不是每一段旅程都以歐洲為終點。佛教的學問從印度傳到中國，再從中國傳到朝鮮半島和日本（第八課）。玄奘的旅行紀錄，歷史學家和考古學家到今天還在用。

lab.numbers_note_en: Each place lights up in the year given on its card. A book's journey shows where it changed language, as one likely path; real copies and translations moved in many directions. Greek books were also kept and copied in Constantinople the whole time, and Arabic, Persian, Hebrew, and Chinese traditions of learning went on in their own right.
lab.numbers_note_zh: 每一個地方在卡片上寫的那一年亮起來。一本書的旅程，畫的是它換語言的地方，是一條可能的路；真正的抄本和譯本往許多方向流動。希臘文的書也一直在君士坦丁堡被保存、抄寫；阿拉伯文、波斯文、希伯來文和中文的學術傳統，也各自延續下去。
lab.scale_en: This is a teaching sketch. The lines connect places of learning in the rough order they flourished; they are not exact roads. The map shows land only, with no modern borders.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意。線把學術的地方依它們興盛的大約先後連起來，不是確切的道路。地圖只畫陸地，不畫今天的國界。
lab.credit_html: Globe: land outlines from Natural Earth (public domain). Places and dates follow the sources listed at the bottom of the page. 地球儀：陸地外形取自 Natural Earth（公有領域）。地方和年代依本頁最下面列出的資料。

paras: Before printing spread, every book had to be copied by hand. A book survived only if people kept making new copies, and only if someone could read its language. When nobody copied a book for a few hundred years, it could be lost forever. So the question “who kept knowledge alive?” has many answers, in many languages.

Some of the most famous books were written in Greek. Plato taught at the Academy in Athens, and Euclid taught geometry in Alexandria about 300 BCE. Around 150 CE Ptolemy wrote his great book of astronomy there, and the physician Galen, born in Pergamum, wrote many books on medicine. In Constantinople, Byzantine scribes went on copying Greek books for centuries.

In India, scholars wrote in Sanskrit. In 628 the astronomer Brahmagupta treated zero as a number with its own rules. The numerals we use today, from 0 to 9, began in India in the 6th or 7th century. At the monastery of Nalanda, the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang learned Sanskrit; back in Chang'an from 645, he translated the scriptures he had brought into Chinese. In China, too, a Buddhist text printed in 868 is the oldest printed book that carries a date.

In Baghdad, the Abbasid caliphs kept a royal library called the House of Wisdom, and their court supported many scholars. Translators turned Persian, Indian, Syriac, and Greek works into Arabic, some of them close to the court. The mathematician al-Khwārizmī wrote about Indian numerals and about algebra. A generation later, Hunayn ibn Ishaq, a Christian physician, gathered Greek manuscripts and translated Galen into Syriac and Arabic.

Scholars did not only copy. Avicenna's Canon of Medicine, Ibn al-Haytham's book on optics, and al-Khwārizmī's algebra added new ideas. In Seville and Córdoba, Averroes wrote commentaries on Aristotle, which also survive in Hebrew translation. Then, in the 12th century, translators in Toledo, a city taken by the Christian king Alfonso VI in 1085, turned many of these Arabic books into Latin. Gerard of Cremona went there to learn Arabic just to read Ptolemy.

In Latin Europe, monks had been copying books in monastery writing rooms all along, and the new universities after 1100 were stimulated by Arabic learning. In West Africa, Timbuktu became a center of Islamic culture and learning. Knowledge survived because people in many places, speaking Greek, Syriac, Arabic, Persian, Sanskrit, Chinese, Hebrew, and Latin, kept copying, translating, and asking new questions.
paras_zh: 在印刷普及以前，每一本書都要用手抄。一本書要留下來，就要有人不斷抄新的，也要有人讀得懂它的語言。如果幾百年都沒有人抄，它就可能永遠失傳。所以「誰把知識保存下來？」有很多答案，用很多種語言。
有些最有名的書是用希臘文寫的。柏拉圖在雅典的學園教書，歐幾里得大約西元前 300 年在亞歷山卓教幾何。大約西元 150 年，托勒密在那裡寫了他的天文學大書；生於帕加馬的醫生蓋倫，寫了許多醫書。在君士坦丁堡，拜占庭的抄寫員好幾百年都繼續抄寫希臘文的書。
在印度，學者用梵文寫作。628 年，天文學家婆羅摩笈多把零當成一個數，替它定了運算規則。我們今天用的 0 到 9，六或七世紀起源於印度。中國的朝聖者玄奘在那爛陀寺學梵文；645 年回到長安以後，他把帶回來的佛經譯成中文。也是在中國，一部 868 年印的佛經，是現存有日期的印刷書裡最古老的。
在巴格達，阿拔斯王朝的哈里發有一座王室圖書館，叫「智慧宮」，宮廷也支持許多學者。譯者把波斯、印度、敘利亞和希臘的著作譯成阿拉伯文，有些和宮廷關係密切。數學家花拉子密寫了印度的數字和代數。一個世代以後，基督徒醫生侯奈因・伊本・伊斯哈格收集希臘文抄本，把蓋倫譯成敘利亞文和阿拉伯文。
學者不只是抄寫。阿維森納的《醫典》、伊本・海什木的光學、花拉子密的代數，都加進了新的想法。在塞維亞和科爾多瓦，阿威羅伊替亞里斯多德寫注釋，這些注釋也有希伯來文譯本留下來。到了十二世紀，在 1085 年被基督徒國王阿方索六世攻下的托雷多，譯者把許多阿拉伯文的書譯成拉丁文。克雷莫納的傑拉德就是為了讀托勒密，才到那裡學阿拉伯文。
在說拉丁文的歐洲，修士一直在修道院的抄寫室裡抄書；1100 年以後新的大學，也受到阿拉伯學術的刺激。在西非，廷巴克圖成為伊斯蘭文化與學術的中心。知識能留下來，是因為許多地方的人，說著希臘文、敘利亞文、阿拉伯文、波斯文、梵文、中文、希伯來文和拉丁文，一直抄寫、翻譯，也一直提出新的問題。
questions: Why could a book be lost forever before printing?
Name two languages that Galen's books passed through on their way to Latin Europe.
Give one example of a scholar who did more than copy older books.
answers: Every copy was made by hand. If nobody copied a book, or nobody could read its language, the last copies could wear out or be destroyed.
Greek (the original), Syriac, Arabic, and then Latin (any two).
Al-Khwārizmī (algebra), Ibn al-Haytham (optics), Avicenna (the Canon of Medicine), Averroes (commentaries on Aristotle), or Brahmagupta (rules for zero).

quiz.q: Why did books have to be copied again and again?
options: Before printing, every copy was made by hand and could wear out
Kings did not allow old books
Paper had not been invented anywhere
Only one person could read each book

quiz.q: Where did the numerals 0 to 9 begin?
Who was Hunayn ibn Ishaq?
options: A Christian physician in Baghdad who translated Greek books

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Athens and Alexandria light up. Most of what was written here was in Greek.
parts.text_zh: 雅典和亞歷山卓亮起來。這裡寫的東西大多是希臘文。

parts.text_en: Follow the Almagest from Greek into Arabic and then into Latin. Count the languages.
parts.text_zh: 跟著《天文學大成》，從希臘文到阿拉伯文，再到拉丁文。數一數有幾種語言。

parts.text_en: The numerals start in India, not in Greece. Watch where they go next.
parts.text_zh: 數字從印度出發，不是從希臘。看它們接下來到哪裡。

parts.text_en: By now places of learning stretch from Toledo and Timbuktu to Dunhuang and Chang'an. Which languages were spoken in each?
parts.text_zh: 這時學術的地方已經從托雷多、廷巴克圖延伸到敦煌和長安。每一個地方說的是哪一種語言？

lessons.parts_note_en: Then follow Avicenna's Canon and the Buddhist scriptures. How are their journeys different from the others?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著跟著阿維森納的《醫典》和佛經走。它們的旅程和其他幾本有什麼不一樣？

terms.en: Where Does This Word Come From?
terms.lead_en: Many English words for science and learning traveled the same road as the books. For each Chinese word, pick the older word it came from and its English form. There is no timer.
terms.lead_zh: 很多英文的科學和學術用字，和書走的是同一條路。每一個中文詞，選出它來源的那個比較古老的字，以及它的英文。不計時。
terms.ask_en: Which older word did it come from, and what is it in English?
terms.ask_zh: 它來自哪一個比較古老的字？英文是哪一個？

items.note_en: Al-jabr means “restoration,” and it was in the title of al-Khwārizmī's famous book. The Latin form became algebra.
items.note_zh: al-jabr 的意思是「還原」，出現在花拉子密那本有名的書的書名裡。拉丁文的寫法變成 algebra。

items.lang: Arabic form of a name, “from Khwarazm”
items.note_en: The word comes from a Latin form of the mathematician's own name, which means “from Khwarazm,” a region in Central Asia. Britannica says his name and his book title live on in algorithm and algebra.
items.note_zh: 這個字來自這位數學家名字的拉丁文寫法；他的名字意思是「來自花剌子模」（中亞的一個地區）。Britannica 說，他的名字和他的書名，留在 algorithm 和 algebra 這兩個字裡。

items.note_en: Ṣifr, itself a translation of Sanskrit śūnya, “empty,” passed into Medieval Latin as zephirum and into Italian, then English. The same Arabic word also gave English “cipher.”
items.note_zh: ṣifr 是梵文 śūnya（「空」）的翻譯；它先變成中世紀拉丁文的 zephirum，再到義大利文，然後到英文。同一個阿拉伯字也變成英文的 cipher。

items.note_en: Sanskrit jyā meant “bowstring” or “chord.” It became Arabic jayb, which also means “pocket,” and Latin translators turned that into sinus, which also meant “pocket,” “fold,” or “curve.”
items.note_zh: 梵文 jyā 是「弓弦」或「弦」的意思，變成阿拉伯文 jayb，而 jayb 剛好也有「口袋」的意思；拉丁文譯者就把它譯成 sinus（也是「口袋」「褶」或「彎」的意思）。

items.note_en: An Arabic form of the Greek word for “greatest.” Ptolemy's own title was “The Mathematical Arrangement.”
items.note_zh: 來自希臘文「最偉大的」的阿拉伯文寫法。托勒密自己取的書名是《數學彙編》。

items.note_en: The Arabic word took the article al-, “the,” and came from a Greek word for the art of alloying metals. Chemistry grew out of alchemy.
items.note_zh: 阿拉伯文的字加上冠詞 al-（「這個」），來自希臘文「熔合金屬的技藝」。化學（chemistry）就是從煉金術發展出來的。

items.note_en: Al-kuḥl first meant a fine powder (powdered antimony); later the word was used for a liquid made by distilling.
items.note_zh: al-kuḥl 原來是一種細粉（銻粉）；後來這個字被用來指蒸餾出來的液體。

items.note_en: Alchemists used al-iksīr for an alchemical preparation; it came from a Greek word for a drying powder for wounds.
items.note_zh: 煉金術士用 al-iksīr 稱呼一種煉金的藥劑；這個字來自希臘文裡一種敷傷口的乾粉。

items.note_en: Plato's school was at a place with a grove, a park, and a gymnasium sacred to the hero Academus, and it took his name.
items.note_zh: 柏拉圖的學校所在的地方，有樹林、公園，和一座獻給英雄阿卡德摩斯的體育場，學校就用了他的名字。

items.note_en: Mouseion means “shrine of the Muses.” The Museum of Alexandria was a research institute, and its Library was part of it.
items.note_zh: Mouseion 的意思是「繆思女神的殿堂」。亞歷山卓的博物院是一座研究機構，圖書館就是它的一部分。

terms.end_en: Words, like books, were passed from language to language. Some kept their sound, like algebra; some were translated by mistake, like sine.
terms.end_zh: 字和書一樣，從一種語言傳到另一種語言。有些保留了聲音，像 algebra；有些是誤譯出來的，像 sine。

when.lead_en: Put these moments in the story of knowledge in order, from earliest to most recent. Use the arrows or drag them. Then check your order.
when.lead_zh: 把這些知識故事裡的時刻，從最早排到最晚。用箭頭或拖曳來移動，然後檢查。

when.hint_zh: 想一想每一個時刻用的是哪一種語言。

timeline.en: Places of learning across the world
timeline.lead_en: Learning flourished in different places at different times. Notice how Baghdad's great age comes between Alexandria's and Toledo's.

timeline.idle_zh: 點一條長條或一個菱形，讀出它的年代。

tips.zh: 柏拉圖的學園延續了九百多年，到西元 529 年。

how_we_know.eyebrow: How Do We Know? · 我們怎麼知道？
how_we_know.en: Old copies, book lists, and hidden words
how_we_know.zh: 古老的抄本、書目，和藏起來的字
how_we_know.lead_en: Historians trace a book's journey by looking at the copies that survive and the lists people made of books.
how_we_know.lead_zh: 歷史學家看留下來的抄本，以及人們編的書目，來追查一本書的旅程。

items.en: Notes at the end of a book
items.limit_en: Many copies have no note at all, and many early printed editions of translations leave out the translator's name, so historians have to argue about who translated what.
items.limit_zh: 很多抄本根本沒有題記；許多早期印刷的譯本也沒寫譯者是誰，所以歷史學家還要爭論誰譯了什麼。
items.src: British Library, International Dunhuang Programme; Britannica, “Gerard of Cremona”
items.text_en: Many manuscripts end with a note, called a colophon, saying who made the copy and when. The Diamond Sutra from Dunhuang has one: it was made for free distribution by Wang Jie on behalf of his parents, on a day equal to May 11, 868.
items.text_zh: 很多抄本在最後有一段題記，寫著誰抄的、什麼時候抄的。敦煌的《金剛經》就有一段：一位叫 Wang Jie 的人，為了父母而印、讓大家免費取得，日期相當於 868 年 5 月 11 日。

items.limit_en: Most of the books on the list have since been lost. A list tells us a book existed, not what was in it.
items.limit_zh: 書目上的書，後來大多已經失傳。書目告訴我們有過這本書，但不告訴我們書裡寫了什麼。
items.src: Britannica, “Ibn al-Nadim”
items.text_en: In 988 a bookseller, Ibn al-Nadim, compiled the Fihrist, an index of the Arabic books of his time, from language study to alchemy.
items.text_zh: 988 年，書商伊本・納迪姆編了《書目》（Fihrist），列出他那個時代的阿拉伯文書，從語言學到煉金術都有。

items.limit_en: Most scraped-off texts are lost for good. We only know about the ones that happened to survive and be studied.
items.limit_zh: 大部分被刮掉的字，已經永遠消失了。我們只知道剛好留下來、又被研究過的那些。
items.src: Smithsonian Magazine, “Reading Between the Lines”
items.text_en: Parchment was expensive, so old writing was sometimes scraped off and the page reused. A copy of works by Archimedes made in the 900s was turned into a prayer book in 1229 at a monastery near Bethlehem. After it was sold in 1998, scientists used ultraviolet light and X-rays to read the Archimedes text underneath.
items.text_zh: 羊皮紙很貴，所以舊的字有時會被刮掉，紙再拿來用。一部 900 年代的阿基米德抄本，1229 年在伯利恆附近的修道院被改成祈禱書。1998 年它被賣出以後，科學家用紫外光和 X 光，讀出了底下阿基米德的字。

views.zh: 關於保存知識的四個問題
views.lead_en: Historians agree that translation mattered enormously, but they disagree on some details. Here are four questions, with the views set side by side.
views.lead_zh: 歷史學家都同意翻譯非常重要，但對一些細節看法不同。下面是四個問題，各種說法並列。
views.rule_en: Notice that even good encyclopedias sometimes give more than one answer.
views.rule_zh: 留意：連很好的百科全書，有時也會給出不只一個答案。

items.topic_en: What was the House of Wisdom?
items.topic_zh: 智慧宮是什麼樣的地方？

sides.en: Britannica's short summary at the top of its article calls it a “royal library and translation center” of the Abbasid caliphs.
sides.zh: Britannica 條目開頭的簡介，把它叫做阿拔斯王朝哈里發的「王室圖書館兼翻譯中心」。

sides.label_en: A royal library; translation happened elsewhere
sides.label_zh: 王室圖書館；翻譯在別的地方
sides.en: Britannica's full article says translation, almost all from Persian, was not one of its main jobs, and that the translation of Greek works, including Hunayn's, took place elsewhere. The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy agrees that it cannot be viewed as an institutional center for translating Greek works, though the first translators had close ties to the court.
sides.zh: Britannica 的正文說，翻譯（幾乎都是從波斯文）不是它主要的工作；希臘著作的翻譯，包括侯奈因的，是在別的地方進行的。《史丹佛哲學百科》也說，它不能看成翻譯希臘著作的正式機構，不過最早的那些譯者和宮廷關係很密切。
sides.src: Britannica, “Bayt al-Hikmah”; Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Greek Sources in Arabic and Islamic Philosophy”

items.note_en: Britannica's full article and the Stanford Encyclopedia agree on the second view. Either way, the caliphs' court and Baghdad's elites supported translators.
items.note_zh: Britannica 的正文和《史丹佛哲學百科》都支持第二種看法。不管哪一種，哈里發的宮廷和巴格達的上層人士都支持譯者。

items.topic_en: Why did the Abbasid court support books and translation?
items.topic_zh: 阿拔斯王朝的宮廷為什麼支持書和翻譯？

sides.en: For the royal library, Britannica points to Persian heritage: possibly modeled on Sasanian practice, it specialized in Persian knowledge and showed the dynasty continuing that heritage.
sides.zh: 就王室圖書館來說，Britannica 指向波斯的傳統：它可能仿照薩珊王朝的做法，專精波斯的知識，表現出這個王朝延續那份傳統。

sides.en: For the translations of Greek works, the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy points to al-Maʾmūn's new view of Islam and of the caliph's role, and to the growing interest of educated elites in the secular sciences.
sides.zh: 就希臘著作的翻譯來說，《史丹佛哲學百科》指出，是馬蒙對伊斯蘭和哈里發角色的新看法，加上受過教育的上層人士對世俗學問越來越有興趣。
sides.src: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Greek Sources in Arabic and Islamic Philosophy”

items.note_en: The two answers are about different kinds of books, and they can overlap: rulers, physicians, astronomers, and officials all had their own uses for these books.
items.note_zh: 兩個答案談的是不同種類的書，也可以同時成立：統治者、醫生、天文學家和官員，對這些書各有各的用處。

items.topic_en: When was the Library of Alexandria destroyed?
items.topic_zh: 亞歷山卓圖書館是什麼時候被毀的？

sides.en: One account in Britannica says the main library was destroyed in a civil war in 48 BCE, and a smaller “daughter library” in 391 CE.
sides.zh: Britannica 的一種說法是，主圖書館在西元前 48 年的內戰中被毀，另一座較小的「分館」在西元 391 年被毀。

sides.en: Another passage in the same encyclopedia says the library was destroyed in a civil war under the Roman emperor Aurelian, in the late 3rd century CE.
sides.zh: 同一部百科的另一段說，圖書館是在三世紀後期羅馬皇帝奧勒良時的內戰中被毀的。

items.note_en: The sources do not agree, and the library probably declined in more than one stage rather than vanishing in a single fire.
items.note_zh: 資料彼此不一致；圖書館大概是分好幾個階段衰落的，不是一場大火就消失。

items.topic_en: When did the Hindu-Arabic numerals reach Europe?
items.topic_zh: 印度—阿拉伯數字什麼時候傳到歐洲？

sides.en: Britannica says the scholar Gerbert, later Pope Sylvester II, introduced an abacus with counters bearing Arabic numerals around 1000 CE, though very few people knew of it.
sides.zh: Britannica 說，學者熱爾貝（後來的教宗西爾維斯特二世）大約在西元 1000 年用了一種算盤，算子上刻著阿拉伯數字；不過知道的人很少。

sides.en: Britannica's article on the numerals says they reached Europe through Middle Eastern mathematicians, especially al-Khwārizmī and al-Kindī, about the 12th century, and Fibonacci's book of 1202 did much to spread them.
sides.zh: Britannica 談數字的條目說，它們大約在十二世紀，透過中東的數學家（特別是花拉子密和金迪）傳到歐洲；費波那契 1202 年的書，大大幫助了它們的傳播。

items.note_en: Both can be true: a few scholars knew the numerals early, but most people in Europe went on using Roman numerals for a long time.
items.note_zh: 兩種說法可以同時成立：少數學者很早就知道這些數字，但歐洲大多數人還用了很久的羅馬數字。

phrases.en: Eight sentences for talking about knowledge
phrases.lead_en: These sentences help you describe how ideas were saved and passed on. Listen, repeat, then make your own sentence with the words in bold.
phrases.lead_zh: 這八句幫你描述想法怎麼被保存、怎麼傳下去。先聽、再跟著唸，然後用粗體的字自己造一句。

rows.en: The book was translated from Greek into Arabic.
rows.html: The book was translated from Greek into Arabic.
rows.zh: 這本書從希臘文被譯成阿拉伯文。
rows.note_en: be translated from A into B: put into another language

rows.en: Every copy was made by hand.
rows.html: Every copy was made by hand.
rows.zh: 每一份都是手抄的。
rows.note_en: by hand: without a machine

rows.en: Monks preserved old books.
rows.html: Monks preserved old books.
rows.zh: 修士保存了古老的書。
rows.note_en: preserve: keep safe for the future

rows.en: Some of Galen's books were lost in Greek.
rows.html: Some of Galen's books were lost in Greek.
rows.zh: 蓋倫有些希臘文原書失傳了。
rows.note_en: be lost: no longer exist

rows.en: Al-Khwārizmī built on Indian ideas.
rows.html: Al-Khwārizmī built on Indian ideas.
rows.zh: 花拉子密以印度的想法為基礎。
rows.note_en: build on: use as a starting point

rows.en: Ibn al-Haytham questioned Ptolemy's models.
rows.html: Ibn al-Haytham questioned Ptolemy's models.
rows.zh: 伊本・海什木質疑托勒密的模型。
rows.note_en: question: ask whether something is right

rows.en: English borrowed the word algebra from Arabic.
rows.html: English borrowed the word algebra from Arabic.
rows.zh: 英文從阿拉伯文借了 algebra 這個字。
rows.note_en: borrow A from B: take a word into your language

rows.en: Scholars passed on what they had learned.
rows.html: Scholars passed on what they had learned.
rows.zh: 學者把學到的東西傳了下去。
rows.note_en: pass on: give to the next person

taiwan_then.eyebrow: Taiwan at That Time · 那時候的台灣
taiwan_then.lead_en: Before 1600 the peoples of Taiwan kept and passed on knowledge through speech, skills, and customs rather than books.
taiwan_then.lead_zh: 1600 年以前，台灣的人群不是用書，而是用語言、技術和習俗，保存、傳下知識。
taiwan_then.intro_en: Archaeologists in Taiwan give dates as “years ago.” About 2,000 years ago is roughly the beginning of the Common Era.
taiwan_then.intro_zh: 台灣的考古學家用「距今幾年」說年代。距今大約兩千年，差不多是西元紀年開始的時候。

facts.en: The museum says the Shisanhang people had the skill to smelt iron themselves. A skill like this lives only if it is taught to the next generation.
facts.zh: 史前館說，十三行文化的人「有自行煉鐵的技術」。這樣的技術，要教給下一代才能留下來。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

facts.en: In the winter of 1602–1603 the Ming scholar Chen Di visited the southwestern coast and wrote about the Indigenous peoples he met there. He noted that they counted a month from full moon to full moon and ten months as a year. He called them by an outsider's word, 夷, and found it strange that they kept no written calendar; but a calendar kept by the moon and by memory is a way of knowing too.
facts.zh: 1602 年冬到 1603 年初，明朝的陳第到過台灣西南海岸，寫下他遇到的原住民族。他記下他們「計月圓為一月，十月為一年」。他用明代外人的字眼「夷」稱呼他們，也覺得他們沒有寫下來的曆法很奇怪；可是看月亮、靠記憶的曆法，也是一種知識。
facts.src: 陳第〈東番記〉

facts.en: Chen Di also wrote that the people he met kept track of trade by tying knots in cord. He was an outsider, and his record shows what he noticed, not everything they knew.
facts.zh: 陳第也寫到，他遇到的人「交易，結繩以識」。他是外來的人，他的紀錄只代表他看到的，不是他們知道的全部。
facts.src: 陳第〈東番記〉

facts.en: In the 1600s missionaries tried to teach the Siraya, a Pingpu people, to write their own language with the Roman alphabet. The Siraya kept using it for contracts; the last known document dates from 1818 (Lesson 10).
facts.zh: 1600 年代，傳教士嘗試教平埔族群的西拉雅人用羅馬字母寫自己的語言。西拉雅人一直用它寫契約，留下的「新港文書」最晚的一件寫於 1818 年（第十課）。
facts.src: 中央研究院臺灣史研究所檔案館〈研究成果問與答〉

links.en: Taiwan's Story: Why Did the Dutch Build a Fort in Tainan?
links.zh: 台灣歷史：荷蘭人為什麼在台南蓋城？

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Evidence · 證據背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A manuscript hunter, a scholar who moved for one book, a hidden Archimedes, and a printed sutra
culture_cards.title_zh: 找抄本的人、為一本書搬家的學者、藏起來的阿基米德，和一部印出來的經
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about people who kept books alive.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事：讓書活下來的人。

cards.body_en: Hunayn ibn Ishaq, a Christian of the Church of the East, became chief physician to the caliph al-Mutawakkil. He traveled to Syria, Palestine, and Egypt looking for Greek manuscripts, and ran a school of translators in Baghdad with his students.
cards.body_zh: 侯奈因・伊本・伊斯哈格是東方教會的基督徒，後來成為哈里發穆塔瓦基勒的首席御醫。他到敘利亞、巴勒斯坦和埃及找希臘文的抄本，和學生在巴格達辦了一所翻譯學校。

cards.body_en: Gerard of Cremona, from northern Italy, wanted to read Ptolemy's Almagest, which did not exist in Latin. He went to Toledo, learned Arabic, finished his translation in 1175, and stayed there for the rest of his life. About 80 translations are credited to him.
cards.body_zh: 義大利北部的克雷莫納的傑拉德，想讀托勒密的《天文學大成》，可是那時沒有拉丁文本。他到托雷多學阿拉伯文，1175 年譯完，然後一輩子留在那裡。大約有 80 部譯作歸在他名下。

cards.zh: 祈禱書底下的阿基米德
cards.body_en: In the 900s a Byzantine scribe copied works of Archimedes onto parchment. In 1229 a priest at a monastery near Bethlehem scraped the pages and reused them for a prayer book. Modern scientists used ultraviolet light and X-rays to read the faint lines underneath.
cards.body_zh: 900 年代，一位拜占庭的抄寫員把阿基米德的著作抄在羊皮紙上。1229 年，伯利恆附近一座修道院的教士把紙頁刮乾淨、拿去寫祈禱書。現代的科學家用紫外光和 X 光，讀出了底下淡淡的字跡。

cards.body_en: A man named Wang Jie had the Diamond Sutra printed from carved wooden blocks, on behalf of his parents and for free distribution. One scroll, about five meters long, was sealed in a cave with tens of thousands of other scrolls and found again in the early 20th century.
cards.body_zh: 一位叫 Wang Jie 的人，為了父母，也為了讓大家免費取得，用雕刻的木版印《金剛經》。其中一卷長約五公尺，和好幾萬件其他的卷子一起被封在洞窟裡，到二十世紀初才又被發現。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum for social studies (October 2018).
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要社會領域（民國 107 年 10 月）。

items.area: 國中・古代文化的遺產
items.area_en: Junior high · the heritage of ancient cultures
items.text: 伊斯蘭教的起源與發展。
items.note_en: The explanation asks students to discuss how the world religions shaped cultures. The translation movement in Baghdad is part of the culture of the Islamic world.
items.note_zh: 課綱的說明建議「討論普世宗教所形塑的文化樣貌及世界版圖」。巴格達的翻譯運動，就是伊斯蘭世界文化的一部分。

items.area: 國中・近代世界的變革
items.area_en: Junior high · changes in the modern world
items.text: 文藝復興。
items.note_en: The explanation suggests discussing the origins of the Renaissance. The Latin translations from Toledo and elsewhere are part of the background.
items.note_zh: 課綱的說明建議討論「文藝復興的起源及其革命性的影響」。托雷多等地的拉丁文譯本，就是它的背景之一。

myths.myth_en: Europe forgot all its learning in the “Dark Ages.”
myths.myth_zh: 歐洲在「黑暗時代」把學問全忘了。
myths.fact_en: Monks kept copying books in monastery writing rooms, and Byzantine scribes kept copying Greek. Britannica notes that European universities after 1100 were stimulated by Arabic scholars.
myths.fact_zh: 修士一直在修道院的抄寫室裡抄書，拜占庭的抄寫員也一直抄希臘文的書。Britannica 指出，1100 年以後歐洲的大學，受到阿拉伯學者的刺激。

myths.myth_en: Arabic numerals were invented by Arabs.
myths.myth_zh: 阿拉伯數字是阿拉伯人發明的。
myths.fact_en: They began in India in the 6th or 7th century and reached Europe through Arabic writers. That is why they are also called Hindu-Arabic numerals.
myths.fact_zh: 它們在六或七世紀起源於印度，再透過阿拉伯文的作者傳到歐洲。所以它們也叫「印度—阿拉伯數字」。

myths.myth_en: Scholars in the Islamic world only kept Greek books safe.
myths.myth_zh: 伊斯蘭世界的學者只是把希臘的書保管好。
myths.fact_en: They also added new work: al-Khwārizmī's algebra in Baghdad, Ibn al-Haytham's correct model of how we see, and Avicenna's Canon of Medicine, which was a textbook in Europe until the mid-17th century.
myths.fact_zh: 他們也做出新的研究：花拉子密在巴格達寫的代數、伊本・海什木對視覺的正確解釋，以及阿維森納的《醫典》（在歐洲一直當教科書，到十七世紀中期）。

myths.myth_en: The Library of Alexandria burned in one great fire.
myths.myth_zh: 亞歷山卓圖書館是在一場大火裡燒光的。
myths.fact_en: The sources disagree. Britannica itself gives a civil war in 48 BCE, another in the late 3rd century CE, and the loss of a daughter library in 391 CE. A story that appeared in the 13th century blamed the Arab general ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, but Britannica says it is now considered a fabrication.
myths.fact_zh: 資料彼此不一致。Britannica 自己就寫了西元前 48 年的內戰、西元三世紀後期的另一場內戰，以及 391 年一座分館的毀滅。十三世紀出現一個故事，把責任推給阿拉伯將領阿慕爾・伊本・阿斯；Britannica 說，這個說法現在被認為是捏造的。

tricks.body_en: Before printing, a book lived only as long as people copied it.
tricks.body_zh: 印刷普及以前，一本書只有在有人抄的時候才活著。

tricks.title_zh: 希臘文 → 阿拉伯文 → 拉丁文
tricks.body_en: Many books reached Latin Europe by way of Arabic.
tricks.body_zh: 很多書是經過阿拉伯文，才到說拉丁文的歐洲。

tricks.body_en: Translators and scholars also corrected and added new ideas.
tricks.body_zh: 譯者和學者也修正錯誤、加進新的想法。

tricks.body_en: Christians, Muslims, Jews, Buddhists, and others all helped.
tricks.body_zh: 基督徒、穆斯林、猶太人、佛教徒和其他人都出了力。

materials.en: One short paragraph about a scientific idea, in English
materials.zh: 一小段英文的科學說明

materials.en: Paper and pencils; one group per “language” (English, Chinese, simple English)
materials.zh: 紙筆；每一種「語言」一組（英文、中文、簡單英文）

steps.en: Group 1 copies the paragraph by hand in two minutes and passes it on.
steps.zh: 第一組在兩分鐘內用手抄寫這段話，然後傳下去。

steps.en: Group 2 translates it into Chinese. Group 3 translates the Chinese back into simple English.
steps.zh: 第二組把它譯成中文；第三組再把中文譯回簡單的英文。

steps.en: Compare the last version with the first. What was lost, and what was made clearer?
steps.zh: 比較最後一版和第一版：少了什麼？哪裡變得更清楚？

steps.en: Discuss in English: “The idea was translated from … into …” and “Something was lost when …”
steps.zh: 用英文討論：「The idea was translated from … into …」和「Something was lost when …」

activities.tip_en: Real translators like Hunayn compared several manuscripts before translating, to avoid copying mistakes. Ask students how they could do the same.
activities.tip_zh: 像侯奈因這樣的譯者，會先比對好幾份抄本，避免抄錯。問學生：他們可以怎麼做到一樣的事？

materials.en: The 3D globe and the word game in this lesson
materials.zh: 這一課的 3D 地球儀和字的小遊戲

materials.en: A dictionary that gives word origins
materials.zh: 一本有字源的字典

steps.en: In pairs, choose two words from the word game.
steps.zh: 兩人一組，從字的小遊戲裡選兩個字。

steps.en: On the globe, find a city where each word's language was spoken.
steps.zh: 在地球儀上，找出這個字的語言當時在哪一個城市說。

steps.en: Look up one more English word that came from Arabic or Greek.
steps.zh: 再查一個從阿拉伯文或希臘文來的英文字。

steps.en: Write two sentences with “borrowed … from” and “was translated from … into.”
steps.zh: 用 borrowed … from 和 was translated from … into 寫兩句英文。

activities.tip_en: Remind students that the stops on the globe show where a book changed language, as one likely path.
activities.tip_zh: 提醒學生：地球儀上的每一站，表示一本書換語言的地方，是一條可能的路。

links.en: What Was Life Like in a Castle?
links.zh: 住在城堡裡是什麼樣子？
links.note_en: Daily life in medieval Europe.
links.note_zh: 中世紀歐洲的日常生活。

links.en: How Did Christianity and Islam Begin and Spread?
links.zh: 基督宗教和伊斯蘭教怎麼開始、怎麼傳開？
links.note_en: Baghdad, Córdoba, and Hunayn ibn Ishaq first appear here.
links.note_zh: 巴格達、科爾多瓦和侯奈因，在這一課第一次出現。

links.en: What Traveled Along the Silk Road?
links.zh: 絲路上走的是什麼？
links.note_en: Paper, which made books cheaper, traveled west to Baghdad.
links.note_zh: 讓書變便宜的紙，往西傳到巴格達。

links.en: Aristotle
links.zh: 亞里斯多德
links.note_en: The philosopher whose books traveled the farthest in this lesson.
links.note_zh: 這一課裡，書走得最遠的哲學家。

links.en: Why Do We Count in Tens?
links.zh: 為什麼我們十個一數？
links.note_en: The number system that traveled from India.
links.note_zh: 從印度傳出來的記數方法。

lessons.sources_note_en: Checked November 2026. What the House of Wisdom was, why the caliphs supported translation, when the Library of Alexandria was destroyed, and when the numerals reached Europe are debated; where they are, the lesson gives more than one view
lessons.sources_note_zh: 2026 年 11 月查證。智慧宮是什麼樣的地方、哈里發為什麼支持翻譯、亞歷山卓圖書館什麼時候被毀，以及數字什麼時候傳到歐洲，都有不同說法；遇到有爭論的地方，課文寫出不只一種說法

sources.en: The House of Wisdom: royal library; translation mostly from Persian and not a main function; Greek translation took place elsewhere; Hārūn al-Rashīd and al-Maʾmūn; destroyed in 1258
sources.zh: 智慧宮：王室圖書館；翻譯幾乎都從波斯文、而且不是主要工作；希臘著作在別處翻譯；哈倫・拉希德與馬蒙；1258 年被毀

sources.en: The House of Wisdom as a court library; motives of the translation movement; Syriac Christian translators
sources.zh: 智慧宮是宮廷圖書館；翻譯運動的動機；敘利亞基督徒譯者
sources.src: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Greek Sources in Arabic and Islamic Philosophy”

sources.en: Al-Khwārizmī: Hindu-Arabic numerals and algebra; his name and book title in algorithm and algebra
sources.zh: 花拉子密：印度—阿拉伯數字與代數；algorithm、algebra 兩個字

sources.en: Hunayn ibn Ishaq: Christian of the Church of the East, chief physician to al-Mutawakkil, gathered Greek manuscripts, translated Galen, Plato, and Aristotle
sources.zh: 侯奈因：東方教會的基督徒、穆塔瓦基勒的首席御醫、收集希臘文抄本、翻譯蓋倫、柏拉圖、亞里斯多德

sources.en: Gerard of Cremona: went to Toledo to read the Almagest; Latin Almagest 1175; about 80 translations
sources.zh: 傑拉德：到托雷多讀《天文學大成》；1175 年拉丁文譯本；大約 80 部譯作

sources.en: Adelard of Bath translated an Arabic version of Euclid into Latin
sources.zh: 巴斯的阿德拉德把阿拉伯文版的歐幾里得譯成拉丁文

sources.en: Euclid in Alexandria about 300 BCE; the Elements
sources.zh: 歐幾里得大約西元前 300 年在亞歷山卓；《幾何原本》

sources.en: The Almagest: about 150 CE; Arabic in the late 8th and early 9th centuries; Latin by Gerard; the name from the Greek for “greatest”
sources.zh: 《天文學大成》：大約西元 150 年；八世紀末到九世紀初譯成阿拉伯文；傑拉德的拉丁文本；名字來自希臘文「最偉大的」

sources.en: Galen, born 129 in Pergamum, died about 216
sources.zh: 蓋倫，129 年生於帕加馬，約 216 年去世

sources.en: Brahmagupta: book of 628, zero as a number, Arabic translation in Baghdad about 771
sources.zh: 婆羅摩笈多：628 年的書、零是一個數、約 771 年在巴格達譯成阿拉伯文

sources.en: Hindu-Arabic numerals: from India in the 6th or 7th century, to Europe about the 12th century
sources.zh: 印度—阿拉伯數字：六或七世紀起源於印度，大約十二世紀傳到歐洲

sources.en: Fibonacci: studied calculation in Bugia; Liber abaci (“Book of the Abacus”) 1202
sources.zh: 費波那契：在貝賈亞（布吉亞）學計算；1202 年《算盤書》

sources.en: Gerbert (Sylvester II) and an abacus with Arabic numerals around 1000; monks copying texts; universities after 1100 stimulated by Arabic scholars
sources.zh: 熱爾貝（思維二世）約 1000 年用刻著阿拉伯數字的算盤；修士抄書；1100 年以後的大學受阿拉伯學者刺激

sources.en: Averroes: born Córdoba 1126; commentaries on Aristotle 1169–1195; Hebrew translations; influence on Aquinas
sources.zh: 阿威羅伊：1126 年生於科爾多瓦；1169–1195 年寫亞里斯多德注釋；影響阿奎那

sources.en: Michael Scot in Toledo in 1217; translations of Aristotle and probably Averroes
sources.zh: 麥可・史考特 1217 年在托雷多；翻譯亞里斯多德，大概也譯了阿威羅伊

sources.en: Avicenna (980–1037): the Canon of Medicine, a textbook in Europe until the mid-17th century
sources.zh: 阿維森納（980–1037）：《醫典》，在歐洲當教科書到十七世紀中期

sources.en: Ibn al-Haytham: Optics, a correct model of vision; Doubts about Ptolemy

lessons.title: What Was Life Like in a Castle?
lessons.title_zh: 住在城堡裡是什麼樣子？
lessons.blurb_en: Watch a castle grow in 3D, from a mound of earth with a wooden tower to two rings of stone walls, and click each part to see what it was for. Find out who lived and worked there, and compare castles with a crusader fortress in Syria and the great stone walls of Great Zimbabwe.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 模型上看一座城堡長大：從一座有木塔的土丘，到兩圈石牆；點每一個部分，看它是做什麼用的。認識住在、工作在城堡裡的人，也和敘利亞的十字軍城堡、大辛巴威的大石牆比一比。
lessons.big_idea_en: A castle was not only a fortress. It was the home of a lord and the center of a small society: the lord's household, soldiers, craftspeople, and servants, and the peasants of the nearby villages, all tied together by land and by duties to one another. Castles changed as weapons and times changed.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 城堡不只是要塞。它是領主的家，也是一個小社會的中心：領主的家人、士兵、工匠、僕人，以及附近村子的農民，靠土地和彼此的義務連在一起。城堡跟著武器和時代一起改變。

lab.how_en: Press “Watch it grow,” or choose a stage, and watch the castle change from earth and timber to two rings of stone walls. Click any part of the castle, or a button below, to read what it was for. Drag to turn the model.
lab.how_zh: 按「看它長大」，或選一個階段，看城堡從泥土和木頭，變成兩圈石牆。點城堡的任何一個部分，或下面的按鈕，讀它是做什麼用的。拖曳可以轉動模型。

stages.text_en: A high mound of earth, the motte, was ringed by a ditch and topped by the lord's stronghold, often a timber tower. At its foot, an enclosed yard, the bailey, held other buildings and animals, behind a wooden fence. In England, well over 500 castles were raised in the 20 years after the Norman Conquest of 1066, to control the newly conquered land; local people were forced to help build them.
stages.text_zh: 一座高高的土丘（motte）四周挖了壕溝，上面是領主的堡壘，常常是一座木塔。土丘腳下有一個圍起來的院子（bailey），在木柵欄後面放其他的房子和牲畜。在英格蘭，1066 年諾曼人征服以後的二十年裡，蓋了五百多座城堡，用來控制剛征服的土地；當地人被強迫來幫忙蓋。

stages.text_en: Timber burned and rotted, so many lords built in stone. The keep, or donjon, became the strongest part of the castle: in a siege the whole garrison could fall back to it. It had a well, rooms for the lord, and stores for a long siege. Examples are Loches in France (about 1020) and Rochester in England (about 1130).
stages.text_zh: 木頭會燒、會爛，所以很多領主改用石頭蓋。主塔（keep，也叫 donjon）成了城堡最堅固的地方：被圍困的時候，整個守軍都可以退進去。裡面有井、領主住的房間，以及撐過長期圍困的存糧。例如法國的洛什（大約 1020 年）和英格蘭的羅徹斯特（大約 1130 年）。

stages.en: Stone walls, towers, and a gatehouse
stages.text_en: The wooden fence of the bailey was replaced by stone curtain walls with towers. A moat, crossed by a drawbridge, protected the gate, and the gateway was defended by portcullises and heavy doors. The hall and chapel stood in the inner yard, and the keep became the last line of defense.
stages.text_zh: 院子的木柵欄換成了有塔樓的石造城牆（curtain wall）。護城河上有吊橋保護城門，門洞裡還有吊閘和厚重的門。大廳和禮拜堂蓋在裡面的院子，主塔變成最後一道防線。

stages.text_en: In a concentric castle, one ring of walls stood inside another. UNESCO says Beaumaris and Harlech in Wales combine the late-13th-century double-wall design with a central plan, and calls them masterpieces of James of St George, King Edward I's architect. Edward built castles to control newly conquered north Wales, and the Welsh rose up against English rule in 1294.
stages.text_zh: 同心圓城堡是一圈城牆套著另一圈城牆。聯合國教科文組織說，威爾斯的博馬里斯和哈萊克，結合了十三世紀後期的雙層城牆和置中的平面，是愛德華一世的建築師聖喬治的詹姆斯的傑作。愛德華蓋城堡是為了控制剛征服的北威爾斯；威爾斯人在 1294 年起來反抗英格蘭的統治。
stages.src: UNESCO, Castles and Town Walls of King Edward in Gwynedd; English Heritage

parts.what_en: Britannica says early castles in France had a high mound encircled by a ditch. In the model one ditch goes around everything.
parts.what_zh: Britannica 說，法國早期的城堡有一座四周挖了壕溝的高土丘。模型裡用一道溝把全部圍起來。

parts.what_en: An artificial mound made of layers of earth and stone. English Heritage says a team of about 100 men needed around forty days to build one.
parts.what_zh: 用一層一層的泥土和石頭堆起來的人造土丘。English Heritage 說，大約一百個人，要花四十天左右才堆得好一座。
parts.src: English Heritage, “How to spot a castle hiding in plain sight”

parts.what_en: The lord's stronghold on top of the mound. The Normans usually built a rectangular timber tower here.
parts.what_zh: 土丘上面領主的堡壘。諾曼人通常在這裡蓋一座長方形的木塔。
parts.src: English Heritage, “How to spot a castle hiding in plain sight”

parts.what_en: A fence of sharpened wooden stakes around the yard. It was quick to build, but it could burn and rot.
parts.what_zh: 繞著院子、用削尖的木樁做的圍欄。蓋起來很快，可是會燒、會爛。

parts.what_en: The large main room of the lord's living quarters. Britannica lists the hall with the chapel and domestic offices in the inner yard, and a 1396 record at Portchester Castle lists a new hall, kitchen, chambers, and offices. (In the model it is timber at first and stone later, a guess for illustration.)
parts.what_zh: 領主居住區的大房間。Britannica 把大廳和禮拜堂、服務的房舍列在裡面的院子；1396 年波特切斯特城堡的一份工程紀錄，也列出新蓋的大廳、廚房、臥房和辦事的房間。（模型裡一開始畫成木造、後來石造，是示意的推想。）

parts.what_en: The strongest part of the castle. In a siege the garrison fell back to it, and it held a well, private rooms, and stores. Later, it was often no longer where the lord lived, but it was still the last line of defense.
parts.what_zh: 城堡最堅固的地方。被圍困的時候，守軍退進去；裡面有井、私人的房間和存糧。後來它常常不再是領主住的地方，但仍然是最後一道防線。

parts.what_en: Britannica notes that the keep had a well, so that it could hold out in a long siege.
parts.what_zh: Britannica 指出，主塔裡有井，好撐過長期的圍城。

parts.what_en: A chapel for worship. Britannica says that after the Third Crusade the hall and the chapel were built in the inner yard.
parts.what_zh: 做禮拜的小教堂。Britannica 說，第三次十字軍以後，大廳和禮拜堂蓋在裡面的院子。

parts.what_en: Kitchens and service rooms. Britannica lists “domestic offices” with the hall and chapel, and the 1396 Portchester record lists a kitchen among the new buildings.
parts.what_zh: 廚房和服務用的房間。Britannica 把「服務的房舍」和大廳、禮拜堂列在一起；1396 年波特切斯特的紀錄，也把廚房列在新蓋的房子裡。

parts.what_en: A stone wall that replaced the wooden fence around the yard.
parts.what_zh: 取代院子木柵欄的石牆。

parts.what_en: Masonry towers built along the walls, when stone replaced the wooden fence around the yard.
parts.what_zh: 院子的木柵欄換成石頭以後，沿著城牆蓋的石造塔樓。

parts.what_en: The gate was the weakest point, so it was heavily defended, with portcullises (sliding grilles of oak plated with iron), doors, and openings for dropping things on attackers.
parts.what_zh: 城門是最弱的地方，所以防守得最嚴密：有吊閘（用鐵包著的橡木格柵，可以上下滑動）、門，以及可以往下丟東西攻擊敵人的開口。

parts.what_en: A ditch around the walls. Britannica says the outer wall was generally defended by one or more lines of moats.
parts.what_zh: 城牆外面的溝。Britannica 說，外牆通常由一道或好幾道護城河來防守。

parts.what_en: A bridge over the moat that could be raised or drawn back from inside, so that the moat could not be crossed.
parts.what_zh: 跨過護城河的橋，可以從裡面拉起來或收回去，讓人過不了河。

parts.what_en: A second ring of walls and towers outside the main wall. UNESCO calls this double-wall, concentric plan characteristic of late 13th-century military architecture.
parts.what_zh: 主牆外面的第二圈牆和塔。聯合國教科文組織說，這種雙層、同心圓的設計，是十三世紀後期軍事建築的特色。
parts.src: UNESCO, Castles and Town Walls of King Edward in Gwynedd

lab.numbers_note_en: This is one imagined castle that passes through all four stages. Real castles were built in many shapes, and many never had all four.
lab.numbers_note_zh: 這是一座想像的城堡，四個階段都走過一遍。真實的城堡形狀各式各樣，很多也沒有經過這四個階段。
lab.scale_en: A simplified model, not to scale and not any one real castle. Heights and distances are only to show how the parts fit together.
lab.scale_zh: 簡化的模型，不照比例，也不是哪一座真實的城堡。高度和距離只是用來表示各部分怎麼組合在一起。
lab.credit_html: Model: drawn for this lesson from the descriptions in the sources listed at the bottom of the page. 模型：依本頁最下面列出的資料，為這一課畫的示意。

paras: Britannica describes the castle as a medieval stronghold that was generally the home of the king or lord of the land around it. Strongholds with the same purpose were built in many parts of the world, including Japan and India. This lesson looks mostly at castles in western Europe, where they developed rapidly from the 9th century, and then at great stone buildings elsewhere in the same centuries.

The first castles were often made of earth and timber. A mound, the motte, was ringed by a ditch and topped by a tower, and a fenced yard, the bailey, lay at its foot. After the Norman Conquest of England in 1066, well over 500 castles were raised in twenty years to control the conquered land. English Heritage notes that local people were forced to help build them.

Timber could burn and rot, so lords rebuilt in stone. The keep became the strongest part of the castle, with a well, private rooms, and stores. Wooden fences were replaced by stone curtain walls with towers, and gates were guarded by drawbridges and portcullises. Sieges were common: in 1215 attackers dug under a corner of Rochester's keep, and in 1216 Dover Castle held out for four months.

A castle was also a household and a place of work. The National Archives lists constables, masons, blacksmiths, and servants among the people who kept a castle running. Most castles in England were granted by the king to his loyal lords. The lord's living quarters included a great hall, and records of 1396 at Portchester Castle list a new hall, kitchen, chambers, and offices.

Most people did not live in castles. Most were farmers in villages, and in much of western Europe many villages were part of a lord's manor, with peasant houses, a church, a mill, and the lord's manor house, surrounded by fields, meadows, and woods. Peasants paid the lord in labor, money, and produce. Serfs were bound to their land and needed the lord's permission to leave, marry, or change jobs; they had little protection in law and passed to a new lord along with the land. From the 14th century serfdom faded in western Europe, but in eastern Europe it lasted into the 1800s.

Great stone buildings rose in other lands too. In Syria, the Hospitaller knights, a European crusading order, built the Crac des Chevaliers from 1142 to 1271, and the Mamluks, Muslim sultans of Egypt and Syria, added to it later. In southern Africa, ancestors of the Shona built the stone walls of Great Zimbabwe, the center of a large state, between about 1100 and 1450, without mortar; scholars think those walls showed the rulers' authority rather than being built for war. In Europe, the age of the medieval castle ended when guns could knock down walls quickly, as French armies showed in Italy in 1494.
paras_zh: Britannica 說，城堡是中世紀的要塞，通常是國王或那一帶領主的家。同樣用途的堡壘，在世界許多地方都有，包括日本和印度。這一課主要看西歐的城堡（從九世紀起很快發展），再看同一個時代別處的大型石造建築。
最早的城堡常常是用泥土和木頭蓋的。一座土丘（motte）四周挖了壕溝，上面蓋一座塔；土丘腳下是一個用柵欄圍起來的院子（bailey）。1066 年諾曼人征服英格蘭以後，二十年內蓋了五百多座城堡，用來控制征服來的土地。English Heritage 指出，當地人被強迫來幫忙蓋。
木頭會燒、會爛，所以領主改用石頭重蓋。主塔成了城堡最堅固的部分，裡面有井、私人的房間和存糧。木柵欄換成有塔樓的石造城牆，城門有吊橋和吊閘守著。圍城很常見：1215 年，攻擊的人在羅徹斯特主塔的一角底下挖地道；1216 年，多佛城堡撐了四個月。
城堡也是一個家，也是一個工作的地方。英國國家檔案館列出城堡總管、石匠、鐵匠和僕人，都是讓城堡運作的人。英格蘭大部分的城堡，是國王賜給忠心的領主的。領主的居住區有大廳；1396 年波特切斯特城堡的紀錄，列出新蓋的大廳、廚房、臥房和辦事的房間。
大部分的人不住在城堡裡。大多數人是住在村子裡的農民；在西歐許多地方，這些村子屬於領主的莊園，有農民的房子、教堂、磨坊和領主的宅邸，四周是田地、草地和樹林。農民用勞動、錢和農產品繳給領主。農奴被綁在自己的土地上，要離開、結婚或換工作，都要領主同意；他們在法律上很少能對抗領主，還會連同土地一起轉給新的領主。從十四世紀起，西歐的農奴制度逐漸消失，可是東歐的農奴制一直延續到十九世紀。

別的地方也有大型的石造建築。在敘利亞，歐洲十字軍的醫院騎士團從 1142 年到 1271 年蓋了騎士堡，後來馬木路克（統治埃及和敘利亞的穆斯林蘇丹）又加蓋。在非洲南部，紹納人（也譯修納人）的祖先在大約 1100 到 1450 年間，替一個大國的中心大辛巴威，不用灰漿蓋起石牆；學者認為這些牆主要是展現統治者的權威，而不是用來打仗。在歐洲，大砲能很快打倒城牆以後，中世紀城堡的時代就結束了；1494 年法國軍隊在義大利就證明了這一點。
questions: Why did many lords rebuild their castles in stone?
Name three kinds of people, besides the lord, who lived or worked in a castle.
How was a serf's life different from a free person's?
answers: Timber could burn and rot. Stone lasted longer and was harder to attack.
Constables, masons, blacksmiths, servants (any three).
A serf was bound to the land, needed the lord's permission to leave, marry, or change jobs, paid the lord in labor, money, and produce, and had little protection in law.

parts.text_en: Earth, timber, and a ditch. How long do you think the wooden tower lasted?
parts.text_zh: 泥土、木頭和壕溝。你覺得木塔能撐多久？

parts.text_en: The strongest place in the castle. What did it need inside to survive a long siege?
parts.text_zh: 城堡最堅固的地方。要撐過長期圍城，裡面需要什麼？

parts.text_en: The gate was the weakest point. Count the ways it was protected.
parts.text_zh: 城門是最弱的地方。數一數它有幾種保護。

parts.text_en: One ring of walls inside another, like the castles of Edward I in Wales.
parts.text_zh: 一圈牆套著另一圈，像愛德華一世在威爾斯蓋的城堡。
