lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著按「看它長大」，看每一個階段加了什麼。哪些部分一直都在？

built.lead_en: Castles changed as builders learned and as attacks changed. For each part, decide whether it belongs to the early castles of earth and timber or to the later castles of stone. There is no timer.
built.lead_zh: 城堡跟著蓋城堡的人學到的經驗、跟著攻擊的方式一起改變。每一題判斷：它屬於早期用泥土和木頭蓋的城堡，還是後來用石頭蓋的城堡？不計時。
built.ask_en: Early earth and timber, or later stone?
built.ask_zh: 早期的泥土木頭，還是後來的石頭？

items.en: A mound of earth and stone with a ditch around it
items.why_en: This is the motte. English Heritage says most earthwork castles in England were built in the years right after 1066.
items.why_zh: 這是土丘（motte）。English Heritage 說，英格蘭大部分的土堆城堡，是 1066 年以後那幾年蓋的。
items.hint_en: It is made by digging and piling.
items.hint_zh: 它是挖土、堆土做成的。

items.en: A rectangular tower of wood on top of the mound
items.zh: 土丘上一座長方形的木塔
items.why_en: The Normans usually built a timber tower on the motte.
items.why_zh: 諾曼人通常在土丘上蓋一座木塔。
items.hint_en: Look at the material.
items.hint_zh: 看看材料。

items.en: A fence of wooden stakes around the yard
items.why_en: Britannica says the baileys were enclosed by palisades, and later by stone walls and towers.
items.why_zh: Britannica 說，院子先是用木柵欄圍起來，後來才換成石牆和塔樓。
items.hint_en: Could it burn?
items.hint_zh: 它會燒起來嗎？

items.en: A castle raised quickly by forced local labor right after a conquest
items.zh: 征服以後，強迫當地人很快蓋好的城堡
items.why_en: English Heritage says earthwork castles were quickly and easily built, with local forced labor; a motte took about 100 men some forty days.
items.why_zh: English Heritage 說，土堆城堡又快又容易蓋，用的是被強迫的當地勞力；一座土丘大約一百人、四十天。
items.hint_en: The National Archives calls timber castles cheap and very quick to build.
items.hint_zh: 英國國家檔案館說，木造城堡又便宜、又很快就能蓋好。

items.en: The great keep at Rochester, about 1130
items.zh: 羅徹斯特的主塔，大約 1130 年
items.why_en: Britannica gives it as an example of the rectangular stone keep.
items.why_zh: Britannica 把它當作長方形石造主塔的例子。
items.hint_en: Keeps were the strongest part.
items.hint_zh: 主塔是最堅固的部分。

items.en: A round “shell keep” on top of an old mound
items.zh: 舊土丘上一圈圓形的「殼形主塔」
items.why_en: English Heritage says the wooden fences on the mottes were replaced with circular stone-walled shell keeps.
items.why_zh: English Heritage 說，土丘上的木柵欄後來換成了圓形的石牆，叫做殼形主塔。
items.hint_en: It replaced something wooden.
items.hint_zh: 它取代了木頭的東西。

items.en: Curtain walls that replaced the bailey's fence
items.why_en: English Heritage says the timber stockades of the bailey were soon replaced with stone curtain walls.
items.why_zh: English Heritage 說，院子的木柵欄很快就換成了石造的城牆。
items.hint_en: “Replaced” is the clue.
items.hint_zh: 「換成」是線索。

items.en: Two rings of walls, one inside the other, in Wales
items.zh: 威爾斯的兩圈城牆，一圈套一圈
items.why_en: UNESCO says Beaumaris and Harlech combine the double-wall concentric design of the late 13th century.
items.why_zh: 聯合國教科文組織說，博馬里斯和哈萊克結合了十三世紀後期的雙層同心圓設計。
items.hint_en: Late 13th century.
items.hint_zh: 十三世紀後期。

built.end_en: Wood was fast and cheap but could burn and rot; stone lasted. The two ages also overlap: the stone keep at Loches (about 1020) is older than many mottes.
built.end_zh: 木頭又快又便宜，但會燒、會爛；石頭耐久。早期和後期也有重疊：洛什的石造主塔（約 1020 年）比很多土丘城寨還早。

terms.en: Where Does This Word Come From?
terms.lead_en: Many English words about castles and medieval life came from Latin and French, the languages of churchmen and of the Norman rulers. For each Chinese word, pick its older form and its English word. There is no timer.
terms.lead_zh: 很多關於城堡和中世紀生活的英文字，來自拉丁文和法文，也就是教會和諾曼統治者的語言。每一個中文詞，選出它比較古老的寫法，以及它的英文。不計時。
terms.ask_en: Which older word did it come from, and what is it in English?
terms.ask_zh: 它來自哪一個比較古老的字？英文是哪一個？

items.note_en: Old English castel came from Latin castellum, a fortified place.
items.note_zh: 古英文的 castel 來自拉丁文 castellum，也就是設防的地方。

items.note_en: Old French mote meant “clod, mound”; its further origin is not clear.
items.note_zh: 古法文的 mote 是「土塊、土丘」的意思；更早的來源不清楚。

items.note_en: Donjon and dungeon both first meant a castle keep, the lord's tower; it comes from a Latin word for mastery or lordship. The prison meaning came later.
items.note_zh: donjon 和 dungeon 原來都是指城堡的主塔，也就是領主的塔，來自拉丁文「主權、統治」的字。「地牢」的意思是後來才有的。

items.note_en: Manoir came from a word meaning “to remain, to dwell.”
items.note_zh: manoir 來自「留下、居住」的意思。

items.note_en: Latin servus meant “slave,” but Britannica notes that, unlike slaves, serfs could not be bought and sold apart from the land they worked.
items.note_zh: 拉丁文 servus 是「奴隸」的意思；但 Britannica 指出，農奴和奴隸不一樣，不能脫離他耕種的土地被單獨買賣。

items.note_en: Cniht meant “boy” or “manservant.” German Knecht, “servant,” is related.
items.note_zh: cniht 是「男孩」或「男僕」的意思。德文的 Knecht（僕人）和它同源。

items.note_en: From chevalier, a horseman or knight.
items.note_zh: 來自 chevalier，也就是騎馬的人、騎士。

items.note_en: The English word feudal is first recorded around 1605–15, long after the period it is used to describe.
items.note_zh: 英文的 feudal 最早的紀錄大約在 1605 到 1615 年，比它用來描述的那個時代晚得多。

items.note_en: Porte coleice meant a “sliding gate.”
items.note_zh: porte coleice 是「會滑動的閘門」的意思。

items.note_en: Covrefeu meant “(it) covers the fire”: a signal at night to cover the hearth.
items.note_zh: covrefeu 是「蓋住火」的意思：晚上的一個訊號，提醒大家把爐火蓋起來。

terms.end_en: Several of these words came into English from French, the language of England's Norman rulers after 1066; others came straight from Latin or were already English.
terms.end_zh: 這些字有好幾個是從法文進入英文的，法文是 1066 年以後英格蘭諾曼統治者的語言；有些直接來自拉丁文，有些本來就是英文。

timeline.en: Great stone buildings across three continents
timeline.zh: 三大洲的大型石造建築
timeline.lead_en: Castles in Europe, crusader and Muslim fortresses in Syria, and the stone walls of Great Zimbabwe overlapped in time.
timeline.lead_zh: 歐洲的城堡、敘利亞的十字軍和穆斯林堡壘，以及大辛巴威的石牆，在時間上是重疊的。
timeline.idle_en: Click a bar or a diamond to read its dates.
timeline.idle_zh: 點一條長條或一個菱形，讀出它的年代。

tips.en: Great Zimbabwe was being built during the same centuries as the stone castles of Europe.
tips.zh: 大辛巴威和歐洲的石造城堡，是在同樣的幾百年裡蓋的。

tips.en: The Crac des Chevaliers took more than a century to finish.
tips.zh: 騎士堡花了一百多年才蓋完。

tips.en: The gray diamonds mark single events, such as the Norman Conquest of 1066.
tips.zh: 灰色的菱形標的是單一事件，例如 1066 年的諾曼征服。

events.note_en: Over 500 castles in the next twenty years.
events.note_zh: 之後二十年蓋了五百多座城堡。

events.note_en: William I's survey of England.
events.note_zh: 威廉一世對英格蘭的調查。

events.note_en: About 1130.

events.en: The Hospitallers build the Crac des Chevaliers
events.note_en: Mamluk rulers added to it later.
events.note_zh: 後來馬木路克的統治者又加蓋。

events.note_en: By ancestors of the Shona.
events.note_zh: 紹納人的祖先所建。

events.en: Edward I's castles in north Wales
events.zh: 愛德華一世在北威爾斯的城堡
events.note_en: Begun from 1277 to control conquered land; the Welsh rose up in 1294, and some building went on until about 1330.
events.note_zh: 1277 年起為了控制征服來的土地陸續動工；威爾斯人 1294 年起來反抗，有些工程一直到大約 1330 年。

events.zh: 法軍的大砲進入義大利
events.note_en: Castle after castle fell quickly.
events.note_zh: 一座又一座城堡很快被攻下。

how_we_know.eyebrow: How Do We Know? · 我們怎麼知道？
how_we_know.lead_en: Castles left many kinds of evidence: royal records, embroidered and painted pictures, and the ruins themselves.
how_we_know.lead_zh: 城堡留下了很多種證據：王室的紀錄、繡出來和畫出來的圖，以及廢墟本身。

items.limit_en: Royal records show what the king and his officials cared about, such as land, money, and permission. They say little about servants or peasants as people.
items.limit_zh: 王室的紀錄表現的是國王和官員在乎的事，例如土地、錢和許可；很少寫到僕人或農民這些人本身。
items.src: Britannica, “Domesday Book”; The National Archives, “Medieval castles”
items.text_en: In 1086 William I ordered a survey of England, later called the Domesday Book. The English crown also kept accounts and licenses: in 1291, for example, a license allowed the owner of Stokesay to fortify it.
items.text_zh: 1086 年，威廉一世下令調查英格蘭，後來叫做《末日審判書》。英格蘭王室也留下帳目和許可：例如 1291 年，一份許可准許斯托克賽的主人替它加上防禦。

items.limit_en: Pictures were made by someone with a point of view. Britannica says it may have been commissioned by William's half-brother, Bishop Odo, and embroidered by English needleworkers about 1092.
items.limit_zh: 圖畫是有立場的人做的。Britannica 說，它可能是威廉同母異父的弟弟奧多主教訂製的，大約 1092 年由英格蘭的繡工繡成。
items.src: Britannica, “Bayeux Tapestry”
items.text_en: The Bayeux Tapestry, an embroidered linen band about 68 meters (224 feet) long with more than 70 scenes, tells the story of the Norman Conquest of 1066.
items.text_zh: 貝葉掛毯是一條長約 68 公尺（224 英尺）的刺繡麻布，有七十多個場景，講 1066 年諾曼征服的故事。

items.limit_en: Timber rots away, so the earliest castles leave only faint traces in the soil.
items.limit_zh: 木頭會爛掉，所以最早的城堡只在土裡留下淡淡的痕跡。
items.src: English Heritage, “History of Totnes Castle”
items.text_en: Archaeologists study castles that still stand and dig where only mounds remain. At Totnes, excavation on the motte found the base of a watchtower, probably built in the 11th century; a stone shell keep was built there in the 1320s.
items.text_zh: 考古學家研究還立著的城堡，也在只剩土丘的地方挖掘。在托特尼斯，挖掘在土丘上找到一座瞭望塔的基座，大概是十一世紀蓋的；1320 年代那裡才蓋了石造的殼形主塔。

views.zh: 歷史學家討論的三個問題
views.lead_en: Even familiar words like “feudal system” are debated. Here are three questions, with the views set side by side.
views.lead_zh: 連「封建制度」這樣熟悉的詞，都有爭論。下面是三個問題，各種說法並列。
views.rule_en: Notice when a word was invented, and by whom.
views.rule_zh: 留意一個詞是什麼時候、被誰發明出來的。

items.topic_en: Was there a “feudal system”?
items.topic_zh: 真的有一個「封建制度」嗎？

sides.en: Textbooks often describe lords who gave land, called a fief, to vassals, who owed military and other services and loyalty in return.
sides.zh: 教科書常常這樣描述：領主把土地（采邑）分給封臣，封臣回報以軍事和其他的服務，以及忠誠。

sides.en: Britannica calls feudalism a “historiographic construct”: the terms were invented long after the Middle Ages. The historian Elizabeth A. R. Brown argued in 1974 that the idea of one “feudal system” hides how different the arrangements were from place to place.
sides.zh: Britannica 說，封建制度是一個「史學建構」：這些詞是中世紀過去很久以後才發明的。歷史學家伊莉莎白・布朗在 1974 年主張，「一個封建制度」的想法，掩蓋了各地安排有多麼不同。

items.note_en: Both views agree that lords, land, and duties mattered. The question is whether one neat “system” describes all of medieval Europe.
items.note_zh: 兩種說法都同意領主、土地和義務很重要；問題在於，是不是有一個整齊的「制度」可以描述整個中世紀歐洲。

items.topic_en: What were castles for?
items.topic_zh: 城堡是做什麼用的？

sides.en: English Heritage says the Normans' intensive program of castle building controlled newly conquered land, and Edward I built castles to control newly conquered north Wales.
sides.zh: English Heritage 說，諾曼人密集蓋城堡，是為了控制剛征服的土地；愛德華一世蓋城堡，也是為了控制剛征服的北威爾斯。

sides.label_en: To live in and to run an estate
sides.en: Britannica describes the castle as generally the residence of the king or lord, and records show halls, kitchens, chambers, and offices, the rooms of a household.
sides.zh: Britannica 說，城堡通常是國王或領主的住所；紀錄裡也有大廳、廚房、臥房和辦事的房間，都是一個家需要的房間。

items.note_en: One way to see it: many castles did both, and which purpose mattered more could change from castle to castle and from war to peace.
items.note_zh: 一種看法是：很多城堡兩種用途都有；哪一種比較重要，要看是哪一座城堡、是戰時還是平時。

items.topic_en: What ended the age of castles?
items.topic_zh: 城堡的時代是怎麼結束的？

sides.en: Britannica says firearms developed so fast in the 15th and 16th centuries that military architecture had to change; French troops in Italy in 1494 took castle after castle with astonishing speed.
sides.zh: Britannica 說，十五、十六世紀火器發展得很快，軍事建築不得不改變；1494 年法國軍隊在義大利，以驚人的速度攻下一座又一座城堡。

sides.label_en: Homes and forts went separate ways
sides.en: Britannica also says that from the Renaissance, military and domestic buildings separated: forts were run by the monarch's army, and lords lived in unfortified palaces and manor houses.
sides.zh: Britannica 也說，從文藝復興開始，軍事建築和住宅分開了：要塞由國王的軍隊管理，領主住在沒有防禦工事的宮殿和宅邸。

items.note_en: One way to see it: the two answers fit together, since once guns made high walls weak, a lord had less reason to live inside them.
items.note_zh: 一種看法是：兩個答案可以放在一起看，大砲讓高牆變得不堪一擊以後，領主就比較沒有理由住在牆裡面了。

phrases.en: Eight sentences for talking about castles and manors
phrases.zh: 談城堡和莊園的八句英文
phrases.lead_en: These sentences help you describe how a castle worked and how people lived. Listen, repeat, then make your own sentence with the words in bold.
phrases.lead_zh: 這八句幫你描述城堡怎麼運作、人們怎麼生活。先聽、再跟著唸，然後用粗體的字自己造一句。

rows.en: The tower was made of timber.
rows.html: The tower was made of timber.
rows.zh: 那座塔是木頭做的。
rows.note_en: be made of: the material

rows.en: Stone walls replaced the wooden fence.
rows.html: Stone walls replaced the wooden fence.
rows.zh: 石牆取代了木柵欄。
rows.note_en: replace: take the place of

rows.en: The castle was surrounded by a moat.
rows.html: The castle was surrounded by a moat.
rows.zh: 城堡被護城河圍著。
rows.note_en: be surrounded by: all around

rows.en: The garrison held out for four months.
rows.html: The garrison held out for four months.
rows.zh: 守軍撐了四個月。
rows.note_en: hold out: keep resisting

rows.en: Peasants owed the lord work and food.
rows.html: Peasants owed the lord work and food.
rows.zh: 農民欠領主勞動和食物。
rows.note_en: owe: have to give

rows.en: A serf needed permission to leave.
rows.html: A serf needed permission to leave.
rows.zh: 農奴要得到允許才能離開。
rows.note_en: need permission to: must be allowed

rows.en: The king granted the castle to a loyal lord.
rows.html: The king granted the castle to a loyal lord.
rows.zh: 國王把城堡賜給一位忠心的領主。
rows.note_en: grant A to B: give officially

rows.en: Guns made high walls weak.
rows.html: Guns made high walls weak.
rows.zh: 大砲讓高牆變得不堪一擊。
rows.note_en: make A weak: cause A to lose strength

taiwan_then.eyebrow: Taiwan at That Time · 那時候的台灣
taiwan_then.en: Villages, fields, and a fort that came later
taiwan_then.zh: 村落、田地，和後來才有的城堡
taiwan_then.lead_en: While castles rose in Europe, the peoples of Taiwan lived in villages by farming, hunting, and fishing. A European-style fort came to Taiwan centuries later.
taiwan_then.lead_zh: 歐洲蓋城堡的時候，台灣的人群住在村落裡，靠農耕、打獵和捕魚生活。歐洲式的城堡，是好幾百年以後才來到台灣的。
taiwan_then.intro_en: Archaeologists in Taiwan give dates as “years ago.” About 1,000 years ago is roughly the 11th century, the age of the motte-and-bailey castle.
taiwan_then.intro_zh: 台灣的考古學家用「距今幾年」說年代。距今大約一千年，差不多是十一世紀，也就是土丘城寨的時代。

facts.en: The museum says the Shisanhang culture arose about 2,000 years ago; its people built wooden houses raised on posts, grew rice, and still relied on hunting, fishing, and gathering shellfish.
facts.zh: 史前館說，十三行文化的「房屋為木造干欄式建築，以種稻為生，但狩獵、捕魚、採貝仍很重要」。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

facts.en: On the east coast, the Jingpu culture lasted from about 1,500 to two or three hundred years ago, the whole age of European castles.
facts.zh: 在東海岸，靜浦文化「距今約一千五百年到二、三百年前」，涵蓋了歐洲城堡的整個時代。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

facts.en: The Dutch began building a fort at Tainan in 1624, named it Zeelandia in 1627, and finished it in 1634. It was a military, trade, and government center.
facts.zh: 荷蘭人 1624 年開始在台南蓋城，1627 年命名為熱蘭遮城，1634 年完工。它是軍事、貿易和行政的中心。
facts.src: 臺南市文化資產管理處〈熱蘭遮城的前世今生〉

links.en: Taiwan's Story: Why Did the Dutch Build a Fort in Tainan?
links.zh: 台灣歷史：荷蘭人為什麼在台南蓋城？

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Evidence · 證據背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A knights' castle, walls without mortar, a license, and a long siege
culture_cards.title_zh: 騎士的城堡、不用灰漿的牆、一份許可，和一場漫長的圍城
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about great stone buildings on three continents.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事：三大洲的大型石造建築。

cards.body_en: The Crac des Chevaliers was built by the Hospitaller knights, a European crusading order, from 1142 to 1271, and Mamluk rulers added to it later. Also in Syria, Qal'at Salah El-Din, named for Saladin, shows Byzantine work from the 10th century, Frankish work, and additions by Saladin's Ayyubid dynasty layered on one another. UNESCO says the two castles show how builders of different peoples influenced each other.
cards.body_zh: 騎士堡由歐洲十字軍的醫院騎士團從 1142 年蓋到 1271 年，後來馬木路克的統治者又加蓋。同樣在敘利亞、以薩拉丁命名的薩拉丁堡，有十世紀拜占庭的工程、法蘭克的工程，以及薩拉丁的阿尤布王朝加蓋的部分，一層疊一層。聯合國教科文組織說，這兩座城堡顯示了不同民族的建造者怎麼互相影響。

cards.body_en: At Great Zimbabwe, builders fitted granite blocks one on top of another without mortar, each layer set back a little so the wall leaned inward and stayed stable. The Great Enclosure's walls reach about 11 meters high. The Metropolitan Museum says scholars doubt the walls ever served a military purpose; they showed the rulers' authority and kept the royal family apart.
cards.body_zh: 在大辛巴威，建造者不用灰漿，把花崗岩石塊一層疊一層，每一層往內縮一點，讓牆往內斜、站得穩。大圍場的牆高到大約 11 公尺。大都會博物館說，學者懷疑這些牆曾經用在軍事上；它們展現統治者的權威，也讓王室和一般人隔開。

cards.body_en: In England, the crown granted licenses to fortify buildings. In 1291 such a license was granted for Stokesay, and the document survives in the royal records.
cards.body_zh: 在英格蘭，王室會發「加上防禦」的許可。1291 年，斯托克賽就拿到這樣一份許可；這份文件留在王室的紀錄裡。

cards.body_en: When French forces besieged Dover Castle in 1216, its defenders held out for four months. A year earlier, at Rochester, attackers had dug a tunnel under one corner of the keep to bring it down.
cards.body_zh: 1216 年法國軍隊圍攻多佛城堡，守軍撐了四個月。前一年在羅徹斯特，攻擊的人在主塔的一角底下挖地道，想讓它倒塌。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum for social studies (October 2018).
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要社會領域（民國 107 年 10 月）。

items.area: 國中・古代文化的遺產
items.area_en: Junior high · the heritage of ancient cultures
items.text: 基督教的起源與發展。
items.note_en: The explanation suggests discussing the character of Christianity in medieval Europe. Castles, chapels, and manors with their churches belong to that world.
items.note_zh: 課綱的說明建議討論「歐洲中古的基督教特色」。城堡、禮拜堂，以及有教堂的莊園，都屬於那個世界。

items.area: 高中・歐洲文化與現代世界
items.area_en: Senior high · European culture and the modern world
items.text: 中古基督教世界。
items.note_en: For senior high school, the curriculum names the medieval Christian world as a topic.
items.note_zh: 高中的課綱把「中古基督教世界」列為一個條目。

myths.myth_en: Castles were only for fighting.
myths.myth_zh: 城堡只是用來打仗的。
myths.fact_en: Castles were generally the homes of kings and lords, with halls, kitchens, and private rooms, and many people worked in them.
myths.fact_zh: 城堡通常是國王和領主的家，有大廳、廚房和私人的房間，也有很多人在裡面工作。

myths.myth_en: All castles were made of stone.
myths.myth_zh: 城堡都是石頭蓋的。
myths.fact_en: Many early castles were earth and timber. Most of the ones that survive are stone, because timber burned and rotted.
myths.fact_zh: 很多早期的城堡是泥土和木頭蓋的。留下來的大多是石造的，因為木頭會燒、會爛。

myths.myth_en: A dungeon was always an underground prison.
myths.myth_zh: dungeon 一直都是地下的牢房。
myths.fact_en: Donjon and dungeon first meant the castle keep, the lord's tower. The prison meaning came later.
myths.fact_zh: donjon 和 dungeon 原來指城堡的主塔，也就是領主的塔。「地牢」的意思是後來才有的。

myths.myth_en: Great Zimbabwe must have been built by outsiders.
myths.myth_zh: 大辛巴威一定是外來的人蓋的。
myths.fact_en: In the 1800s some European travelers and colonizers, stunned by its grandeur, credited it to foreign powers. Archaeology in the early 20th century confirmed its African origin: the Metropolitan Museum says it was built by Bantu-speaking ancestors of the Shona, and UNESCO says it was built by Bantu/Shona people.
myths.fact_zh: 十九世紀有些歐洲旅人和殖民者，被它的宏偉震懾，就把它歸功於外來的勢力。二十世紀初的考古確認了它是非洲人蓋的：大都會博物館說，它是說班圖語的紹納人祖先蓋的；聯合國教科文組織也說是班圖／紹納人。

tricks.body_en: Mound and timber first; keeps and walls of stone later.
tricks.body_zh: 先是土丘和木頭，後來才是石造的主塔和城牆。

tricks.body_en: Halls, kitchens, chapels, and many workers.
tricks.body_zh: 大廳、廚房、禮拜堂，和許多工作的人。

tricks.body_en: Manor villages, fields, and duties to the lord.
tricks.body_zh: 莊園村落、田地，和對領主的義務。

tricks.body_en: A crusader castle in Syria and Great Zimbabwe's walls in the same centuries.
tricks.body_zh: 同樣的幾百年，敘利亞的十字軍城堡和大辛巴威的石牆。

materials.en: Role cards: lord, constable, mason, blacksmith, cook, servant, peasant, serf
materials.zh: 角色卡：領主、總管、石匠、鐵匠、廚師、僕人、農民、農奴

materials.en: The 3D model in this lesson
materials.zh: 這一課的 3D 模型

steps.en: Each student draws a role card and finds where that person would spend the day, in the model or on the manor.
steps.zh: 每個學生抽一張角色卡，在模型裡或莊園上，找出這個人一天會待在哪裡。

steps.en: Write three sentences: “I live …,” “I work …,” and “I owe …”
steps.zh: 寫三句英文：「I live …」「I work …」「I owe …」

steps.en: In groups, compare: who had the most choice about their life, and who had the least?
steps.zh: 分組比較：誰對自己的生活最有選擇？誰最少？

steps.en: Share one thing that surprised you.
steps.zh: 分享一件讓你驚訝的事。

activities.tip_en: Keep the discussion about duties and choices, not about cruelty. Remind students that life varied a great deal from place to place.
activities.tip_zh: 討論的重點放在義務和選擇，不要放在殘酷的細節。提醒學生：各地的生活差別很大。

materials.en: Pictures of a motte-and-bailey castle, a concentric castle, the Crac des Chevaliers, and Great Zimbabwe (from museum or UNESCO websites)
materials.zh: 土丘城寨、同心圓城堡、騎士堡和大辛巴威的照片（取自博物館或聯合國教科文組織網站）

steps.en: In pairs, list what each was built of and roughly when.
steps.zh: 兩人一組，列出每一個是用什麼蓋的、大約在什麼時候。

steps.en: Find one thing they share and one thing that is different.
steps.zh: 找出一個共同點和一個不同點。

steps.en: Write two sentences with “was made of” and “was surrounded by.”
steps.zh: 用 was made of 和 was surrounded by 寫兩句英文。

activities.tip_en: Avoid ranking them. Castles and the Crac des Chevaliers were built for defense, while Great Zimbabwe's walls probably showed the rulers' status and kept them apart. Ask students why people build great walls.
activities.tip_zh: 不要替它們排名次。城堡和騎士堡是為了防守而蓋的；大辛巴威的牆大概是為了展現統治者的地位、和一般人隔開。問學生：人為什麼要蓋大牆？

links.en: How Did Gold and Salt Build Kingdoms in Africa?
links.zh: 黃金和鹽怎麼在非洲建起王國？
links.note_en: Mali, Timbuktu, and the trade across the Sahara.
links.note_zh: 馬利、廷巴克圖，和橫越撒哈拉的貿易。

links.en: Who Kept Knowledge Alive?
links.zh: 誰把知識保存下來？
links.note_en: Monks, monasteries, and the books of the same centuries.
links.note_zh: 同一個時代的修士、修道院和書。

links.en: How Did Rome Hold an Empire Together?
links.zh: 羅馬怎麼管住那麼大的地方？
links.note_en: Stone arches and roads that castle builders inherited.
links.note_zh: 城堡的建造者承接下來的石拱和道路。

links.en: Why Did the Dutch Build a Fort in Tainan?
links.zh: 荷蘭人為什麼在台南蓋城？
links.note_en: A European fort in Taiwan, six or seven centuries after the first castles.
links.note_zh: 第一批城堡出現六、七百年後，台灣的一座歐洲式城堡。

lessons.sources_note_en: Checked November 2026. The idea of a “feudal system,” the purposes of castles, and the reasons the age of castles ended are discussed by historians; where they are, the lesson gives more than one view
lessons.sources_note_zh: 2026 年 11 月查證。「封建制度」這個說法、城堡的用途，以及城堡時代結束的原因，歷史學家都有討論；遇到這些地方，課文寫出不只一種說法

sources.en: The castle as a medieval stronghold and residence; motte and bailey from the 10th–11th centuries; palisades and later stone walls and towers; Loches and Rochester keeps; keep with a well; moats, drawbridges, portcullises; hall and chapel in the inner bailey after the Third Crusade; guns and 1494; separation of forts and residences
sources.zh: 城堡是中世紀的要塞與住所；十到十一世紀的土丘城寨；木柵欄後來換成石牆和塔；洛什與羅徹斯特的主塔；主塔裡有井；護城河、吊橋、吊閘；第三次十字軍以後大廳和禮拜堂在內院；大砲與 1494 年；要塞與住宅分家

sources.en: The motte as a mound of earth and stone; a rectangular timber tower; about 100 men for forty days; most built just after 1066; out of fashion by 1200 in most places
sources.zh: 土丘是泥土和石頭堆成的；長方形的木塔；大約一百人四十天；大多在 1066 年後不久蓋的；多數地方到 1200 年就不流行
sources.src: English Heritage, “How to spot a castle hiding in plain sight” (2017)

sources.en: Over 500 castles in twenty years after 1066; local forced labor; timber replaced by stone curtain walls and shell keeps; Rochester 1215; Dover 1216; Edward I's castles from 1277
sources.zh: 1066 年後二十年五百多座城堡；強迫的當地勞力；木頭換成石造城牆與殼形主塔；羅徹斯特 1215 年；多佛 1216 年；愛德華一世 1277–1294 年的城堡

sources.en: Excavation at Totnes: the base of an 11th-century watchtower on the motte; the shell keep of the 1320s
sources.zh: 托特尼斯的挖掘：土丘上木造瞭望塔的基座

sources.en: Timber castles vulnerable to fire and rot; people who ran a castle; castles granted to loyal lords; Stokesay license 1291; Portchester buildings 1396
sources.zh: 木造城堡怕火、會爛；讓城堡運作的人；城堡賜給忠心的領主；1291 年斯托克賽的許可；1396 年波特切斯特的工程

sources.en: Beaumaris and Harlech: double-wall concentric design with a central plan; James of St George; Edward I (1272–1307); building from 1283, the 1294 uprising, work continuing to 1330–31
sources.zh: 博馬里斯與哈萊克：雙層同心圓設計；聖喬治的詹姆斯；愛德華一世（1272–1307）
sources.src: UNESCO World Heritage List, Castles and Town Walls of King Edward in Gwynedd

sources.en: Crac des Chevaliers (1142–1271, Mamluk additions) and Qal'at Salah El-Din (Byzantine, Frankish, Ayyubid)
sources.zh: 騎士堡（1142–1271，馬木路克加蓋）與薩拉丁堡（拜占庭、法蘭克、阿尤布）
sources.src: UNESCO World Heritage List, Crac des Chevaliers and Qal'at Salah El-Din

sources.en: Great Zimbabwe built between 1100 and 1450 by the Bantu/Shona
sources.zh: 大辛巴威在 1100 到 1450 年間由班圖／紹納人建造
sources.src: UNESCO World Heritage List, Great Zimbabwe National Monument

sources.en: Great Zimbabwe: built by Bantu-speaking ancestors of the Shona; granite without mortar; walls up to 36 feet; scholars doubt a military purpose; 1800s claims of foreign builders
sources.zh: 大辛巴威：說班圖語的紹納人祖先所建；不用灰漿的花崗岩；牆高到 36 英尺；十九世紀「外來者所建」的說法
sources.src: Metropolitan Museum of Art, “Great Zimbabwe (11th–15th Century)”

sources.en: Feudalism as a historiographic construct; terms invented long after
sources.zh: 封建制度是史學建構；這些詞很晚才發明

sources.en: Vassals, fiefs, and services
sources.zh: 封臣、采邑和服務

sources.en: “The Tyranny of a Construct: Feudalism and Historians of Medieval Europe”
sources.zh: 〈一個建構的專制：封建制度與中世紀歐洲的歷史學家〉
sources.src: Elizabeth A. R. Brown, American Historical Review 79 (1974)

sources.en: Manors: peasant houses, church, mill, manor house; labor, money, and produce
sources.zh: 莊園：農民的房子、教堂、磨坊、宅邸；勞動、錢和農產品

sources.en: Serfs bound to the land; permission to leave, marry, or change jobs; harsh treatment and little legal redress; transferred with the land; replacement by a free peasantry in the west from the 14th century; longer in the east
sources.zh: 農奴被綁在土地上；離開、結婚、換工作要允許；常受苛待、很少法律保障；連同土地轉讓；西歐從十四世紀起被自由農民取代；東歐延續較久

sources.en: The Domesday Book, 1086
sources.zh: 《末日審判書》，1086 年

sources.en: The Bayeux Tapestry: about 224 feet long, over 70 scenes; may have been commissioned by Odo; English needleworkers about 1092
sources.zh: 貝葉掛毯：約 224 英尺長、七十多個場景；可能是奧多訂製的；大約 1092 年英格蘭繡工繡成

sources.en: Word origins: castle, moat, dungeon, manor, serf, knight, chivalry, feudal, portcullis, curfew
sources.zh: 字源：castle、moat、dungeon、manor、serf、knight、chivalry、feudal、portcullis、curfew

sources.en: Shisanhang houses raised on posts, rice, hunting, fishing, and shellfish; Jingpu culture 1,500 to 200–300 years ago
sources.zh: 十三行的干欄式房屋、種稻、狩獵捕魚採貝；靜浦文化距今約一千五百年到二、三百年前
sources.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

sources.en: Fort Zeelandia: begun 1624, named 1627, finished 1634; military, trade, and government center
sources.zh: 熱蘭遮城：1624 年開工、1627 年命名、1634 年完工；軍事、貿易與行政中心
sources.src: 臺南市文化資產管理處〈熱蘭遮城的前世今生〉

sources.en: Curriculum entries 歷 Nb-Ⅳ-2 and 歷 La-Ⅴ-2
sources.zh: 課綱條目 歷 Nb-Ⅳ-2、歷 La-Ⅴ-2
sources.src: 十二年國民基本教育課程綱要・社會領域（民國 107 年 10 月）
sources.url: https://www.naer.edu.tw/upload/1/16/doc/819/十二年國民基本教育課程綱要國民中小學暨普通型高級中等校-社會領域.pdf

units.blurb_en: Trading kingdoms in Africa, cities and mountain roads in the Americas, inventions and voyages from China, and two ways of crossing great distances: the steppe and the open Pacific.
units.blurb_zh: 非洲的貿易王國、美洲的城市與山路、中國的發明與遠航，以及跨越遠距離的兩種路：草原和太平洋。

lessons.title: How Did Gold and Salt Build Kingdoms in Africa?
lessons.title_zh: 黃金和鹽怎麼在非洲建起王國？
lessons.blurb_en: Watch the trading cities of West and East Africa light up on a 3D globe, then follow gold north, salt south, Mansa Musa to Mecca, and Ibn Battuta across the Sahara. Sort what went north and what went south, and find English words that came along the trade routes.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 地球儀上看西非和東非的貿易城市亮起來，再跟著黃金往北、鹽往南、曼薩・穆薩去麥加、伊本・巴杜達穿越撒哈拉。分一分哪些往北、哪些往南，也找一找跟著商路來的英文字。
lessons.big_idea_en: West Africa had gold; the Sahara had salt. Camel caravans linked the two, and the kingdoms of Ghana, Mali, and Songhai grew rich and powerful by controlling and taxing that trade. On the east coast, Swahili city-states such as Kilwa grew rich from the trade of the Indian Ocean.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 西非有黃金，撒哈拉有鹽。駱駝商隊把兩者連起來；迦納、馬利、桑海這些王國靠控制、抽稅這門貿易而富強。在東海岸，基爾瓦這些斯瓦希里城邦，靠印度洋的貿易致富。

lab.aria: 3D globe of Africa showing, in rough outline, the caravan routes across the Sahara and the sea routes along the East African coast, with the trading cities on them; only land, sea, and routes are drawn, with no borders · 3D 非洲地球儀，大略畫出橫越撒哈拉的商隊路線、東非海岸的海路，以及路上的貿易城市；只畫陸地、海洋與路線，沒有國界
lab.how_en: Drag the slider from 700 to 1600 CE, or press Play, and watch the trading cities of West and East Africa light up. Gold lines are caravan and river routes; blue lines go by sea. Under “Follow one thing,” choose gold, salt, or a traveler, and a pink dot will carry it from stop to stop. Click a city to read about it and how we know.
lab.how_zh: 把滑桿從西元 700 年拉到 1600 年，或按「播放」，看西非和東非的貿易城市一個一個亮起來。金色的線是商隊和河上的路，藍色的線走海路。在「跟著一件東西走」選黃金、鹽或一位旅人，粉紅色的小點會把它一站一站帶過去。點一座城市，讀它的故事和我們怎麼知道。

cities.what_en: An Amazigh (Berber) town on the caravan route from the Niger River to Tangier on the coast. It became the leading center of trans-Saharan trade in the western Maghrib.
cities.what_zh: 阿馬齊格人（柏柏人）的城鎮，位在從尼日河到海岸的丹吉爾的商隊路線上。它成為北非西部橫越撒哈拉貿易最重要的中心。
cities.when_en: Founded in 757 CE; destroyed in 1363.
cities.when_zh: 西元 757 年建立；1363 年被毀。
cities.how_en: Britannica's account, based on Arabic sources, and the ruins in the Tafilalt oasis.
cities.how_zh: Britannica 依阿拉伯文史料寫的介紹，以及塔菲拉勒特綠洲的遺址。

cities.what_en: The last capital of ancient Ghana, a kingdom of Soninke people that grew rich as a middleman between the salt traders of the north and the gold producers of the south. The king taxed the trade, especially gold.
cities.what_zh: 古迦納最後的首都。迦納是索寧克人的王國，在北方的鹽商和南方的黃金產地之間當中間人而致富；國王向貿易抽稅，尤其是黃金。
cities.when_en: Ghana flourished from about the 7th or 8th century; before 1240 Kumbi was the greatest city of western Africa, with more than 15,000 people. The model uses 1000.
cities.when_zh: 迦納大約從七、八世紀開始興盛；1240 年以前，昆比是西非最大的城市，人口超過一萬五千。模型用 1000 年。
cities.how_en: Archaeology: Britannica says the 11th-century capital described by the geographer al-Bakrī has been tentatively identified as Kumbi. Like other early capitals, it had two towns, one for the king and one for Muslim traders.
cities.how_zh: 考古：Britannica 說，十一世紀地理學家巴克里描述的首都，暫時被認定就是昆比。和其他早期的首都一樣，它有兩個城區，一個是國王的，一個是穆斯林商人的。

cities.what_en: A salt-mining village in the middle of the desert. Ibn Battuta wrote that its houses and mosques were built of blocks of salt, roofed with camel skins, and that the salt was dug by enslaved workers of the Massufa.
cities.what_zh: 沙漠中間一個挖鹽的村子。伊本・巴杜達寫道，那裡的房子和清真寺是用鹽塊蓋的，屋頂鋪著駱駝皮；鹽是馬蘇法人手下被奴役的人挖出來的。
cities.when_en: Ibn Battuta passed through in 1352. The mines are older; the model uses his date.
cities.when_zh: 伊本・巴杜達在 1352 年經過。鹽礦比這更早；模型用他經過的年代。
cities.how_en: Ibn Battuta's own account of his travels. He also wrote that people further south used salt as money, the way gold and silver were used.
cities.how_zh: 伊本・巴杜達自己的遊記。他也寫到，再往南的人把鹽當錢用，就像用金銀一樣。
cities.src: Ibn Battuta, Travels, trans. Gibb (Fordham Internet History Sourcebooks)

cities.what_en: The first town of the Mali empire that caravans reached after crossing the desert from the north.
cities.what_zh: 從北方穿越沙漠的商隊，進入馬利帝國時到的第一個城鎮。
cities.when_en: Mansa Musa passed through on his pilgrimage in 1324; Ibn Battuta arrived in 1352.
cities.when_zh: 曼薩・穆薩 1324 年去朝覲時經過這裡；伊本・巴杜達在 1352 年到達。
cities.how_en: Britannica's account of Musa's pilgrimage, and Ibn Battuta's account, which calls it the northernmost province of the lands to the south.
cities.how_zh: Britannica 對曼薩・穆薩朝覲的記載，以及伊本・巴杜達的遊記（說這裡是南方國度最北邊的一省）。
cities.src: Britannica, “Musa I of Mali”; Ibn Battuta, Travels, trans. Gibb

cities.what_en: Sundiata Keita founded the Mali empire about 1235 and, according to Britannica, made Niani its capital. (Ibn Battuta does not name the capital he reached; the model assumes it was Niani.) Mali's wealth came from its gold and its place on the trade routes.
cities.what_zh: 松迪亞塔・凱塔大約在 1235 年建立馬利帝國；依照 Britannica 的說法，他以尼亞尼為首都。（伊本・巴杜達沒有寫出他到的首都叫什麼；模型假設是尼亞尼。）馬利的財富，來自它的黃金和它在貿易路線上的位置。
cities.when_en: About 1235. Niani reached its height under Mansa Musa (1307–32).
cities.when_zh: 大約 1235 年。尼亞尼在曼薩・穆薩（1307–32）的時候最興盛。
cities.how_en: Oral traditions kept by griots, and later Arabic writers such as al-ʿUmarī and Ibn Battuta, who reached Mali's capital in 1352. Britannica notes that the sources do not always agree.
cities.how_zh: 格里奧（griot）保存的口傳歷史，以及後來的阿拉伯文作者，例如烏馬里和 1352 年到過馬利首都的伊本・巴杜達。Britannica 指出，這些資料彼此不一定一致。

cities.what_en: Founded by Tuareg nomads where the desert meets the Niger River. Merchants met here to exchange gold and enslaved people for Saharan salt, North African cloth, and horses.
cities.what_zh: 圖阿雷格遊牧民在沙漠和尼日河交會的地方建立。商人在這裡用黃金和被奴役的人，交換撒哈拉的鹽、北非的布和馬。
cities.when_en: Founded around 1100; part of the Mali empire from the late 13th or early 14th century (Lessons 10 and 11).
cities.when_zh: 大約 1100 年建立；十三世紀末或十四世紀初成為馬利帝國的一部分（第十、十一課）。
cities.how_en: Its old mosques, and histories of the region.
cities.how_zh: 城裡的老清真寺，以及這個地區的史書。

cities.what_en: A trading city and center of Muslim scholarship on the floodlands between the Bani and Niger rivers. In the flood season it becomes an island.
cities.what_zh: 位在巴尼河和尼日河之間氾濫平原上的貿易城市和穆斯林學術中心。雨季淹水時，它會變成一座島。
cities.when_en: Its founding is uncertain, likely between the 8th and 13th centuries. The model uses 1250.
cities.when_zh: 它什麼時候建立並不確定，大概在八到十三世紀之間。模型用 1250 年。
cities.how_en: Archaeology and later histories.
cities.how_zh: 考古和後來的史書。

cities.what_en: A city on the Niger that the Songhai people made their capital. In the 15th and 16th centuries Songhai became a great trading state of West Africa.
cities.what_zh: 尼日河邊的城市，桑海人以它為首都。十五、十六世紀，桑海成為西非重要的貿易國家。
cities.when_en: The Songhai are said to have settled in Gao about 800, and made it their capital at the beginning of the 11th century.
cities.when_zh: 據說桑海人大約在 800 年住進加奧，十一世紀初以它為首都。
cities.how_en: Arabic chronicles and archaeology. Ibn Battuta visited in 1353 and called it one of the finest towns he saw in the region.
cities.how_zh: 阿拉伯文的編年史和考古。伊本・巴杜達 1353 年到過這裡，說它是那一帶最好的城鎮之一。
cities.src: Britannica, “Songhai empire”; Ibn Battuta, trans. Gibb

cities.what_en: Mansa Musa of Mali stopped here on his pilgrimage to Mecca. Chroniclers said he spent and gave away so much gold that its value in Cairo fell for years.
cities.what_zh: 馬利的曼薩・穆薩去麥加朝覲，途中在這裡停留。編年史家說，他花掉、送掉的黃金多到讓開羅的金價好幾年都下跌。
cities.when_en: 1324 (Lesson 10).
cities.how_en: Chroniclers of the time, writing in Arabic.
cities.how_zh: 當時用阿拉伯文寫作的編年史家。

cities.what_en: The goal of Mansa Musa's pilgrimage, the hajj (Lesson 10).
cities.what_zh: 曼薩・穆薩朝覲（hajj）的目的地（第十課）。
cities.how_en: Britannica's account of the pilgrimage.
cities.how_zh: Britannica 對這次朝覲的記載。

cities.what_en: The stone-walled center of a large state, built by ancestors of the Shona (Lesson 12). It supplied gold, ivory, and food to the coast.
cities.what_zh: 一個大國有石牆的中心，由紹納人的祖先所建（第十二課）。它供應黃金、象牙和食物給海岸。
cities.when_en: Built between about 1100 and 1450.
cities.when_zh: 大約在 1100 到 1450 年間興建。
cities.how_en: The ruins themselves. UNESCO dates the building to about 1100–1450; the Met gives about 1250–1450 for its height.
cities.how_zh: 遺址本身。聯合國教科文組織說大約 1100–1450 年間興建；大都會博物館說最興盛是大約 1250–1450 年。
cities.src: UNESCO, Great Zimbabwe; Metropolitan Museum of Art

cities.what_en: The oldest harbor in southern Africa. Traders came here for the gold of the interior, and it traded with the state centered on Great Zimbabwe.
cities.what_zh: 南部非洲最古老的港口。商人到這裡來買內陸的黃金；它也和以大辛巴威為中心的國家做生意。
cities.when_en: Arab traders began visiting in 915; in the 14th and 15th centuries it was an outpost of Kilwa. The Portuguese seized it in 1505.
cities.when_zh: 阿拉伯商人從 915 年開始來；十四、十五世紀是基爾瓦的前哨。葡萄牙人在 1505 年佔領它。
cities.how_en: Arabic geographers, and later Portuguese records.
cities.how_zh: 阿拉伯文的地理書，以及後來葡萄牙人的紀錄。

cities.what_en: A Swahili city-state on an island off the East African coast. Its wealth came from linking the gold and ivory of the interior, near Great Zimbabwe, with ports across the Indian Ocean (Lesson 9).
cities.what_zh: 東非外海一座島上的斯瓦希里城邦。它的財富來自把內陸（大辛巴威附近）的黃金和象牙，和印度洋對岸的港口連起來（第九課）。
cities.when_en: A town was there by the 8th or 9th century; Britannica dates its founding as a city-state to the late 10th century. The model uses 980.
cities.when_zh: 八或九世紀這裡已經有聚落；Britannica 把它成為城邦的年代定在十世紀後期。模型用 980 年。
cities.how_en: Its extensive ruins, including the Great Mosque and the Husuni Kubwa palace, and the Kilwa Chronicle, written in the 16th century. Historians debate who founded it (see “Different Accounts”).
cities.how_zh: 城裡大片的遺址，包括大清真寺和胡蘇尼庫布瓦宮，以及十六世紀寫成的《基爾瓦編年史》。它是誰建立的，歷史學家有不同的看法（見「不同的說法」）。

cities.what_en: For much of the 13th century the leading city of the East African coast, until Kilwa overtook it in the trade with Sofala.
cities.what_zh: 十三世紀大部分的時候是東非海岸最重要的城市，直到基爾瓦在和索法拉的貿易上超過它。
cities.when_en: 13th century.
cities.when_zh: 十三世紀。
cities.how_en: Britannica's account of the Shirazi period on the coast.
cities.how_zh: Britannica 對海岸設拉子時期的記載。

legs.en: Niani, Mali's capital, was a commercial and caravan center for gold, salt, kola nuts, and enslaved people. From such centers, gold is thought to have moved along the Niger toward Timbuktu.
legs.zh: 馬利的首都尼亞尼，是黃金、鹽、可樂果和被奴役的人的商業與商隊中心。黃金大概從這樣的中心，沿著尼日河往廷巴克圖去。

legs.en: At Timbuktu, where the desert meets the river, merchants exchanged gold for Saharan salt, North African cloth, and horses, and caravans carried it north across the Sahara.
legs.zh: 在沙漠和河交會的廷巴克圖，商人用黃金交換撒哈拉的鹽、北非的布和馬；商隊再把黃金往北帶過撒哈拉。

goods.note_en: This is one likely journey, not the record of one load. Sijilmasa lay on the caravan route from the Niger to Tangier. Centuries earlier, the kings of Ghana had grown rich by taxing this same gold trade.
goods.note_zh: 這是一條可能的旅程，不是某一批貨的紀錄。西吉爾馬薩位在從尼日河到海岸的丹吉爾的商隊路線上。好幾百年前，迦納的國王就是向同樣的黃金貿易抽稅而致富的。

legs.en: Slabs of salt dug at Taghaza were loaded onto camels for the desert crossing.
legs.zh: 在塔加扎挖出來的鹽板，放上駱駝，準備穿越沙漠。

legs.en: From Walata, the first town of Mali, traders carried it on south into the empire, where Ibn Battuta saw salt used as money.
legs.zh: 從馬利的第一個城鎮瓦拉塔，商人再把它往南帶進帝國；伊本・巴杜達在那裡看到鹽被當成錢用。

goods.note_en: Ibn Battuta wrote that the trade in salt at Taghaza was worth an enormous amount in gold dust. The stops follow his route in 1352.
goods.note_zh: 伊本・巴杜達寫道，塔加扎的鹽生意，值大量的金砂。這幾站照他 1352 年走的路線。

goods.same_en: One caravan the whole way: a pilgrimage, not a relay of traders
goods.same_zh: 一支商隊走完全程：這是朝覲，不是商人一段一段轉手

legs.en: Musa set out from Mali with a huge caravan; chroniclers of the time put it at some 60,000 people.
legs.zh: 曼薩・穆薩帶著龐大的商隊從馬利出發；當時的編年史家說大約有六萬人。

legs.en: The caravan went north through Walata and Tuat, across the Sahara, to Cairo, where Musa spent and gave away so much gold that its value fell.
legs.zh: 商隊經過瓦拉塔和圖瓦特，穿越撒哈拉到開羅；曼薩・穆薩在那裡花掉、送掉大量黃金，讓金價下跌。

legs.en: From Cairo the pilgrims went on to Mecca.
legs.zh: 朝覲的人從開羅再往麥加去。

goods.note_en: Carried by the same group the whole way: a pilgrimage, not a relay of traders. Britannica says Musa traveled from Niani to Walata and on to Tuat before reaching Cairo; he visited Gao on the way back. The model draws the desert crossing roughly.
goods.note_zh: 一路由同一批人帶：這是朝覲，不是商人一段一段的轉手。Britannica 說，他從尼亞尼到瓦拉塔，再到圖瓦特，然後到開羅；回程時他才去了加奧。模型只大略畫出穿越沙漠的路。

goods.same_en: One traveler the whole way, joining caravans and boats as he went
goods.same_zh: 一個旅人走完全程，一路搭商隊和船

legs.en: He left Sijilmasa with a caravan in February 1352.
legs.zh: 1352 年 2 月，他跟著商隊從西吉爾馬薩出發。

legs.en: After Taghaza, the caravan crossed more desert to Walata.
legs.zh: 過了塔加扎，商隊再穿越沙漠到瓦拉塔。

legs.en: He reached the capital of Mali in June 1352.
legs.zh: 1352 年 6 月，他到了馬利的首都。

legs.en: He left in February 1353 and went on to Timbuktu,
legs.zh: 1353 年 2 月他離開，先到廷巴克圖，

legs.en: and then down the Niger by boat to Gao, which he called one of the finest towns of the region.
legs.zh: 再坐船沿著尼日河到加奧；他說那是那一帶最好的城鎮之一。

goods.note_en: One traveler going the whole way, so no one handed anything on. His book, dictated later, is one of the main written sources for Mali, though some passages show the attitudes of an outsider, and the 1929 English translation uses outdated racial terms that this lesson does not repeat.
goods.note_zh: 一個旅人自己走完全程，所以沒有轉手。他後來口述的遊記，是馬利最主要的文字史料之一，不過有些段落也看得出外來者的成見；1929 年的英譯本還用了過時的種族稱呼，本課不沿用。

legs.en: Gold and ivory from the lands near Great Zimbabwe went down to the coast at Sofala.
legs.zh: 大辛巴威附近的黃金和象牙，被運到海岸的索法拉。

legs.en: Ships carried it north to Kilwa, which controlled the trade with Sofala, exchanging cloth and glass beads for gold.
legs.zh: 船把它往北運到基爾瓦；基爾瓦控制了和索法拉的貿易，用布和玻璃珠換黃金。

goods.note_en: From Kilwa, goods went on to ports across the Indian Ocean, which sent back glazed ceramics, textiles, perfumes, and silver. This is one likely journey.
goods.note_zh: 從基爾瓦，貨物再到印度洋對岸的港口；那些港口送回上釉的陶瓷、布、香水和白銀。這是一條可能的旅程。
goods.src: Metropolitan Museum of Art, “Kilwa Kisiwani and Songo Mnara”; Britannica, “Sofala”

lab.numbers_note_en: Each city lights up in the year given on its card, roughly when our evidence places it on the network; many are older. Routes show only the rough direction of travel, and appear only roughly in time. Two journeys follow real travelers; the others show likely paths.
lab.numbers_note_zh: 每一座城市在卡片上寫的那一年亮起來，大約是證據顯示它在這張網上的時候；很多城市其實更早就有了。路線只表示大致的方向，出現的時間也只是大約的。有兩段旅程跟著真實的旅人走，其他是可能的路徑。
lab.scale_en: This is a teaching sketch. The routes show only the rough direction of travel; caravans and boats used many paths. The map shows land only, with no modern borders.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意。路線只表示大致的方向；商隊和船走過許多不同的路。地圖只畫陸地，不畫今天的國界。
lab.credit_html: Globe: land outlines from Natural Earth (public domain). Places and dates follow the sources listed at the bottom of the page. 地球儀：陸地外形取自 Natural Earth（公有領域）。地方和年代依本頁最下面列出的資料。

paras: In the lands along the upper Niger and Senegal rivers, people mined gold. Far to the north, in the middle of the Sahara, salt was dug from the ground. Caravans of camels crossed the Sahara between the two, carrying salt south and gold north, and towns grew up where the routes began and ended.

The first great trading empire was Ghana, called Wagadu by its rulers. Its Soninke people acted as middlemen between the salt traders of the north and the producers of gold and ivory to the south, and the king taxed the trade, especially gold. Its last capital, Kumbi, had two towns: one for the king and one for Muslim traders. Before 1240 it was the greatest city of western Africa.

About 1235 Sundiata Keita founded the empire of Mali. Much of what we know about him comes from oral traditions kept by griots, who were hereditary historians, poets, and spokespeople for the king. Mali reached its height under Mansa Musa, whose pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324, with a caravan of some 60,000 people and great amounts of gold, made Mali famous in North Africa and Europe.

Mali's cities became centers of trade and learning. At Timbuktu, where the desert meets the Niger, merchants exchanged gold and enslaved people for salt, North African cloth, and horses. Enslaved people were bought and sold across the Sahara, and some served in the king's administration; historians study this too. In 1352 the traveler Ibn Battuta crossed the Sahara from Sijilmasa and described Taghaza, a village whose houses were built of blocks of salt.

In the 15th and 16th centuries, the Songhai empire, centered on Gao, became a great trading state of West Africa. Timbuktu reached the height of its trade and scholarship under the Askia rulers, from 1493 to 1591. In 1591 an army from Morocco took Timbuktu, and the city declined.

On the east coast, Swahili towns such as Mogadishu and Kilwa traded across the Indian Ocean with ports in Arabia, Persia, and India, and Chinese porcelain reached them too. Kilwa grew rich by controlling the trade with Sofala, where gold arrived from the lands near Great Zimbabwe. In 1505 Portuguese ships seized Sofala and briefly held Kilwa, trying to take over the gold trade.
paras_zh: 在上尼日河和塞內加爾河一帶，人們開採黃金。遠在北方的撒哈拉沙漠中間，人們從地下挖鹽。駱駝商隊在兩者之間穿越撒哈拉，把鹽往南運、把黃金往北運；路線的起點和終點，就長出了城鎮。
第一個大的貿易帝國是迦納，統治者自稱瓦加杜（Wagadu）。迦納的索寧克人，在北方的鹽商和南方出產黃金、象牙的人之間當中間人；國王向貿易抽稅，尤其是黃金。它最後的首都昆比有兩個城區：一個是國王的，一個是穆斯林商人的。1240 年以前，它是西非最大的城市。
大約 1235 年，松迪亞塔・凱塔建立馬利帝國。我們對他的了解，很多來自格里奧（griot）保存的口傳歷史；格里奧（吟遊詩人史家）是世襲的史家、詩人和國王的發言人。馬利在曼薩・穆薩的時候最興盛：他 1324 年去麥加朝覲，帶著大約六萬人的商隊和大量的黃金，讓馬利在北非和歐洲出了名。
馬利的城市成為貿易和學術的中心。在沙漠和尼日河交會的廷巴克圖，商人用黃金和被奴役的人，交換鹽、北非的布和馬。被奴役的人在撒哈拉兩邊被買賣，有些還在國王的行政裡工作；歷史學家也研究這一部分。1352 年，旅行家伊本・巴杜達從西吉爾馬薩穿越撒哈拉，描述了塔加扎：一個房子用鹽塊蓋的村子。
十五、十六世紀，以加奧為中心的桑海帝國，成為西非重要的貿易國家。廷巴克圖在阿斯基亞王朝（1493 到 1591 年）的時候，貿易和學術最興盛。1591 年，摩洛哥的軍隊攻下廷巴克圖，這座城從此衰落。
在東海岸，摩加迪休、基爾瓦這些斯瓦希里城鎮，橫越印度洋和阿拉伯、波斯、印度的港口做生意，中國的瓷器也運到了這裡。基爾瓦控制了和索法拉的貿易而致富；大辛巴威一帶的黃金就是運到索法拉。1505 年，葡萄牙的船佔領了索法拉，也短暫佔領了基爾瓦，想要接管黃金貿易。
questions: Why did people in West Africa trade gold for salt?
How did the kings of Ghana and Mali become rich?
Name two kinds of sources historians use to learn about Mali.
answers: The south had gold; the Sahara had salt. Each side traded what it had for what the other had.
They controlled the trade routes and the gold-producing lands, and they taxed the trade, especially gold.
Oral traditions kept by griots; Arabic writers such as Ibn Battuta and al-ʿUmarī; archaeology (any two).

quiz.q: What did the Sahara have that the lands to the south needed?
Who founded the empire of Mali, about 1235?
Who kept the oral history of Mali?

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Gold lines link Sijilmasa in the north with Kumbi, Ghana's capital, in the south.
parts.text_zh: 金色的線把北方的西吉爾馬薩和南方迦納的首都昆比連起來。

parts.text_en: Follow gold from Mali's capital to Timbuktu and across the desert. Count how many hands it passed through.
parts.text_zh: 跟著黃金從馬利的首都到廷巴克圖，再穿越沙漠。數一數它經過幾手。

parts.text_en: Ibn Battuta crossed the desert with a caravan. What did he see at Taghaza?
parts.text_zh: 伊本・巴杜達跟著商隊穿越沙漠。他在塔加扎看到了什麼？

parts.text_en: Gold from Great Zimbabwe reaches Kilwa by sea. Compare this network with the one across the Sahara.
parts.text_zh: 大辛巴威的黃金從海路到了基爾瓦。比一比這張網和撒哈拉的那一張。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then follow Mansa Musa. Why doesn't his journey count as changing hands?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著跟著曼薩・穆薩走。為什麼他的旅程不算換手？

northsouth.lead_en: Caravans crossed the Sahara in both directions. For each item, decide whether it mostly traveled north, toward North Africa and the Mediterranean, or south, toward the lands of the Niger. There is no timer.
northsouth.lead_zh: 商隊往兩個方向穿越撒哈拉。每一題判斷：它主要是往北走（往北非和地中海），還是往南走（往尼日河一帶的土地）？不計時。
northsouth.ask_en: Which way did it mostly travel?

items.why_en: Britannica says Ghana grew rich between the gold producers to the south and the salt traders to the north.
items.why_zh: Britannica 說，迦納夾在南方的黃金產地和北方的鹽商之間而致富。
items.hint_en: Where were the goldfields?
items.hint_zh: 金礦在哪裡？

items.why_en: Britannica says Ghana stood between the salt traders to the north and the producers of gold and ivory to the south, so the ivory, like the gold, went north.
items.why_zh: Britannica 說，迦納夾在北方的鹽商和南方出產黃金、象牙的人之間，所以象牙和黃金一樣往北走。
items.hint_en: It came from elephants of the savanna.
items.hint_zh: 它來自草原上的大象。

items.why_en: Britannica says merchants at Timbuktu exchanged gold and enslaved people for salt, cloth, and horses. This trade in people was part of the caravan routes too.
items.why_zh: Britannica 說，廷巴克圖的商人用黃金和被奴役的人，交換鹽、布和馬。這種人口的買賣，也是商隊路線的一部分。
items.hint_en: Read what was exchanged at Timbuktu.
items.hint_zh: 看看廷巴克圖交換的東西。

items.why_en: Salt was dug in the desert and carried south, where Ibn Battuta saw it used as money.
items.why_zh: 鹽在沙漠裡挖出來，往南運；伊本・巴杜達在南方看到人們把它當錢用。
items.hint_en: The salt mines were in the middle of the desert.
items.hint_zh: 鹽礦在沙漠中間。

items.why_en: Britannica lists North African cloth among the goods exchanged for gold at Timbuktu.
items.why_zh: Britannica 把北非的布列在廷巴克圖用來換黃金的貨物裡。
items.hint_en: It is named for where it came from.
items.hint_zh: 名字就說了它從哪裡來。

items.why_en: Britannica lists horses among the goods traded for gold at Timbuktu, and says Mali kept a large cavalry.
items.why_zh: Britannica 把馬列在廷巴克圖用來換黃金的貨物裡，也說馬利有一支很大的騎兵。
items.hint_en: Armies in the south needed them.
items.hint_zh: 南方的軍隊需要牠們。

northsouth.end_en: The trade made both sides rich in different ways, but it also carried people who were bought and sold. Historians study both.
northsouth.end_zh: 這些貿易讓兩邊都用不同的方式富起來，可是它也載運被買賣的人。歷史學家兩方面都要研究。

terms.en: Where Does This Word Come From?
terms.lead_en: Many English words about trade came along trade routes, through Arabic, Persian, Swahili, and Latin. For each Chinese word, pick the older word it came from and its English form. There is no timer.
terms.lead_zh: 很多關於貿易的英文字，是沿著貿易的路傳來的：經過阿拉伯文、波斯文、斯瓦希里文和拉丁文。每一個中文詞，選出它來源的那個比較古老的字，以及它的英文。不計時。
terms.ask_en: Which older word did it come from, and what is it in English?
terms.ask_zh: 它來自哪一個比較古老的字？英文是哪一個？

items.note_en: The Arabic word means “desert,” so “the Sahara Desert” really says “desert” twice.
items.note_zh: 這個阿拉伯字的意思就是「沙漠」，所以 Sahara Desert 其實說了兩次「沙漠」。

items.note_en: Sawāḥil means “coasts”; Swahili means “of the coast.”
items.note_zh: sawāḥil 是「海岸」（複數），Swahili 就是「海岸的」。

items.note_en: Mawsim means “season”; the word reached English through Portuguese and Dutch.
items.note_zh: mawsim 是「季節」的意思；這個字經過葡萄牙文和荷蘭文才進入英文。

items.note_en: Arabic safar means “journey”; English took the word from Swahili.
items.note_zh: 阿拉伯文 safar 是「旅程」；英文是從斯瓦希里文借來的。

items.note_en: Latin salārium was money given to Roman soldiers to buy salt, “salt money.”
items.note_zh: 拉丁文 salārium 是發給羅馬士兵買鹽的錢，也就是「鹽錢」。

items.note_en: From Persian, through Italian.
items.note_zh: 來自波斯文，經過義大利文。

items.note_en: From an Arabic word meaning “to make known,” through Italian.
items.note_zh: 來自阿拉伯文「讓人知道」的字，經過義大利文。

items.note_en: Makhāzin means “storehouses.” Through Italian and French, a magazine was first a warehouse, then a “storehouse of information.”
items.note_zh: makhāzin 是「倉庫」。magazine 原來指倉庫，後來才變成「資訊的倉庫」。

items.note_en: Through Italian, Latin, and French; related to Persian shakar.
items.note_zh: 經過義大利文、拉丁文和法文；和波斯文 shakar 有關。

items.note_en: Through Old French coton.
items.note_zh: 經過古法文 coton。

terms.end_en: Traders needed words for what they bought, sold, and taxed, and the words traveled as far as the goods.
terms.end_zh: 商人需要字眼來說買了什麼、賣了什麼、抽了什麼稅；這些字和貨物一樣走得很遠。

timeline.lead_en: Ghana, Mali, and Songhai followed one another in West Africa, while the Swahili coast and Great Zimbabwe flourished in the east and south.
timeline.lead_zh: 迦納、馬利、桑海在西非一個接一個；同時，斯瓦希里海岸和大辛巴威在東部和南部興盛。
timeline.idle_en: Click a bar or a diamond to read its dates.
timeline.idle_zh: 點一條長條或一個菱形，讀出它的年代。

tips.en: Ghana and Mali barely overlap: Sundiata took Kumbi in 1240.
tips.zh: 迦納和馬利幾乎沒有重疊：松迪亞塔在 1240 年拿下昆比。

tips.en: Great Zimbabwe and Kilwa rose together; the Met says Great Zimbabwe supplied Kilwa with gold and ivory.
tips.zh: 大辛巴威和基爾瓦一起興起；大都會博物館說，大辛巴威供應基爾瓦黃金和象牙。

tips.en: The gray diamonds mark single events, such as Mansa Musa's pilgrimage in 1324.
tips.zh: 灰色的菱形標的是單一事件，例如 1324 年曼薩・穆薩的朝覲。

events.note_en: Wealthy by the 8th century; Kumbi destroyed by Sundiata in 1240.
events.note_zh: 八世紀時已經富有；1240 年昆比被松迪亞塔摧毀。

events.note_en: On the caravan route to the Niger.
events.note_zh: 位在通往尼日河的商隊路線上。

events.note_en: Founded about 1235; by about 1550 no longer important as a state, and largely dissolved by the 17th century.
events.note_zh: 大約 1235 年建立；大約 1550 年已經不再是重要的國家，到十七世紀大多瓦解。

events.note_en: Through Cairo to Mecca.
events.note_zh: 經過開羅到麥加。

events.note_en: From Sijilmasa to Mali's capital, Timbuktu, and Gao.
events.note_zh: 從西吉爾馬薩到馬利的首都、廷巴克圖和加奧。

events.note_en: Morocco took Timbuktu in 1591.
events.note_zh: 1591 年摩洛哥攻下廷巴克圖。

events.note_en: Lesson 12.
events.note_zh: 第十二課。

events.note_en: They also held Kilwa from 1505 to 1512.
events.note_zh: 1505 到 1512 年也佔領基爾瓦。

events.note_en: Lesson 12: the age of castles.
events.note_zh: 第十二課：城堡的時代。

events.note_en: Lessons 10 and 11.
events.note_zh: 第十、十一課。

how_we_know.eyebrow: How Do We Know? · 我們怎麼知道？
how_we_know.en: Spoken histories, Arabic writers, and the ground
how_we_know.zh: 口傳的歷史、阿拉伯文作者，和土地本身
how_we_know.lead_en: Historians of these kingdoms put together three very different kinds of evidence.
how_we_know.lead_zh: 研究這些王國的歷史學家，要把三種很不一樣的證據拼起來。

items.limit_en: Britannica notes discrepancies between the oral and written accounts. In general, oral traditions keep the memory and meaning of events but rarely give exact dates.
items.limit_zh: Britannica 指出，口傳和文字的記載之間有出入。一般來說，口傳歷史保存了事件的記憶和意義，但很少有確切的年代。
items.src: Britannica, “Mali”
items.text_en: In Mali, griots were hereditary keepers of the empire's history and spokespeople for the king. Much of what we know about Sundiata comes from the stories and songs they passed down.
items.text_zh: 在馬利，格里奧是世襲的帝國史家，也是國王的發言人。我們對松迪亞塔的了解，很多來自他們一代一代傳下來的故事和歌。

items.limit_en: Britannica notes that these sources, valuable as they are, are not infallible. Travelers also wrote as outsiders, and the 1929 English translation of Ibn Battuta uses outdated racial terms that this lesson does not repeat.
items.limit_zh: Britannica 指出，這些資料雖然寶貴，但不是不會錯。旅人也是用外來者的眼光在寫；伊本・巴杜達 1929 年的英譯本還用了過時的種族稱呼，本課不沿用。
items.src: Britannica, “Mali” and “Ghana”; Ibn Battuta, trans. Gibb
items.text_en: Geographers and travelers writing in Arabic described these lands: al-Bakrī described Ghana's capital in the 11th century, and Ibn Battuta visited Mali in 1352–53 and gave exact dates for his journey.
items.text_zh: 用阿拉伯文寫作的地理學家和旅人描述了這些地方：十一世紀的巴克里描述了迦納的首都；伊本・巴杜達 1352 到 1353 年到過馬利，還寫下旅程確切的日期。

items.limit_en: Ruins show buildings and objects, but not the names, beliefs, and stories of the people who used them.
items.limit_zh: 遺址能看到建築和東西，但看不到使用它們的人的名字、信仰和故事。
items.src: Britannica, “Ghana,” “Kumbi,” and “Kilwa”
items.text_en: Archaeologists have excavated ruins at Koumbi Saleh, which Britannica says have been tentatively identified as Ghana's capital. At Kilwa, extensive ruins of the Great Mosque and the Husuni Kubwa palace remain.
items.text_zh: 考古學家在昆比薩利赫挖掘遺址；Britannica 說，它暫時被認定是迦納的首都。在基爾瓦，大清真寺和胡蘇尼庫布瓦宮留下了大片的遺址。

views.zh: 歷史學家討論的三個問題
views.lead_en: New evidence, from Arabic texts to ancient DNA, has changed some old stories. Here are three questions, with the views side by side.
views.lead_zh: 從阿拉伯文的文獻到古代的 DNA，新的證據改寫了一些舊故事。下面是三個問題，各種說法並列。
views.rule_en: Ask who wrote each source, and when.
views.rule_zh: 問一問：每一份資料是誰寫的？什麼時候寫的？

items.topic_en: Who founded Kilwa?
items.topic_zh: 基爾瓦是誰建立的？

sides.en: Britannica says Kilwa was founded in the late 10th century by settlers from Arabia and Persia. The Kilwa Chronicle, written in the 16th century, tells of Shirazi founders from Persia, though Britannica adds that whether they were really Persian is “somewhat doubtful.”
sides.zh: Britannica 說，基爾瓦是十世紀後期由阿拉伯和波斯來的移民建立的。十六世紀寫成的《基爾瓦編年史》說，建立者是從波斯來的設拉子人；不過 Britannica 也說，他們是不是真的來自波斯，「有點可疑」。

sides.label_en: An African town that joined a wider world
sides.label_zh: 一座和外面世界連起來的非洲城鎮
sides.en: The Metropolitan Museum describes Kilwa as first a fishing and weaving community of the 8th or 9th century, and the Swahili towns as primarily African communities. A 2023 study of ancient DNA estimated that people of African and Asian origin were mixing along the Swahili coast by about 1000 CE; before about 1500 the Asian ancestry was mostly Persian-related, which fits part of the chronicle.
sides.zh: 大都會博物館說，基爾瓦最早是八或九世紀的一個捕魚、織布的社群，斯瓦希里的城鎮主要是非洲人的社群。2023 年一項古代 DNA 的研究推估，大約西元 1000 年，斯瓦希里海岸上非洲和亞洲來源的人已經在混居、通婚；1500 年以前的亞洲血統主要和波斯有關，這和編年史的一部分相符。
sides.src: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Timeline of Art History; Brielle et al., Nature (2023)

items.note_en: Both views can fit: an African town on the coast, with newcomers from across the ocean who married into it. The Nature study notes that Swahili is an African Bantu language that took in words from Asian languages.
items.note_zh: 兩種說法可以同時成立：一座海岸邊的非洲城鎮，有從海外來、和當地人通婚的新住民。那篇 Nature 研究也指出，斯瓦希里語是吸收了亞洲語言字彙的非洲班圖語。

items.topic_en: Did the Almoravids conquer Ghana in 1076?
items.topic_zh: 穆拉比特人（阿爾摩拉維德人）在 1076 年征服了迦納嗎？

sides.label_zh: 阿爾摩拉維德人讓迦納衰落
sides.en: Britannica says Ghana began to decline in the 11th century with the rise of the Almoravids, a Muslim movement of Saharan Amazigh peoples. It says Abū Bakr, leader of their southern wing, took Audaghost in 1054 and seized Kumbi in 1076, though their rule over Ghana lasted only a few years.
sides.zh: Britannica 說，迦納在十一世紀開始衰落，是因為阿爾摩拉維德人（撒哈拉阿馬齊格人，也就是柏柏人的穆斯林運動）興起。它說，他們南路的領袖阿布・巴克爾 1054 年攻下奧達戈斯特，1076 年奪取昆比，不過他們統治迦納只有短短幾年。

sides.en: In 1982 the historians David Conrad and Humphrey Fisher re-read the external Arabic sources and argued that none of them clearly describes an Almoravid conquest of Ghana in 1076.
sides.zh: 1982 年，歷史學家康拉德和費雪重新讀了外部的阿拉伯文資料，主張其中沒有一份清楚記載阿爾摩拉維德人在 1076 年征服迦納。
sides.src: Conrad and Fisher, History in Africa 9 (1982)

items.note_en: Most historians accept that the Almoravids changed the trade of the western Sahara. The question is whether that happened by one conquest or by slower pressure.
items.note_zh: 多數歷史學家接受，阿爾摩拉維德人改變了撒哈拉西部的貿易；問題在於，那是一次征服，還是比較慢的壓力。

items.topic_en: Which sources tell Mali's story best?
items.topic_zh: 哪一種資料最能說出馬利的故事？

sides.en: Griots kept the history of Mali from the inside, in the words of its own people, including the story of Sundiata.
sides.zh: 格里奧從裡面保存了馬利的歷史，用的是馬利人自己的話，包括松迪亞塔的故事。

sides.en: Arabic writers such as al-ʿUmarī, Ibn Battuta, and Ibn Khaldūn recorded names, dates, and descriptions that oral traditions often leave out.
sides.zh: 烏馬里、伊本・巴杜達和伊本・赫勒敦這些阿拉伯文作者，記下了口傳歷史常常沒有的名字、年代和描述。

items.note_en: Britannica says the oral and written sources are both valuable but not infallible, and that they sometimes disagree. Historians compare them.
items.note_zh: Britannica 說，口傳和文字的資料都很寶貴，但都不是不會錯，有時還彼此矛盾。歷史學家會把它們互相比對。

phrases.en: Eight sentences for talking about trade and kingdoms
phrases.zh: 談貿易和王國的八句英文
phrases.lead_en: These sentences help you describe how trade made kingdoms rich. Listen, repeat, then make your own sentence with the words in bold.
phrases.lead_zh: 這八句幫你描述貿易怎麼讓王國富起來。先聽、再跟著唸，然後用粗體的字自己造一句。

rows.en: Gold was traded for salt.
rows.html: Gold was traded for salt.
rows.zh: 黃金被拿去換鹽。
rows.note_en: be traded for: be exchanged for

rows.en: The king taxed the gold trade.
rows.html: The king taxed the gold trade.
rows.zh: 國王向黃金貿易抽稅。
rows.note_en: tax: take money from

rows.en: Caravans crossed the Sahara.
rows.html: Caravans crossed the Sahara.
rows.zh: 商隊穿越撒哈拉。
rows.note_en: cross: go from one side to the other

rows.en: Ghana acted as a middleman.
rows.html: Ghana acted as a middleman.
rows.zh: 迦納扮演中間人的角色。
rows.note_en: act as a middleman: stand between buyers and sellers

rows.en: Mali grew rich from gold.
rows.html: Mali grew rich from gold.
rows.zh: 馬利靠黃金致富。
rows.note_en: grow rich from: become wealthy because of

rows.en: Salt was used as money.
rows.html: Salt was used as money.
rows.zh: 鹽被當成錢來用。
rows.note_en: be used as: serve as

rows.en: Griots passed down the story of Sundiata.
rows.html: Griots passed down the story of Sundiata.
rows.zh: 格里奧把松迪亞塔的故事傳了下來。
rows.note_en: pass down: give to the next generation

rows.en: Ships sailed across the Indian Ocean.
rows.html: Ships sailed across the Indian Ocean.
rows.zh: 船航行橫越印度洋。
rows.note_en: sail across: go over the sea

taiwan_then.eyebrow: Taiwan at That Time · 那時候的台灣
taiwan_then.lead_en: Taiwan was not on these routes, but gold and trade goods appear in its story too.
taiwan_then.lead_zh: 台灣不在這些路線上，但黃金和貿易品也出現在台灣的故事裡。
taiwan_then.intro_en: Archaeologists in Taiwan give dates as “years ago.” The Shisanhang culture began about 2,000 years ago; its Tang and Song coins point to overseas contact in the centuries of Ghana and Mali.
taiwan_then.intro_zh: 台灣的考古學家用「距今幾年」說年代。十三行文化大約兩千年前興起；遺址裡的唐宋古錢，說明了它在迦納和馬利那幾百年和海外的往來。

facts.en: The museum says Shisanhang sites held gold ornaments, glass bracelets, and Tang and Song coins, which show overseas trade.
facts.zh: 史前館說，從出土的唐宋古錢及金飾、玻璃手環等，「可知他們有海外貿易的情形」。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

facts.en: On the east coast, the Jingpu culture, from about 1,500 to a few hundred years ago, had copper and gold ornaments and agate and glass that came from overseas.
facts.zh: 在東海岸，大約距今一千五百年到兩、三百年前的靜浦文化，有銅、金的裝飾品，以及來自海外的瑪瑙和琉璃。
facts.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

facts.en: In the 14th century, at the time of Mali's greatest wealth, the Yuan traveler Wang Dayuan wrote that an island called Liuqiu, very near Penghu, produced gold dust, sulfur, and the hides of deer and leopards, among other goods. Scholars still debate whether it means Taiwan (Lesson 9).
facts.zh: 十四世紀，正是馬利最富有的時候，元朝旅行家汪大淵寫道，「自彭湖望之甚近」的「琉球」出產「沙金、黃荳、黍子、硫黃、黃蠟、鹿、豹、麂皮」。這是不是指台灣，學者還在討論（第九課）。
facts.src: 汪大淵《島夷誌略》「琉球」

links.en: World History · Lesson 9: What Traveled Along the Silk Road?
links.zh: 世界歷史・第九課：絲路上走的是什麼？

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Evidence · 證據背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A town of salt, the keepers of memory, a two-town capital, and a palace by the sea
culture_cards.title_zh: 鹽蓋的村子、記憶的守護者、兩個城區的首都，和海邊的宮殿
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about the people and places of the gold and salt trade.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事：黃金和鹽的貿易裡的人和地方。

cards.body_en: Ibn Battuta found that at Taghaza even the houses and mosques were built of blocks of salt, roofed with camel skins. The salt was dug by enslaved workers of the Massufa, and the trade there was worth huge amounts of gold dust.
cards.body_zh: 伊本・巴杜達發現，在塔加扎，連房子和清真寺都是用鹽塊蓋的，屋頂鋪駱駝皮。鹽由馬蘇法人手下被奴役的人挖掘，那裡的生意值大量的金砂。

cards.body_en: Griots were hereditary keepers of Mali's history and spokespeople for the king. Through them the story of Sundiata, who founded the empire about 1235, has been told for centuries.
cards.body_zh: 格里奧是世襲的馬利歷史守護者，也替國王說話。靠著他們，大約 1235 年建立帝國的松迪亞塔的故事，被講了好幾百年。

cards.body_en: Ghana's capital had two towns: one for the king and one for Muslim traders. With more than 15,000 people, it was the greatest city of western Africa before 1240.
cards.body_zh: 迦納的首都有兩個城區：一個是國王的，一個是穆斯林商人的。它有一萬五千多人，1240 年以前是西非最大的城市。

cards.body_en: The great palace of Husuni Kubwa at Kilwa was built of coral stone in the 13th–14th century. The Met describes Swahili, Arab, Persian, and Indian influences there, combined into a style distinct to the Swahili coast.
cards.body_zh: 基爾瓦的胡蘇尼庫布瓦大宮殿，在十三到十四世紀用珊瑚石蓋成。大都會博物館說，那裡融合了斯瓦希里本地、阿拉伯、波斯和印度的影響，成為斯瓦希里海岸獨有的風格。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum for social studies (October 2018).
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要社會領域（民國 107 年 10 月）。

items.area: 國中・古代文化的遺產
items.area_en: Junior high · the heritage of ancient cultures
items.text: 非洲與西亞的早期文化。
items.note_en: The explanation suggests using Egypt as the main example for Africa. This lesson adds the trading kingdoms of West and East Africa.
items.note_zh: 課綱的說明建議「非洲可以埃及文化為主」。這一課補上西非和東非的貿易王國。

items.area: 國中・地理・漠南非洲
items.area_en: Junior high · geography · sub-Saharan Africa
items.text: 漠南非洲的文化特色與影響。
items.note_en: The history of Ghana, Mali, Songhai, and the Swahili coast helps explain the cultures of sub-Saharan Africa today.
items.note_zh: 迦納、馬利、桑海和斯瓦希里海岸的歷史，有助於理解今天漠南非洲的文化。

myths.myth_en: Africa had no kingdoms or written history before Europeans arrived.
myths.myth_zh: 歐洲人來以前，非洲沒有王國，也沒有寫下來的歷史。
myths.fact_en: Ghana was wealthy by the 8th century, and Mali and Songhai followed. Their history survives in oral traditions, in Arabic writings, in archaeology, and in writings by Africans themselves, such as the Kilwa Chronicle of the 16th century.
myths.fact_zh: 迦納在八世紀就已經富有，接著是馬利和桑海。它們的歷史保存在口傳、阿拉伯文的著作、考古，以及非洲人自己寫的著作裡，例如十六世紀的《基爾瓦編年史》。

myths.myth_en: The Sahara cut Africa off from the rest of the world.
myths.myth_zh: 撒哈拉把非洲和世界隔開了。
myths.fact_en: Caravan routes crossed it for centuries. Sijilmasa, founded in 757, became the leading center of trans-Saharan trade in the western Maghrib.
myths.fact_zh: 商隊路線穿越它好幾百年。757 年建立的西吉爾馬薩，成為北非西部橫越撒哈拉貿易最重要的中心。

myths.myth_en: Salt was too common to matter.
myths.myth_zh: 鹽太普通了，不重要。
myths.fact_en: Ibn Battuta saw salt used as money south of the Sahara. Even the English word salary comes from the Latin for “salt money.”
myths.fact_zh: 伊本・巴杜達看到撒哈拉以南的人把鹽當錢用。連英文的 salary（薪水）都來自拉丁文的「鹽錢」。

myths.myth_en: The Swahili towns were foreign colonies.
myths.myth_zh: 斯瓦希里城鎮是外國的殖民地。
myths.fact_en: The Met describes them as primarily African communities. Swahili is an African Bantu language that took in words from Asian languages, and an ancient-DNA study estimates that African and Asian families were mixing on the coast by about 1000 CE.
myths.fact_zh: 大都會博物館說它們主要是非洲人的社群。斯瓦希里語是吸收了亞洲語言字彙的非洲班圖語；一項古代 DNA 研究推估，大約西元 1000 年，海岸上非洲和亞洲的家族已經在混居、通婚。

tricks.body_en: The south had gold; the desert had salt.
tricks.body_zh: 南方有黃金，沙漠有鹽。

tricks.body_en: Ghana, Mali, and Songhai grew rich by controlling the routes.
tricks.body_zh: 迦納、馬利、桑海靠控制商路致富。

tricks.body_en: Griots spoke it; Arabic writers wrote it.
tricks.body_zh: 格里奧用說的，阿拉伯文作者用寫的。

tricks.body_en: Camels across the Sahara; ships across the Indian Ocean.
tricks.body_zh: 駱駝穿越撒哈拉；船橫越印度洋。

materials.en: Cards for gold, salt, cloth, horses, and ivory; a few “tax” tokens for the king
materials.zh: 黃金、鹽、布、馬、象牙的卡片；幾個國王收稅用的代幣

steps.en: Split the class into northern traders (with salt, cloth, horses) and southern traders (with gold and ivory). One student is the king of Ghana in the middle.
steps.zh: 全班分成北方商人（有鹽、布、馬）和南方商人（有黃金、象牙），中間一個學生當迦納國王。

steps.en: Traders must pass through the king, who takes one tax token for each trade.
steps.zh: 每一筆交易都要經過國王，國王每一筆收一個稅的代幣。

steps.en: After five minutes, count: who became richest, and why?
steps.zh: 五分鐘後清點：誰最富有？為什麼？

steps.en: Discuss in English: “The king grew rich from …” and “Salt was traded for …”
steps.zh: 用英文討論：「The king grew rich from …」和「Salt was traded for …」

activities.tip_en: Do not include people as trade cards. If students ask, explain plainly that enslaved people were traded too, and that this is part of the history, not part of the game.
activities.tip_zh: 不要把人當成交易卡。學生問的時候，清楚地說明：被奴役的人也被買賣，這是歷史的一部分，不是遊戲的一部分。

materials.en: The 3D globe in this lesson
materials.zh: 這一課的 3D 地球儀

materials.en: A blank map of Africa (land only)
materials.zh: 一張只畫陸地的非洲空白地圖

steps.en: Follow Ibn Battuta's journey on the globe and draw it on the map.
steps.zh: 在地球儀上跟著伊本・巴杜達走，畫在地圖上。

steps.en: At each stop, write one thing he saw or did.
steps.zh: 每一站寫下他看到或做的一件事。

steps.en: Then follow Mansa Musa. Write two sentences comparing the two journeys.
steps.zh: 接著跟著曼薩・穆薩走，用兩句英文比較這兩段旅程。

activities.tip_en: Remind students that Ibn Battuta was an outsider, and that the people of Mali told their own history through the griots.
activities.tip_zh: 提醒學生：伊本・巴杜達是外來的人，馬利人用格里奧講自己的歷史。

links.note_en: Islam reached West Africa with traders across the Sahara.
links.note_zh: 伊斯蘭教跟著商人穿越撒哈拉到了西非。

links.zh: 絲路上走的是什麼？

lessons.sources_note_en: Checked November 2026. Who founded Kilwa, whether the Almoravids conquered Ghana in 1076, and how to weigh oral and written sources are debated; where they are, the lesson gives more than one view
lessons.sources_note_zh: 2026 年 11 月查證。基爾瓦是誰建立的、阿爾摩拉維德人有沒有在 1076 年征服迦納，以及口傳和文字資料怎麼比重，都有爭論；遇到這些地方，課文寫出不只一種說法

sources.en: Ghana: 7th–13th centuries; Soninke middlemen between salt traders and gold and ivory producers; taxes on gold; capital described by al-Bakrī tentatively identified as Kumbi; Almoravids took Kumbi in 1076; Sundiata in 1240
sources.zh: 迦納：七到十三世紀；索寧克人在鹽商和黃金象牙產地之間當中間人；黃金稅；阿爾摩拉維德人興起後衰落；1240 年松迪亞塔

sources.en: Kumbi: last capital of Ghana; two towns; more than 15,000 people before 1240
sources.zh: 昆比：迦納最後的首都；兩個城區；1240 年以前一萬五千多人

sources.en: Sijilmasa founded 757 on the caravan route; leading center of trans-Saharan trade in the western Maghrib; destroyed 1363
sources.zh: 西吉爾馬薩 757 年建於商隊路線上；北非西部橫越撒哈拉貿易的中心；1363 年被毀

sources.en: The Almoravids: Saharan Berber movement of the 11th century
sources.zh: 阿爾摩拉維德人：十一世紀撒哈拉柏柏人的運動

sources.en: “The Conquest that Never Was: Ghana and the Almoravids, 1076. I. The External Arabic Sources”
sources.zh: 〈從來沒有發生的征服：迦納與阿爾摩拉維德人，1076（一）外部的阿拉伯文資料〉
sources.src: Conrad and Fisher, History in Africa 9 (1982): 21–59

sources.en: Mali: Sundiata about 1235; Kirina; Mansa Musa (about 1307–32) and 1324; griots; Arabic chroniclers; sources not infallible; decline
sources.zh: 馬利：約 1235 年的松迪亞塔；基里納之戰；曼薩・穆薩（約 1307–32）與 1324 年；格里奧；阿拉伯文的編年史家；資料不是不會錯；衰落

sources.en: Sundiata Keita
sources.zh: 松迪亞塔・凱塔

sources.en: Niani as Mali's capital; gold, salt, kola nuts, and enslaved people
sources.zh: 尼亞尼是馬利的首都；黃金、鹽、可樂果、被奴役的人

sources.en: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage of 1324: about 60,000 people; gold in Cairo
sources.zh: 曼薩・穆薩 1324 年的朝覲：約六萬人；開羅的黃金

sources.en: Timbuktu: founded about 1100 by Tuareg nomads; gold and enslaved people exchanged for salt, cloth, and horses; Askia period 1493–1591
sources.zh: 廷巴克圖：約 1100 年由圖阿雷格人建立；用黃金和被奴役的人交換鹽、布、馬；阿斯基亞時期 1493–1591

sources.en: Djenné: trading city and center of Muslim scholarship; founded between the 8th and 13th centuries
sources.zh: 傑內：貿易城市與穆斯林學術中心；八到十三世紀之間建立

sources.en: The Songhai empire, centered on Gao
sources.zh: 以加奧為中心的桑海帝國

sources.en: Ibn Battuta: Taghaza's salt houses; salt as money; Walata; Mali's capital (June 1352–February 1353); Timbuktu; Gao
sources.zh: 伊本・巴杜達：塔加扎的鹽屋；鹽當錢用；瓦拉塔；馬利的首都（1352 年 6 月–1353 年 2 月）；廷巴克圖；加奧
sources.src: Ibn Battuta, Travels in Asia and Africa, trans. H. A. R. Gibb (1929), Fordham Internet History Sourcebooks. This translation uses outdated racial terms; the lesson does not repeat them.

sources.en: Kilwa: founded in the late 10th century by settlers from Arabia and Persia (Britannica); Portuguese 1505–12; Husuni Kubwa
sources.zh: 基爾瓦：十世紀後期由阿拉伯和波斯移民建立（Britannica）；1505–12 年葡萄牙；胡蘇尼庫布瓦宮

sources.en: Sofala: oldest harbor in southern Africa; Arab traders from 915; outpost of Kilwa; trade with the Zimbabwe state; Portuguese 1505
sources.zh: 索法拉：南部非洲最古老的港口；915 年起阿拉伯商人來；基爾瓦的前哨；和辛巴威的貿易；1505 年葡萄牙

sources.en: Mogadishu leading the coast in the 13th century; the Shirazi migration
sources.zh: 十三世紀摩加迪休領先海岸；設拉子人的遷移

sources.en: Kilwa's wealth from linking gold and ivory near Great Zimbabwe with Indian Ocean ports
sources.zh: 基爾瓦的財富來自把大辛巴威附近的黃金象牙和印度洋港口連起來
sources.src: Metropolitan Museum of Art, “Kilwa Kisiwani and Songo Mnara”

sources.en: Swahili towns as primarily African communities; Kilwa first a fishing and weaving community; Great Zimbabwe supplying Kilwa
sources.zh: 斯瓦希里城鎮主要是非洲人的社群；基爾瓦最早是捕魚織布的社群；大辛巴威供應基爾瓦
sources.src: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History, Eastern and Southern Africa 500–1000 and 1000–1400

sources.en: Ancient DNA: African and Asian ancestry mixing on the Swahili coast by about 1000 CE (estimate); mostly Persian-related Asian ancestry before 1500; Swahili a Bantu language with Asian loanwords
sources.zh: 古代 DNA：約西元 1000 年起斯瓦希里海岸非洲與亞洲血統的混合
sources.src: Brielle et al., “Entwined African and Asian genetic roots of medieval peoples of the Swahili coast,” Nature (2023)

sources.en: Word origins: Sahara, Swahili, monsoon, safari, salary, caravan, tariff, magazine, sugar, cotton
sources.zh: 字源：Sahara、Swahili、monsoon、safari、salary、caravan、tariff、magazine、sugar、cotton

sources.en: Shisanhang gold ornaments and coins; Jingpu agate and glass from overseas
sources.zh: 十三行的金飾與古錢；靜浦來自海外的瑪瑙與琉璃
sources.src: 國立臺灣史前文化博物館 考古學習資源

sources.en: Liuqiu's gold dust in the Daoyi zhilüe
sources.zh: 《島夷誌略》的「琉球」沙金
sources.src: 汪大淵《島夷誌略》（維基文庫）
