lessons.title: What Did the Maya, Aztecs, and Inca Build?
lessons.title_zh: 馬雅、阿茲特克、印加蓋了什麼？
lessons.blurb_en: Watch Maya and Aztec cities and the Inca roads light up on a 3D globe, then follow tribute to Tenochtitlan, a runner's message down the Andes, and the Spanish march to Cusco. Read and write Maya numbers, and find English words that came from Nahuatl and Quechua.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 地球儀上看馬雅、阿茲特克的城市和印加的道路亮起來，再跟著貢品到特諾奇提特蘭、跟著信差的消息沿安地斯山南下、跟著西班牙人行軍到庫斯科。讀一讀、寫一寫馬雅的數字，也找一找來自納瓦特語和克丘亞語的英文字。
lessons.big_idea_en: Long before Europeans arrived, peoples of the Americas built great cities, calendars, and roads. The Maya carved stone cities and a full writing system; the Aztecs built Tenochtitlan on a lake; the Inca linked the Andes with more than 30,000 km of roads. They did it without carts or draft animals. The Maya, Nahua, and Quechua peoples still live there today.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 早在歐洲人來以前，美洲的人們就蓋出了偉大的城市、曆法和道路。馬雅人用石頭蓋城市，還有完整的文字；阿茲特克人把特諾奇提特蘭蓋在湖上；印加人用超過三萬公里的道路把安地斯山連起來。他們沒有車子，也沒有拉車的牲口，還是做到了。馬雅人、納瓦人、克丘亞人今天都還住在那裡。

lab.title_en: Cities and Roads of the Americas
lab.aria: 3D globe of the Americas showing, in rough outline, the cities of the Maya and the Aztecs and the Inca road network along the Andes; only land, sea, and routes are drawn, with no borders · 3D 美洲地球儀，大略畫出馬雅和阿茲特克的城市，以及沿著安地斯山的印加道路網；只畫陸地、海洋與路線，沒有國界
lab.how_en: Drag the slider from 1 to 1600 CE, or press Play. First the cities of Mexico and Central America light up; later the Inca roads spread along the Andes. Under “Follow one thing,” choose tribute, a runner's message, or the Spanish march, and a pink dot will carry it from stop to stop. Click a city to read about it and how we know.
lab.how_zh: 把滑桿從西元 1 年拉到 1600 年，或按「播放」。先是墨西哥和中美洲的城市亮起來，後來印加的道路沿著安地斯山展開。在「跟著一件東西走」選貢品、信差的消息或西班牙人的行軍，粉紅色的小點會把它一站一站帶過去。點一座城市，讀它的故事和我們怎麼知道。

cities.what_en: The largest city of central Mexico before the Aztecs, with the Pyramid of the Sun and the Avenue of the Dead. Its trade and influence reached across Mesoamerica. The name, meaning “City of the Gods,” is what the Aztecs called it centuries later; the language of its own people is unknown.
cities.what_zh: 阿茲特克人之前，墨西哥中部最大的城市，有太陽金字塔和「亡者大道」。它的貿易和影響遍及中美洲。「眾神之城」這個名字，是幾百年後阿茲特克人給它取的；城裡的人自己說什麼語言，我們不知道。
cities.when_en: Settled by 400 BCE, with large-scale growth from about three centuries later; at its height about 500 CE it covered some 20 square km, with an estimated 125,000–200,000 people. The model starts it at 1 CE.
cities.when_zh: 西元前 400 年已有人居住，大約三百年後開始大規模成長；大約西元 500 年最興盛時，面積約 20 平方公里，估計有十二萬五千到二十萬人。模型從西元 1 年開始。
cities.how_en: Archaeology: its pyramids, avenues, and apartment compounds.
cities.how_zh: 考古：它的金字塔、大道和集合住宅。

cities.what_en: The largest city of the southern Maya lowlands, in the rainforest of northern Guatemala. Britannica says it became part of the trading network set up by Teotihuacan. Its tallest temple-pyramid rises about 65 meters.
cities.what_zh: 馬雅南部低地最大的城市，在瓜地馬拉北部的雨林裡。Britannica 說，它成為特奧蒂瓦坎建立的貿易網的一部分。它最高的神廟金字塔大約 65 公尺高。
cities.when_en: A village by 900–300 BCE; a ceremonial center by 100 CE; at its height between 600 and 800. The model uses 250, the start of the Classic Period.
cities.when_zh: 西元前 900–300 年已是村落；西元 100 年前成為祭典中心；600 到 800 年最興盛。模型用古典期開始的 250 年。
cities.how_en: Archaeology and the Maya inscriptions carved on its monuments.
cities.how_zh: 考古，以及刻在紀念碑上的馬雅文字。

cities.what_en: A Maya city famous for its carved stelae and its Hieroglyphic Stairway, whose 63 remaining steps carry some 1,260 glyphs.
cities.what_zh: 以雕刻的石碑和「象形文字階梯」聞名的馬雅城市；留下來的 63 級階梯上刻了大約 1,260 個字符。
cities.when_en: A dynasty of at least 16 kings ruled from about 426 to 822; at its peak, early in the 9th century, perhaps 20,000 people lived there.
cities.when_zh: 至少十六位國王的王朝，大約從 426 年統治到 822 年；九世紀初最興盛時，可能有兩萬人。
cities.how_en: Its inscriptions: since 1975, decipherment has revealed much of its political and dynastic history.
cities.how_zh: 它的銘文：1975 年起，解讀出來的文字讓我們知道了它大部分的政治和王朝歷史。

cities.what_en: A Maya city in the Yucatán built beside cenotes, natural sinkholes that gave water. It has El Castillo, a stepped pyramid, the largest ball court in the Americas, and the round building called El Caracol.
cities.what_zh: 猶加敦半島上，蓋在天然水井（cenote，石灰岩陷落形成的水坑）旁邊的馬雅城市。城裡有階梯金字塔「卡斯蒂略」、美洲最大的球場，還有圓形的建築「蝸牛」（El Caracol）。
cities.when_en: Founded around the 6th century; most of its major buildings date from about 900 to 1200; overtaken by Mayapán around 1200.
cities.when_zh: 大約六世紀建立；主要的建築大多在大約 900 到 1200 年間；大約 1200 年被馬雅潘取代。
cities.how_en: Archaeology since the 19th century.
cities.how_zh: 十九世紀以來的考古。

cities.what_en: The Aztec (Mexica) capital, built on islands in Lake Texcoco and joined to the shore by causeways. It grew by building more islands, and its farmers raised crops on chinampas, narrow fields built up from the mud of the lake. Mexico City stands on it today.
cities.what_zh: 阿茲特克（墨西加）人的首都，蓋在特斯科科湖的島上，用堤道和岸邊相連。它靠著再造新的島長大；農人在浮田（chinampa）上種作物，浮田是用湖底的泥一層一層堆起來的狹長田地。今天的墨西哥城就在它上面。
cities.when_en: Founded about 1325 on a small island; by 1519 it covered more than 13 square km. Spanish forces under Hernán Cortés, with thousands of Indigenous allies, took it in August 1521.
cities.when_zh: 大約 1325 年在一座小島上建立；到了 1519 年，面積超過 13 平方公里。1521 年 8 月，科爾特斯率領的西班牙軍隊，加上數千名原住民盟軍，攻下了它。
cities.how_en: Aztec tradition tells of an eagle on a cactus that showed the founders where to build. Writings in Nahuatl from the 16th century, Spanish accounts, and archaeology under Mexico City tell the rest.
cities.how_zh: 阿茲特克的傳統說，一隻停在仙人掌上的老鷹，告訴建城的人要蓋在哪裡。其餘的，靠十六世紀用納瓦特語寫的文獻、西班牙人的記載，以及墨西哥城地底下的考古。

cities.what_en: A province near the Gulf Coast that paid tribute to the Aztec capital. The Codex Mendoza shows its seven towns and what they sent: mostly garments, along with warrior costumes, feather shields, bags of feathers, beads of jadeite and turquoise, and baskets of dry chili peppers.
cities.what_zh: 墨西哥灣岸附近，向阿茲特克首都進貢的一個省。《門多薩抄本》畫出它的七個城鎮和送去的東西：大多是衣服，還有戰士的服裝、羽毛盾牌、一袋袋羽毛、翡翠和綠松石的珠子，以及一籃籃的乾辣椒。
cities.when_en: The tribute was paid in the 15th and early 16th centuries; the model uses 1500.
cities.when_zh: 這些貢品是在十五世紀到十六世紀初繳的；模型用 1500 年。
cities.how_en: The Codex Mendoza, painted in 1542 by Nahua scribes, called tlacuilos, two decades after the conquest, likely for the king of Spain.
cities.how_zh: 《門多薩抄本》：征服之後二十年、1542 年，由納瓦人的書記（tlacuilo）畫成，大概是要給西班牙國王看的。
cities.src: Metropolitan Museum of Art, “Paying the Man: Ancient Tributes in Golden Kingdoms”

cities.what_en: The Inca capital, high in the Andes. Its name comes from a Quechua word for “navel” or “center.” Its walls were built of stones cut so precisely that they fit without mortar, and many still stand under Spanish colonial buildings. UNESCO says the four main Inca roads began at its central square.
cities.what_zh: 印加的首都，在安地斯山的高處。名字來自克丘亞語的「肚臍」或「中心」。城牆的石頭切得非常精準，不用灰漿就能密合，很多到今天還在西班牙殖民時期的建築底下。UNESCO 說，印加的四條主要道路從它的中央廣場出發。
cities.when_en: The Inca made it their capital in the 12th century. Spanish forces took it in November 1533.
cities.when_zh: 印加人在十二世紀以它為首都。1533 年 11 月，西班牙軍隊攻下了它。
cities.how_en: Archaeology, the surviving stonework, and accounts written by Spaniards from what Inca officials told them.
cities.how_zh: 考古、留下來的石造建築，以及西班牙人根據印加官員的口述寫下的記載。

cities.what_en: An Inca site in a narrow saddle between two peaks, high above the Urubamba River. Its building style and other evidence suggest it was a palace complex of the ruler Pachacuti, and its remains suggest a royal retreat. It was one of many sites along the Inca road.
cities.what_zh: 在烏魯班巴河上方高處、兩座山峰之間狹窄鞍部上的印加遺址。從建築風格和其他證據看，它可能是統治者帕查庫蒂的宮殿群；遺骸和遺物也顯示它是王室休憩的地方。它是印加道路沿線許多據點中的一個。
cities.when_en: Built and lived in from the mid-15th to the early or mid-16th century.
cities.when_zh: 大約從十五世紀中期到十六世紀初或中期，有人興建、居住。
cities.how_en: Archaeology. In 1911 a local Quechua-speaking resident, Melchor Arteaga, led the Yale professor Hiram Bingham to it; it was not lost to the people who lived nearby.
cities.how_zh: 考古。1911 年，當地說克丘亞語的居民梅爾喬・阿特亞加，帶耶魯大學的教授賓漢來到這裡；住在附近的人一直知道它在那裡。

cities.what_en: A rope bridge over a gorge of the Apurímac River. Every year four Quechua-speaking communities rebuild it in three days, twisting grass into ropes with traditional Inca techniques and tying them to ancient stone bases.
cities.what_zh: 跨越阿普里馬克河峽谷的繩橋。每年，四個說克丘亞語的社區花三天重建它：用傳統的印加技術把草搓成繩子，綁在古老的石頭基座上。
cities.when_en: Rebuilt every year to this day. The source does not give the crossing's age; the model uses 1450, with the other Inca roads.
cities.when_zh: 直到今天每年重建。資料沒有說這個渡口有多古老；模型用 1450 年，和其他印加道路一起亮起來。
cities.how_en: UNESCO lists the knowledge and rituals of its renewal as intangible cultural heritage (2013). Families pass on the weaving skills.
cities.how_zh: UNESCO 在 2013 年把重建它的知識和儀式列為非物質文化遺產；編織的技術在家族裡傳承。

cities.what_en: A city in the northern Andes that the Inca brought into their empire. Later the emperor Huayna Capac's son Atahuallpa ruled the northern part of the empire from here.
cities.what_zh: 安地斯山北部的城市，被納入印加帝國。後來，皇帝瓦伊納・卡帕克的兒子阿塔瓦爾帕從這裡統治帝國的北半部。
cities.when_en: Conquered under Pachacuti (1438–71); the model uses 1470.
cities.when_zh: 在帕查庫蒂（1438–71）的時候被征服；模型用 1470 年。
cities.how_en: Inca histories written down by Spaniards in the 16th century.
cities.how_zh: 十六世紀西班牙人記下來的印加歷史。

cities.what_en: The southern edge of the Inca empire, in central Chile. UNESCO says the empire stretched up to 4,200 km at its height.
cities.what_zh: 印加帝國的南邊，在智利中部。UNESCO 說，帝國最大的時候長達 4,200 公里。
cities.when_en: Reached under Topa Inca Yupanqui (1471–93); the model uses 1490.
cities.when_zh: 在圖帕克・印加・尤潘基（1471–93）的時候到達；模型用 1490 年。
cities.how_en: Inca histories written down by Spaniards, and archaeology along the road.
cities.how_zh: 西班牙人記下來的印加歷史，以及道路沿線的考古。

cities.what_en: An Inca city in the northern Andes, on the road between Quito and Cusco. In November 1532 Francisco Pizarro's men ambushed and captured the emperor Atahuallpa here, killing thousands of his men.
cities.what_zh: 安地斯山北部的印加城市，在基多和庫斯科之間的路上。1532 年 11 月，皮薩羅的人馬在這裡埋伏，俘虜了皇帝阿塔瓦爾帕，殺了他好幾千人。
cities.when_en: An Inca city before 1532 (the model uses 1470, when Inca rule reached the north). Atahuallpa paid a ransom of gold and silver, but the Spanish executed him in 1533.
cities.when_zh: 1532 年以前就是印加的城市（模型用 1470 年，印加勢力到達北方的時候）。阿塔瓦爾帕付了金銀的贖金，西班牙人還是在 1533 年處死了他。
cities.how_en: Accounts written by the Spanish conquerors and later Spanish chroniclers.
cities.how_zh: 西班牙征服者和後來的西班牙編年史家寫的記載。

goods.zh: 送到阿茲特克首都的貢品
goods.hands_en: Not bought or sold on the way: it was tribute, owed to the capital
goods.hands_zh: 路上沒有買賣：這是貢品，是欠首都的

legs.en: From the towns of Tochpan, garments, feathers, beads of jadeite and turquoise, and baskets of dry chili peppers went inland and up to the capital on its lake.
legs.zh: 托奇潘的城鎮把衣服、羽毛、翡翠和綠松石的珠子，還有一籃籃的乾辣椒，往內陸、往上送到湖上的首都。

goods.note_en: The Met says the Aztecs collected tribute from 38 provinces, mostly lightweight luxury goods worth carrying a long way. We know Tochpan's list because Nahua scribes painted it in the Codex Mendoza in 1542.
goods.note_zh: 大都會博物館說，阿茲特克人向 38 個省收取貢品，大多是輕巧、值得遠送的貴重物品。我們知道托奇潘送了什麼，是因為納瓦人的書記在 1542 年把它畫進了《門多薩抄本》。
goods.src: Metropolitan Museum of Art, “Paying the Man”; Britannica, “Aztec”

goods.hands_en: Passed from runner to runner the whole way: a relay
goods.hands_zh: 一路由一個信差交給下一個信差：這是接力

legs.en: Imagine a message, often in the form of a khipu of knotted cords, handed from runner to runner along the road south from Quito,
legs.zh: 想像一則消息（常常是一串打了結的繩子，khipu）從基多沿著道路往南，一個信差交給下一個信差，

legs.en: past Cajamarca and on toward the capital, at a rate of about 241 km (150 miles) a day.
legs.zh: 經過卡哈馬卡，再往首都送，一天大約可以走 241 公里（150 英里）。

goods.note_en: Britannica says use of the road system was limited to government and military business, while UNESCO says caravans and travelers used it too. This journey is an example, not a record of one message. Even in a straight line, Quito is about 1,650 km from Cusco, so at Britannica's rate a message took about a week, and longer on the winding road.
goods.note_zh: Britannica 說，這套道路只准政府和軍隊使用；UNESCO 則說商隊和旅人也走過。這段旅程是舉例，不是某一則消息的紀錄。就算走直線，基多到庫斯科也大約 1,650 公里，照 Britannica 的速度要走大約一個星期，彎彎曲曲的路還要更久。

goods.same_en: One armed force the whole way: soldiers, not traders
goods.same_zh: 一路是同一支軍隊：是軍人，不是商人

legs.en: After capturing Atahuallpa at Cajamarca in November 1532 and executing him in 1533, Pizarro's forces went south, using the Inca road network, and took Cusco in November 1533.
legs.zh: 1532 年 11 月在卡哈馬卡俘虜阿塔瓦爾帕、1533 年處死他之後，皮薩羅的軍隊利用印加的道路網往南，在 1533 年 11 月攻下庫斯科。

goods.note_en: Britannica says the Inca road network greatly helped the Spanish conquest, and that the empire was already divided by a civil war between Atahuallpa and his half-brother Huáscar. A small Inca state held out in the mountains until 1572.
goods.note_zh: Britannica 說，印加的道路網大大幫助了西班牙人的征服；而且帝國那時已經因為阿塔瓦爾帕和同父異母的哥哥瓦斯卡爾的內戰而分裂。一個小小的印加國家在山裡撐到 1572 年。

lab.numbers_note_en: Each city lights up in the year given on its card, roughly when our evidence places it on the network; many are older. Routes show only the rough direction of travel. The lines in Mexico and Central America, and the short line to the Q'eswachaka bridge, are rough sketches of contact, trade, and tribute, not mapped roads; the long Andean lines show the Inca road system, which UNESCO says covered more than 30,000 km.
lab.numbers_note_zh: 每一座城市在卡片上寫的那一年亮起來，大約是證據顯示它在這張網上的時候；很多城市其實更早就有了。路線只表示大致的方向。墨西哥和中美洲的線，以及通到克斯瓦恰卡吊橋的短線，只是往來、貿易和進貢的大略示意，不是畫出真正的路；安地斯山上的長線是印加的道路系統，UNESCO 說總長超過三萬公里。
lab.scale_en: This is a teaching sketch. The routes show only the rough direction of travel. The map shows land only, with no modern borders.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意。路線只表示大致的方向。地圖只畫陸地，不畫今天的國界。
lab.credit_html: Globe: land outlines from Natural Earth (public domain). Places and dates follow the sources listed at the bottom of the page. 地球儀：陸地外形取自 Natural Earth（公有領域）。地方和年代依本頁最下面列出的資料。

paras: By about 1500 BCE, Maya people in southern Mexico and Central America were living in villages and growing corn, beans, and squash. By 200 CE their ceremonial centers had become cities with temples, pyramids, palaces, ball courts, and plazas. They cut limestone blocks with tools of harder stone, such as chert. In the Classic Period, from about 250 to 900, there were more than 40 Maya cities, among them Tikal, Copán, and Calakmul.

The Maya developed a full writing system; Britannica calls it the only true writing system of the Americas before Europeans arrived. They carved inscriptions on stone monuments and painted books, called codices, on paper made from fig-tree bark. They counted in twenties, with a sign for zero, and kept careful calendars and tables of the Moon and Venus. After about 900, many cities of the southern lowlands emptied, while cities in the Yucatán, such as Chichén Itzá, went on. The Maya people did not disappear: more than five million people speak some 30 Mayan languages today.

The Aztecs, who called themselves the Mexica, spoke Nahuatl. Their tradition says they wandered until they saw an eagle on a cactus on a small island in Lake Texcoco, and there, about 1325, they founded Tenochtitlan. They built causeways to the shore and farmed chinampas, narrow fields built up from lake mud that gave several harvests a year. By 1519 the Aztecs and their allies ruled some 5 to 6 million people, who paid tribute to the capital.

The Inca made their capital at Cusco, high in the Andes. From 1438, under the ruler Pachacuti and his successors, they conquered an empire that stretched from what is now Ecuador to central Chile. They had no writing in the European sense; officials kept records on khipus, cords with knots that stood for numbers. They built a road network of more than 30,000 km, partly on older roads, with rope bridges over the gorges, and relay runners carried messages along it.

These peoples built without wheeled carts and without horses or oxen. Wheels existed in Mesoamerica, but only on small clay figures. People carried loads themselves, and in the Andes llamas carried them too. The Maya cut limestone with tools of harder stone, and Inca builders cut stone so precisely that their walls still stand without mortar.

In 1519 Spanish soldiers led by Hernán Cortés reached Mexico. With thousands of Indigenous allies who resented Aztec rule, and with diseases the people had never met, they took Tenochtitlan in 1521. In 1532 Francisco Pizarro captured the Inca ruler Atahuallpa at a time of civil war, and the Spanish took Cusco in 1533. Many of the first written accounts of these peoples were made by the conquerors and missionaries, so historians read them carefully, next to archaeology and the peoples' own records.
paras_zh: 大約西元前 1500 年，墨西哥南部和中美洲的馬雅人已經住在村子裡，種玉米、豆子和南瓜。到了西元 200 年，他們的祭典中心已經變成城市，有神廟、金字塔、宮殿、球場和廣場。他們用比較硬的石頭（例如燧石）做工具，切下石灰岩的石塊。在大約 250 到 900 年的古典期，馬雅有四十多座城市，例如提卡爾、科潘和卡拉克穆爾。

馬雅人發展出完整的文字系統；Britannica 說，這是歐洲人來以前美洲唯一真正的文字系統。他們把文字刻在石頭紀念碑上，也畫在用無花果樹皮做的紙上，做成書，叫做抄本（codex）。他們用二十進位，有零的符號，還有精細的曆法，以及月亮和金星的表。大約 900 年以後，南部低地的許多城市沒有人住了，猶加敦半島上的城市，例如奇琴伊察，卻繼續興盛。馬雅人並沒有消失：今天有五百多萬人說大約三十種馬雅語言。
阿茲特克人自稱墨西加人，說納瓦特語。他們的傳統說，他們四處遷移，直到在特斯科科湖的一座小島上看到一隻停在仙人掌上的老鷹；大約 1325 年，他們就在那裡建立了特諾奇提特蘭。他們修了通往岸邊的堤道，在浮田（chinampa）上耕作：浮田是用湖底的泥堆成的狹長田地，一年可以收好幾次。到了 1519 年，阿茲特克人和盟友統治了大約五、六百萬人，這些人要向首都進貢。
印加人以安地斯山高處的庫斯科為首都。從 1438 年起，在帕查庫蒂和他的繼承者手下，他們征服了一個從今天的厄瓜多延伸到智利中部的帝國。他們沒有歐洲那種意思的文字；官員用 khipu（結繩）記錄，繩子上的結代表數字。他們蓋了超過三萬公里的道路網（部分建在更早的道路上），用繩橋跨過峽谷，接力的信差沿著道路傳遞消息。
這些民族蓋這一切，沒有用有輪子的車，也沒有馬或牛。中美洲有輪子，但只出現在小小的陶土像上。東西靠人自己背；在安地斯山，駱馬也幫忙馱。馬雅人用比較硬的石頭做工具切石灰岩；印加的工匠把石頭切得非常精準，石牆不用灰漿，到今天還立著。
1519 年，科爾特斯帶領的西班牙士兵來到墨西哥。數千名不滿阿茲特克統治的原住民盟軍和他們一起作戰，加上當地人從來沒有碰過的疾病，他們在 1521 年攻下特諾奇提特蘭。1532 年，皮薩羅趁印加內戰的時候，俘虜了印加的統治者阿塔瓦爾帕；1533 年，西班牙人攻下庫斯科。關於這些民族最早的文字記載，很多是征服者和傳教士寫的，所以歷史學家讀的時候很小心，會和考古以及這些民族自己的紀錄對照。
questions: Name one thing each of the Maya, the Aztecs, and the Inca built.
How did the Inca keep records without writing in the European sense?
Why do historians read the first Spanish accounts of these peoples carefully?
answers: Maya: stone cities with pyramids (or writing, or calendars); Aztecs: Tenochtitlan on a lake, causeways, or chinampas; Inca: roads, rope bridges, or stone walls without mortar.
Officials kept khipus, knotted cords whose knots stood for numbers.
Many were written by conquerors and missionaries, who were outsiders and had their own purposes.

vocab.exzh: 馬雅的曆法用來數日子。

vocab.exzh: 馬雅人有零的符號。

vocab.ex: Tenochtitlan was built on an island.
vocab.exzh: 特諾奇提特蘭蓋在島上。

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Teotihuacan, Tikal, Copán, and Chichén Itzá are lit. Which is farthest from the others?
parts.text_zh: 特奧蒂瓦坎、提卡爾、科潘、奇琴伊察都亮了。哪一座離其他的最遠？

parts.text_en: Follow chili peppers and feathers from Tochpan to Tenochtitlan. Why doesn't this count as trade?
parts.text_zh: 跟著辣椒和羽毛從托奇潘到特諾奇提特蘭。為什麼這不算貿易？

parts.text_en: Two long roads, one in the mountains and one by the coast, all tied to Cusco.
parts.text_zh: 兩條長路，一條在山上、一條沿海，全都連到庫斯科。

parts.text_en: A message runs from Quito to Cusco, passed from hand to hand.
parts.text_zh: 一則消息從基多跑到庫斯科，一手傳一手。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then follow the Spanish march of 1532–33. How did the Inca roads help the conquerors?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著跟著 1532–33 年西班牙人的行軍走。印加的道路怎麼反而幫了征服者？

mayanum.zh: 讀一讀、寫一寫馬雅的數字
mayanum.lead_en: The Maya wrote numbers with just three signs: a dot for one, a bar for five, and a sign for zero. Numbers of 20 and more use places, like ours, but counted in twenties: the top place counts twenties and the bottom place counts ones. First read some numbers, then write some. There is no timer.
mayanum.lead_zh: 馬雅人寫數字只用三種符號：一點是 1，一橫是 5，還有一個零的符號。20 以上的數字和我們一樣用「位」，不過是二十進位：上面那一位數「幾個二十」，下面那一位數「幾個一」。先讀幾個，再自己寫幾個。不計時。
mayanum.ask_en: A dot is 1, a bar is 5; the top place counts twenties.
mayanum.ask_zh: 一點是 1、一橫是 5；上面那一位數的是幾個二十。

items.note_en: Three dots make 3. Up to four dots can sit in one place.
items.note_zh: 三個點就是 3。同一位最多可以放四個點。

items.note_en: One bar (5) and two dots (2) make 7. The dots are written above the bar.
items.note_zh: 一橫（5）加兩點（2）就是 7。點寫在橫的上面。

items.note_en: Three bars and four dots: 15 + 4 = 19, the largest number one place can hold.
items.note_zh: 三橫四點：15 + 4 = 19，一個位能放的最大的數。

items.note_en: One dot on top (1 × 20) and a zero sign below. Penn Museum's Simon Martin explains that this is how the Maya wrote 20, the same idea as our “10.”
items.note_zh: 上面一點（1 × 20），下面一個零的符號。賓州大學博物館的西蒙・馬丁說，馬雅人就是這樣寫 20 的，和我們的「10」是同一個想法。

items.note_en: Top: one dot = 20. Bottom: two bars and three dots = 13. 20 + 13 = 33.
Two bars and two dots. You didn't need the top place at all.
items.note_zh: 兩橫兩點。根本不用上面那一位。

items.note_en: Two dots on top (2 × 20) and a zero sign below. Without the zero, you could not tell 40 from 2.
items.note_zh: 上面兩點（2 × 20），下面一個零。沒有零，就分不出 40 和 2。

items.note_en: Top: one bar = 5 twenties = 100. Bottom: one bar = 5. 100 + 5 = 105.

mayanum.end_en: Britannica calls the Maya use of place value and zero among the most brilliant achievements of the human mind. The Maya used it mainly for their calendars, counting days.
mayanum.end_zh: Britannica 說，馬雅人的位值和零，可以算是人類心智最傑出的成就之一。馬雅人主要用它來算曆法、數日子。

terms.en: Where Does This Word Come From?
terms.lead_en: Foods and animals from the Americas went around the world, and many kept their names from Nahuatl, the language of the Aztecs, or Quechua, the language of the Inca. Both are still spoken today. For each Chinese word, pick the older word it came from and its English form. There is no timer.
terms.lead_zh: 美洲的食物和動物傳遍了世界，很多連名字也一起帶走：來自阿茲特克人說的納瓦特語，或印加人說的克丘亞語。這兩種語言今天都還有人在說。每一個中文詞，選出它來源的那個比較古老的字，以及它的英文。不計時。
terms.ask_en: Which older word did it come from, and what is it in English?
terms.ask_zh: 它來自哪一個比較古老的字？英文是哪一個？

items.note_en: Through Spanish. Dictionary.com says the second part, ātl, means “water,” and the first part is of unknown meaning, perhaps “bitter.”
items.note_zh: 經過西班牙文。Dictionary.com 說，後半的 ātl 是「水」，前半的意思不清楚，也許是「苦」。

items.note_en: Through Spanish tomate.
items.note_zh: 經過西班牙文 tomate。

items.note_en: Spanish speakers mixed it up with abogado, “lawyer,” which is how English got avocado.
items.note_zh: 說西班牙文的人把它和 abogado（律師）混在一起，英文的 avocado 就是這樣來的。

items.note_en: Through Mexican Spanish chile.
items.note_zh: 經過墨西哥的西班牙文 chile。

items.note_en: Through Mexican Spanish.
items.note_zh: 經過墨西哥的西班牙文。

items.note_en: Through Spanish. The Inca raised llamas and alpacas for wool and carrying loads.
items.note_zh: 經過西班牙文。印加人養駱馬和羊駝，取毛、也用來馱東西。

items.note_en: Through South American Spanish.
items.note_zh: 經過南美洲的西班牙文。

items.note_en: Through Spanish quinoa or quinua.
items.note_zh: 經過西班牙文 quinoa 或 quinua。

items.note_en: English jerky is an altered form of charqui, which came through Spanish from Quechua ch'arki.
items.note_zh: 英文的 jerky 是 charqui 變來的；charqui 經過西班牙文，來自克丘亞語 ch'arki。

items.note_en: Quechua wanu meant dung used for fuel or fertilizer.
items.note_zh: 克丘亞語 wanu 指當燃料或肥料的糞。

terms.end_en: Not every word from the Americas is Nahuatl or Quechua: potato, for example, came from Spanish patata, which first meant “sweet potato,” from Taíno, a language of the Caribbean. The words traveled with the foods.
terms.end_zh: 不是每一個美洲來的字都來自納瓦特語或克丘亞語：例如 potato（馬鈴薯）來自西班牙文 patata，原本指的是番薯，再往前是加勒比海的泰諾語。字跟著食物一起旅行。

timeline.lead_en: The Classic Maya flourished in the same centuries as the Tang dynasty; the Aztec and Inca empires rose in the 1400s, just before Spanish ships arrived.
timeline.lead_zh: 馬雅的古典期和唐朝在同樣的幾百年興盛；阿茲特克和印加帝國在十五世紀興起，就在西班牙船隻到來之前。
timeline.idle_en: Click a bar or a diamond to read its dates.
timeline.idle_zh: 點一條長條或一個菱形，讀出它的年代。

tips.en: The Classic Maya lasted about 650 years, longer than the Aztec and Inca empires put together.
tips.zh: 馬雅的古典期大約 650 年，比阿茲特克和印加帝國加起來還長。

tips.en: Tenochtitlan was founded about 1325, in the same century Mansa Musa made his pilgrimage (Lesson 13).
tips.zh: 特諾奇提特蘭大約在 1325 年建立，和曼薩・穆薩朝覲是同一個世紀（第十三課）。

tips.en: The gray diamonds mark single events, such as the fall of Tenochtitlan in 1521.
tips.zh: 灰色的菱形標的是單一事件，例如 1521 年特諾奇提特蘭陷落。

events.note_en: Large-scale growth from about 100 BCE; at its height about 500 CE; its center burned about 750.
events.note_zh: 大約西元前 100 年起大規模成長；大約 500 年最興盛；大約 750 年市中心被燒毀。

events.note_en: More than 40 cities, among them Tikal and Copán.
events.note_zh: 四十多座城市，包括提卡爾和科潘。

events.note_en: On an island in Lake Texcoco, about 1325.
events.note_zh: 大約 1325 年，在特斯科科湖的島上。

events.note_en: Alliance with Texcoco and Tlacopan under Itzcóatl (1428–40); Tenochtitlan fell on August 13, 1521.
events.note_zh: 伊茲科阿特爾（1428–40）時和特斯科科、特拉科潘結盟；1521 年 8 月 13 日特諾奇提特蘭陷落。

events.note_en: From Pachacuti (1438) to the fall of Cusco (1533); a small Inca state lasted until 1572.
events.note_zh: 從帕查庫蒂（1438）到庫斯科陷落（1533）；一個小小的印加國家撐到 1572 年。

events.note_en: Ordered by the Franciscan Diego de Landa; only four Maya codices survive today.
events.note_zh: 方濟會士蘭達下令；今天只剩四本馬雅抄本。

events.note_en: Lesson 9: the Silk Road.
events.note_zh: 第九課：絲路。

events.note_en: Lesson 13.
events.note_zh: 第十三課。

events.note_en: People had lived in the Americas for many thousands of years (Lesson 1).
events.note_zh: 美洲早就有人住了好幾萬年（第一課）。

how_we_know.eyebrow: How Do We Know? · 我們怎麼知道？
how_we_know.en: Carved stone, painted books, and knotted cords
how_we_know.zh: 刻字的石頭、畫的書，和打結的繩子
how_we_know.lead_en: Each of these peoples left its own kind of record, and each has limits. Then there are the accounts written by the Spanish.
how_we_know.lead_zh: 這幾個民族各自留下不一樣的紀錄，每一種都有限制。另外還有西班牙人寫的記載。

items.limit_en: Most Maya books were destroyed as “pagan” by Spanish priests; in 1562 Diego de Landa had books and statues burned at Maní. Only four codices survive.
items.limit_zh: 大部分的馬雅書被西班牙神父當成「異教」毀掉了；1562 年，蘭達在馬尼燒掉書和神像。今天只剩四本抄本。
items.src: Britannica, “Maya hieroglyphic writing” and “Diego de Landa”
items.text_en: Maya writing goes back at least to 300–200 BCE. Since the 1950s scholars have learned to read a substantial number of inscriptions, and they turned out to be mainly histories: events in the lives of rulers and their families, such as births, deaths, and captures.
items.text_zh: 馬雅文字至少可以追溯到西元前 300–200 年。1950 年代以來，學者讀懂了相當多的銘文；結果發現，它們主要是歷史：統治者和他們家族一生中的事，例如出生、死亡和被俘。

items.limit_en: The Codex Mendoza was made two decades after the conquest, likely for the king of Spain, with notes in Spanish. Other Nahuatl writings of the 16th century use the alphabet that Spanish priests brought.
items.limit_zh: 《門多薩抄本》是征服之後二十年才畫的，大概是要給西班牙國王看，還加了西班牙文的註記。其他十六世紀的納瓦特語文獻，用的是西班牙神父帶來的字母。
items.src: Metropolitan Museum of Art, “Paying the Man”; Britannica, “Aztec”
items.text_en: Aztec scribes, called tlacuilos, painted records in pictures and glyphs. In 1542 they painted the Codex Mendoza, with the history of the rulers, the tribute of 38 provinces, and daily life.
items.text_zh: 阿茲特克的書記叫做 tlacuilo，用圖畫和符號作紀錄。1542 年，他們畫了《門多薩抄本》，裡面有統治者的歷史、38 個省的貢品，以及日常生活。

items.limit_en: Scholars can read the numbers, but khipus that may record words have not been deciphered. Much of Inca history comes to us through Spaniards who wrote down what Inca officials told them.
items.limit_zh: 學者讀得懂數字，但可能記了話語的 khipu 還沒有解讀出來。印加的歷史，很多是透過西班牙人記下印加官員的口述才傳下來的。
items.src: Britannica, “quipu” and “Inca”
items.text_en: Inca officials at every level kept khipus. Knots stood for numbers: a figure-eight knot for 1, a long knot for 2 to 9, and single knots for tens and hundreds, with a space for zero. More than 600 khipus have been found, and roads, bridges, and buildings still stand.
items.text_zh: 印加各層級的官員都用 khipu。結代表數字：8 字結是 1，繞 2 到 9 圈的長結是 2 到 9，單結代表十、百，空著不打結就是零。目前已經找到六百多條 khipu，道路、橋和建築也還在。

views.zh: 歷史學家討論的三個問題
views.lead_en: Even good sources disagree, and old ideas get replaced. Here are three questions, with the views side by side.
views.lead_zh: 就算是好的資料也會彼此不一樣，舊的想法也會被取代。下面是三個問題，各種說法並列。
views.rule_en: Ask who wrote each source, and when.
views.rule_zh: 問一問：每一份資料是誰寫的？什麼時候寫的？

items.topic_en: How many people lived in Tenochtitlan in 1519?
items.topic_zh: 1519 年，特諾奇提特蘭住了多少人？

sides.en: Britannica's article on the Aztecs says the city covered more than 13 square km and had upward of 140,000 people, the most densely populated settlement any Mesoamerican civilization ever built.
sides.zh: Britannica 的「阿茲特克」條目說，這座城面積超過 13 平方公里，人口十四萬以上，是中美洲文明人口最密集的聚落。

sides.en: Britannica's article on Tenochtitlan gives an estimate of about 400,000 people in 1519, the largest concentration of people in Mesoamerican history.
sides.zh: Britannica 的「特諾奇提特蘭」條目估計，1519 年大約有四十萬人，是中美洲歷史上人口最集中的地方。

items.note_en: Even one encyclopedia gives two numbers, and Britannica does not explain the difference. No census survives, so every number is an estimate.
items.note_zh: 連同一套百科全書都寫了兩個數字，Britannica 也沒有解釋為什麼不一樣。當時沒有留下人口普查，所以每一個數字都是估計。

items.topic_en: Why did the Classic Maya cities of the south empty after 900?
items.topic_zh: 900 年以後，南部的馬雅古典期城市為什麼沒有人住了？

sides.en: Some scholars have pointed to armed conflict between cities and to the exhaustion of farmland.
sides.zh: 有些學者指出城市之間的戰爭，以及農地被用到耗盡。

sides.label_en: Broken trade, cut forests, and drought
sides.label_zh: 斷掉的貿易、砍光的森林和乾旱
sides.en: Discoveries in the 21st century led scholars to suggest more causes. One likely cause was wars that disrupted river and land trade routes; deforestation and drought may also have played a part.
sides.zh: 二十一世紀的新發現讓學者又提出別的原因：一個很可能的原因是戰爭讓河上和陸上的貿易路線中斷；森林被砍伐和乾旱也可能有影響。

items.note_en: Britannica lists several possible causes together and does not say which mattered most. Cities emptied, but the people did not vanish: Maya cities in the Yucatán went on for centuries, and Maya communities live in the region today.
items.note_zh: Britannica 把幾個可能的原因並列，沒有說哪一個最重要。城市空了，人卻沒有消失：猶加敦的馬雅城市又興盛了好幾百年，今天馬雅人的社區也還在那一帶。

items.topic_en: What was Machu Picchu?
items.topic_zh: 馬丘比丘到底是什麼地方？

sides.en: After 1911, Hiram Bingham claimed it was Vilcabamba, the last refuge of the Inca rulers, and later suggested it was a sanctuary for women chosen to serve the Sun. Britannica says many sources still call it the “lost city,” wrongly.
sides.zh: 1911 年以後，賓漢說它就是印加統治者最後的避難所比爾卡班巴，後來又說它是侍奉太陽的女子住的聖所。Britannica 說，很多資料到今天還把它叫做「失落之城」，這是錯的。

sides.en: Its building style and other evidence suggest it was a palace complex of the ruler Pachacuti, and its remains suggest a royal retreat. Britannica adds that the reason it was abandoned is also unknown.
sides.zh: 從建築風格和其他證據看，它可能是統治者帕查庫蒂的宮殿群；遺物也顯示它可能是王室休憩的地方。Britannica 補充說，它為什麼被放棄，也不知道。

items.note_en: Vilcabamba was later identified with another site, Espíritu Pampa. And Machu Picchu was never lost to the Quechua-speaking people who lived nearby: one of them guided Bingham there.
items.note_zh: 比爾卡班巴後來被認定是另一個遺址，埃斯皮里圖潘帕。而且，馬丘比丘對住在附近、說克丘亞語的人從來不是「失落」的：帶賓漢上去的，就是其中一位。

phrases.en: Eight sentences for talking about what people built
phrases.zh: 談人們蓋了什麼的八句英文
phrases.lead_en: These sentences help you describe how a city or road was built and how we know. Listen, repeat, then make your own sentence with the words in bold.
phrases.lead_zh: 這八句幫你描述一座城、一條路是怎麼蓋的，以及我們怎麼知道。先聽、再跟著唸，然後用粗體的字自己造一句。

rows.en: Tenochtitlan was built on an island.
rows.html: Tenochtitlan was built on an island.
rows.zh: 特諾奇提特蘭蓋在一座島上。
rows.note_en: be built on: have its base on

rows.en: The roads linked the mountains to the coast.
rows.html: The roads linked the mountains to the coast.
rows.zh: 道路把高山和海岸連起來。
rows.note_en: link: join together

rows.en: The stones fit together without mortar.
rows.html: The stones fit together without mortar.
rows.zh: 石頭不用灰漿就密合在一起。
rows.note_en: fit together without: join with nothing in between

rows.en: Farmers grew corn on chinampas.
rows.html: Farmers grew corn on chinampas.
rows.zh: 農人在浮田上種玉米。
rows.note_en: grow: raise plants

rows.en: Runners carried messages along the road.
rows.html: Runners carried messages along the road.
rows.zh: 信差沿著道路傳遞消息。
rows.note_en: carry … along: take from place to place on

rows.en: The Maya kept track of time with calendars.
rows.html: The Maya kept track of time with calendars.
rows.zh: 馬雅人用曆法記錄時間。
rows.note_en: keep track of: follow and record

rows.en: Most Maya books were destroyed.
rows.html: Most Maya books were destroyed.
rows.zh: 大部分的馬雅書被毀了。
rows.note_en: be destroyed: be ruined completely

rows.en: Maya people still live in the region today.
rows.html: Maya people still live in the region today.
rows.zh: 馬雅人今天還住在那一帶。
rows.note_en: still live: continue to live

taiwan_then.eyebrow: Taiwan at That Time · 那時候的台灣
taiwan_then.en: An ocean between, and then a link
taiwan_then.zh: 隔著一個大洋，後來連了起來
taiwan_then.lead_en: No contact between Taiwan and the Americas is known from the centuries of this lesson, but after the Spanish conquest, ships tied the two sides of the Pacific together.
taiwan_then.lead_zh: 在這一課的那幾百年，沒有台灣和美洲往來的紀錄；可是西班牙人征服美洲之後，船隻隔著太平洋把兩邊連了起來。
taiwan_then.intro_en: When Tenochtitlan was young, a Chinese traveler was writing about an island near Penghu. Nearly three centuries later, the Spanish, who by then ran the Manila galleon trade across the Pacific, founded a settlement in northern Taiwan.
taiwan_then.intro_zh: 特諾奇提特蘭剛建立不久的時候，一位中國旅行家正在寫澎湖附近的一座島。將近三百年後，已經在太平洋上經營馬尼拉大帆船貿易的西班牙人，在台灣北部建立了聚落。

facts.en: In the century when Tenochtitlan was founded, the Yuan traveler Wang Dayuan wrote of an island called Liuqiu, very near Penghu. Scholars still debate whether it means Taiwan (Lessons 9 and 13).
facts.zh: 在特諾奇提特蘭建立的那個世紀，元朝旅行家汪大淵寫到一座「自彭湖望之甚近」的「琉球」。這是不是指台灣，學者還在討論（第九、十三課）。
facts.src: 汪大淵《島夷誌略》「琉球」

facts.en: From 1565 to 1815, a Spanish galleon sailed each year between Acapulco in Mexico and Manila. It carried Chinese silk to the Americas and brought back huge quantities of Mexican silver.
facts.zh: 從 1565 到 1815 年，每年有一艘西班牙大帆船在墨西哥的阿卡普爾科和馬尼拉之間往返，把中國的絲綢運到美洲，再運回大量墨西哥的白銀。
facts.src: Britannica, “Manila galleon”

facts.en: In 1626 the Spanish founded a settlement, San Salvador, on today's Heping Island in Keelung. Archaeologists found the foundations of a church or convent and a cemetery; early findings suggest the people buried there most likely came from Europe, Asia, and possibly Africa.
facts.zh: 1626 年，西班牙人在今天基隆的和平島建立聚落「聖薩爾瓦多」。考古學家挖到教堂（或修道院）的地基和墓地；初步結果顯示，葬在那裡的人很可能來自歐洲、亞洲，也可能來自非洲。
facts.src: University of Konstanz, “A new perspective on the European colonisation of Asia” (2017)

links.en: Taiwan's Story · Lesson 6: What Did the Spanish Leave in the North?
links.zh: 台灣歷史・第六課：西班牙人在北部留下了什麼？

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Evidence · 證據背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A bridge rebuilt every year, gardens on a lake, books that were burned, and a stairway of words
culture_cards.title_zh: 每年重建的橋、湖上的田、被燒掉的書，和一道寫滿字的階梯
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about what these peoples built and how it has lasted.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 四個小故事：這些民族蓋了什麼，又怎麼留了下來。

cards.k: Every year · Q'eswachaka · 克斯瓦恰卡
cards.body_en: Over a gorge of the Apurímac River, four Quechua-speaking communities rebuild a rope bridge each year in three days. Families twist grass into thin ropes; bridge builders braid them into six great ropes; the communities weave the bridge from both ends and then hold a festival.
cards.body_zh: 在阿普里馬克河的峽谷上，四個說克丘亞語的社區每年花三天重建一座繩橋。各家先把草搓成細繩；造橋的師傅把它們編成六條大繩；社區的人從兩端一起編橋，最後辦一場慶典。

cards.body_en: Chinampas are narrow islands, some 6 to 10 meters wide and 100 to 200 meters long, built from layers of plants, earth, and mud. The lake waters and fertilizes them. Britannica says the technique is still used in Xochimilco, in Mexico City.
cards.body_zh: 浮田是狹長的人工島，大約寬 6 到 10 公尺、長 100 到 200 公尺，用一層層的植物、泥土和湖泥堆成，湖水會替它澆水、施肥。Britannica 說，墨西哥城的霍奇米爾科到今天還在用這種方法。

cards.body_en: The Franciscan friar Diego de Landa had some 5,000 Maya statues and many books destroyed at Maní, calling them the devil's work. Later, on trial in Spain, he wrote one of the main early accounts of Maya life. Only four Maya codices survive today, in Dresden, Madrid, Paris, and Mexico City.
cards.body_zh: 方濟會士蘭達在馬尼毀掉大約五千尊馬雅神像和許多書，說那是魔鬼的東西。後來他在西班牙受審時，卻寫了一本最重要的早期馬雅生活紀錄。今天只剩四本馬雅抄本，分別在德勒斯登、馬德里、巴黎和墨西哥城。

cards.body_en: At Copán, a stairway leading up to a temple carries some 1,260 glyphs on its 63 remaining steps. Reading such inscriptions since 1975 has revealed much of the city's political and dynastic history, with at least 16 kings.
cards.body_zh: 在科潘，一道通往神廟的階梯，留下來的 63 級上刻了大約 1,260 個字符。1975 年起，學者讀懂這類銘文，知道了這座城大部分的政治和王朝歷史，至少有十六位國王。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum for social studies (October 2018).
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要社會領域（民國 107 年 10 月）。

items.area: 國中・近代世界・多元世界的互動
items.area_en: Junior high · the early modern world · a world of many cultures
items.text: 美洲和澳洲的政治與文化。
items.note_en: The explanation suggests discussing the Americas before and after Europeans arrived, and how Indigenous peoples responded. This lesson tells the “before.”
items.note_zh: 課綱的說明建議討論「歐洲人抵達前後的美洲」，以及原住民族的回應。這一課講的是「抵達前」。

items.area: 高中・環境與歷史
items.area_en: Senior high · environment and history
items.text: 大航海時代的物種交流與影響。
items.note_en: Chocolate, tomatoes, chilies, and quinoa: the words game shows foods that left the Americas with their names.
items.note_zh: 巧克力、番茄、辣椒、藜麥：字源遊戲裡的食物，是連名字一起離開美洲的。

myths.myth_en: Columbus discovered America.
myths.myth_zh: 哥倫布發現了美洲。
myths.fact_en: Millions of people already lived there, and around 500 CE Teotihuacan was one of the largest cities in the world (Lesson 1 tells how people first arrived). In 1492 Columbus reached the Caribbean; Europeans met the Americas, they did not discover them.
myths.fact_zh: 那裡早就住了好幾百萬人；大約西元 500 年，特奧蒂瓦坎是世界上最大的城市之一（人最早怎麼到美洲，見第一課）。1492 年哥倫布到了加勒比海；是歐洲人遇見了美洲，不是發現了美洲。

myths.myth_en: The Maya vanished.
myths.myth_zh: 馬雅人消失了。
myths.fact_en: Many southern cities emptied after 900, but cities in the Yucatán went on, and more than five million people speak Mayan languages today. Nahuatl and Quechua are spoken today too.
myths.fact_zh: 900 年以後，南部的許多城市空了，但猶加敦的城市繼續興盛；今天有五百多萬人說馬雅語言。納瓦特語和克丘亞語今天也都還有人說。

myths.myth_en: Without wheels or iron, they could only build small things.
myths.myth_zh: 沒有輪子和鐵，只能蓋小東西。
myths.fact_en: Teotihuacan's Pyramid of the Sun rises about 66 meters, Inca walls of precisely cut stone stand without mortar, and the Inca roads covered more than 30,000 km. Wheels existed in Mesoamerica only on small figures; people and llamas carried the loads.
myths.fact_zh: 特奧蒂瓦坎的太陽金字塔大約 66 公尺高，印加精準切割的石牆不用灰漿也立得住，印加的道路總長超過三萬公里。中美洲的輪子只出現在小陶像上；東西靠人和駱馬搬運。

myths.myth_en: The Maya were peaceful stargazers.
myths.myth_zh: 馬雅人是一群愛好和平、只看星星的人。
myths.fact_en: Britannica says scholars of the mid-20th century thought so, mistakenly. Once the inscriptions could be read, they told of kings, wars, and captives, alongside the calendars and astronomy.
myths.fact_zh: Britannica 說，二十世紀中期的學者是這樣想的，但想錯了。等到讀得懂銘文，才發現上面除了曆法和天文，也記了國王、戰爭和俘虜。

tricks.body_en: The Maya: cities, writing, and a zero.
tricks.body_zh: 馬雅：城市、文字，還有零。

tricks.body_en: The Aztecs: Tenochtitlan, causeways, and chinampas.
tricks.body_zh: 阿茲特克：特諾奇提特蘭、堤道和浮田。

tricks.body_en: The Inca: 30,000 km of roads and the khipu.
tricks.body_zh: 印加：三萬公里的路和 khipu。

tricks.body_en: Maya, Nahua, and Quechua peoples live there today.
tricks.body_zh: 馬雅人、納瓦人、克丘亞人今天還住在那裡。

materials.en: Pieces of string or yarn, one per team
materials.zh: 每組一條繩子或毛線

materials.en: A card with a number for each team
materials.zh: 每組一張寫了數字的卡片

steps.en: Show the khipu code: single knots near the top for tens, a long knot (wrapped 2 to 9 times) at the bottom for ones.
steps.zh: 先說明 khipu 的記法：上面的單結代表幾個十，最下面繞 2 到 9 圈的長結代表個位。

steps.en: The first student in each team ties the number on its card. No talking and no writing.
steps.zh: 每組第一個學生把卡片上的數字打成結。不能說話、不能寫字。

steps.en: Pass the cord down the line like relay runners. The last student reads the number aloud.
steps.zh: 像接力的信差一樣，把繩子一個一個傳下去，最後一個學生大聲讀出數字。

steps.en: Discuss in English: “The message was carried along …” and “The knots stood for …”
steps.zh: 用英文討論：「The message was carried along …」和「The knots stood for …」

activities.tip_en: Real khipus used a figure-eight knot for 1; for this game, any knot will do. Remind students that khipus that may record words are still not deciphered.
activities.tip_zh: 真正的 khipu 用 8 字結代表 1；遊戲裡打什麼結都可以。提醒學生：可能記了話語的 khipu 到今天還沒有解讀出來。

materials.en: The three “How Do We Know?” cards in this lesson
materials.zh: 這一課「我們怎麼知道？」的三張卡

steps.en: In groups, list the kinds of sources: Maya inscriptions, the Codex Mendoza, khipus, and Spanish accounts.
steps.zh: 分組列出史料的種類：馬雅銘文、《門多薩抄本》、khipu，以及西班牙人的記載。

steps.en: For each, answer: Who made it? When? For whom?
steps.zh: 每一種都回答：誰做的？什麼時候？給誰看的？

steps.en: Share one thing each source can tell us and one thing it cannot.
steps.zh: 說出每一種史料能告訴我們的一件事，和不能告訴我們的一件事。

activities.tip_en: Keep the focus on evidence. If students ask about sacrifice or the conquest, answer plainly and briefly, and point out who wrote each account.
activities.tip_zh: 重點放在證據。學生問到人祭或征服時，簡短、平實地回答，並指出每一份記載是誰寫的。

links.en: What Did China Invent, and Where Did Zheng He Sail?
links.zh: 中國發明了什麼？鄭和的船去了哪裡？
links.note_en: Great voyages on the other side of the Pacific, in the same century as the Inca roads.
links.note_zh: 和印加道路同一個世紀，太平洋另一邊的大航行。

links.en: How Did Gold and Salt Build Kingdoms in Africa?
links.zh: 黃金和鹽怎麼在非洲建起王國？
links.note_en: Kingdoms of the same centuries, built on trade.
links.note_zh: 同樣的幾百年，靠貿易建起的王國。

links.en: Why Did People Invent Writing?
links.zh: 人為什麼發明文字？
links.note_en: Mesoamerica was one of the few places where writing was invented from nothing.
links.note_zh: 中美洲是少數幾個從無到有發明文字的地方之一。

links.en: How Did Humans Spread Across the World?
links.zh: 人類怎麼走到世界各地？
links.note_en: How people first reached the Americas, many thousands of years earlier.
links.note_zh: 好幾萬年前，人類最早怎麼到了美洲。

lessons.sources_note_en: Checked November 2026. Population figures, why the Classic Maya cities emptied, and what Machu Picchu was are debated; where they are, the lesson gives more than one view
lessons.sources_note_zh: 2026 年 11 月查證。人口數字、馬雅古典期城市為什麼空了，以及馬丘比丘的用途都有爭論；遇到這些地方，課文寫出不只一種說法

sources.en: The Maya: villages by 1500 BCE; cities by 200 CE; limestone cut with chert; Classic Period about 250–900; more than 40 cities; decline after 900 and its proposed causes; Postclassic Yucatán; about 30 Mayan languages and more than five million speakers today; mid-20th-century “peaceful stargazers” view mistaken
sources.zh: 馬雅：西元前 1500 年的村落；西元 200 年的城市；用燧石切石灰岩；古典期約 250–900；四十多座城市；900 年後的衰落與原因；後古典期的猶加敦；今天約三十種馬雅語言、五百多萬人；二十世紀中期「愛好和平的觀星者」的看法是錯的

sources.en: Maya writing: at least 300–200 BCE; the only true writing system of the pre-Columbian Americas; Knorozov, Berlin, Proskouriakoff; most books destroyed by Spanish priests; four codices survive
sources.zh: 馬雅文字：至少西元前 300–200 年；美洲唯一真正的文字系統；克諾羅佐夫、柏林、普羅斯庫里亞科夫的解讀；大部分的書被西班牙神父毀掉；四本抄本留存

sources.en: Maya positional numeration and zero; Dresden Codex tables of Venus and the Moon; codices on bark paper
sources.zh: 馬雅的位值記數與零；德勒斯登抄本的金星與月亮表；樹皮紙抄本
sources.src: Britannica, “Pre-Columbian civilizations: The Maya calendar and writing system”

sources.en: Maya numbers: base 20 with grouping to base 5, written vertically, used mainly for the calendar
sources.zh: 馬雅數字：二十進位、以五為一組、直寫，主要用於曆法

sources.en: A dot for one, a bar for five, and signs for zero; 20 written as a dot over a zero sign
sources.zh: 一點是一、一橫是五，以及零的符號；20 寫成一點加一個零
sources.src: Simon Martin, “Maya Calendars: An Overview,” Expedition 54, no. 1 (Penn Museum, 2012)

sources.en: Diego de Landa: the burning at Maní in 1562; Relación de las cosas de Yucatán
sources.zh: 蘭達：1562 年馬尼的焚燒；《猶加敦紀事》

sources.en: Tikal: village, ceremonial center, height 600–800; Teotihuacan's trading network; Temple IV about 65 m
sources.zh: 提卡爾：村落、祭典中心、600–800 年最興盛；特奧蒂瓦坎的貿易網；四號神廟約 65 公尺

sources.en: Copán: dynasty about 426–822; the Hieroglyphic Stairway; decipherment since 1975
sources.zh: 科潘：約 426–822 年的王朝；象形文字階梯；1975 年起的解讀

sources.en: Chichén Itzá: founded around the 6th century beside cenotes; El Castillo; ball court; Mayapán about 1200
sources.zh: 奇琴伊察：約六世紀建於天然水井旁；卡斯蒂略金字塔；球場；約 1200 年的馬雅潘

sources.en: Teotihuacan: settled by 400 BCE, large-scale growth three centuries later; about 20 square km and 125,000–200,000 people about 500 CE; center burned about 750; Pyramid of the Sun 216 feet; name from Aztec times
sources.zh: 特奧蒂瓦坎：西元前 400 年已有人居住，三百年後大規模成長；500 年時約 20 平方公里、十二萬五千到二十萬人；約 750 年市中心燒毀；太陽金字塔 216 英尺；名字是阿茲特克時代取的

sources.en: The Aztecs: Mexica and Nahuatl; the eagle and cactus tradition; 1325; Itzcóatl's alliance; 5–6 million people by 1519; Tenochtitlan upward of 140,000; Cortés, Indigenous allies, and disease; August 13, 1521; chinampas; tribute; Nahuatl writings in the Spanish alphabet
sources.zh: 阿茲特克：墨西加人與納瓦特語；老鷹與仙人掌的傳統；1325；伊茲科阿特爾的同盟；1519 年五、六百萬人；特諾奇提特蘭十四萬以上；科爾特斯、原住民盟軍和疾病；1521 年 8 月 13 日；浮田；貢品；用西班牙字母寫的納瓦特語文獻

sources.en: Tenochtitlan: about 1325; artificial islands; causeways; about 400,000 people in 1519 (estimate)
sources.zh: 特諾奇提特蘭：約 1325；人工島；堤道；1519 年約四十萬人（估計）

sources.en: Chinampas: size, construction, and use today in Xochimilco
sources.zh: 浮田：大小、做法，以及今天在霍奇米爾科的使用

sources.en: The Codex Mendoza: painted in 1542 by tlacuilos; tribute of 38 provinces; Tochpan's tribute on folio 52
sources.zh: 《門多薩抄本》：1542 年由書記畫成；38 個省的貢品；第 52 頁托奇潘的貢品
sources.src: Ji Mary Seo, “Paying the Man: Ancient Tributes in Golden Kingdoms,” Metropolitan Museum of Art (2018)

sources.en: The Inca: capital at Cusco in the 12th century; 1438 and Pachacuti; Topa Inca and Huayna Capac; about 12 million people; two north–south roads, tunnels, and suspension bridges; relay runners at about 150 miles (241 km) a day; no written records in the European sense; Spanish accounts; 1532–33; Vitcos to 1572; Quechua-speaking descendants today
sources.zh: 印加：十二世紀以庫斯科為首都；1438 年與帕查庫蒂；圖帕克・印加與瓦伊納・卡帕克；約一千兩百萬人；兩條南北向道路、隧道與吊橋；接力信差一天約 241 公里；沒有歐洲意義的文字；西班牙人的記載；1532–33；維特科斯到 1572；今天說克丘亞語的後代

sources.en: Khipus: knots for numbers; more than 600 found; possible narrative khipus not deciphered
sources.zh: 結繩：結代表數字；已發現六百多條；可能記事的結繩還沒解讀

sources.en: Qhapaq Ñan: more than 30,000 km; four main routes from Cusco's central square; up to 4,200 km; partly on pre-Inca roads; communities still care for it
sources.zh: 印加路網：超過三萬公里；從庫斯科中央廣場出發的四條主要道路；帝國長達 4,200 公里；部分建在印加之前的道路上；沿線社區至今仍守護它
sources.src: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, “Qhapaq Ñan, Andean Road System”

sources.en: The annual renewal of the Q'eswachaka bridge
sources.zh: 克斯瓦恰卡吊橋每年的重建

sources.en: Cusco: name meaning “navel” or “center”; mortarless stone walls; Koricancha; Spanish occupation in November 1533
sources.zh: 庫斯科：名字是「肚臍、中心」；不用灰漿的石牆；太陽神殿；1533 年 11 月西班牙人佔領

sources.en: Machu Picchu: mid-15th to 16th century; Pachacuti; Melchor Arteaga and Hiram Bingham in 1911; the “lost city” error; a palace complex and royal retreat
sources.zh: 馬丘比丘：十五世紀中到十六世紀；帕查庫蒂；1911 年阿特亞加與賓漢；「失落之城」的錯誤；宮殿群與王室休憩地

sources.en: Atahuallpa: civil war with Huáscar; capture at Cajamarca in November 1532; ransom; execution in 1533
sources.zh: 阿塔瓦爾帕：和瓦斯卡爾的內戰；1532 年 11 月在卡哈馬卡被俘；贖金；1533 年被處死

sources.en: Cajamarca: an ancient Inca city; the capture of Atahuallpa in 1532
sources.zh: 卡哈馬卡：古老的印加城市；1532 年阿塔瓦爾帕被俘

sources.en: Llamas: pack animals for thousands of years; raised by the Inca for wool and meat
sources.zh: 駱馬：幾千年來的馱獸；印加人養來取毛和肉

sources.en: Wheels in Mesoamerica only on small figures; no oxen or horses
sources.zh: 中美洲的輪子只在小陶像上；沒有牛和馬
sources.src: Bowers Museum, “Wheeled Jaguar Effigy, Veracruz, Mexico” (2012)

sources.en: Word origins: chocolate, tomato, avocado, chili, coyote, llama, condor, quinoa, jerky (charqui), guano, potato
sources.zh: 字源：chocolate、tomato、avocado、chili、coyote、llama、condor、quinoa、jerky（charqui）、guano、potato

sources.en: The Manila galleons, 1565–1815: Chinese silk and Mexican silver
sources.zh: 馬尼拉大帆船（1565–1815）：中國絲綢與墨西哥白銀

sources.en: Spanish Keelung: San Salvador founded in 1626; a church or convent and cemetery on Heping Island; people most likely from Europe, Asia, and possibly Africa
sources.zh: 西班牙時期的基隆：和平島的挖掘；來自歐洲、亞洲，可能還有非洲的人

sources.en: Liuqiu in the Daoyi zhilüe
sources.zh: 《島夷誌略》的「琉球」
sources.src: 汪大淵《島夷誌略》（維基文庫）

sources.en: Curriculum entries 歷 Ob-Ⅳ-2 and 歷 Ta-Ⅴ-1
sources.zh: 課綱條目 歷 Ob-Ⅳ-2、歷 Ta-Ⅴ-1
sources.src: 十二年國民基本教育課程綱要・社會領域（民國 107 年 10 月）
sources.url: https://www.naer.edu.tw/upload/1/16/doc/819/十二年國民基本教育課程綱要國民中小學暨普通型高級中等校-社會領域.pdf

sources.en: Land outlines on the globe (public domain)
sources.zh: 地球儀的陸地外形（公有領域）

lessons.title: What Did China Invent, and Where Did Zheng He Sail?
lessons.title_zh: 中國發明了什麼？鄭和的船去了哪裡？
lessons.blurb_en: Watch Zheng He's fleets reach port after port from China to East Africa on a 3D globe, and follow the first voyage, the cargo, a giraffe, and the interpreter Ma Huan. Compare ship sizes from different sources, put inventions in order, and find English words that sailed the seas of Asia.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 地球儀上看鄭和的船隊從中國一港一港到東非，跟著第一次航行、船上的貨、一隻長頸鹿和通譯馬歡走。比一比不同資料說的船有多大，把發明排出先後，也找一找在亞洲海上旅行的英文字。
lessons.big_idea_en: Paper, movable clay type, and gunpowder were developed in China, and printing grew up across East Asia; sailors in China and Europe found the compass apparently on their own. Other peoples improved these inventions, and they changed the world. From 1405 to 1433, Zheng He led seven great fleets across the Indian Ocean to ports that were already busy with trade.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 紙、膠泥活字和火藥在中國發展出來，印刷在整個東亞成長；指南針則是中國和歐洲的水手似乎各自發現的。其他民族也改良了這些發明，它們改變了世界。從 1405 到 1433 年，鄭和帶領七支大船隊橫越印度洋，到達那些本來就很熱鬧的貿易港口。

lab.title_en: The Voyages to the Western Oceans
lab.aria: 3D globe of the seas from China to East Africa showing, in rough outline, the sea routes of Zheng He's fleets from 1405 to 1433 and the ports they visited; only land, sea, and routes are drawn, with no borders · 3D 地球儀，大略畫出 1405 到 1433 年鄭和船隊從中國到東非的海路，以及停靠的港口；只畫陸地、海洋與路線，沒有國界
lab.how_en: Drag the slider from 1400 to 1440 CE, or press Play, and watch the sea routes grow voyage by voyage. Under “Follow one thing,” choose the first voyage, the cargo, a giraffe, or the interpreter Ma Huan, and a pink dot will carry it from port to port. Click a port to read about it and how we know.
lab.how_zh: 把滑桿從西元 1400 年拉到 1440 年，或按「播放」，看海路一次航行一次航行地長出來。在「跟著一件東西走」選第一次航行、船上的貨物、一隻長頸鹿或通譯馬歡，粉紅色的小點會把它一港一港帶過去。點一個港口，讀它的故事和我們怎麼知道。

cities.what_en: The Ming capital when the voyages began. The ships were built at the Longjiang shipyard here on the Yangzi River, and an 11-meter rudderpost was later found at the treasure-ship shipyard.
cities.what_zh: 下西洋開始時明朝的首都。船在這裡長江邊的龍江船廠建造；後來在寶船廠的遺址找到一根 11 公尺長的舵桿。
cities.when_en: The first fleet set out in 1405.
cities.when_zh: 第一支船隊在 1405 年出發。
cities.how_en: Ming records and the shipyard site.
cities.how_zh: 明朝的紀錄和船廠的遺址。
cities.src: Education About Asia (2014); Church, Monumenta Serica (2005)

cities.what_en: A port on the Yangzi near Suzhou where the fleet assembled before sailing south.
cities.what_zh: 長江邊、蘇州附近的港口，船隊在這裡集合，再往南航行。
cities.when_en: 1405, the first voyage.
cities.when_zh: 1405 年，第一次航行。
cities.how_en: Accounts of the voyages, summarized by Education About Asia.
cities.how_zh: 下西洋的記載（依 Education About Asia 的整理）。

cities.what_en: Where the fleet waited for the north wind before sailing out. Here in 1431 Zheng He and his officers set up a stone inscription listing all seven voyages and thanking Tianfei, the sea goddess, for protecting them.
cities.what_zh: 船隊在這裡等北風，再出海。1431 年，鄭和和他的部屬在這裡立了一塊石碑，列出七次航行，並感謝保護航海的天妃。
cities.when_en: National Geographic says the fleets went south to Fujian to take on expert sailors; the inscription says the fleet stopped here many times. The model uses 1405.
cities.when_zh: 國家地理說，船隊南下福建，招募有經驗的水手；石碑說船隊多次停在這裡。模型用 1405 年。
cities.how_en: The inscription “Tianfei lingying zhi ji” (1431), written by the fleet's own leaders.
cities.how_zh: 《天妃靈應之記》碑（1431），由船隊的領導者自己寫的。
cities.src: Tianfei lingying zhi ji (1431), Wikisource; National Geographic

cities.what_en: A kingdom on the coast of what is now southern Vietnam, the first stop of the first voyage.
cities.what_zh: 位在今天越南南部海岸的王國，第一次航行的第一站。
cities.how_en: Britannica's account of the voyages.
cities.how_zh: Britannica 對下西洋的記載。

cities.what_en: A kingdom in what is now Thailand, visited on the first voyage.
cities.what_zh: 位在今天泰國的王國，第一次航行時造訪。
cities.how_en: Britannica's account of the voyages.
cities.how_zh: Britannica 對下西洋的記載。

cities.what_en: The island of Java, visited on the first voyage.
cities.what_zh: 爪哇島，第一次航行時造訪。
cities.how_en: Britannica's account of the voyages.
cities.how_zh: Britannica 對下西洋的記載。

cities.what_en: A port on the strait between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra. National Geographic says the fleets rested here, waiting for the winter monsoon winds that blow toward the west. The inscription of 1431 says Malacca's king came to China with his family.
cities.what_zh: 馬來半島和蘇門答臘之間海峽上的港口。國家地理說，船隊在這裡休息，等待吹向西方的冬季季風。1431 年的石碑說，滿剌加的國王帶著家人到中國朝貢。
cities.when_en: 1405, the first voyage.
cities.when_zh: 1405 年，第一次航行。
cities.how_en: Britannica, National Geographic, and the fleet's own inscription.
cities.how_zh: Britannica、國家地理，以及船隊自己的石碑。

cities.what_en: A port on the northern tip of Sumatra.
cities.what_zh: 蘇門答臘北端的港口。
cities.when_en: Education About Asia lists it on the first voyage; Britannica says the fleet touched there on the way back from the third, in 1411. The model uses 1405.
cities.when_zh: Education About Asia 把它列在第一次航行；Britannica 說第三次回程的 1411 年停過這裡。模型用 1405 年。
cities.how_en: Accounts of the voyages.
cities.how_zh: 下西洋的記載。

cities.what_en: The island now called Sri Lanka. On one of the early voyages the fleet fought the forces of its king, Alagonakkara, and took him to Nanjing as a captive; the inscription of 1431 says he was later pardoned and sent home.
cities.what_zh: 今天叫斯里蘭卡的島。早期的一次航行中，船隊和國王亞烈苦奈兒的軍隊交戰，把他俘虜帶回南京；1431 年的石碑說，他後來被赦免、送回本國。
cities.when_en: First visited in 1405–07; the fighting happened on the second or third voyage (the sources differ).
cities.when_zh: 1405–07 年第一次造訪；交戰發生在第二或第三次航行（資料說法不同）。
cities.how_en: Britannica, and the fleet's own inscription, which tells it from the fleet's side.
cities.how_zh: Britannica，以及船隊自己的石碑（是從船隊的角度寫的）。
cities.src: Britannica, “Zheng He”; Tianfei lingying zhi ji (1431)

cities.what_en: A great trading port on the Malabar Coast of India and one of the most important destinations of the voyages. Britannica says Zheng He died here in 1433, on the last voyage; Education About Asia says he died on the way home, and National Geographic says during or shortly after the voyage.
cities.what_zh: 印度馬拉巴爾海岸的大貿易港，是下西洋最重要的目的地之一。Britannica 說，鄭和在最後一次航行時、1433 年死在這裡；Education About Asia 說他死在回程上，國家地理則說是在航行期間或結束不久。
cities.when_en: 1405, the first voyage, and again on later voyages.
cities.when_zh: 1405 年第一次航行，之後的航行也再來。
cities.how_en: Britannica, and the inscription, which names Calicut as the goal of the first voyage.
cities.how_zh: Britannica，以及石碑（說第一次航行「至古里等國」）。

cities.what_en: A port south of Calicut, visited on the second voyage.
cities.what_zh: 古里南邊的港口，第二次航行時造訪。
cities.how_en: Britannica and the inscription.
cities.how_zh: Britannica 和石碑。

cities.what_en: A trading city at the mouth of the Persian Gulf and one of the most important destinations of the voyages. The inscription says Hormuz sent lions, leopards, and horses to the emperor.
cities.what_zh: 波斯灣口的貿易城市，下西洋最重要的目的地之一。石碑說，忽魯謨斯送給皇帝獅子、金錢豹和大馬。
cities.when_en: Britannica says the third voyage (1409–11) reached it; the inscription, Education About Asia, and National Geographic put the first arrival on the fourth (1413). The model uses 1409.
cities.when_zh: Britannica 說第三次航行（1409–11）到達；石碑、Education About Asia 和國家地理則說第四次（1413）才第一次到。模型用 1409 年。
cities.how_en: Britannica, the inscription, and Education About Asia.
cities.how_zh: Britannica、石碑和 Education About Asia。

cities.what_en: A region on the coast of Arabia, in what is now Oman, visited by part of the fleet on the fourth voyage.
cities.what_zh: 阿拉伯半島海岸的地區（今天的阿曼），第四次航行時一支分隊造訪。
cities.when_en: Britannica: the fourth voyage (1413–15); Education About Asia puts it on the sixth.
cities.when_zh: Britannica：第四次航行（1413–15）；Education About Asia 說是第六次。
cities.how_en: Britannica's account of the voyages.
cities.how_zh: Britannica 對下西洋的記載。

cities.what_en: A port at the mouth of the Red Sea, in what is now Yemen. The inscription of 1431 says Aden sent a qilin, “called zulafa in the foreign tongue”: a giraffe.
cities.what_zh: 紅海口的港口（今天的葉門）。1431 年的石碑說，阿丹國進貢「麒麟，番名祖剌法」，也就是長頸鹿。
cities.when_en: Britannica: first visited on the fourth voyage (1413–15); Education About Asia puts it on the sixth.
cities.when_zh: Britannica：第四次航行（1413–15）第一次造訪；Education About Asia 說是第六次。
cities.how_en: Britannica and the inscription.
cities.how_zh: Britannica 和石碑。
cities.src: Britannica, “Zheng He”; Tianfei lingying zhi ji (1431)

cities.what_en: Britannica says a Chinese mission from the fleet visited Mecca and went on to Egypt. Zheng He came from a Muslim family; his father had made the pilgrimage to Mecca (Lesson 10).
cities.what_zh: Britannica 說，船隊派出的使團到過麥加，還繼續到了埃及。鄭和出身穆斯林家庭，他的父親曾到麥加朝聖（第十課）。
cities.when_en: During the fourth voyage (1413–15).
cities.when_zh: 第四次航行（1413–15）期間。
cities.how_en: Britannica's account of the voyages.
cities.how_zh: Britannica 對下西洋的記載。

cities.what_en: A port on the Somali coast of East Africa (Lesson 13). The inscription says it sent zebras and lions.
cities.what_zh: 東非索馬利亞海岸的港口（第十三課）。石碑說，它進貢了斑馬（花福祿）和獅子。
cities.when_en: Britannica says the fleet first visited towns on this coast on the fourth voyage (1413–15); Education About Asia puts Mogadishu on the sixth.
cities.when_zh: Britannica 說，船隊第四次航行（1413–15）第一次造訪這段海岸的城鎮；Education About Asia 說摩加迪休是第六次。
cities.how_en: Britannica and the inscription.
cities.how_zh: Britannica 和石碑。
cities.src: Britannica, “Zheng He”; Tianfei lingying zhi ji (1431)

cities.what_en: Britannica says the fleet visited towns in what are now Somalia and Kenya and almost reached the Mozambique Channel, without naming the Kenyan towns. The model places this dot at Malindi to stand for them.
cities.what_zh: Britannica 說，船隊造訪了今天索馬利亞和肯亞的城鎮，幾乎到了莫三比克海峽，但沒有寫出肯亞的城鎮叫什麼。模型把這一點放在馬林迪，代表那些城鎮。
cities.when_en: Fourth voyage (1413–15) or later.
cities.when_zh: 第四次航行（1413–15）或之後。
cities.how_en: Britannica's account of the voyages.
cities.how_zh: Britannica 對下西洋的記載。

goods.same_en: One fleet the whole way, stopping at port after port
goods.same_zh: 一路是同一支船隊，一港一港停靠

legs.en: Britannica says the first fleet had 62 ships and 27,800 men. It sailed south along the coast to Champa.
legs.zh: Britannica 說，第一支船隊有 62 艘船、27,800 人。它沿著海岸往南到占城。

legs.en: Then on to the island of Java,
legs.zh: 接著到爪哇島，

legs.en: and to Malacca, on the strait,
legs.zh: 再到海峽上的滿剌加，

legs.en: and Samudra, at the tip of Sumatra.
legs.zh: 和蘇門答臘北端的蘇門答剌。

legs.en: The fleet crossed the Indian Ocean to Ceylon,
legs.zh: 船隊橫越印度洋到錫蘭，

legs.en: and reached Calicut on the coast of India, returning to China in 1407.
legs.zh: 再到印度海岸的古里，1407 年回到中國。

goods.note_en: The order of stops follows Education About Asia; Britannica lists Siam too. The sources give different sizes for the fleet (see “Different Accounts”). The fleet sailed with the monsoon winds, waiting in port for the wind to change.
goods.note_zh: 停靠的順序依 Education About Asia；Britannica 還列了暹羅。各種資料說的船隊規模不一樣（見「不同的說法」）。船隊順著季風航行，在港口等風向改變。

goods.hands_en: Carried by the fleet, then traded or given as gifts at each port
goods.hands_zh: 由船隊載運，在每個港口交易或當作禮物送出

legs.en: The ships carried silk, embroidery, cotton cloth, porcelain, tea, iron, and more.
legs.zh: 船上載著絲綢、刺繡、棉布、瓷器、茶、鐵等等。

legs.en: At the great port of Calicut, merchants traded with the fleet.
legs.zh: 在古里這個大港，商人和船隊交易。

legs.en: Some went on to Hormuz, a trading city at the mouth of the Persian Gulf.
legs.zh: 有些再往忽魯謨斯去，那是波斯灣口的貿易城市。

goods.note_en: Education About Asia lists the cargo and says the fleet traded at the ports. Britannica says the Ming government used the fleets to collect tribute and extend China's influence: gifts went out, and tribute and envoys came back.
goods.note_zh: Education About Asia 列出了船上的貨物，也說船隊在各港口做生意。Britannica 說，明朝用這些船隊收取貢品、擴大影響力：禮物送出去，貢品和使節帶回來。

goods.hands_en: A gift from Aden's ruler, carried home by the fleet
goods.hands_zh: 阿丹的統治者送的禮物，由船隊帶回

legs.en: The inscription says Aden presented a qilin, “called zulafa in the foreign tongue”: a giraffe. Zulafa sounds like the Arabic zirāfah, which Dictionary.com says gave English “giraffe.”
legs.zh: 石碑說，阿丹國進貢「麒麟，番名祖剌法」，也就是長頸鹿。「祖剌法」聽起來就像阿拉伯文的 zirāfah；Dictionary.com 說，英文的 giraffe 也來自這個字。

legs.en: The fleet carried it across the Indian Ocean,
legs.zh: 船隊帶著牠橫越印度洋，

legs.en: through the strait, and home to the capital.
legs.zh: 穿過海峽，回到首都。

goods.note_en: This follows the fifth voyage (1417–19) in the inscription; the route through Calicut and Malacca is a sketch. Education About Asia and National Geographic say giraffes also came from East Africa, where the interpreter Ma Huan saw one. Qilin is the name of a creature in Chinese tradition; the fleet gave that old name to a new animal.
goods.note_zh: 這段依石碑記的第五次航行（1417–19）；經過古里和滿剌加的路線只是示意。Education About Asia 和國家地理說，長頸鹿也有從東非來的，通譯馬歡就是在東非看到的。麒麟是中國傳統裡的一種動物；船隊用這個古老的名字，稱呼一種新的動物。
goods.src: Tianfei lingying zhi ji (1431); National Geographic

goods.same_en: One traveler the whole way, writing down what he saw
goods.same_zh: 一個人走完全程，一路記下他看到的

legs.en: Ma Huan, a Muslim who had studied Arabic and Persian, served as an interpreter on the fourth voyage.
legs.zh: 馬歡是學過阿拉伯文和波斯文的穆斯林，第四次航行時擔任通譯。

legs.en: He went through the strait to Sumatra,
legs.zh: 他穿過海峽到蘇門答臘，

legs.en: across the ocean to Calicut,
legs.zh: 橫越大洋到古里，

legs.en: and on to Hormuz. He later sailed on the sixth and seventh voyages too.
legs.zh: 再到忽魯謨斯。後來他也參加了第六、第七次航行。

goods.note_en: Ma Huan wrote a book about the lands he visited, the Yingya shenglan. National Geographic calls him perhaps the most reliable of the three people who wrote about the voyages.
goods.note_zh: 馬歡把造訪過的地方寫成一本書：《瀛涯勝覽》。國家地理說，在寫下下西洋經過的三個人裡，他大概是最可靠的。

lab.numbers_note_en: Each port lights up in the year of the voyage that, according to the sources, first reached it. Routes show only the rough direction of sailing; the real routes followed the coasts and the seasonal winds.
lab.numbers_note_zh: 每一個港口在資料記載船隊第一次到達的那一年亮起來。路線只表示大致的航行方向；實際的航線沿著海岸，也跟著季節的風走。
lab.scale_en: This is a teaching sketch. The routes show only the rough direction of sailing. The map shows land only, with no modern borders.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意。路線只表示大致的航行方向。地圖只畫陸地，不畫今天的國界。
lab.credit_html: Globe: land outlines from Natural Earth (public domain). Places and dates follow the sources listed at the bottom of the page. 地球儀：陸地外形取自 Natural Earth（公有領域）。地方和年代依本頁最下面列出的資料。

paras: The oldest known piece of paper, a map found in a tomb in Gansu, was made in the 2nd century BCE. About 105 CE an official named Cai Lun recorded a way of making paper from bark, rags, hemp, and old fishnets. Paper reached Samarkand by 751 and Baghdad by 793, and by the 1300s there were paper mills in Europe.

Printing came next. Buddhist charms were printed from wood blocks in Japan about 764–770, and the Diamond Sutra, printed in China in 868, is the oldest known printed book. About 1041–48 Bi Sheng made movable type from baked clay. In Korea, movable type appeared by the 1200s, and in 1403 the king ordered 100,000 pieces of bronze type. Britannica says this knowledge does not seem to have reached Europe, where a printing press was invented about 1450.

The magnetic compass has a shared story. Late in the 11th century Shen Kuo wrote that a needle rubbed with lodestone points south, though slightly east. Britannica says that in the 12th century sailors in China and Europe found, apparently on their own, that lodestone could show them north. Gunpowder was used in China for fireworks and signals by the 10th century; knowledge of it later reached Europe, possibly through the Mongols or the Arab world.

In 1402 the Yongle emperor took the throne of the Ming dynasty. He chose Zheng He, a man from a Muslim family in Yunnan who had been captured as a boy and served the Prince of Yan, who became the Yongle emperor, to command great fleets to the “Western Oceans.” Between 1405 and 1433 Zheng He led seven voyages to Southeast Asia, India, the Persian Gulf, Arabia, and the coast of East Africa.

The fleets carried silk, porcelain, and other goods, traded at the ports, and brought envoys and tribute back to China, including a giraffe. Education About Asia says the fleet was by and large meant for peaceful diplomacy and trade, though the History of Ming says force was used against those who would not submit, and the fleet did fight: it defeated a pirate leader and captured a king of Ceylon. Calicut and Hormuz were already great trading cities; Malacca, founded only a few years earlier, grew into a major hub in that century (Lesson 9 tells of the older sea roads).

After the Yongle emperor died in 1424, the voyages were suspended; one last fleet sailed in 1431. Zheng He died in 1433, and the great fleets never sailed again. Chinese merchants and migrants, however, kept sailing to Southeast Asia, and Chinese communities grew there. About 65 years later, Portuguese ships reached India by sailing around Africa.
paras_zh: 已知最古老的紙，是在甘肅一座墓裡找到的一張地圖，做於西元前二世紀。大約西元 105 年，一位叫蔡倫的官員記下了一種用樹皮、破布、麻和舊漁網造紙的方法。紙在 751 年傳到撒馬爾罕，793 年到巴格達；到了十四世紀，歐洲已經有了造紙廠。
接下來是印刷。日本大約在 764–770 年用木版印了佛教的咒文；868 年在中國印的《金剛經》，是已知最古老的印刷書。大約 1041–48 年，畢昇用燒過的膠泥做活字。在朝鮮，活字在十三世紀已經出現；1403 年，國王下令鑄造十萬個銅活字。Britannica 說，這些知識似乎沒有傳到歐洲；歐洲大約在 1450 年發明了印刷機。
指南針的故事是大家一起寫的。十一世紀後期，沈括寫道，用磁石磨過的針會指向南方，不過「常微偏東」。Britannica 說，十二世紀時，中國和歐洲的水手似乎各自發現，磁石可以告訴他們北方在哪裡。火藥在十世紀時已經在中國用來做煙火和信號；後來它的知識傳到歐洲，可能是經由蒙古人或阿拉伯世界。
1402 年，永樂皇帝登上明朝的皇位。他選了鄭和來指揮前往「西洋」的大船隊。鄭和出身雲南的穆斯林家庭，小時候被俘，後來在燕王（後來的永樂皇帝）府中做事。從 1405 到 1433 年，鄭和七次航行，到過東南亞、印度、波斯灣、阿拉伯半島和東非海岸。
船隊載著絲綢、瓷器和其他貨物，在各港口交易，再把使節和貢品帶回中國，其中還有一隻長頸鹿。Education About Asia 說，船隊大體上是為了和平的外交和貿易；不過《明史》說，對不服的國家會「以武懾之」，船隊也確實打過仗：它打敗了一個海盜首領，也俘虜了錫蘭的一位國王。古里和忽魯謨斯本來就是大貿易城市；滿剌加才剛建立不久，在那個世紀裡成長為重要的貿易樞紐（更早的海路見第九課）。
1424 年永樂皇帝死後，航行就停了下來；1431 年又出航最後一次。鄭和在 1433 年過世，大船隊從此沒有再出海。不過，中國的商人和移民繼續航向東南亞，那裡的華人社群越來越大。大約 65 年後，葡萄牙的船繞過非洲到了印度。
questions: Name two inventions that were developed in China.
Where did Zheng He's fleets sail between 1405 and 1433?
Why do historians disagree about the size of the treasure ships?
answers: Paper, movable clay type (Bi Sheng), gunpowder (any two).
Southeast Asia, India, the Persian Gulf, Arabia, and the coast of East Africa.
The biggest number was written down more than 300 years later, and it does not match most shipwrecks, though some scholars say a giant rudderpost points to large ships.

vocab.ex: Who invented paper?
vocab.exzh: 誰發明了紙？

vocab.ex: Paper was made from bark and rags.
vocab.exzh: 紙是用樹皮和破布做的。

vocab.ex: The book was printed from wood blocks.
vocab.exzh: 這本書是用木版印的。

vocab.ex: A compass helps sailors find north.
vocab.exzh: 指南針幫水手找到北方。

vocab.ex: Zheng He led a huge fleet.
vocab.exzh: 鄭和率領一支龐大的船隊。

vocab.ex: He made seven voyages.

options: In a tomb in Gansu, China
