parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: The routes of the first voyage light up, from Nanjing down the coast and across to India.
parts.text_zh: 第一次航行的路線亮起來：從南京沿海岸往南，再橫越到印度。

parts.text_en: Follow the fleet from port to port. Why does it count as one group the whole way?
parts.text_zh: 跟著船隊一港一港走。為什麼它算是一路同一批人？

parts.text_en: A gift from Aden crosses the Indian Ocean. What did the fleet call it?
parts.text_zh: 阿丹送的禮物橫越印度洋。船隊把牠叫做什麼？

parts.text_en: Ma Huan had studied Arabic and Persian. Why would the fleet need him?
parts.text_zh: 馬歡學過阿拉伯文和波斯文。船隊為什麼需要他？

lessons.parts_note_en: Then follow the cargo. How is it different from the giraffe's journey?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著跟著船上的貨物走。它和長頸鹿的旅程有什麼不一樣？

ships.lead_en: The size of Zheng He's largest ships is one of the great debates of this story. Here the numbers from different sources are drawn to the same scale, so you can compare them. Read where each number comes from.
ships.lead_zh: 鄭和最大的船有多大，是這段歷史裡最有名的爭論之一。這裡把不同資料的數字，用同樣的比例畫出來，讓你比一比。看看每一個數字是從哪裡來的。
key: A number written down long after
很久以後才寫下的數字
A modern reading of that number
現代對那個數字的解讀

items.en: Largest treasure ship, as the History of Ming records it
items.note_en: The History of Ming, finished in 1739, more than 300 years after the voyages, says 62 great ships were 44 zhang long and 18 zhang wide. Sally Church gives this as 447 by 183 feet. Some scholars think the figure may come from a novel published in 1597.
items.note_zh: 《明史》在 1739 年完成，比下西洋晚了三百多年。它說 62 艘大船「修四十四丈、廣十八丈」；學者丘絲麗（Sally Church）換算成 447 × 183 英尺。有些學者認為，這個數字可能來自 1597 年出版的一本小說。
items.src: 明史 卷304; Church (2005)

items.en: Treasure ship, as one modern article reads the records
items.zh: 一篇現代文章對紀錄的解讀
items.note_en: An article in Education About Asia (2014) accepts ships of this size, pointing to a giant rudder found at the shipyard and to dry docks wide enough for them.
items.note_zh: 《Education About Asia》2014 年的一篇文章接受這麼大的船，理由是船廠找到的巨大舵桿，以及寬到容得下它們的船塢。
items.src: Education About Asia (2014)

items.en: Chinese ships of the 1300s and 1400s found by archaeologists
items.zh: 考古找到的十四、十五世紀中國船
items.len_zh: 通常不超過 100 英尺（30 公尺）
items.note_en: National Geographic says most marine archaeological finds suggest ships of this time were usually no longer than this, and that the claims of a 1597 adventure tale sound exaggerated.
items.note_zh: 國家地理說，大多數海底考古的發現顯示，這個時代的船通常不比這更長；1597 年一本冒險故事裡的說法聽起來太誇張。
items.src: National Geographic

items.en: Rudderpost found at the Nanjing shipyard
items.len_zh: 大約 11 公尺（36 英尺）
items.note_en: Found in 1957. Scholars disagree about what size of ship it fits: Education About Asia says it supports the records; National Geographic says it raises the possibility; Sally Church examined how it has been interpreted.
items.note_zh: 1957 年出土。它配得上多大的船，學者看法不同：Education About Asia 說它支持記載；國家地理說它讓「那麼大」有可能；丘絲麗則檢討大家怎麼解讀它。
items.src: Education About Asia; National Geographic; Church (2005)

items.note_en: Even this ship's size is uncertain: Britannica says about 117 feet; the Education About Asia article says 85 feet.
items.note_zh: 連這艘船有多大也不確定：Britannica 說大約 117 英尺；Education About Asia 那篇文章說 85 英尺。
items.src: Britannica, “Santa María”; Education About Asia

ships.foot_en: No plan or picture of a treasure ship from the time of the voyages gives its size. That is why historians argue: they weigh records written later, shipwrecks, the rudderpost, and what wooden ships can do.
ships.foot_zh: 下西洋那個時代，沒有一張寶船的圖或設計圖寫下它的大小。所以歷史學家才會爭論：他們要把後來寫的紀錄、沉船、舵桿，以及木船能做到什麼，放在一起衡量。

when.lead_en: Put these moments in the story of paper, printing, the compass, and the voyages in order, from earliest to most recent. Use the arrows or drag them. Then check your order.
when.lead_zh: 把紙、印刷、指南針和下西洋故事裡的這些時刻，從最早排到最晚。用箭頭或拖曳來移動，然後檢查。
when.hint_en: Paper had to exist before printing could spread.
when.hint_zh: 先要有紙，印刷才傳得開。

items.en: The oldest known piece of paper, a map, is made in China
items.zh: 已知最古老的紙（一張地圖）在中國做成
items.note_en: Found in a tomb at Fangmatan, Gansu, in 1986.
items.note_zh: 1986 年在甘肅放馬灘的墓裡找到。

items.note_en: Britannica: the first records of a formal papermaking process.
items.note_zh: Britannica：最早有正式造紙方法的紀錄。

items.en: The Diamond Sutra, the first known printed book
items.note_en: Printed from wood blocks (Lesson 11). Buddhist charms were printed in Japan about 764–770.
items.note_zh: 用木版印的（第十一課）。日本在大約 764–770 年印了佛教的咒文。

items.en: Bi Sheng makes movable type of baked clay
items.zh: 畢昇用燒過的膠泥做活字
items.note_en: Described by Shen Kuo in the Mengxi bitan.
items.note_zh: 沈括在《夢溪筆談》裡記下來。

items.en: Sailors in China and Europe use magnetic lodestone to find north
items.zh: 中國和歐洲的水手用磁石找北方
items.note_en: Britannica: apparently independently in both places.
items.note_zh: Britannica：兩地似乎是各自發現的。

items.en: Korea casts 100,000 pieces of bronze type
items.zh: 朝鮮鑄造十萬個銅活字
items.note_en: Ordered by King Taejong; movable type had appeared in Korea by the first half of the 13th century.
items.note_zh: 太宗下令；活字印刷在十三世紀前半已經出現在朝鮮。

items.en: Zheng He's first fleet sets sail
items.note_en: Seven voyages followed until 1433.
items.note_zh: 到 1433 年一共七次。

items.en: The printing press is invented in Europe
items.note_en: Britannica says knowledge of movable type does not seem to have reached Europe from China (Lesson 17).
items.note_zh: Britannica 說，活字的知識似乎沒有從中國傳到歐洲（第十七課）。

terms.en: Where Does This Word Come From?
terms.lead_en: Many words traveled the trade routes of Asia before reaching English. Some English words come from Chinese, often from the languages of the southern coast such as Cantonese and the Xiamen dialect, and some came by way of Malay, Arabic, or Sanskrit. Each item shows a Chinese word for a thing; pick the English word for it and the older word behind that English word. (The older word explains the English, not the Chinese.) There is no timer.
terms.lead_zh: 很多字先在亞洲的貿易路線上旅行，才進入英文。有些英文字來自漢語，常常是南方沿海的語言，例如粵語和廈門話；有些是經過馬來語、阿拉伯文或梵文才傳來的。每一題給一個中文詞，選出它的英文，以及那個英文字背後比較古老的字。（古老的字說明的是英文字的來源，不是中文詞的來源。）不計時。
terms.ask_en: Which English word is it, and what older word is behind it?
terms.ask_zh: 英文是哪一個？它背後是哪一個比較古老的字？

items.note_en: Dictionary.com: from the Xiamen dialect t'e, akin to Mandarin chá.
items.note_zh: Dictionary.com：來自廈門話的 t'e，和普通話的 chá 同源。

items.note_en: Dictionary.com traces it through Arabic ṭūfān and Cantonese taaî fung, “great wind,” influenced by Greek. Two roots met in one word.
items.note_zh: Dictionary.com 說它經過阿拉伯文 ṭūfān，也來自粵語的「大風」，又受到希臘文的影響。兩條根在一個字裡會合。

items.note_en: Literally “knock one's head”: kneeling and touching the head to the ground to show respect.
items.note_zh: 字面意思是「叩頭」：跪下、以頭觸地，表示尊敬。

items.note_en: Malay kəchap meant “fish sauce,” perhaps from a southern Chinese word. Tomatoes came much later (Lesson 14).
items.note_zh: 馬來語 kəchap 原本指「魚露」，可能來自中國南方的字。番茄是很久以後才加進去的（第十四課）。

items.note_en: Malay jong, “large ship,” possibly from the Xiamen word for a ship; English took it from Portuguese junco.
items.note_zh: 馬來語 jong 是「大船」，可能來自廈門話的「船」；英文是從葡萄牙文 junco 借來的。

items.note_en: “Three planks”: a small boat.
items.note_zh: 「三塊板」：一種小船。

items.note_en: Through Italian and French. The fleet's inscription of 1431 wrote the name as 祖剌法 (zulafa).
items.note_zh: 經過義大利文和法文。1431 年船隊的石碑把這個名字寫成「祖剌法」。

items.note_en: The name China probably goes back to Sanskrit Cīnas, “the Chinese,” from the Qin dynasty; china for porcelain is short for chinaware.
items.note_zh: China 這個名字大概來自梵文 Cīnas（「中國人」），源頭是秦；小寫的 china（瓷器）是 chinaware 的簡稱。

items.note_en: Greek sērikós meant “silken,” literally “Chinese”; the word reached Old English by way of Latin or Greek.
items.note_zh: 希臘文 sērikós 是「絲的」，字面意思是「中國的」；這個字經過拉丁文或希臘文進入古英文。

items.note_en: Cantonese for “gold citrus fruit.”
items.note_zh: 粵語的「金橘」。

terms.end_en: Many of these words come from the languages of south China's coast and Southeast Asia, and most reached English long after Zheng He. Words traveled with trade, the way silk did.
terms.end_zh: 這些字很多來自中國南方沿海和東南亞的語言，大多在鄭和之後很久才進入英文。字跟著貿易旅行，就像絲一樣。

timeline.lead_en: Paper took more than a thousand years to cross Asia to Europe. Zheng He's voyages came a lifetime before the Portuguese reached India.
timeline.lead_zh: 紙花了一千多年才橫越亞洲到歐洲。鄭和下西洋，比葡萄牙人到印度早了大約一輩子的時間。
timeline.idle_en: Click a bar or a diamond to read its dates.
timeline.idle_zh: 點一條長條或一個菱形，讀出它的年代。

tips.en: Follow paper from the East Asia lane to West Asia (751, 793) and Europe (1300s).
tips.zh: 跟著紙從東亞那一條走到西亞（751、793）和歐洲（十四世紀）。

tips.en: Korea's bronze type (1403) and Zheng He's first voyage (1405) are only two years apart.
tips.zh: 朝鮮的銅活字（1403）和鄭和第一次出航（1405）只差兩年。

tips.en: The gray diamonds mark single events, such as the Diamond Sutra in 868.
tips.zh: 灰色的菱形標的是單一事件，例如 868 年的《金剛經》。

events.note_en: The oldest paper is older still: 2nd century BCE.
events.note_zh: 最古老的紙還要更早：西元前二世紀。

events.note_en: Then Baghdad by 793 (Lesson 11).
events.note_zh: 793 年到巴格達（第十一課）。

events.note_en: The oldest known printed book.
events.note_zh: 已知最古老的印刷書。

events.note_en: Baked clay, described by Shen Kuo.
events.note_zh: 燒過的膠泥；沈括記下。

events.note_en: By the 14th century in Spain, Italy, France, and Germany.
events.note_zh: 十四世紀時，西班牙、義大利、法國和德國已經有了。

events.note_en: 100,000 pieces, ordered by King Taejong.
events.note_zh: 太宗下令鑄造十萬個。

events.note_en: Across the Indian Ocean to Calicut, Hormuz, Aden, and East Africa.
events.note_zh: 橫越印度洋到古里、忽魯謨斯、阿丹和東非。

events.note_en: About 1450 (Lesson 17).
events.note_zh: 大約 1450 年（第十七課）。

events.note_en: By sailing around Africa (Lesson 18).
events.note_zh: 繞過非洲（第十八課）。

how_we_know.eyebrow: How Do We Know? · 我們怎麼知道？
how_we_know.en: A stone the sailors carved, a book by an interpreter, and a history written much later
how_we_know.zh: 水手刻的石碑、通譯寫的書，和很久以後才寫的史書
how_we_know.lead_en: The sources for the voyages were written by different people, at different times, for different reasons.
how_we_know.lead_zh: 關於下西洋的資料，是不同的人、在不同的時候、為了不同的理由寫的。

items.limit_en: It was written by the fleet's leaders to praise the emperor and thank the sea goddess Tianfei. It tells the fighting in Ceylon and Sumatra only from the fleet's side.
items.limit_zh: 它是船隊的領導者為了頌揚皇帝、感謝海神天妃而寫的；錫蘭和蘇門答剌的戰事，只寫了船隊這一方的說法。
items.src: Tianfei lingying zhi ji (1431), Wikisource
items.text_en: Before the last voyage, Zheng He and his officers set up a stone at Changle in Fujian. It lists all seven voyages, the countries reached, and the gifts sent back, such as lions, zebras, and a giraffe.
items.text_zh: 最後一次出航前，鄭和和部屬在福建長樂立了一塊石碑，列出七次航行、到過的國家，以及送回來的禮物，例如獅子、斑馬和長頸鹿。

items.limit_en: He saw the world as a member of the fleet, and sometimes exaggerated; National Geographic notes that he described a giraffe's neck as more than 16 feet long.
items.limit_zh: 他是用船隊一員的眼光看世界，有時也會誇張；國家地理指出，他說長頸鹿的脖子有十六英尺長。
items.src: National Geographic
items.text_en: Ma Huan, an interpreter who had studied Arabic and Persian, sailed on three of the voyages and described the lands he visited in the Yingya shenglan. National Geographic calls him perhaps the most reliable of the three men who wrote about the voyages.
items.text_zh: 通譯馬歡學過阿拉伯文和波斯文，參加了三次航行，把造訪過的地方寫成《瀛涯勝覽》。國家地理說，在寫下下西洋經過的三個人裡，他大概是最可靠的。

items.limit_en: It was finished in 1739, under the next dynasty, more than 300 years after the voyages. Some scholars think its ship size came from a novel of 1597.
items.limit_zh: 它在 1739 年、下一個朝代才完成，比下西洋晚了三百多年。有些學者認為，它的寶船尺寸來自 1597 年的一本小說。
items.src: 明史 卷304 鄭和傳; Church (2005)
items.text_en: The official history of the Ming gives the famous numbers: 27,800 men and 62 great ships 44 zhang long. It also says the emperor wanted to search for the emperor he had overthrown, and to show off China's wealth and power.
items.text_zh: 明朝的正史寫下了有名的數字：二萬七千八百多人、六十二艘長四十四丈的大船。它也說，皇帝想追查被他推翻的前一位皇帝的下落，並且「耀兵異域，示中國富強」。

views.zh: 歷史學家討論的三個問題
views.lead_en: The famous numbers and reasons in this story come from sources of different ages and purposes. Here are three questions, with the views side by side.
views.lead_zh: 這段故事裡有名的數字和理由，來自年代和目的都不一樣的資料。下面是三個問題，各種說法並列。
views.rule_en: Ask who wrote each source, and when.
views.rule_zh: 問一問：每一份資料是誰寫的？什麼時候寫的？

items.topic_en: How big were the largest treasure ships?
items.topic_zh: 最大的寶船有多大？

sides.en: The History of Ming gives 44 zhang, about 447 feet. An article in Education About Asia (2014) accepts ships of about 390–408 feet, pointing to an 11-meter rudderpost found at the shipyard in 1957 and to dry docks wide enough for them.
sides.zh: 《明史》寫四十四丈，大約 447 英尺。《Education About Asia》2014 年的一篇文章接受大約 390–408 英尺的說法，理由是 1957 年在船廠找到的 11 公尺舵桿，以及寬到容得下它們的船塢。
sides.src: 明史 卷304; Education About Asia (2014)

sides.en: National Geographic says the claim of a 1597 adventure tale sounds exaggerated, and that most finds suggest ships of the time were usually no longer than 100 feet. Sally Church tested the 447-foot figure against the earlier sources, shipwrecks, the rudderpost, and the wood such ships would need, and notes the suggestion that the number came from that novel.
sides.zh: 國家地理說，1597 年那本冒險故事的說法聽起來太誇張，大部分的發現顯示那個時代的船通常不超過 100 英尺。丘絲麗拿更早的資料、沉船、舵桿，以及造船要用的木材，來檢驗 447 英尺這個數字，並提到有人認為這個數字來自那本小說。

items.note_en: Both sides agree the fleets were very large for their time. The question is how large the biggest ship really was.
items.note_zh: 兩邊都同意，以那個時代來說船隊非常龐大；爭的是最大的那一艘到底有多大。

items.topic_en: How big was the fleet?
items.topic_zh: 船隊有多大？

sides.en: The inscription of 1431, written by Zheng He and his officers, speaks of the voyages in general: “tens of thousands” of officers and soldiers on “more than a hundred great ships.”
sides.zh: 1431 年鄭和和部屬立的石碑，概括地說整個下西洋：「統率官校旗軍數萬人，乘巨舶百餘艘」。

sides.en: The History of Ming gives 27,800 men and 62 great ships for the first voyage; Britannica gives 62 ships. National Geographic gives 255 ships, 62 of them treasure ships, and Education About Asia gives 317 ships.
sides.zh: 《明史》說第一次有二萬七千八百多人、六十二艘大船；Britannica 寫 62 艘船。國家地理說 255 艘，其中 62 艘是寶船；Education About Asia 說 317 艘。
sides.src: 明史; Britannica; National Geographic; Education About Asia

items.note_en: Part of the difference is what is counted: only the great treasure ships, or every supply ship, horse ship, and warship too.
items.note_zh: 差別有一部分在於算的是什麼：只算大寶船，還是連補給船、馬船、戰船都算進去。

items.topic_en: Why did the voyages happen, and why did they stop?
items.topic_zh: 為什麼要下西洋？又為什麼停了？

sides.en: The History of Ming says the emperor wanted to find the emperor he had overthrown and to show off China's power. Education About Asia says most historians doubt the search story, and lists other motives: showing power, gaining influence and trade, finding allies, and winning foreign recognition for an emperor who had seized the throne.
sides.zh: 《明史》說，皇帝想找出被他推翻的前一位皇帝，並且炫耀中國的力量。Education About Asia 說，多數歷史學家不太相信「尋人」的說法，另外列出其他動機：展示武力、擴大影響和貿易、尋找盟友，以及讓外國承認這位奪位的皇帝。

sides.en: Britannica says some historians see no achievement beyond flattering the emperor's vanity, while the voyages did extend China's political influence over maritime Asia for half a century. After 1424 the court suspended them, and after 1433 they ended. Education About Asia points to the cost and to objections from Confucian officials; National Geographic says the problem was political, not economic: concern with the northern frontier and suspicion from powerful officials.
sides.zh: Britannica 說，有些歷史學家認為，除了滿足皇帝的虛榮以外沒有什麼成就；不過這些航行確實讓中國在海上亞洲的政治影響力維持了半個世紀。1424 年以後朝廷暫停了航行，1433 年以後就結束了。Education About Asia 指出花費太大，以及儒家官員的反對；國家地理則說問題不在經濟而在政治：朝廷把注意力轉向北方邊境，有權勢的官員也對航行有疑慮。

items.note_en: Britannica also notes that, unlike later European voyages, these did not lead to trading empires, though Chinese migration to Southeast Asia grew after them.
items.note_zh: Britannica 也指出，和後來歐洲人的航行不同，下西洋沒有建立起貿易帝國；不過在那之後，中國人移居東南亞的越來越多。

phrases.en: Eight sentences for talking about inventions and voyages
phrases.zh: 談發明和航行的八句英文
phrases.lead_en: These sentences help you describe who invented or improved something, and where a voyage went. Listen, repeat, then make your own sentence with the words in bold.
phrases.lead_zh: 這八句幫你描述誰發明或改良了什麼，以及一次航行去了哪裡。先聽、再跟著唸，然後用粗體的字自己造一句。

rows.en: Paper was invented in China.
rows.html: Paper was invented in China.
rows.zh: 紙是在中國發明的。
rows.note_en: be invented in: be first made in

rows.en: Papermaking spread to Baghdad.
rows.html: Papermaking spread to Baghdad.
rows.zh: 造紙術傳到了巴格達。
rows.note_en: spread to: reach a new place

rows.en: Korea improved movable type.
rows.html: Korea improved movable type.
rows.zh: 朝鮮改良了活字。
rows.note_en: improve: make better

rows.en: Sailors in two places found it independently.
rows.html: Sailors in two places found it independently.
rows.zh: 兩個地方的水手各自發現了它。
rows.note_en: independently: each on their own

rows.en: Zheng He set sail in 1405.
rows.html: Zheng He set sail in 1405.
rows.zh: 鄭和在 1405 年出航。
rows.note_en: set sail: begin a voyage

rows.en: The fleet called at Calicut.
rows.html: The fleet called at Calicut.
rows.zh: 船隊停靠古里。
rows.note_en: call at: stop at a port

rows.en: Envoys returned with the fleet.
rows.html: Envoys returned with the fleet.
rows.zh: 使節跟著船隊回來。
rows.note_en: return with: come back together with

rows.en: Historians disagree about the size of the ships.
rows.html: Historians disagree about the size of the ships.
rows.zh: 歷史學家對船的大小意見不一。
rows.note_en: disagree about: have different views on

taiwan_then.eyebrow: Taiwan at That Time · 那時候的台灣
taiwan_then.en: Legends of a eunuch, and a visit by the Ming navy
taiwan_then.zh: 三保太監的傳說，和明朝水師的一次來訪
taiwan_then.lead_en: Taiwan is not among the places that the inscription of 1431 or Britannica lists for the voyages. Yet stories about Zheng He grew up here later.
taiwan_then.lead_zh: 1431 年的石碑和 Britannica 列出的下西洋地點裡，沒有台灣。可是後來，台灣也長出了關於鄭和的故事。
taiwan_then.intro_en: Separate what a source says happened from what it says people believed. Taiwan's oldest gazetteer marks some of these stories with the words “it is said.”
taiwan_then.intro_zh: 要分清楚：資料說「發生了什麼」，和資料說「人們相信什麼」。台灣最早的方志，在其中一些故事前面寫著「相傳」。

facts.en: Taiwan's first gazetteer, compiled in 1685, says that in the Xuande years (1426–35) the eunuch “Wang Sanbao” took water from a great well in Tainan, and that ginger he planted on a mountain could cure any illness. It begins the ginger story with “it is said.”
facts.zh: 1685 年編成的台灣第一部府志說，明宣德年間（1426–35），「太監王三保」曾到台南的大井取水；又說「相傳」三保太監在山上種的薑，「百病食之皆瘳」。
facts.src: 蔣毓英《臺灣府志》卷10（1685）

facts.en: The History of Ming says Zheng He was the one known as the Sanbao eunuch, and his fellow envoy was Wang Jinghong. The gazetteer does not explain the “Wang.” One guess is that two names got mixed, but no source says so. These stories were written down more than 250 years after the voyages.
facts.zh: 《明史》說，鄭和就是「世所謂三保太監者」，和他一起出使的是王景弘。府志沒有解釋這個「王」字。一種猜測是兩個人的名字被弄混了，但沒有任何資料這樣說。這些故事是在下西洋兩百五十多年後才寫下來的。
facts.src: 明史 卷304; 天妃靈應之記

facts.en: In the winter of 1602–03 a Ming general, General Shen of Wuyu (usually identified as Shen Yourong), sailed to Taiwan to fight pirates, and Chen Di went with him. His Dongfan ji is an early, detailed record of Taiwan's customs (Lesson 11). It also repeats an older story that early in the Yongle years a eunuch named Zheng sailed to instruct foreign peoples; like the gazetteer's stories, no record of the voyages confirms that he reached Taiwan.
facts.zh: 1602 年冬，「浯嶼沈將軍」（一般認為是沈有容）到台灣剿滅倭寇，陳第跟著去。他的《東番記》是一份早期、詳細的台灣風俗紀錄（第十一課）。它也轉述了一個更早的故事：永樂初年，「鄭內監航海諭諸夷」；和府志的故事一樣，下西洋的紀錄裡找不到他到過台灣的證據。

links.en: Taiwan's Story · Lesson 4: How Did the World First Draw Taiwan?
links.zh: 台灣歷史・第四課：世界最早怎麼畫台灣？

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Evidence · 證據背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A needle that leans east, clay type, a goddess of the sea, and a qilin with long legs
culture_cards.title_zh: 偏東的針、膠泥活字、海上的女神，和長腿的麒麟
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories from the books and stones of this lesson.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 這一課的書和石碑裡的四個小故事。

cards.k: Late 11th century · Shen Kuo · 沈括
cards.en: A needle that leans a little east
cards.body_en: Shen Kuo wrote that a needle rubbed on lodestone points south, “but always slightly east, not exactly south.” He compared floating it on water, balancing it on a fingernail or a bowl's rim, and hanging it from a thread, which he found best.
cards.body_zh: 沈括寫道，用磁石磨過的針會指南，「然常微偏東，不全南也」。他比較了把針浮在水上、放在指甲或碗邊上，以及用絲線吊起來，結論是「不若縷懸為最善」。

cards.en: Type as thin as a coin's edge
cards.body_en: Shen Kuo also recorded that a commoner named Bi Sheng carved characters in clay, each one a separate piece “as thin as the edge of a coin,” and baked them hard. Britannica says the idea was not followed up in China, while Korea developed movable type further.
cards.body_zh: 沈括也記下，平民畢昇「用膠泥刻字，薄如錢唇，每字為一印，火燒令堅」。Britannica 說，這個方法在中國沒有繼續發展，朝鮮則把活字發展得更遠。

cards.body_en: On their stone, Zheng He and his officers wrote that in storms “a divine lantern” appeared on the masts, and thanked Tianfei, the sea goddess known in Taiwan today as Mazu, for every safe return.
cards.body_zh: 鄭和和部屬在石碑上寫道，遇到風濤時，「有神燈燭於帆檣」；他們感謝天妃（今天台灣熟悉的媽祖）保佑每一次平安歸來。

cards.body_en: The inscription lists the gifts of the fifth voyage: lions, leopards, and horses from Hormuz; a qilin, “called zulafa in the foreign tongue,” from Aden; zebras from Mogadishu; and ostriches from Brava.
cards.body_zh: 石碑列出第五次航行帶回的禮物：忽魯謨斯的獅子、金錢豹和大馬；阿丹的「麒麟，番名祖剌法」；木骨都束的花福祿（斑馬）；卜剌哇的駝雞（鴕鳥）。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: These entries come from Taiwan's 12-Year Basic Education curriculum for social studies (October 2018).
curric.lead_zh: 下面的條目出自十二年國民基本教育課程綱要社會領域（民國 107 年 10 月）。

items.area: 國中・從傳統到現代・東亞世界
items.area_en: Junior high · from tradition to modern times · the East Asian world
items.text: 明、清時期東亞世界的商貿與文化交流。
items.note_en: The explanation names trade networks and cultural exchange, including pirates and sea merchants. Zheng He's voyages and the Ming navy's visit to Taiwan in 1603 fit here.
items.note_zh: 課綱的說明提到商貿網絡與文化交流，包括海盜、「倭寇」與海商的活動。鄭和下西洋和 1603 年明朝水師到台灣，都可以放在這裡。

items.area: 高中・人群的移動與交流
items.area_en: Senior high · the movement and exchange of peoples
items.text: 明、清時期東亞人群移動的特色與影響。
items.note_en: The explanation mentions migration to Southeast Asia from the middle and late Ming. Britannica says Chinese migration there grew after the voyages.
items.note_zh: 課綱的說明提到明代中晚期以後向東南亞的移民。Britannica 說，下西洋之後移居東南亞的中國人越來越多。

myths.myth_en: China invented everything first, and the rest of the world just copied.
myths.myth_zh: 什麼都是中國最先發明的，別人只是照抄。
myths.fact_en: Japan printed charms before the Diamond Sutra; Korea developed bronze movable type; Britannica says sailors in China and Europe found the lodestone compass apparently independently, and that movable type does not seem to have reached Europe from China. Inventions often have more than one home.
myths.fact_zh: 日本印咒文比《金剛經》還早；朝鮮發展了銅活字；Britannica 說，中國和歐洲的水手似乎各自發現了磁石指北，活字的知識似乎也沒有從中國傳到歐洲。很多發明不只有一個家鄉。

myths.myth_en: Zheng He discovered new lands.
myths.myth_zh: 鄭和發現了新的土地。
myths.fact_en: Great ports such as Calicut and Hormuz were already busy. Britannica says Indian and Muslim visitors had long sailed to China, and Chinese seaborne trade had been growing for some 300 years. The fleet even brought interpreters who knew Arabic and Persian.
myths.fact_zh: 古里、忽魯謨斯這些大港本來就很熱鬧。Britannica 說，印度人和穆斯林早就航行到中國，中國的海上貿易也已經成長了大約三百年。船隊甚至帶了懂阿拉伯文和波斯文的通譯。

myths.myth_en: The fleets never fought anyone.
myths.myth_zh: 船隊從來沒有打過仗。
myths.fact_en: Education About Asia says the fleet was mostly meant for peaceful diplomacy and trade, but the fleet's own inscription tells of defeating a pirate leader, capturing a king of Ceylon, and capturing a rival ruler in Sumatra. The fleet carried soldiers.
myths.fact_zh: Education About Asia 說船隊大體上是為了和平的外交和貿易，但船隊自己的石碑寫著：打敗海盜首領、俘虜錫蘭國王、在蘇門答剌活捉一位爭位的統治者。船隊是載著軍人的。

myths.myth_en: After 1433 China turned its back on the sea.
myths.myth_zh: 1433 年以後，中國就背對大海了。
myths.fact_en: The great state fleets stopped, but Britannica says Chinese emigration to Southeast Asia grew, along with tributary trade that lasted into the 19th century.
myths.fact_zh: 國家派出的大船隊是停了，但 Britannica 說，移居東南亞的中國人越來越多，朝貢貿易也一直延續到十九世紀。

tricks.body_en: Paper, then printing, then books for many.
tricks.body_zh: 先有紙，再有印刷，書才多起來。

tricks.body_en: China, Korea, Japan, and Europe each added a piece.
tricks.body_zh: 中國、朝鮮、日本、歐洲各添了一塊。

tricks.body_en: 1405 to 1433, to India, Arabia, and Africa.
tricks.body_zh: 1405 到 1433，到印度、阿拉伯、非洲。

tricks.body_en: A famous size was written 300 years later.
tricks.body_zh: 有名的尺寸是三百年後才寫的。

activities.title_zh: 做一個浮在水上的指南針

materials.en: A sewing needle, a magnet, a small piece of cork or leaf, and a bowl of water
materials.zh: 一根縫衣針、一塊磁鐵、一小片軟木或葉子、一碗水

steps.en: Stroke the needle with one end of the magnet about 30 times, always in the same direction.
steps.zh: 用磁鐵的一端，朝同一個方向把針摩擦大約三十次。

steps.en: Lay the needle on the cork and float it in the bowl. Wait until it stops turning.
steps.zh: 把針放在軟木上，浮在碗裡，等它停下來。

steps.en: Compare with a phone compass. Does it point north–south? Is it a little off?
steps.zh: 和手機的指南針比一比：它指著南北嗎？是不是有一點偏？

steps.en: Read Shen Kuo's words aloud and say in English: “The needle points …”
steps.zh: 讀一讀沈括的話，再用英文說：「The needle points …」

activities.tip_en: Shen Kuo noticed his needle pointed slightly east of south. A magnetic needle does not point exactly to true north; how far off it is depends on where and when you are.
activities.tip_zh: 沈括發現他的針「常微偏東」。磁針不會正好指著真正的北方；偏多少，要看你在哪裡、在什麼時候。

materials.en: The ship-size chart and the three “How Do We Know?” cards in this lesson
materials.zh: 這一課的船長度圖，和「我們怎麼知道？」的三張卡

steps.en: In groups, take one number each: 447 feet, 390–408 feet, 100 feet, the 11-meter rudderpost.
steps.zh: 分組，每組拿一個數字：447 英尺、390–408 英尺、100 英尺、11 公尺的舵桿。

steps.en: Find out who gave the number, when, and what evidence they used.
steps.zh: 查出這個數字是誰說的、什麼時候說的、用了什麼證據。

steps.en: Measure the length on the school field with a tape or by counting steps.
steps.zh: 在操場上用捲尺或數步伐，量出那個長度。

steps.en: Discuss in English: “Historians disagree about …” and “This number comes from …”
steps.zh: 用英文討論：「Historians disagree about …」和「This number comes from …」

activities.tip_en: Let students stand at the end of each length. The point is not to decide the answer but to see why the evidence matters.
activities.tip_zh: 讓學生站在每一個長度的終點。重點不是決定答案，而是看出證據為什麼重要。

links.en: How Did the Mongols and the Pacific Navigators Cross Such Distances?
links.zh: 蒙古人和太平洋的航海者怎麼跨過那麼遠的距離？
links.note_en: Other ways of crossing great distances, by land and by sea.
links.note_zh: 跨越遙遠距離的其他方法，陸上和海上。

links.en: What Did the Maya, Aztecs, and Inca Build?
links.zh: 馬雅、阿茲特克、印加蓋了什麼？
links.note_en: Roads and runners in the Andes in the same century.
links.note_zh: 同一個世紀，安地斯山上的道路和信差。

links.en: Who Kept Knowledge Alive?
links.zh: 誰把知識保存下來？
links.note_en: Paper's journey west and the Diamond Sutra.
links.note_zh: 紙往西的旅程和《金剛經》。

links.en: What Traveled Along the Silk Road?
links.zh: 絲路上走的是什麼？
links.note_en: The sea roads of the Indian Ocean before Zheng He.
links.note_zh: 鄭和之前的印度洋海路。

lessons.sources_note_en: Checked November 2026. The size of the treasure ships, the size of the fleet, and the reasons for the voyages are debated; where they are, the lesson gives more than one view
lessons.sources_note_zh: 2026 年 11 月查證。寶船的大小、船隊的規模和下西洋的理由都有爭論；遇到這些地方，課文寫出不只一種說法

sources.en: Zheng He: Hui family, 1381 capture, Yongle emperor, seven voyages 1405–33, 62 ships and 27,800 men, ports, Ceylon, Hormuz, Aden, Mecca mission, East Africa, envoys, suspension after 1424, death in Calicut 1433, assessment and migration
sources.zh: 鄭和：回族家庭、1381 年被俘、永樂皇帝、1405–33 年七次航行、62 艘船 27,800 人、港口、錫蘭、忽魯謨斯、阿丹、麥加使團、東非、使節、1424 年後暫停、1433 年死於古里、評價與移民

sources.en: The Ming dynasty: tribute-collecting flotillas commanded by Zheng He
sources.zh: 明朝：鄭和率領的收取貢品的船隊

sources.en: Zheng He's voyages: motives, Longjiang shipyard, ship types, cargo, Liujiagang, 390–408 ft reading, 1957 rudder, dry docks, Santa María 85 ft
sources.zh: 鄭和下西洋：動機、龍江船廠、船的種類、貨物、劉家港、390–408 英尺的解讀、1957 年的舵、船塢、聖瑪利亞號 85 英尺
sources.src: Yang Wei, “Admiral Zheng He's Voyages to the ‘West Oceans’,” Education About Asia (Association for Asian Studies, 2014)

sources.en: Fleet of 255 ships with 62 treasure ships; Fujian sailors; Malacca and the monsoon; the 1597 tale; shipwrecks usually under 100 ft; Ma Huan; giraffe; end of the voyages
sources.zh: 255 艘船、其中 62 艘寶船；福建水手；麻六甲與季風；1597 年的故事；沉船通常不到 100 英尺；馬歡；長頸鹿；航行的結束
sources.src: Dolors Folch, “China's greatest naval explorer sailed his treasure fleets as far as East Africa,” National Geographic (2020)

sources.en: “Zheng He: An Investigation into the Plausibility of 450-ft Treasure Ships” (44 by 18 zhang = 447 by 183 ft; the 1597 novel; the 11-meter rudderpost)
sources.zh: 〈鄭和：450 英尺寶船可信度的探討〉（四十四丈 × 十八丈 ＝ 447 × 183 英尺；1597 年的小說；11 公尺的舵桿）
